1.name: Calcium Chloride
1.description: An inorganic salt used as a firming agent, preservative, and mineral supplement in food products.
1.benefits: Enhances texture by firming, provides a source of calcium, acts as a preservative
1.risks: Irritation or sensitization at high concentrations, potential excess calcium intake with very high consumption

sources.label: Safety evaluation of calcium chloride in food
Calcium chloride use as a firming agent and mineral source

2.name: Magnesium Chloride
2.description: An inorganic salt used as a dietary supplement and in small amounts as a food additive. It contributes magnesium ions which are essential minerals for many physiological functions.
2.benefits: Provides bioavailable magnesium essential for muscle and nerve function, electrolyte balance, and enzymatic reactions
2.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation and laxative effects at high oral doses, irritation risk if in direct skin contact in concentrated form

sources.label: Magnesium absorption from magnesium chloride in humans
Safety and efficacy of magnesium chloride

3.name: Potassium Bicarbonate
3.description: Potassium bicarbonate is a potassium salt used as a leavening agent, pH buffer, and acidity regulator in food products.
3.benefits: Regulates acidity, acts as leavening agent, source of dietary potassium

sources.label: Effects of potassium bicarbonate intake on health

4.name: Electrolytes
4.description: Minerals such as sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium that help maintain fluid balance and electric activity in the body.
4.benefits: Supports hydration, nerve function, muscle contraction, and electrolyte balance
4.risks: Excessive intake may cause electrolyte imbalance, hypertension, or kidney strain

5.name: Sodium Bicarbonate
5.description: Inorganic compound commonly used as a leavening agent in food, and as an acid neutralizer.
5.benefits: Leavening agent in baking, pH neutralizer, inexpensive and effective
5.risks: Irritation risk if inhaled or in high oral doses causing alkalosis, digestive discomfort at high intake

sources.label: PMC2709278 - Safety and applications of sodium bicarbonate

6.name: Magnesium Sulfate
6.description: An inorganic salt commonly used as a dietary supplement and laxative, also found in bath salts for topical use.
6.benefits: Provides magnesium essential for muscle and nerve function, electrolyte balance, mild laxative effect
6.risks: Irritation if ingested in high doses, potential laxative effects, possible skin dryness or irritation with topical use

sources.label: PMCID: PMC3193655 - Magnesium in human health
PMID: 19703202 - Magnesium sulfate as a laxative

8.name: Bromide
8.description: Bromide is a halide ion derived from bromine, commonly found in various industrial and chemical applications. It can be present as inorganic salts or as organic brominated compounds.
8.risks: Toxicity from ingestion or chronic exposure, potential neurotoxicity, interference with iodine uptake affecting thyroid function, possible contamination with brominated compounds

9.name: Chloride
9.description: An essential inorganic anion commonly found in body fluids and chloride-containing compounds. It helps maintain fluid balance and acid-base equilibrium.
9.benefits: Supports electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and proper nerve and muscle function
9.risks: Excessive intake may contribute to hypertension and cardiovascular risk when associated with high sodium intake

10.name: Sulfate
10.description: A chemical compound containing the sulfate ion (SO4²⁻), commonly used in personal care products as surfactants (e.g., sodium lauryl sulfate) due to their cleansing and foaming properties.
10.benefits: Effective cleansing and foaming agent in personal care products
10.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, potential to disrupt skin barrier with prolonged exposure

12.name: Total Trihalomethanes
12.description: Group of chemical compounds formed as disinfection byproducts during chlorination of water, including chloroform, bromodichloromethane, dibromochloromethane, and bromoform.
12.risks: Carcinogenic potential, contaminated drinking water, regulatory limits due to toxicity, ingestion toxicity

sources.label: PMC1369070 – Health effects of trihalomethanes in drinking water
EPA - Total Trihalomethanes (TTHMs) Drinking Water Regulations

13.name: Sodium Sulfate
13.description: Inorganic salt commonly used as a filler or processing aid in cleaning products. Generally regarded as safe with low toxicity and minimal skin or eye irritation potential.
13.benefits: Inert filler, cost-effective, low environmental impact

sources.label: ECHA Sodium Sulfate Registration Dossier
PubChem Sodium Sulfate Summary

14.name: Gross Alpha
14.description: Measures the total alpha radiation emitted by all alpha-emitting radionuclides in a water sample, such as uranium and thorium, to assess overall alpha radiation levels.
14.risks: Internal tissue damage and increased cancer risk due to their ionizing nature when ingested or inhaled.

sources.label: Gross Alpha Radiation in Drinking Water - Vermont Department of Health

Yan Shi, Wa Gao, Tuya Siqin, Zhigang Li, Jianwei Zhang, Rongshu Guan, Jinfeng Li, Peilin Sun, Hongtao Zhao, The gross α and β radioactivity levels of drinking water source in one oil industrial city in northeast China, 2021

15.name: Gross Beta
15.description: Measures the total beta radiation emitted by all beta-emitting radionuclides in a water sample, such as strontium-90 and cesium-137, to evaluate overall beta radiation levels.
15.risks: Internal tissue damage, increased cancer risk, and potential harm to the thyroid.

16.name: Radium 226/228
16.description: Radioactive isotopes of radium that emit alpha, beta, and gamma radiation. Not used as a food ingredient. Exposure poses significant radiological health risks including cancer and radiation sickness.
16.risks: Radiation exposure, carcinogenicity, bone cancer, organ damage, radiation sickness

sources.label: Radium Toxicity - NCBI Bookshelf
ATSDR - Toxicological Profile for Radium

17.name: Silica
17.description: Inert mineral compound (silicon dioxide) used primarily as an anti-caking agent and absorbent in food and industrial products.
17.benefits: Prevents clumping and improves texture in powdered products
17.risks: Minor respiratory irritation risk from inhalation of fine dust; minimal concern at typical ingestion levels

sources.label: PMC5826121 - Safety evaluation of synthetic amorphous silica

20.name: Arsenic
20.description: A toxic metalloid element found in the environment often as a contaminant in water, soil, and food.
20.risks: Carcinogenicity, acute and chronic poisoning, neurotoxicity, skin lesions, cardiovascular disease, contamination risk

sources.label: PMC1241816 – Arsenic exposure and toxicity mechanisms
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Arsenic
EPA – Arsenic in Drinking Water

21.name: Barium
21.description: A soft, silvery alkaline earth metal used in various industrial applications and sometimes as a contrast agent in medical imaging.
21.risks: Toxic if ingested or inhaled, can cause muscle weakness, cardiovascular effects, and respiratory paralysis, contamination risk

sources.label: Barium Toxicity - NCBI Bookshelf
ECHA Registration Dossier for Barium

22.name: Fluoride
22.description: Inorganic compound commonly used in dental care products to prevent tooth decay through enamel remineralization.
22.benefits: Prevents dental caries, strengthens tooth enamel
22.risks: Dental fluorosis with excessive ingestion, neurotoxicity concerns at high exposure, skeletal fluorosis in chronic high doses

sources.label: PMC5804329 – Review on fluoride safety and efficacy in dental health
PMID 25156844 – Fluoride neurotoxicity systematic review

23.name: Nitrate (as NO₃⁻)
23.description: An inorganic ion commonly found in soil, water, and food, used as a preservative and nutrient source in agriculture and food processing.
23.benefits: Used as a food preservative to inhibit microbial growth, supports plant nutrition and growth
23.risks: Potential to form nitrosamines which are carcinogenic, methemoglobinemia risk especially in infants, contamination from agricultural runoff

sources.label: PMID 23821563 - Nitrate in drinking water and health risks
PMID 24647704 - Nitrate, nitrite and N-nitroso compounds in food and cancer risk

24.name: Uranium
24.description: A radioactive heavy metal element used primarily as fuel in nuclear reactors and in military applications.
24.benefits: None in food or cosmetic applications
24.risks: Radioactivity leading to radiation poisoning, heavy metal toxicity causing kidney damage, carcinogenic potential, environmental persistence.

sources.label: ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Uranium
ECHA assessment on uranium hazards

25.name: Dipotassium Phosphate
25.description: An inorganic salt used as a buffering agent, emulsifier, and nutrient source providing potassium and phosphate ions in food and beverages.
25.benefits: Provides potassium and phosphate electrolytes, stabilizes pH in formulations
25.risks: Excessive intake may contribute to mineral imbalance, potential renal burden in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Use and safety of food-grade phosphates in human nutrition (PMID 15731582)
Dietary phosphorus and health outcomes (PMID 20821431)

26.name: Bicarbonate Alkalinity (as HCO3)
26.description: Bicarbonate is a form of alkalinity commonly found in water and biological systems, acting as a buffer to maintain pH balance. In food and beverage contexts, it contributes to regulating acidity and can affect flavor and preservation. It is generally recognized as safe when consumed within typical dietary levels.
26.benefits: Buffers acid, supports pH balance, aids digestion, contributes to electrolyte balance
26.risks: Excessive intake may lead to alkalosis or digestive disturbances in sensitive individuals

28.name: Pink Himalayan Salt
28.description: Salt mineral mainly composed of sodium chloride, with trace minerals giving pink color. Used as a dietary salt.
28.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
28.risks: Excessive sodium intake associated with hypertension and cardiovascular risk

29.name: Bromodichloromethane
29.description: Bromodichloromethane is a trihalomethane compound commonly found as a disinfection byproduct in chlorinated drinking water. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical contaminant associated with water treatment processes.
29.risks: Carcinogenic potential, liver and kidney toxicity, reproductive toxicity, neurotoxicity, possible endocrine disruption

sources.label: EPA toxicological profile for bromodichloromethane

30.name: Chloroform
30.description: A halogenated organic solvent formerly used as an anesthetic and industrial solvent. It is not a food ingredient and is toxic to humans with potential carcinogenic effects. Exposure is primarily hazardous via inhalation, ingestion, or skin contact.
30.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenicity, respiratory depression, liver and kidney damage, central nervous system depression

sources.label: PubChem Chloroform compound summary

31.name: Dibromochloromethane
31.description: A halogenated methane disinfection byproduct commonly found in chlorinated drinking water. Listed as a potential human carcinogen by the EPA and associated with adverse health effects upon ingestion.
31.risks: Potential carcinogen, reproductive toxicity, liver and kidney damage, mutagenicity

sources.label: EPA IRIS Toxicological Review of Dibromochloromethane

32.name: Radon
32.description: Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas resulting from the decay of uranium in soil, rock, and water. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material due to its radioactive properties. Exposure mainly occurs by inhalation of indoor air containing radon gas and is a known human carcinogen.
32.risks: Lung cancer, radioactive exposure, respiratory hazards

sources.label: EPA - Health Risk of Radon

33.name: Potassium Chloride
33.description: Potassium chloride is an inorganic salt used primarily as a potassium supplement and a salt substitute to manage potassium deficiency and lower sodium intake.
33.benefits: Electrolyte balance maintenance, potassium supplementation, blood pressure regulation support
33.risks: Excessive intake can cause hyperkalemia leading to cardiac arrhythmias, irritation at high doses, ingestion toxicity in overdose

sources.label: Role of Potassium in Human Health (PMC4245569)
Potassium supplementation and cardiovascular health (PMID 21492777)

34.name: Chloramine
34.description: Chloramine is a disinfectant used primarily to treat drinking water as an alternative to chlorine. It is formed by combining chlorine and ammonia and is used to control microbial growth. It is not a food ingredient for consumption but a water treatment chemical.
34.benefits: Effective water disinfectant, longer-lasting residual disinfectant in distribution systems compared to chlorine, reduces formation of some harmful chlorinated by-products
34.risks: Respiratory irritation, skin irritation, potential formation of harmful disinfection by-products, possible toxic effects at high levels

sources.label: NLM Hazardous Substances Data Bank - Chloramine

35.name: CO2
35.description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a naturally occurring, colorless, and odorless gas used in food and beverage processing for carbonation, preservation, and packaging. In the body, it is a normal metabolic byproduct expelled during respiration.
35.risks: None at concentrations typically used in food and beverages

36.name: Haloacetic acids (HAA9)
36.description: A group of nine haloacetic acids commonly found as disinfection by-products in chlorinated drinking water. They form during water treatment processes when chlorine reacts with natural organic matter.
36.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, reproductive and developmental toxicity, possible endocrine disruption, regulated contaminant due to health concerns

sources.label: EPA - Haloacetic Acids in Drinking Water

37.name: Haloacetic acids (HAA5)
37.description: Group of five haloacetic acids (monochloroacetic acid, dichloroacetic acid, trichloroacetic acid, monobromoacetic acid, and dibromoacetic acid) commonly found as disinfection byproducts in chlorinated drinking water. They form when chlorine reacts with natural organic matter. Not used as a food ingredient but are contaminants regulated due to potential health risks.
37.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, liver toxicity, genotoxicity, water contaminant

38.name: Chromium (hexavalent)
38.description: Hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) is a toxic form of chromium used industrially; it is a known carcinogen with no safe nutritional role. Not a food ingredient, but a hazardous material primarily encountered in occupational or environmental exposure.
38.risks: Carcinogenicity, respiratory sensitization, skin irritation, genotoxicity, occupational exposure hazards

39.name: Nitrite
39.description: Nitrites are food additives commonly used as preservatives and color fixatives in processed meats. They help prevent bacterial growth, especially Clostridium botulinum, but can form potentially carcinogenic nitrosamines under certain conditions.
39.benefits: Prevents growth of harmful bacteria in processed meats, extends shelf life, maintains meat color and flavor
39.risks: Potential formation of carcinogenic nitrosamines, possible association with increased cancer risk, may cause methemoglobinemia in infants at high exposure

40.name: Bromate
40.description: Bromate is an oxidizing agent commonly formed as a byproduct during ozonation of water and can also be present in some baking processes involving bromate salts.
40.risks: Carcinogenicity, genotoxicity, regulatory restriction, ingestion toxicity

sources.label: EPA Drinking Water Contaminant Candidate List - Bromate
EU Regulation on Bromate Limits in Drinking Water

41.name: Calcium
41.description: Essential mineral involved in bone formation, muscle function, nerve transmission, and vascular contraction.
41.benefits: Supports bone health, muscle contraction, nerve signaling
41.risks: Excessive intake may cause hypercalcemia, kidney stones

sources.label: Calcium and bone health in adults: The clinical evidence
Calcium intake and risk of kidney stones

42.name: Magnesium
42.description: Essential mineral involved in numerous biochemical reactions, including energy production, muscle and nerve function, and bone development.
42.benefits: Supports muscle and nerve function, contributes to bone health, involved in enzymatic reactions
42.risks: Gastrointestinal upset at very high doses, risk of overdose primarily in individuals with impaired kidney function

sources.label: Magnesium - Dietary Reference Intakes, NCBI Bookshelf

43.name: Potassium
43.description: Essential dietary mineral important for maintaining cellular function, nerve transmission, and muscle contraction.
43.benefits: Supports electrolyte balance, helps regulate blood pressure, essential for nerve and muscle function
43.risks: Hyperkalemia risk at excessive intake or impaired kidney function, minor ingestion toxicity at high doses

sources.label: PMID 26973993 - Potassium intake and health effects
PMID 28795746 - Potassium and cardiovascular health

45.name: Sodium
45.description: Sodium is an essential electrolyte involved in fluid balance, nerve transmission, and muscle function.
45.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
45.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

sources.label: PMC5418743 – Sodium intake and health outcomes

46.name: Manganese
46.description: Essential trace mineral involved in enzymatic reactions, bone formation, and metabolism.
46.benefits: Supports antioxidant enzyme function, bone development, and metabolism
46.risks: Neurotoxicity at high exposure levels, impaired motor function with excessive intake

sources.label: PMID 26482543 - Manganese in human nutrition and health

47.name: Aluminum
47.description: Metallic element commonly used in cookware, packaging, and cosmetics, with potential for human exposure via ingestion, inhalation, or skin contact.
47.benefits: None at typical consumer exposure levels
47.risks: Neurological toxicity at high exposure, potential accumulation in body tissues, possible respiratory irritation upon inhalation, contamination risk

49.name: Bromoform
49.description: Bromoform is a trihalomethane compound often formed as a byproduct during water chlorination and disinfection processes. It is not used as a food ingredient. Bromoform is considered a hazardous material due to its potential toxicity and carcinogenicity upon exposure.
49.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, respiratory irritation, central nervous system effects, environmental pollutant

50.name: Dibromoacetic acid
50.description: A halogenated acetic acid commonly found as a disinfection byproduct in chlorinated drinking water. Not intended for consumption and associated with potential toxic effects.
50.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, genotoxicity, developmental toxicity, harmful if ingested

51.name: Dichloroacetic acid
51.description: A synthetic chemical primarily used in industrial and laboratory applications; not approved as a food ingredient or additive. Known for its potential to interfere with metabolic enzymes and induce toxic effects at certain doses.
51.risks: Toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, liver damage, metabolic disruption, environmental pollutant

52.name: Trichloroacetic acid
52.description: Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) is a synthetic chemical primarily used in chemical peels and as a chemical reagent. It is not used as a food ingredient and is known for its corrosive and caustic properties. In dermatological applications, it requires careful handling and professional administration due to skin irritation and chemical burn risks. It is hazardous if ingested, inhaled, or comes into contact with skin in high concentrations.
52.benefits: Used medically for controlled skin peeling and tattoo removal
52.risks: Corrosive, skin irritation, chemical burns, toxic if ingested or inhaled, environmental hazard

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary - Trichloroacetic acid

58.name: Nickel
58.description: A metallic element commonly used in alloys, plating, and industrial applications. Not a food ingredient. In materials context, exposure via skin contact or inhalation can cause allergic reactions and respiratory issues. Not suitable for ingestion.
58.risks: Allergic contact dermatitis, respiratory sensitization, carcinogenic potential upon inhalation, systemic toxicity if ingested in large amounts

59.name: Zinc
59.description: Essential trace mineral important for immune function, enzyme activity, and cellular metabolism.
59.benefits: Supports immune system, wound healing, enzyme function, and growth
59.risks: Excessive intake can cause gastrointestinal irritation, interfere with copper absorption, and cause toxicity

sources.label: PMC7468694 - Zinc in human health

60.name: Chlorine Dioxide
60.description: Chlorine dioxide is a strong oxidizing agent used as a disinfectant and bleaching agent. It is a gaseous or dissolved compound used in cleaning formulations at low concentrations.
60.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum disinfectant and sanitizer, effective against bacteria, viruses, and spores
60.risks: Respiratory irritation, eye irritation, skin irritation, toxicity at higher inhalation exposures, potential oxidative damage

sources.label: PubChem Chlorine Dioxide
EPA Chlorine Dioxide Factsheet

61.name: Chlorine
61.description: Chlorine is a highly reactive halogen gas widely used as a disinfectant and bleaching agent in cleaning products. It is typically present as a gas or in aqueous solutions such as hypochlorite. Known for strong oxidizing properties.
61.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum disinfectant and bleaching agent, rapid antimicrobial activity
61.risks: Respiratory irritation, skin irritation, eye irritation, corrosive effects, toxic by inhalation, potential for release of toxic chlorine gas

sources.label: ECHA Chlorine substance info
EPA Chlorine factsheet

62.name: Lead
62.description: Heavy metal element commonly found as a contaminant in environmental and industrial contexts, toxic to multiple organ systems.
62.risks: Neurotoxicity, developmental toxicity, kidney damage, cardiovascular effects, carcinogenicity, cumulative toxicity

sources.label: PMC2717163 – Lead toxicity: a review
PMC4183914 – Toxic effects of lead exposure
CDC Lead Toxicity and Exposure Safety Guidelines

63.name: Mercury
63.description: A heavy metal element that is toxic to humans. Not used as a food ingredient. Exposure mainly occurs through contaminated fish, occupational hazards, or environmental pollution. Known to cause neurotoxicity and other systemic effects.
63.risks: Neurotoxicity, kidney damage, cognitive impairment, developmental toxicity, carcinogenic potential

64.name: Cadmium
64.description: Cadmium is a heavy metal contaminant that can accumulate in food and soil. It is not intentionally added as an ingredient but can contaminate products.
64.risks: Heavy metal toxicity, nephrotoxicity, carcinogenicity, bioaccumulation, regulatory restrictions

sources.label: PMID 22592468 - Cadmium exposure and health risks
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Cadmium
EU REACH Regulation on Cadmium Restrictions

65.name: Copper
65.description: Copper is a trace essential mineral necessary for various enzymatic processes, iron metabolism, and neurological function. It is required in small amounts in diet but is toxic at high doses. In non-food contexts, copper metal or compounds can cause skin irritation or toxicity if improperly handled.
65.benefits: Essential trace mineral, supports enzymatic functions, iron metabolism, connective tissue formation, and neurological health
65.risks: Toxicity in excess, gastrointestinal distress if ingested in large amounts, skin irritation with direct prolonged contact or occupational exposure

sources.label: Copper in Human Health - NCBI Bookshelf

66.name: Spring water
66.description: Water sourced from natural springs, typically free of contaminants and used for hydration or product formulation.

67.name: 1,4-Dioxane
67.description: Cyclic ether used as a solvent and stabilizer in some cleaning products. Classified as a probable human carcinogen.
67.risks: Carcinogenicity, potential respiratory irritation, probable carcinogen (IARC 2B), possible skin irritation

sources.label: PubChem 1,4-Dioxane
IARC Monograph on 1,4-Dioxane
ECHA 1,4-Dioxane Profile

68.name: Bromochloroacetic acid
68.description: A halogenated acetic acid classified as a disinfection by-product formed during water chlorination and bromination processes. Not used as a food ingredient or material. Known for potential toxicity and environmental persistence.
68.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, genotoxicity, cytotoxicity, environmental persistence, contamination risk in drinking water

69.name: PFAS
69.description: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are synthetic fluorinated chemicals used for their water-, oil-, and stain-resistant properties in various consumer products and industrial applications.
69.risks: Persistence, bioaccumulation, potential carcinogenicity, endocrine disruption, immune system effects, contamination of water and soil

sources.label: EPA - Basic Information on PFAS
ECHA - PFAS regulatory status

70.name: Tap water
70.description: Water supplied through municipal systems that is treated to meet safety standards for human consumption. Quality varies regionally and may contain trace minerals and disinfectant byproducts.
70.benefits: Essential for hydration, universal solvent, supports physiological functions, generally safe to drink in regulated areas
70.risks: Potential contaminants depending on local water quality, disinfectant byproducts, heavy metals in some areas

sources.label: WHO Drinking Water Quality Guidelines

71.name: Benzene
71.description: A volatile organic compound widely recognized as a toxic industrial chemical and known human carcinogen. Not a food ingredient and not safe for consumption or direct exposure; exposure is primarily by inhalation and is associated with significant health risks.
71.risks: Carcinogenicity, bone marrow suppression, leukemia, respiratory toxicity, mutagenicity

sources.label: NLM Toxnet Benzene Profile

72.name: Asbestos
72.description: A naturally occurring fibrous silicate mineral once used in insulation and fireproofing; known for its severe health hazards when inhaled.
72.risks: Carcinogenic, causes asbestosis, lung cancer, mesothelioma, respiratory diseases, fatal

sources.label: WHO - Asbestos and related diseases

75.name: Mineral Water
75.description: Natural water containing various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, and bicarbonates; safe for consumption and often provides hydration along with trace mineral benefits. Regulated by FDA as a water source with specified mineral content.
75.benefits: Hydration, provides essential minerals like calcium and magnesium, may support bone health and electrolyte balance
75.risks: Potential contaminants if source is polluted, possible high sodium content in some mineral waters

sources.label: FDA on Bottled Mineral Water

76.name: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
76.description: Carbon dioxide used as a food additive to carbonate beverages, creating effervescence and bubbly texture.
76.benefits: Provides carbonation and texture to beverages

sources.label: Properties and uses of CO2 in carbonation of beverages

77.name: Boron
77.description: Boron is a trace mineral found naturally in foods and water. It plays a role in bone health, hormone regulation, and cognitive function. While beneficial in small dietary amounts, excessive intake can be toxic.
77.benefits: Supports bone health, hormone regulation, cognitive function, anti-inflammatory effects
77.risks: Toxicity in high doses, nausea, hormonal imbalance

78.name: Thallium
78.description: A heavy metal element that is highly toxic to humans. It has no role as a food ingredient and is not approved for consumption. Exposure can occur through contaminated water, air, or industrial sources.
78.risks: Highly toxic, carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity, organ damage, fatal poisoning

80.name: Antimony
80.description: A metalloid element not used as a food ingredient; primarily encountered as an environmental contaminant or in industrial contexts. Exposure can occur via inhalation, ingestion, or skin contact, often from mining, smelting, or manufacturing processes.
80.risks: Toxicity, respiratory irritation, skin irritation, potential carcinogenicity, chronic exposure can cause lung and heart problems

81.name: Beryllium
81.description: A toxic metal element not used as a food ingredient. Exposure primarily occurs via inhalation in industrial settings, causing serious respiratory diseases including chronic beryllium disease (berylliosis). It is not safe for ingestion or contact and has no nutritional value.
81.risks: Toxicity, chronic beryllium disease, lung cancer, respiratory sensitization, carcinogenicity

sources.label: NIOSH: Beryllium Toxicity

82.name: Iron
82.description: Essential mineral involved in oxygen transport, energy metabolism, and various enzymatic processes in the body.
82.benefits: Supports oxygen transport via hemoglobin, essential for energy production, supports immune function
82.risks: Excessive intake can cause gastrointestinal irritation, iron overload leading to tissue damage, and interference with absorption of other minerals

sources.label: PMC5855200 - Iron metabolism and its role in health
Iron supplementation: benefits and risks

83.name: Selenium
83.description: Essential trace mineral important for antioxidant defense and thyroid hormone metabolism.
83.benefits: Supports antioxidant enzymes, thyroid function, immune system support
83.risks: Toxicity at high doses leading to selenosis, gastrointestinal symptoms, hair loss, nail brittleness

sources.label: PMID 21778153 - Selenium in human health and disease
PMID 15270666 - Selenium and immune function

84.name: Silver
84.description: Metallic element sometimes found as trace contamination in water and consumer products.
84.risks: Potential argyria with chronic ingestion at high levels, possible cellular toxicity in high doses

sources.label: Silver, elemental and inorganic compounds - Toxicological Profile

86.name: Cyanide
86.description: A highly toxic chemical compound that inhibits cellular respiration by blocking cytochrome c oxidase in mitochondria. Not a food ingredient and not safe for consumption or any direct human exposure.
86.risks: Acute poisoning, respiratory failure, cardiovascular collapse, death

sources.label: Cyanide Toxicity - StatPearls

88.name: Carbon tetrachloride
88.description: Carbonate refers to salts or esters of carbonic acid containing the carbonate ion (CO3). In trace amounts (<1 mg), it typically appears as a minor component or impurity in various products.

sources.label: PubChem - Carbonate
NIH - Carbonate in biological systems

89.name: Chlorate
89.description: Chlorate is a chemical compound often found as a contaminant in food and water due to its use in herbicides and disinfectants. It is not an intentional food ingredient and is considered a toxicant. Exposure to chlorate through ingestion can disrupt thyroid function and damage red blood cells.
89.risks: Thyroid disruption, hemolytic anemia, oxidative stress, toxicity from ingestion

91.name: 1,2,3-Trichloropropane
91.description: A synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon used historically as a solvent and chemical intermediate; recognized as a probable human carcinogen by multiple health agencies; not approved for food use.
91.risks: Carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental persistence, contamination risk in water and soil

sources.label: NTP Report on 1,2,3-Trichloropropane Carcinogenicity
EPA Fact Sheet on 1,2,3-Trichloropropane

93.name: 1,2-Dibromo-3-chloropropane
93.description: A synthetic chemical formerly used as a soil fumigant and pesticide. It is classified as a toxic compound with known carcinogenicity and environmental persistence. Not approved for direct food use and poses significant health risks upon exposure.
93.risks: Carcinogenic, reproductive toxicity, environmental pollutant, neurotoxicity

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary

94.name: Tetrachloroethylene (perchloroethylene)
94.description: Tetrachloroethylene, also known as perchloroethylene or PCE, is a chlorinated solvent commonly used in dry cleaning and industrial degreasing. It is not a food ingredient and is primarily considered a hazardous material due to its toxicity and environmental persistence. The compound is regulated for occupational exposure and environmental release due to its classification as a possible human carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC).
94.risks: Carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity, respiratory irritation, environmental contamination, liver and kidney toxicity

sources.label: IARC Monographs on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans - Perchloroethylene

103.name: Trichloroethylene
103.description: A synthetic volatile organic compound primarily used as an industrial solvent and degreasing agent. Not used as a food ingredient. Recognized as a hazardous air pollutant with potential toxic effects including carcinogenicity.
103.risks: Carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity, liver toxicity, kidney toxicity, environmental pollutant, occupational exposure risks

sources.label: US EPA – Toxicological Review of Trichloroethylene

104.name: Molybdenum
104.description: An essential trace mineral required for enzyme function, including metabolism of sulfur-containing amino acids and nitrogen fixation. Recognized as safe and necessary in small amounts for human nutrition.
104.benefits: Essential cofactor for enzymes, supports metabolic processes, antioxidant functions
104.risks: Excessive intake may cause gout-like symptoms, joint pain, elevated uric acid levels

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Molybdenum

105.name: Added Sugar
105.description: Sugars incorporated into foods during processing or preparation, not naturally occurring in foods.
105.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, metabolic disturbances

107.name: Bisphenols
107.description: Bisphenols, including Bisphenol A (BPA) and related analogs, are industrial chemicals used in manufacturing plastics and resins. They are not food ingredients but materials that can contaminate food via packaging. They are endocrine disruptors with documented hormonal effects.
107.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, developmental effects, potential carcinogenicity, metabolic disorders

110.name: Chlorodibromoacetic acid
110.description: A disinfection byproduct formed in chlorinated water; not used as a food ingredient. It is known to be a toxic environmental contaminant with potential carcinogenic and genotoxic effects.
110.risks: Carcinogenic potential, genotoxicity, environmental toxin, potential reproductive toxicity

sources.label: EPA Haloacetic Acids Factsheet

111.name: Perfluoroheptanoic acid (PFHpA)
111.description: A perfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) used in industrial applications and manufacturing with persistent environmental and biological presence. Not a food ingredient; exposure mainly via environmental contamination. Known for bioaccumulation and potential toxicity.
111.risks: Persistent in environment, bioaccumulative, potential endocrine disruption, developmental toxicity, carcinogenicity concerns, immunotoxicity

sources.label: ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)

112.name: Vanadium
112.description: Vanadium is a trace metal element found in various environmental sources and used in some industrial applications. It can enter the human body primarily through ingestion or inhalation.
112.benefits: None at typical consumer exposure levels
112.risks: Inhalation toxicity, potential heavy metal contamination, toxicity at high doses, respiratory and renal effects with exposure

118.name: Sunflower Oil
118.description: Edible oil extracted from sunflower seeds, primarily composed of polyunsaturated fatty acids, mainly linoleic acid.
118.benefits: Source of unsaturated fats that can replace saturated fats in diet, provides vitamin E as an antioxidant
118.risks: High omega-6 fatty acid content leading to oxidative instability, potential pro-inflammatory effects at high intake levels

sources.label: PMID 19308966 - Composition and health effects of sunflower oil
PMID 17993575 - Dietary fats and inflammation

119.name: Canola Oil
119.description: Edible oil obtained from rapeseed, characterized by a low saturated fat content and moderate omega-3 fatty acids.
119.benefits: Heart-healthy fatty acid profile, supports cholesterol management
119.risks: PUFA oxidation instability, potential processing contaminants in refined oil

sources.label: PMID:25659462 - Health effects of canola oil

120.name: Natural and Artificial Flavors
120.description: Complex mixtures of chemical compounds added to food and products to impart flavor, derived from natural sources or synthesized artificially.
120.risks: Lack of transparency in composition, potential presence of solvents or undisclosed additives, possible sensitization or allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, ultra-processed ingredient

sources.label: PMC8026810 – Health implications of flavor additives

125.name: Soluble Corn Fiber
125.description: A type of dietary fiber derived from corn starch, used to increase fiber content and reduce calories in food products.
125.benefits: Dietary fiber source, may improve bowel regularity and reduce caloric content in foods
125.risks: Excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal discomfort such as bloating or gas

sources.label: PMC3705358 - Functional benefits and potential adverse effects of dietary fibers
27416510 - Effects of soluble corn fiber on gastrointestinal tolerance and metabolic markers

138.name: Organic Jerusalem artichoke powder
138.description: Powdered form of Jerusalem artichoke, a tuber rich in dietary fiber, particularly inulin, a prebiotic fructan that supports gut health. Organic designation indicates cultivation without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Generally recognized as safe for consumption with noted digestive benefits.
138.benefits: Prebiotic dietary fiber (inulin), supports gut microbiota, may improve digestion, low glycemic index, potential blood sugar regulation
138.risks: Digestive discomfort such as bloating or gas in sensitive individuals or when consumed in large amounts

140.name: Olive oil
140.description: Edible oil extracted primarily from olives, rich in monounsaturated fatty acids, mainly oleic acid. Commonly used in cooking and food preparation.
140.benefits: Rich source of monounsaturated fats, associated with cardiovascular health benefits, contains antioxidants such as polyphenols
140.risks: Oxidation instability at high heat, possible allergic reaction in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMC Associated cardiovascular benefits of olive oil
Oxidative stability and health effects of olive oil

141.name: Pea protein
141.description: Protein isolate derived from Pisum sativum (pea), used primarily as a plant-based protein source in food products.
141.benefits: Rich source of plant protein, supports muscle maintenance, alternative for dairy and soy allergies
141.risks: Possible allergenicity in sensitive individuals, processing may involve anti-nutritional factors if not treated

sources.label: PMC6603045 - Nutritional and health benefits of pea protein

145.name: Polydextrose
145.description: Polydextrose is a synthetic polymer of glucose used primarily as a humectant, bulking agent, and soluble fiber in food products.
145.benefits: Low-calorie bulking agent, source of soluble fiber, supports digestive health
145.risks: Digestive discomfort at high intake, potential laxative effect

sources.label: PMC2095278 – Safety and effects of polydextrose consumption

149.name: Stevia Sweetener
149.description: Natural non-nutritive sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant, primarily composed of steviol glycosides.
149.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose levels, useful for sugar reduction
149.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, rare allergic reactions

151.name: Acesulfame Potassium
151.description: Acesulfame Potassium (Ace-K) is a synthetic, calorie-free sweetener used to provide sweetness in food and beverages without added calories.
151.benefits: Calorie-free sweetener, helps reduce sugar intake, stable under heat and acidic conditions
151.risks: Potential gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, possible concerns over chronic toxicity though regulatory bodies consider it safe at typical use levels

sources.label: PMID 17268187 - Safety assessment of acesulfame potassium

153.name: Strontium-90
153.description: A radioactive isotope produced by nuclear fission found in nuclear fallout. It is not a food ingredient and poses significant health hazards when ingested, inhaled, or contacted, due to its beta radiation emissions and propensity to accumulate in bones.
153.risks: Radioactive contamination, bone cancer, leukemia, radiation sickness, genetic damage, mutagenesis

sources.label: ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Strontium

154.name: Tritium
154.description: Tritium is a radioactive isotope of hydrogen used primarily in self-luminous devices such as watch dials and exit signs. It is not a food ingredient and is not intended for ingestion or direct human contact. Exposure to tritium via inhalation or ingestion can pose radiological health risks.
154.risks: Radioactive exposure, potential radiation sickness, increased cancer risk

sources.label: IAEA Tritium Environmental and Health Impact

155.name: Turbidity
155.description: Turbidity is a measure of the level of particles such as sediment, plankton, or organic by-products, in a body of water.
155.benefits: It can indicate the presence of pathogenic microorganisms.

sources.label: WATER QUALITY AND HEALTH -  REVIEW OF TURBIDITY: Information for regulators  and water suppliers. World Health Organization

157.name: Borate
157.description: Borates are boron-containing compounds commonly used in industrial applications, detergents, cosmetics, and as preservatives. They are not used as food ingredients and have potential toxicity concerns upon ingestion or significant exposure. Borates exhibit mild antiseptic and antifungal properties but pose health risks mainly due to their potential toxicity when absorbed or ingested.
157.benefits: Antiseptic, antifungal properties in non-food uses
157.risks: Toxicity, reproductive toxicity, developmental toxicity, skin irritation, inhalation hazards

sources.label: PubChem - Borate Overview
WHO Concise International Chemical Assessment Document 61: Borates

159.name: 1,3-Butadiene
159.description: 1,3-Butadiene is a colorless gas used primarily in the production of synthetic rubber and plastics. It is not a food ingredient and is classified as a hazardous air pollutant. Exposure concerns include inhalation risks in industrial settings. It is not safe for ingestion or casual exposure due to its carcinogenic potential.
159.risks: Carcinogenicity, respiratory irritation, mutagenicity, genotoxicity, exposure in industrial environments

sources.label: EPA Integrated Risk Information System (IRIS) - 1,3-Butadiene

160.name: Deethylatrazine
160.description: Deethylatrazine is a degradation product of the herbicide atrazine, commonly found as an environmental contaminant in soil and water. It is not used as a food ingredient and is considered a material contaminant with potential toxicological effects.
160.risks: Potential endocrine disruption, environmental toxicity, possible contamination in food/water leading to health risks

162.name: Radium 228
162.description: Radium-228 is a radioactive isotope of radium, a naturally occurring radioactive element in the actinide series, known for its alpha and beta radiation emissions.
162.risks: Radioactivity, carcinogenic potential, radiation poisoning risk, contamination hazard

sources.label: EPA Radium Radiation Facts

163.name: Radium 226
163.description: Radium-226 is a radioactive isotope of radium, historically used in luminous paints and medical treatments. It emits alpha, beta, and gamma radiation.
163.risks: Radioactive contamination, high radiotoxicity, carcinogenicity, bone deposition leading to bone cancer, radiation sickness

sources.label: IAEA Radiation Protection and Safety of Radium
EPA Radium 226 Information

165.name: PFOS & PFOA
165.description: Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) are synthetic per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) used historically in stain repellents, firefighting foams, and industrial applications. They are persistent environmental pollutants with bioaccumulative properties and are not food ingredients but contaminants or materials of concern.
165.risks: Bioaccumulation, endocrine disruption, carcinogenicity, immune system impairment, liver toxicity, developmental toxicity

166.name: Chromium (Total)
166.description: Chromium is a trace mineral required in small amounts for normal carbohydrate, lipid, and protein metabolism, often included as a nutrient supplement. Total chromium measures all forms including trivalent (Cr3+) and hexavalent (Cr6+) chromium.
166.benefits: Supports normal glucose metabolism and insulin function at essential trace levels
166.risks: Potential toxicity from hexavalent chromium (Cr6+) forms, occupational inhalation toxicity, contamination risk if Cr6+ present, ingestion toxicity possible only with contaminated forms

sources.label: Chromium essentiality and safety profile
Health effects and safety of chromium exposure

170.name: DDT
170.description: DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) is a synthetic organochlorine pesticide, banned or restricted in many countries due to its environmental persistence and bioaccumulative toxicity.
170.risks: Endocrine disruption, carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity, bioaccumulation, environmental persistence, toxicity to wildlife and humans

171.name: Aldrin
171.description: Aldrin is an organochlorine insecticide historically used in agriculture. It is not a food ingredient and is classified as a persistent organic pollutant with high environmental and human toxicity. Aldrin is banned or severely restricted in many countries due to its bioaccumulation, carcinogenicity, and neurotoxicity.
171.risks: Carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, toxicity to humans and wildlife

sources.label: WHO – Aldrin toxicological profile

172.name: Sunflower Lecithin
172.description: A phospholipid-rich emulsifier derived from sunflower seeds, used to stabilize mixtures of oil and water.
172.benefits: Emulsification, improves texture and stability, suitable alternative to soy lecithin
172.risks: Possible mild allergenicity, minimal irritation risk

sources.label: PMC: Safety and technological aspects of lecithins
PMC: Use and benefits of sunflower lecithin compared to soy lecithin

177.name: Carbofuran
177.description: Carbofuran is a highly toxic carbamate pesticide used in agriculture. It is not a food ingredient and poses significant health risks due to its toxicity and potential for causing acute poisoning in humans and animals. Carbofuran exposure can occur through contaminated food or environment, raising serious safety concerns.
177.risks: Highly toxic, acute poisoning, neurotoxic effects, carcinogenic potential, environmental contamination, harmful to wildlife and humans

178.name: Chlordane
178.description: Chlordane is a synthetic organochlorine pesticide formerly used extensively for termite control and agricultural pests. It is banned in many countries due to its environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity to humans and wildlife.
178.risks: Carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity, endocrine disruption, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, harmful if ingested or inhaled

182.name: Cyanazine
182.description: Cyanazine is a synthetic triazine herbicide widely used in agriculture for weed control. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical material used as a pesticide.
182.benefits: Effective broadleaf weed control in crops such as corn and sorghum
182.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, endocrine disruption, environmental toxicity, contamination of water sources, persistence in soil

185.name: Dieldrin
185.description: Dieldrin is a synthetic organochlorine pesticide that is highly toxic and banned or restricted worldwide due to its persistence in the environment and bioaccumulative properties.
185.risks: Neurotoxicity, carcinogenicity, endocrine disruption, bioaccumulation, environmental persistence, acute poisoning

189.name: Glyphosate
189.description: Glyphosate is a broad-spectrum systemic herbicide used to kill weeds, primarily by inhibiting a plant enzyme involved in amino acid synthesis.
189.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum weed control in agriculture
189.risks: Toxicity concerns including potential carcinogenicity debated, environmental persistence, contamination risk in food and water, regulatory restrictions in various jurisdictions

sources.label: EPA Glyphosate Fact Sheet
ECHA Glyphosate hazard assessment

192.name: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS)
192.description: A measure of combined inorganic and organic substances dissolved in water, including minerals, salts, metals, and organic matter. It is not a food ingredient but an indicator of water quality and composition.
192.benefits: Indicator of mineral content in water, can reflect water purity and nutritional mineral levels
192.risks: Depends on the nature of dissolved solids, potential for heavy metals or contaminants if high

194.name: Endosulfan Sulfate
194.description: Inorganic anion commonly found in water and various food sources; typically present as sulfate salts or dissolved ions.
194.benefits: None specific at typical dietary levels

sources.label: NIH PubChem Compound Summary - Sulfate

195.name: Endrin
195.description: Endrin is a synthetic organochlorine pesticide that was widely used in agriculture but is now banned or severely restricted in many countries due to its toxicity and persistence in the environment. It is not a food ingredient and poses significant health hazards through environmental exposure.
195.risks: Highly toxic, carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, reproductive toxicity

sources.label: WHO Concise International Chemical Assessment Document 29 - Endrin

200.name: Ethoproph
200.description: Ethorop is one of a family of organophosphorus pesticides. It is combustible though it may require some effort to ignite.
200.benefits: It is used as an insecticide.
200.risks: It is extremely toxic to mammals.

sources.label: Compound Summary Ethorophos. National Library of Medicine

203.name: Gamma BHC (Lindane)
203.description: Gamma BHC, also known as Lindane, is an organochlorine insecticide once widely used in agriculture and for pharmaceutical treatment of lice and scabies. It is persistent in the environment and bioaccumulates in fatty tissues.
203.benefits: Effective insecticide and ectoparasiticide in past applications
203.risks: Neurotoxicity, carcinogenic potential, endocrine disruption, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, toxicity to humans and wildlife

sources.label: WHO Environmental Health Criteria on Lindane

204.name: Heptachlor
204.description: Heptachlor is a synthetic organochlorine insecticide formerly used for termite and mosquito control. It is highly persistent in the environment and bioaccumulative. The EPA classifies it as a probable human carcinogen. It is banned or severely restricted in many countries due to its toxicity and environmental impact.
204.risks: Carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity, endocrine disruption, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, toxicity to wildlife and humans

sources.label: EPA Fact Sheet on Heptachlor
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Heptachlor

206.name: Molinate
206.description: Molinate is a thiocarbamate herbicide primarily used in rice cultivation to control grasses and sedges. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a material/chemical. Exposure to molinate, especially occupational or environmental, has been linked to potential neurotoxicity and reproductive toxicity. It is regulated for use by environmental and agricultural agencies due to its toxicity.
206.benefits: Effective herbicide for crop protection, helps increase rice yield
206.risks: Neurotoxicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental contamination, potential carcinogenicity, acute toxicity via inhalation and dermal exposure

sources.label: ATSDR ToxFAQs for Molinate

209.name: Toxaphene
209.description: Toxaphene is a highly toxic chlorinated pesticide formerly used but now banned in many countries due to its environmental persistence and bioaccumulation. It is not a food ingredient and exposure is primarily through environmental contamination.
209.risks: Highly toxic, carcinogenic potential, neurotoxic, endocrine disruption, persistent organic pollutant, bioaccumulative

sources.label: WHO IPCS - Concise International Chemical Assessment Document on Toxaphene

211.name: Anthracene
211.description: Anthracene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) primarily used in industrial applications such as the production of dyes, plastics, and pesticides. It is not a food ingredient and is considered an environmental pollutant.
211.risks: Carcinogenic potential, respiratory irritation, skin sensitization, environmental pollutant

213.name: Benzo[b]fluoranthene
213.description: Benzo[b]fluoranthene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) commonly formed during incomplete combustion of organic material. It is not used as a food ingredient but may be present as a contaminant in smoked or grilled foods and environmental pollutants.
213.risks: Carcinogenic potential, mutagenicity, genotoxicity, environmental pollutant, respiratory irritation

sources.label: PubChem Benzo[b]fluoranthene summary

214.name: Benzo[k]fluoranthene
214.description: Benzo[k]fluoranthene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) commonly formed during incomplete combustion of organic matter. It is not used as a food ingredient but may be a contaminant in smoked or grilled foods and environmental pollutants. Classified as a probable human carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC).

sources.label: IARC Monographs on PAHs carcinogenicity

215.name: Benzo[a]pyrene
215.description: Benzo[a]pyrene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) formed during incomplete combustion of organic matter and is found in charred foods, tobacco smoke, and environmental pollution. It is metabolized in the body to reactive compounds that can bind to DNA.
215.risks: Carcinogen, DNA damage, mutagenicity, developmental toxicity, liver toxicity

216.name: Benzo[ghi]perylene
216.description: Benzo[ghi]perylene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) produced primarily by the incomplete combustion of organic matter, found as an environmental contaminant in air, soil, and some foods, especially those that are grilled or smoked.
216.risks: Carcinogenicity, mutagenic potential, environmental persistence, potential for bioaccumulation, possible endocrine disruption

217.name: Butyl Benzyl phthalate
217.description: A synthetic plasticizer commonly used to increase flexibility in plastics and sometimes found in fragrance formulations. Not approved as a food ingredient. Known endocrine disruptor with potential reproductive toxicity and environmental persistence.
217.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, developmental toxicity, environmental contamination, potential carcinogenicity

222.name: DCPA (Dacthal)
222.description: DCPA, also known as Dacthal, is a chlorophenyl herbicide used primarily for pre-emergent weed control in agricultural settings. It is not a food ingredient but an agrochemical with potential environmental and human health concerns. Classified by the EPA as a possible human carcinogen, exposure primarily occurs through agricultural residues and environmental contamination.
222.benefits: Effective herbicide for weed control in crops, reduces crop losses
222.risks: Possible carcinogen, environmental persistence, potential endocrine disruption, soil and water contamination

sources.label: EPA – Dacthal (DCPA) pesticide information

226.name: Sodium Citrates
226.description: Sodium salts of citric acid used as acidity regulators and emulsifying salts in foods and pharmaceuticals.
226.benefits: Acidity regulation, buffering capacity, emulsification support

sources.label: Use of citrates as food additives

228.name: Strawberry Flavor
228.description: Complex ingredient typically containing sugar, corn starch, carrageenan, salt, artificial flavorings, and natural colorants such as red beet juice concentrate. Used to impart strawberry taste in food products.
228.benefits: Provides strawberry-like flavor and color enhancing palatability
228.risks: Artificial flavor (potential for sensitization and ultra-processed additive), carrageenan (possible gastrointestinal irritation at high intake), corn starch (minimal risk), sugar (excessive intake associated with metabolic effects), salt (excessive intake associated with hypertension)

sources.label: Sodium intake and cardiovascular health

229.name: Whey Protein Concentrate
229.description: A dairy-derived protein source obtained from the liquid remaining after milk has been curdled and strained. It provides a mixture of proteins, lactose, and minerals.
229.benefits: High-quality protein source, supports muscle protein synthesis and recovery
229.risks: Allergic reactions in individuals with milk allergy, potential lactose intolerance symptoms in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Effect of Whey Protein on Muscle Protein Synthesis
Milk Allergy and Whey Protein Sensitivity

236.name: Tripotassium Phosphate
236.description: An inorganic salt used as an acidity regulator, emulsifier, and nutrient supplement in food products. Recognized as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by the FDA for use in food. It can alter phosphate balance if consumed in extremely high amounts.
236.benefits: Acts as an emulsifier and buffer in foods, source of potassium and phosphate minerals
236.risks: Excess phosphate intake may affect kidney function, electrolyte imbalance in large amounts

sources.label: FDA Food Additive Status List

243.name: Pyridoxine Hydrochloride
243.description: A synthetic form of vitamin B6 used as a dietary supplement and food additive to support normal metabolism and neurological function.
243.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, neurological function, and red blood cell production
243.risks: High-dose supplementation may cause sensory neuropathy in rare cases, minor irritation if used topically

sources.label: National Institutes of Health Office of Dietary Supplements - Vitamin B6
Risk of sensory neuropathy from excessive pyridoxine intake

246.name: Pentachlorophenol
246.description: Pentachlorophenol (PCP) is a synthetic organochlorine compound formerly used as a wood preservative and biocide. It is not a food ingredient and is recognized for its toxicity and environmental persistence. PCP exposure is associated with significant health risks including carcinogenicity and organ toxicity. Its use is heavily restricted or banned in many countries due to safety concerns.
246.risks: Carcinogenic, neurotoxicity, immunotoxicity, endocrine disruption, environmental persistence, liver damage, respiratory toxicity

sources.label: ATSDR Toxicological Profile for PCP

252.name: Propachlor
252.description: Propachlor is a herbicide used primarily in agriculture to control weeds in crops like corn. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a chemical material with potential toxicological effects. It is classified as a hazardous substance with concerns about carcinogenicity and environmental persistence.
252.risks: Toxicity, potential carcinogen, environmental contaminant, endocrine disruption, groundwater contamination

sources.label: EPA Pesticide Fact Sheet on Propachlor

255.name: Phthalates
255.description: Phthalates are a group of synthetic chemicals used as plasticizers to increase flexibility in plastics and found as contaminants in various consumer products including personal care items.
255.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, developmental toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, contamination in consumer products

sources.label: EMA - Scientific guideline on phthalates
US EPA - Phthalates overview and regulatory considerations

256.name: PFAS (PFOA/PFOS)
256.description: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) including PFOA and PFOS are synthetic chemicals used for their water, stain, and heat resistant properties. They are persistent environmental pollutants and bioaccumulate in humans and wildlife. Not food ingredients; exposure mostly occurs via contaminated food packaging, water, or materials.
256.risks: Bioaccumulation, endocrine disruption, carcinogenicity, liver toxicity, immune dysfunction, developmental toxicity

267.name: Organic Lime Juice
267.description: Organic lime juice is derived from organically grown limes and is rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, and minor phytonutrients. In the diet, it can provide immune support and aid in iron absorption. In food products, it acts as a natural acidulant and flavor enhancer.
267.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidant properties, supports iron absorption, natural flavoring
267.risks: Mild dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption

268.name: Organic Orange Juice
268.description: Juice extracted from oranges grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Contains vitamin C, sugars, and flavonoids.
268.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, and hydration
268.risks: High natural sugar content, potential dental erosion with excessive consumption

287.name: DEET (n,n-diethyl-meta-toluamide)
287.description: A synthetic chemical widely used as an insect repellent in topical applications. Approved by the EPA for use on skin to prevent arthropod bites. Considered effective but can cause skin irritation and toxicity if misused or overapplied.
287.benefits: Effective insect repellent, reduces risk of insect-borne diseases such as malaria, Lyme disease, and Zika virus
287.risks: Skin irritation, neurotoxicity at high doses, potential for systemic toxicity, environmental toxicity to aquatic life

sources.label: EPA - DEET Insect Repellents

290.name: Metolachlor
290.description: Metolachlor is a synthetic herbicide primarily used in agriculture to control grasses and broadleaf weeds. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical substance with potential exposure through environmental contamination or residues on food crops.
290.benefits: Effective weed control in agriculture, increases crop yield
290.risks: Carcinogenic potential, endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, environmental persistence, water contamination

296.name: Dinoseb
296.description: Dinoseb is a herbicide and pesticide chemical, not used as a food ingredient. It is known to be toxic and hazardous, and exposure poses significant health risks. It is not approved for use in food products by regulatory authorities.
296.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, reproductive toxicity, acute poisoning, environmental hazard

sources.label: PubChem - Dinoseb

297.name: Heptachlor Epoxide
297.description: Heptachlor epoxide is a persistent organochlorine pesticide metabolite of heptachlor, known for its environmental persistence and bioaccumulation. It is not a food ingredient but a toxic pollutant with significant health risks, including carcinogenicity and neurotoxicity. It is banned or restricted in many countries due to its harmful effects.
297.risks: Carcinogenic, neurotoxicity, endocrine disruption, bioaccumulation, environmental persistence, toxic

298.name: Methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE)
298.description: MTBE is a synthetic organic compound primarily used as a gasoline additive to increase octane and reduce engine knocking. It is not a food ingredient but can contaminate water or food supplies due to environmental exposure.
298.risks: Carcinogenic potential, groundwater contamination, toxic to liver and kidneys, possible neurotoxicity

sources.label: NCBI Bookshelf – Methyl Tert-Butyl Ether (MTBE) Toxicity

299.name: Fenoprop (2,4,5 - TP silvex)
299.description: Fenoprop, also known as 2,4,5-TP or Silvex, is a synthetic herbicide used historically for broadleaf weed control. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material due to toxicity and environmental persistence.
299.risks: Toxicity to humans, carcinogenic potential, endocrine disruption, environmental persistence, contamination of water sources

sources.label: EPA fact sheet on Fenoprop (2,4,5-TP)

301.name: 4-(2,4-Dichlorophenoxy)butanoic acid / 2,4 -DB
301.description: 2,4-DB is a synthetic chlorophenoxy herbicide used in agriculture to control broadleaf weeds. It is not intended for food consumption. Exposure through residues on food or environment may pose health risks due to its chemical nature and potential toxic effects.
301.benefits: Effective broadleaf weed control in agriculture
301.risks: Toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, endocrine disruption, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, acute poisoning symptoms

sources.label: EPA IRIS Toxicological Review of 2,4-DB

302.name: 2,4,5-Trichlorophenoxyacetic acid / 2,4,5-T
302.description: A synthetic herbicide formerly used in agriculture and weed control, part of the phenoxy herbicides. It was banned in many countries due to contamination with dioxin (TCDD) during its manufacture, a highly toxic compound. Not a food ingredient and not safe for consumption.
302.risks: Highly toxic dioxin contamination, carcinogenicity, endocrine disruption, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, acute poisoning

303.name: 3,5-Dichlorobenzoic acid
303.description: A synthetic chlorinated aromatic carboxylic acid primarily used in chemical synthesis and industrial applications, not approved for food use.
303.risks: Potential toxicity if ingested, not approved for human consumption, possible skin and respiratory irritation on exposure

sources.label: PubChem - 3,5-Dichlorobenzoic acid profile

305.name: Bentazone
305.description: Bentazone is a selective herbicide used to control broadleaf weeds in crops such as soybeans, potatoes, and tobacco. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical material for agricultural use. Human exposure mainly occurs through environmental residues. It is classified for use under regulatory controls and has been evaluated for toxicological effects.
305.benefits: Effective broadleaf weed control in agriculture, supports crop yield optimization
305.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, endocrine disruption, acute toxicity, environmental contamination, residue ingestion risks

sources.label: PubChem Bentazone
Environmental fate and toxicity of bentazone
EFSA assessment on bentazone residues in food

307.name: 2,2-Dichloropropionic acid / Dalapon
307.description: Dalapon is a chlorinated herbicide used primarily for weed control in agriculture and non-food areas. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a synthetic chemical with potential toxicity concerns when exposed via dermal, inhalation, or oral routes.
307.benefits: Effective herbicide for weed control in non-food crops and industrial areas
307.risks: Toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, environmental persistence, skin and respiratory irritation, contamination risk if ingested

sources.label: PubChem - Dalapon chemical and safety information
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Dalapon

308.name: 3,6-Dichloro-2-methoxybenzoic acid / Dicamba
308.description: Dicamba is a chlorinated benzoic acid herbicide primarily used to control broadleaf weeds in agriculture. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a chemical material with potential toxic effects due to its herbicidal properties and environmental persistence.
308.benefits: Effective herbicide for controlling broadleaf weeds, widely used in agriculture for crop yield protection
308.risks: Toxicity to aquatic life, potential endocrine disruption, soil and water contamination, toxicity to non-target plants and animals, possible human health risks from exposure including respiratory and skin irritation

sources.label: EPA Dicamba Pesticide Factsheet

309.name: 4-Amino-3,5,6-trichloropicolinic acid / Picloram
309.description: Picloram is a synthetic chlorinated pesticide and herbicide used to control broadleaf weeds in agriculture, forestry, and pasture management. It is known to persist in soil and water, raising concerns about environmental and human exposure.
309.risks: Potential environmental persistence, water contamination, possible developmental and reproductive toxicity, not intended for human consumption

sources.label: NCBI – Occupational and environmental health risk assessment for Picloram

310.name: 3,7-Dichloro-8-quinolinecarboxylic acid / Quinclorac
310.description: Quinclorac is a synthetic herbicide belonging to the quinolone class, primarily used in agriculture to control grassy and broadleaf weeds in crops such as rice, turf, and some cereal grains. It disrupts plant growth hormone pathways, leading to selective weed control.
310.risks: Potential environmental contamination, possible bioaccumulation, harmful to non-target plants, limited toxicity data for human exposure, aquatic ecosystem disruption

312.name: Perfluorodecanoic acid / PFDA
312.description: Perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA) is a synthetic perfluorinated carboxylic acid belonging to the broad class of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). PFDA is persistent in the environment and bioaccumulative. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical of concern primarily due to environmental contamination and toxicological effects. PFDA is not approved for food use and poses health risks via exposure mainly through contaminated water, food, or consumer products.
312.risks: Toxicity, bioaccumulation, endocrine disruption, immune system adverse effects, developmental toxicity, carcinogenic potential, environmental persistence, contamination

313.name: Polytetrafluoroethylene / PTFE
313.description: A synthetic fluoropolymer widely used for non-stick coatings in cookware and various industrial applications. Stable under normal conditions but can release toxic fumes when overheated above 260°C (500°F). Not a food ingredient, classified as a material with inhalation risks in thermal degradation.
313.benefits: Durable, chemically inert, non-stick surface for cookware, low friction
313.risks: Toxic fumes on overheating (polymer fume fever), respiratory irritation, environmental persistence

314.name: Bis(2-chloroethyl) ether
314.description: Bis(2-chloroethyl) ether is a synthetic industrial chemical used mainly as a chemical intermediate and solvent in manufacturing. It is not intended for use in food and is highly toxic, with known carcinogenic and mutagenic effects.
314.risks: Carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, respiratory toxicity, liver toxicity, skin and eye irritation, environmental persistence

sources.label: PubChem – Bis(2-chloroethyl) ether
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Bis(2-chloroethyl) Ether

319.name: Hexachlorobenzene (HCB)
319.description: Hexachlorobenzene (HCB) is a persistent organic pollutant and chlorinated aromatic hydrocarbon historically used as a fungicide in agriculture and as an industrial chemical. It is highly resistant to degradation, accumulates in fatty tissues, and is toxic to humans even at low exposures.
319.risks: Carcinogenicity, hepatotoxicity, neurotoxicity, endocrine disruption, immunosuppression, bioaccumulation, teratogenic effects

320.name: Metribuzin
320.description: Metribuzin is a synthetic herbicide commonly used in agriculture to control broadleaf weeds and grasses. It is not intended for direct human consumption and is considered a contaminant if found in food products.
320.risks: Potential toxicity, carcinogenicity concerns, endocrine disruption, environmental persistence, groundwater contamination

322.name: 17-beta-Estradiol
322.description: A potent natural estrogen hormone involved in the regulation of the female reproductive system and secondary sex characteristics. Used medically in hormone replacement therapy and contraception. Not intended for general food use.
322.benefits: Regulates menstrual cycle, supports bone health, alleviates menopausal symptoms, helps maintain secondary sexual characteristics
322.risks: Hormonal imbalance, increased risk of certain cancers (breast, endometrial), thrombosis, cardiovascular events, reproductive toxicity

sources.label: Mechanisms of estrogen action

323.name: Ethinyl estradiol
323.description: A synthetic estrogen commonly used in hormonal contraceptives. It mimics natural estrogen but has a longer half-life and greater potency. Not used as a food ingredient but as a pharmaceutical material.
323.benefits: Effective oral contraceptive, regulates menstrual cycles, treats hormonal deficiencies
323.risks: Increased risk of thromboembolism, hormone-sensitive cancers, cardiovascular events, nausea, breast tenderness, potential endocrine disruption

325.name: Testosterone
325.description: Testosterone is a steroid hormone primarily produced in the testes and ovaries, essential for male sexual development and anabolic effects. It is not a food ingredient but a biological hormone used medically as a drug for hormone replacement therapy. Testosterone is not safe for ingestion as a food additive and must be used under medical supervision due to significant physiological effects.
325.benefits: Supports male secondary sexual characteristics, muscle mass maintenance, bone density, and libido when used appropriately in medical contexts
325.risks: Hormonal imbalance, cardiovascular risks, liver toxicity, behavioral changes, potential for abuse and dependency

sources.label: Testosterone Replacement Therapy - NCBI Bookshelf

327.name: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)
327.description: A synthetic plasticizer used to increase the flexibility of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) products. Not intended for food consumption; known for potential endocrine-disrupting effects and used in some materials including medical devices and plastics.
327.benefits: Used industrially to increase plastic flexibility, no health benefits for consumption
327.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, developmental toxicity

333.name: 2,4-Dimethylphenol
333.description: A synthetic organic compound classified as a methylated phenol, used primarily in industrial applications including disinfectants, resins, and as a chemical intermediate. Not approved as a food ingredient by the FDA. Exposure may occur mainly via inhalation or skin contact in occupational settings.
333.risks: Toxic if ingested, skin and respiratory irritation, potential carcinogenicity with chronic exposure, environmental toxicity

sources.label: PubChem 2,4-Dimethylphenol
Toxicity of methylphenols
OSHA Chemical Safety Database

336.name: 2,4-Dichlorophenol
336.description: 2,4-Dichlorophenol is a synthetic chemical compound used as an intermediate in the production of herbicides, antiseptics, and other industrial chemicals. It is not approved as a food ingredient and can contaminate water or food through environmental pollution.
336.risks: Toxicity, potential carcinogen, possible endocrine disruption, organ damage, environmental contamination

339.name: 2,4,6-Trichlorophenol
339.description: Synthetic chemical used as a wood preservative and intermediate in pesticide production. Not approved as a food ingredient due to toxicity. Recognized as an environmental pollutant with potential carcinogenic effects upon exposure.
339.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, environmental pollutant, skin irritation, respiratory hazards

sources.label: PubChem - 2,4,6-Trichlorophenol

340.name: 2,6-Dinitrotoluene
340.description: 2,6-Dinitrotoluene is a synthetic chemical compound used primarily in the manufacture of polyurethane foams and explosives. It is not intended for human consumption and is considered a hazardous environmental contaminant.
340.risks: Carcinogenicity, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, genotoxicity, potential reproductive toxicity

sources.label: PubChem – 2,6-Dinitrotoluene Toxicity and Properties
NCBI Bookshelf – Toxicological Profile for Dinitrotoluenes

342.name: 4-Chloro-3-methylphenol
342.description: 4-Chloro-3-methylphenol is a synthetic chlorinated phenolic compound primarily used as a disinfectant and preservative in some pharmaceutical and personal care products, not as a food ingredient. It possesses antimicrobial properties but is not intended for ingestion.
342.benefits: Antimicrobial activity (when used topically or as a preservative)
342.risks: Potential toxicity, skin and mucous membrane irritation, environmental persistence, suspected endocrine disruption

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Occurrence and fate of chloro-phenols

348.name: Fluoranthene
348.description: Fluoranthene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) formed from incomplete combustion of organic material. It is considered an environmental contaminant and has no nutritional value or purpose in food products.
348.risks: Carcinogenic potential, mutagenic, liver toxicity, respiratory irritation

sources.label: PubChem – Fluoranthene Compound Summary
ScienceDirect – Occurrence and toxicity of PAHs in food

351.name: Nitrobenzene
351.description: Nitrobenzene is a synthetic aromatic compound used primarily in industry for the production of aniline and as a solvent. It is not intended for use in food and is a recognized environmental and occupational hazard.
351.risks: Highly toxic if ingested, possible carcinogen, methemoglobinemia, organ damage, neurotoxicity

sources.label: NCBI Bookshelf – Nitrobenzene Toxicity

352.name: Phenols
352.description: A class of aromatic organic compounds characterized by one or more hydroxyl groups attached to an aromatic ring, found naturally in plants and used in various industrial and pharmaceutical applications.
352.benefits: Antioxidant properties, antimicrobial activity, natural preservative effect
352.risks: Skin and respiratory irritation, potential sensitization, toxic if ingested in high amounts, potential contamination with harmful derivatives depending on source and purity

sources.label: PMC Antioxidant and antimicrobial properties of phenolic compounds
Toxicity and sensitization potential of phenols in occupational exposure

353.name: Pyrene
353.description: Pyrene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) found in foods exposed to high-heat cooking, grilling, or environmental contamination. It is not intentionally added to foods but can be present as a contaminant.
353.risks: Potential carcinogen, bioaccumulation, may cause DNA damage, associated with increased cancer risk

356.name: 1,1-Dichloropropane
356.description: A synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon solvent primarily used industrially. Not approved as a food ingredient and not intended for consumption; potential toxicity through inhalation or ingestion.
