356.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, respiratory irritation, neurotoxicity, environmental persistence

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for 1,1-Dichloropropane
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Chlorinated Hydrocarbons

357.name: 1,1,2,2-Tetrachloroethane
357.description: A synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon solvent formerly used industrially and as a pesticide component. Not approved for food use. Classified as a probable human carcinogen with known toxic effects on the liver and central nervous system upon exposure.
357.risks: Carcinogenic potential, hepatotoxicity, neurotoxicity, environmental persistence, inhalation and dermal toxicity

sources.label: PubChem 1,1,2,2-Tetrachloroethane

358.name: 1,2,3-Trichlorobenzene
358.description: A synthetic chlorinated aromatic hydrocarbon used primarily as an industrial solvent. Not used as a food ingredient. Exposure may occur via inhalation or skin contact in industrial settings and is associated with toxic effects.
358.risks: Toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, environmental persistence, respiratory and skin irritation, liver and kidney damage

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary - 1,2,3-Trichlorobenzene
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Chlorinated Benzenes

359.name: 1,2,4-Trimethylbenzene
359.description: 1,2,4-Trimethylbenzene is an aromatic hydrocarbon commonly used as a solvent and component in fragrances and industrial products. It is not a food ingredient and primarily considered a material with inhalation exposure risks. It can be emitted during combustion or volatilization and may pose health risks upon inhalation or skin contact.
359.risks: Respiratory irritation, central nervous system effects, potential toxicity upon prolonged exposure, skin irritation, possible carcinogenic risk due to aromatic hydrocarbon structure

sources.label: PubChem 1,2,4-Trimethylbenzene Profile
NTP Toxicology Overview of Aromatic Hydrocarbons

360.name: 1,3-Dichlorobenzene
360.description: An aromatic organic chemical compound used as a solvent and intermediate in chemical synthesis. Not approved for use as a food ingredient. Known for environmental persistence and potential toxicity.
360.risks: Toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, environmental pollutant, inhalation hazard, skin irritation

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary - 1,3-Dichlorobenzene
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Chlorobenzenes

361.name: 1,3-Dichloropropane
361.description: A synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon mainly used as an industrial solvent and chemical intermediate. It is not a food ingredient and is recognized as a hazardous environmental contaminant. It is not intended for food or consumer product use and is toxic upon exposure.
361.risks: Carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity, liver and kidney damage, environmental pollutant, toxicity via inhalation and dermal exposure

sources.label: PubChem - 1,3-Dichloropropane

364.name: 2,2-Dichloropropane
364.description: 2,2-Dichloropropane is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon solvent historically used in industrial applications. It is not a food ingredient and is not intended for consumption. Exposure primarily occurs through inhalation or skin contact in occupational settings.
364.risks: Carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity, liver toxicity, respiratory irritation, environmental persistence

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for 2,2-Dichloropropane
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Chlorinated Aliphatic Hydrocarbons

365.name: 4-Isopropyltoluene / p-CYMENE
365.description: p-Cymene is a naturally occurring aromatic organic compound found in various essential oils such as cumin and thyme oils. It is used in fragrances, flavorings, and as an intermediate in chemical syntheses. In food, it occurs as a minor component and is generally recognized as safe in low concentrations. However, inhalation or high exposure can cause respiratory irritation and potential neurotoxicity in animal studies.
365.benefits: Naturally occurring flavor and fragrance component, antimicrobial properties in essential oils
365.risks: Respiratory irritation, potential neurotoxicity at high exposure, skin irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary - p-Cymene

367.name: Bromobenzene
367.description: Bromobenzene is an aromatic organic chemical primarily used as a solvent and intermediate in chemical synthesis. It is not a food ingredient but a synthetic material with potential toxic effects upon exposure.
367.risks: Toxicity, skin and eye irritation, respiratory irritation, potential carcinogenicity, environmental persistence

sources.label: PubChem - Bromobenzene
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Halogenated Hydrocarbons

368.name: Bromochloromethane
368.description: Bromochloromethane is a halomethane compound used mainly as a solvent and previously as a flame retardant and fumigant. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous chemical with potential toxic and environmental effects.
368.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, respiratory irritation, environmental persistence, ozone depletion potential

sources.label: PubChem - Bromochloromethane
EPA Risk Assessment for Bromochloromethane

369.name: Bromomethane
369.description: Bromomethane (methyl bromide) is a synthetic fumigant and pesticide, not used as a food ingredient. It is a volatile organic compound primarily used for soil fumigation and quarantine treatments. It is toxic and potentially carcinogenic to humans with exposure via inhalation or skin contact.
369.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory irritation, carcinogenic potential, ozone depletion, acute poisoning, environmental toxicity

sources.label: US EPA: Methyl Bromide Regulatory Information

371.name: Chloroethane
371.description: Chloroethane is a volatile chlorinated hydrocarbon primarily used as a refrigerant, solvent, and in medical applications as a topical anesthetic spray. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous chemical if inhaled or ingested. Exposure can cause central nervous system depression, respiratory irritation, and cardiac sensitization.
371.benefits: Used medically as topical anesthetic spray, solvent properties
371.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory irritation, cardiac sensitization, flammability, potential carcinogenicity

sources.label: PubChem - Chloroethane
ATSDR - Toxicological Profile for Chloroethane

372.name: Chloromethane
372.description: Chloromethane (methyl chloride) is a volatile organic compound used industrially as a solvent and refrigerant. It is not approved as a food ingredient and is considered toxic with potential harmful effects if ingested, inhaled, or absorbed. It poses health risks from exposure and is not safe for consumption.
372.risks: Toxicity, central nervous system depression, respiratory issues, carcinogenic potential, neurotoxicity

sources.label: PubChem Chloromethane Compound Summary

374.name: cis-1,3-Dichloropropene
374.description: A synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon used primarily as a soil fumigant pesticide. Not a food ingredient; exposure occurs mainly through contaminated air, water, or occupational contact. Classified as a probable human carcinogen by the EPA with potential neurotoxic and reproductive toxicity effects.
374.risks: Probable carcinogen, neurotoxicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental contaminant, respiratory irritation

375.name: Dibromomethane
375.description: Dibromomethane, also known as methylene dibromide, is a volatile halogenated organic compound used primarily as a solvent and chemical intermediate. It is not a food ingredient and is classified as a material with recognized toxicity and carcinogenic potential upon exposure. It can cause irritation, central nervous system effects, and has potential environmental toxicity.
375.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, respiratory irritation, central nervous system effects, environmental hazard

sources.label: PubChem - Dibromomethane

376.name: Dichloroacetonitrile
376.description: A chemical compound used as an intermediate in chemical synthesis and occasionally found as a disinfection byproduct in chlorinated water. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material due to its toxicological profile.
376.risks: Toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, environmental pollutant, respiratory irritation, skin and eye irritation

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for Dichloroacetonitrile
Environmental fate and toxicity of chlorinated by-products

378.name: Hexachlorobutadiene
378.description: Hexachlorobutadiene is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon used industrially as a solvent and chemical intermediate. It is not a food ingredient and is recognized as a hazardous environmental pollutant with toxic effects.
378.risks: Hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, carcinogenic potential, environmental toxin, bioaccumulation

380.name: m-Xylene
380.description: m-Xylene is an aromatic hydrocarbon used primarily as an industrial solvent and in chemical manufacturing. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material due to its toxicity and potential health risks upon inhalation, ingestion, or skin contact.
380.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory tract irritation, central nervous system depression, carcinogenic potential, skin irritation, environmental toxicity

sources.label: PubChem - Xylene Compound Summary
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Xylenes

382.name: Propylbenzene
382.description: An aromatic hydrocarbon used mainly as an industrial solvent and intermediate in chemical synthesis. Not approved as a food ingredient by the FDA.
382.risks: Toxicity with inhalation or ingestion, possible carcinogenicity, respiratory and neurological effects

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for Propylbenzene

383.name: o-Chlorotoluene
383.description: o-Chlorotoluene is an aromatic chlorinated hydrocarbon used primarily as an industrial chemical intermediate. It is not a food ingredient and is not intended for consumption. Exposure concerns relate to inhalation, skin contact, or environmental contamination.
383.risks: Toxic if inhaled or ingested, skin and eye irritant, potential environmental pollutant, possible carcinogenicity with prolonged exposure

sources.label: PubChem - o-Chlorotoluene
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Chlorinated Aromatic Hydrocarbons

385.name: Naphthalene
385.description: A polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon used in mothballs as a fumigant and insect repellent. Known to be toxic and potentially carcinogenic with prolonged exposure.
385.risks: Inhalation toxicity, hemolytic anemia, skin irritation, respiratory irritation, carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity

sources.label: EPA Naphthalene Toxicological Review
PubChem Naphthalene Health Hazards
ECHA Naphthalene Substance Information

386.name: o-Xylene
386.description: o-Xylene is an aromatic hydrocarbon commonly used as a solvent in industrial applications. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a chemical material with potential toxic effects upon inhalation, ingestion, or skin contact.
386.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory irritation, skin irritation, central nervous system effects, potential carcinogenicity with chronic exposure

sources.label: PubChem: o-Xylene compound summary

388.name: Sec-Butylbenzene
388.description: An aromatic hydrocarbon used primarily as an industrial solvent and intermediate in chemical syntheses. Not a food ingredient; exposure mainly through inhalation or dermal contact in occupational settings.
388.risks: Toxicity with inhalation or skin contact, potential respiratory irritation, possible central nervous system effects, flammability

sources.label: PubChem - Sec-Butylbenzene
ATSDR - Toxicological Profile for Aromatic Hydrocarbons

389.name: Tert-Butylbenzene
389.description: Tert-Butylbenzene is a synthetic aromatic hydrocarbon used mainly as an industrial solvent and chemical intermediate, not intended for food consumption. It is a volatile organic compound with potential toxicological effects upon inhalation or skin contact.
389.risks: Toxic if inhaled or ingested, skin irritation, respiratory tract irritation, potential neurotoxicity

sources.label: PubChem - Tert-Butylbenzene
ScienceDirect - Tert-Butylbenzene Toxicity and Uses

391.name: trans-1,3-Dichloropropene
391.description: A synthetic chemical primarily used as a soil fumigant pesticide. Not a food ingredient; exposure mainly occurs via occupational or environmental routes. Classified as a probable human carcinogen by the EPA and associated with respiratory and neurological toxicity.
391.benefits: Effective soil fumigant for controlling nematodes in agriculture
391.risks: Carcinogenic potential, respiratory irritation, neurotoxicity, environmental contaminant, occupational hazard

sources.label: EPA Assessment of trans-1,3-Dichloropropene Carcinogenicity

393.name: Xylene
393.description: Xylene is a volatile aromatic hydrocarbon commonly used as an industrial solvent and in manufacturing processes. It is not a food ingredient and is known for its toxicity when inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin.
393.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory irritation, CNS effects, kidney and liver damage, potential carcinogen

sources.label: NIH - Toxicological Profile for Xylene

394.name: Chloropicrin
394.description: Chloropicrin is a highly toxic chemical compound primarily used as a soil fumigant and pesticide. It is not intended for food consumption and poses significant health risks upon inhalation, dermal exposure, or ingestion.
394.benefits: Used as a soil fumigant and pesticide to control pests and soil-borne pathogens
394.risks: Toxicity, respiratory irritation, eye and skin irritation, potential carcinogenicity, environmental hazard

sources.label: PubChem - Chloropicrin
CDC NIOSH - Chloropicrin
EPA - Chloropicrin Pesticide Information

395.name: 1,2-Dichloroethane
395.description: Chlorinated hydrocarbon solvent used in some industrial cleaning products. Classified as a probable human carcinogen with significant toxicity concerns.
395.benefits: Effective solvent for stubborn grease and oils
395.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, central nervous system toxicity, carcinogenicity, liver toxicity, respiratory irritation, potential mutagenicity

sources.label: ECHA restriction and hazard classification

Toxicology and carcinogenicity review of 1,2-Dichloroethane

398.name: Chlorodibromomethane
398.description: Chlorodibromomethane is a halogenated methane compound often found as a disinfection byproduct in chlorinated water. It is not used as a food ingredient and is considered an environmental contaminant with potential toxic effects.
398.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental contaminant, water disinfection byproduct toxicity

399.name: Ammonia
399.description: Inorganic alkaline compound commonly used as a cleaning agent and degreaser. Known for strong alkalinity and volatility.
399.benefits: Effective cleaning and degreasing agent, removes stains and cuts grease
399.risks: Eye irritation, respiratory irritation, skin irritation, potential for respiratory sensitization, hazardous if inhaled at high concentrations

sources.label: ECHA Substance Information for Ammonia
Study on respiratory and eye irritation from ammonia exposure

400.name: Calcium hypochlorite
400.description: Calcium hypochlorite is a chemical compound used primarily as a disinfectant and bleaching agent. It is not a food ingredient and is hazardous if ingested. It releases chlorine and is commonly used for water treatment and sanitation but has significant safety concerns when in contact with skin, inhaled, or ingested.
400.benefits: Effective disinfectant, water treatment agent, antimicrobial properties
400.risks: Corrosive, toxic if ingested, skin and eye irritation, respiratory irritation, potential for chemical burns

sources.label: PubChem Calcium hypochlorite

401.name: Formaldehyde
401.description: A volatile organic compound used as a preservative and disinfectant. Classified as a human carcinogen and respiratory sensitizer.
401.risks: Carcinogenicity, respiratory sensitization, skin sensitization, severe eye irritation, skin irritation, mutagenicity

sources.label: ECHA Substance Information
Formaldehyde carcinogenicity review PMC
Formaldehyde respiratory sensitization and irritation

402.name: Iodine
402.description: Essential trace element necessary for thyroid hormone synthesis and normal thyroid function.
402.benefits: Supports thyroid hormone production, essential for metabolic regulation and normal growth
402.risks: Excessive intake may cause thyroid dysfunction or iodine poisoning, possible allergic reactions at high doses

sources.label: PMID 23865237 - Iodine nutrition and thyroid disease
PMID 28478894 - Iodine excess and thyroid disease

408.name: Cobalt
408.description: A naturally occurring metal element used industrially and as a dietary trace mineral. While cobalt is essential in small amounts as a component of vitamin B12, excessive exposure, particularly by inhalation or skin contact in industrial settings, can pose health risks including respiratory and skin sensitization, and potential carcinogenicity. Cobalt metal is not a food ingredient and poses toxicity risks when used inappropriately.
408.benefits: Essential trace element as part of vitamin B12 (in biological form), important for red blood cell formation
408.risks: Respiratory sensitization, skin sensitization, carcinogenic potential, toxicity with inhalation or ingestion in excess, systemic toxicity

sources.label: Cobalt - Essential Trace Elements, NIH

409.name: Germanium
409.description: Germanium is a metalloid element sometimes marketed as a dietary supplement in organic form (e.g., germanium sesquioxide). It is not recognized as an essential nutrient. High doses or prolonged use have been associated with toxicity.
409.benefits: None proven, claims of immune support lack robust evidence
409.risks: Kidney damage, toxicity with excessive intake, unknown safety with consumption

410.name: Lithium
410.description: A naturally occurring alkali metal and trace element found in rocks, soil, and water. Used therapeutically as lithium carbonate for bipolar disorder and as an OTC supplement (lithium orotate, lithium aspartate) for mood support and neuroprotection. Has a narrow therapeutic index; serum levels above 1.5 mEq/L are toxic.
410.benefits: Mood stabilization and prevention of manic/depressive episodes at therapeutic doses; neuroprotective effects including potential protection against Alzheimer's disease; may support cognitive function at low doses; preliminary evidence for aiding alcohol cessation
410.risks: Toxicity at high doses (serum >1.5 mEq/L); nephrotoxicity with long-term use; thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, goiter); neurological side effects (tremor, cognitive impairment, ataxia); cardiac arrhythmias; teratogenic risk; narrow therapeutic window; OTC supplements are unregulated and lack FDA approval for any condition

sources.label: Wikipedia – Lithium (medication)

413.name: DCPA di-acid degradate
413.description: DCPA di-acid degradate is a breakdown product of Dithiopyr chloropropionic acid (DCPA), a herbicide used primarily in agriculture and turf management. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical residue potentially found in the environment due to pesticide use.
413.risks: Potential toxicity, environmental persistence, possible carcinogenicity, endocrine disruption, non-food grade chemical

sources.label: EPA Evaluation of Dithiopyr Herbicide

415.name: Paraquat
415.description: Paraquat is a highly toxic non-selective herbicide used in agriculture. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical material with high acute toxicity and potential for causing severe health effects upon exposure.
415.benefits: Effective herbicide for weed control in agriculture
415.risks: Highly toxic if ingested, inhaled, or via skin contact, causes acute poisoning, pulmonary fibrosis, neurotoxicity, carcinogenic potential, environmental persistence

418.name: Microplastics
418.description: Small plastic particles less than 5mm in size originating from plastic debris breakdown or manufactured as microbeads.
418.risks: Environmental persistence, contamination of food and water, potential ingestion toxicity, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption

sources.label: PMC7172636 - Microplastics as emerging contaminants in food and water
PMC7563493 - Health effects of microplastic exposure

420.name: Perfluoro-2-methyl-3-oxahexanoic acid (GenX)
420.description: A synthetic fluorinated chemical used as a processing aid in the manufacture of fluoropolymers, intended as a replacement for legacy perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Not approved as a food ingredient. Known environmental contaminant with potential for bioaccumulation and adverse health effects including liver toxicity, immune system effects, and developmental toxicity.
420.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, liver toxicity, immune toxicity, developmental toxicity, potential carcinogenicity

sources.label: EPA – GenX chemical information

421.name: Perfluorobutanoic Acid / PFBA
421.description: PFBA is a short-chain perfluoroalkyl acid used industrially for its water and stain-resistant properties. It is persistent in the environment and bioaccumulative to a lesser extent than long-chain PFAS. PFBA is not a food ingredient but a material contaminant of concern due to environmental and human health impacts. It is not approved for ingestion and exposure primarily occurs via contaminated water or products.
421.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, liver toxicity, thyroid disruption, developmental toxicity

sources.label: ATSDR Toxicological profile for PFAS

423.name: 3-Hydroxycarbofuran
423.description: 3-Hydroxycarbofuran is a metabolite of carbofuran, a carbamate pesticide. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical contaminant potentially found as a residue in agricultural products. It is highly toxic and acts as an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, leading to neurotoxicity. It is not approved for direct consumption and poses significant health hazards upon exposure.
423.risks: Neurotoxicity, acetylcholinesterase inhibition, acute poisoning, carcinogenic potential, environmental toxicity

sources.label: PubChem description of 3-Hydroxycarbofuran
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Carbofuran

424.name: Alachlor ESA
424.description: Alachlor ESA (Ethane sulfonic acid) is a primary metabolite of the herbicide alachlor, commonly detected as an environmental contaminant. It is not a food ingredient but rather a chemical residue considered a pollutant from pesticide degradation. Alachlor and its metabolites are associated with potential toxicity and environmental persistence.
424.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, environmental toxicity, endocrine disruption, water contamination

425.name: Aldicarb Sulfone
425.description: Aldicarb sulfone is a metabolite of aldicarb, a highly toxic carbamate pesticide. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material due to its neurotoxic effects. It inhibits acetylcholinesterase leading to accumulation of acetylcholine causing overstimulation of nervous system.
425.risks: Highly toxic, neurotoxic, acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, potential fatal poisoning, environmental pollutant

426.name: Aldicarb Sulfoxide
426.description: Aldicarb sulfoxide is a toxic metabolite of aldicarb, a potent carbamate pesticide. It acts as an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor leading to accumulation of acetylcholine and overstimulation of the nervous system. Not approved as a food ingredient; exposure usually occurs via pesticide residues in food or environment. Considered highly toxic to humans and animals.
426.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory distress, seizures, death in acute exposure, environmental toxicity, potential carcinogenicity

sources.label: WHO Carbamate Pesticides: Aldicarb Profile

427.name: Carbaryl
427.description: Carbaryl is a synthetic carbamate insecticide widely used in agriculture and gardening. It is not a food ingredient but a material primarily used for pest control.
427.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum insecticide for controlling various pests in agriculture and horticulture
427.risks: Toxic if ingested, inhaled or absorbed through the skin; potential neurotoxin; possible carcinogen; harmful to aquatic life; causes cholinesterase inhibition leading to nervous system disruption

sources.label: PubChem Carbaryl Summary
EPA Carbaryl Pesticide Information

434.name: Iodomethane
434.description: Iodomethane (methyl iodide) is a volatile halomethane compound used primarily as a pesticide and a chemical reagent. It is not a food ingredient and is considered toxic with recognized carcinogenic and neurotoxic properties. Exposure can occur via inhalation, skin contact, or ingestion, posing health risks.
434.risks: Toxicity, neurotoxicity, carcinogenicity, respiratory irritation, potential reproductive toxicity

439.name: Oxamyl
439.description: Oxamyl is a carbamate pesticide used for controlling nematodes, insects, and mites on crops. It is not a food ingredient and is considered highly toxic. It acts as a cholinesterase inhibitor affecting the nervous system and is classified as hazardous to human health upon exposure.
439.risks: Neurotoxicity, acute poisoning, cholinesterase inhibition, potential carcinogenicity, environmental toxicity, high toxicity to humans and animals

sources.label: PubChem Oxamyl overview
EPA Pesticide Fact Sheet on Oxamyl
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Carbamates

442.name: 4-Androstene-3,17-dione
442.description: A steroid hormone precursor that converts to testosterone and estrogen in the body. It is used as a dietary supplement with claims to boost testosterone but lacks FDA approval for safety or efficacy.
442.benefits: May increase testosterone levels moderately, potential improvement in muscle mass and strength
442.risks: Hormonal imbalance, potential endocrine disruption, liver toxicity, cardiovascular risks, illegal in some sports due to performance-enhancing effects

sources.label: FDA - Androstenedione and Dietary Supplements

443.name: Estriol
443.description: Estriol is a naturally occurring estrogen hormone, one of the three main endogenous estrogens in humans. It is sometimes used in hormone replacement therapy and topical treatments. Not a food ingredient but a pharmaceutical/hormonal compound. Safety and effects depend on dosage and context; typically used under medical supervision.
443.benefits: May relieve menopausal symptoms, supports vaginal and skin health, weaker estrogen with possibly lower risk compared to estradiol
443.risks: Hormonal imbalance, potential cancer risk with long-term use, possible side effects related to estrogen therapy such as blood clots, stroke, breast tenderness

445.name: Diisobutyl phthalate
445.description: A synthetic phthalate plasticizer commonly used to increase flexibility in plastics and sometimes as a solvent or fixative in fragrances. It is not a food ingredient and is primarily a chemical material. Known to be an endocrine disruptor with potential reproductive toxicity.
445.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, potential carcinogenic effects, developmental toxicity, environmental persistence

sources.label: HSDB: Diisobutyl phthalate toxicity

446.name: 1,1,1,2-Tetrachloroethane
446.description: A synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon solvent used industrially; not approved for food use and classified as a toxic chemical with potential carcinogenicity.
446.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, liver damage, respiratory irritation, environmental pollutant

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for 1,1,1,2-Tetrachloroethane

447.name: 1,2,3-Trimethylbenzene
447.description: A group of isomeric aromatic hydrocarbons (C9H12), commonly used as solvents in industrial and cleaning applications. They are volatile organic compounds (VOCs) with moderate toxicity potential.
447.benefits: Effective solvent for removing oily and greasy soils
447.risks: Inhalation toxicity, respiratory tract irritation, skin irritation, potential central nervous system effects, eye irritation, environmental toxicity

sources.label: ECHA Registered Substance Information on Trimethylbenzene
PubChem Trimethylbenzenes Summary
OSHA Occupational Chemical Database – Trimethylbenzene

448.name: 2-Hexanone
448.description: 2-Hexanone is a volatile organic compound used industrially as a solvent and in chemical syntheses. It is not a food ingredient and is categorized as a chemical material. Exposure, especially by inhalation or dermal contact in occupational settings, poses neurotoxic risks. It can cause peripheral neuropathy and has been associated with central nervous system effects. Not approved for use in food products, and inhalation or ingestion is hazardous.
448.risks: Neurotoxicity, peripheral neuropathy, central nervous system effects, occupational exposure hazards

449.name: 2-Methylbutane / isopentane
449.description: A branched alkane hydrocarbon commonly used as a solvent, blowing agent in foam production, and in chromatography as a mobile phase. It is not a food ingredient and primarily considered a chemical material. Exposure is mostly by inhalation of vapors in industrial settings.
449.benefits: Effective solvent and blowing agent in industrial applications
449.risks: Flammability, inhalation toxicity, respiratory irritation, CNS effects, potential environmental pollutant

sources.label: PubChem - Isopentane
NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards - Alkanes

450.name: 2-Nitropropane
450.description: 2-Nitropropane is a synthetic organic solvent used industrially in manufacturing and as a fuel additive. It is not intended for food use and is classified as a hazardous chemical by regulatory agencies.
450.risks: Carcinogenicity, respiratory toxicity, skin irritation, central nervous system effects, suspected human carcinogen

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for 2-Nitropropane
OSHA Chemical Safety Data on 2-Nitropropane

451.name: Acetone
451.description: A volatile organic solvent widely used in cleaning products and cosmetics. It is a simple ketone with strong solvent properties.
451.benefits: Effective solvent and degreaser, fast evaporation, good cleaning properties
451.risks: Eye irritation, skin irritation, inhalation toxicity at high concentrations, CNS depression if inhaled in large amounts

sources.label: PubChem Acetone
ECHA Substance Information Acetone
EPA Acetone Chemical Summary

454.name: Benzaldehyde
454.description: Aromatic aldehyde used as a fragrance and flavoring agent in cleaning products. Provides almond-like scent but can have mild irritant properties.
454.benefits: Used as a chemical intermediate and a solvent for resins and oils. Used as a flavoring agent in food and perfume additive.
454.risks: The primary hazard is to the environment.

sources.label: Compound Summary Benzaldehyde. National Library of Medicine
ECHA Registered Substance - Benzaldehyde
PubChem Benzaldehyde Safety and Hazards

455.name: Carbon Disulfide
455.description: A volatile, colorless liquid used industrially as a solvent and in the manufacture of viscose rayon and cellophane. Not a food ingredient; exposure concerns arise from inhalation and skin contact in occupational settings.
455.risks: Neurotoxicity, reproductive toxicity, cardiovascular toxicity, respiratory irritation, chronic exposure risks, carcinogenic potential

sources.label: ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Carbon Disulfide

458.name: Cyclohexane
458.description: A volatile hydrocarbon solvent commonly used in industrial applications, including as a cleaning agent or in chemical synthesis. Not a food ingredient and not safe for ingestion. Exposure primarily concerns inhalation or skin contact, with potential neurotoxic and irritant effects.
458.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory tract irritation, skin irritation, central nervous system effects, potential carcinogenicity with chronic exposure

sources.label: PubChem - Cyclohexane
NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards: Cyclohexane

459.name: Dichlorodifluoromethane
459.description: A chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) formerly used as a refrigerant and propellant gas in aerosol products. It has ozone-depleting properties, and its use as an aerosol propellant has been largely banned or phased out under the Montreal Protocol due to environmental concerns.
459.risks: Ozone depletion, potential respiratory irritation on inhalation, environmental toxicity, greenhouse gas effects, central nervous system depression in high concentrations

sources.label: PubChem Dichlorodifluoromethane
EPA on CFC phaseout

460.name: Hexane
460.description: Hexane is a solvent commonly used in the extraction of edible oils and other food ingredients. It is a volatile hydrocarbon and its residues may remain in trace amounts in processed foods. Hexane exposure is mainly a concern in occupational settings or high-level contamination. It is not approved as a food additive by the FDA but is allowed as a processing aid with regulated residue levels.
460.benefits: Effective solvent for oil extraction efficiency enabling lower cost food production
460.risks: Neurotoxicity with high/chronic exposure, possible residual solvent ingestion, environmental pollutant

sources.label: FDA on Processing Aids

462.name: Methyl ethyl ketone
462.description: Solvent commonly used in cleaning products and coatings; also known as 2-butanone. Classified as a volatile organic compound (VOC) with moderate acute toxicity and irritant properties.
462.benefits: Effective solvent for removing oils, greases, and resins
462.risks: Eye irritation, skin irritation, respiratory tract irritation, dizziness, central nervous system depression at high exposures, potential reproductive toxicity with chronic high-level exposure

sources.label: PubChem 2-Butanone Overview
ECHA 2-Butanone Skin and Eye Irritation Data
NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards - Methyl Ethyl Ketone

463.name: Methyl isobutyl ketone
463.description: A solvent commonly used in industrial applications such as paint thinning and cleaning. It is not a food ingredient and is toxic if ingested. Exposure typically occurs via inhalation or skin contact in occupational settings.
463.risks: Toxic if ingested, respiratory irritation, central nervous system depression, skin irritation, potential occupational hazard

sources.label: PubChem - Methyl Isobutyl Ketone
NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards - Methyl Isobutyl Ketone

464.name: Methylcyclopentane
464.description: A hydrocarbon solvent, not used as a food ingredient. Typically a material used in industrial applications and possibly found in fragrances or solvents. It is a volatile organic compound with potential inhalation hazards.
464.risks: Inhalation toxicity, respiratory irritation, flammability, central nervous system effects at high exposure

sources.label: PubChem - Methylcyclopentane Hazard Identification
ToxNet - Toxicology Data on Hydrocarbon Solvents

466.name: Pentane
466.description: Pentane is a volatile hydrocarbon often used as a blowing agent in foam production and solvent in chemical applications. It is not a food ingredient and is primarily considered a material with potential inhalation and flammability hazards.
466.risks: Flammability, inhalation toxicity, CNS depression, respiratory irritation

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for Pentane
Pentane and Related Hydrocarbons - NCBI Toxicology Textbook

467.name: Tert-Butyl Alcohol
467.description: A synthetic tertiary alcohol used mainly as a solvent and in chemical synthesis; not approved as a food additive or ingredient for consumption. Exposure primarily occurs through inhalation, dermal contact, or accidental ingestion, with known toxic effects at higher doses.
467.risks: Toxicity upon ingestion or inhalation, central nervous system depression, irritation to skin and respiratory tract, potential for liver and kidney damage in high doses

sources.label: PubChem - Tert-Butyl Alcohol Safety and Toxicity

468.name: Tetrahydrofuran
468.description: Tetrahydrofuran (THF) is a synthetic organic solvent commonly used in industrial applications and chemical synthesis. It is not a food ingredient and is not safe for ingestion. Exposure risks primarily relate to inhalation or skin contact during manufacturing or use in materials.
468.risks: Toxic if ingested, respiratory irritation, central nervous system effects, flammability, potential carcinogenicity with long-term exposure

sources.label: PubChem - Tetrahydrofuran
OSHA Chemical Sampling Information - Tetrahydrofuran

469.name: Trichlorofluoromethane
469.description: Also known as CFC-11, this is a chlorofluorocarbon once widely used as a refrigerant and aerosol propellant. It is a synthetic compound banned under the Montreal Protocol due to its ozone-depleting properties. Not a food ingredient; exposure concerns relate to inhalation and environmental impact.
469.risks: Ozone layer depletion, environmental persistence, potential respiratory toxicity if inhaled, greenhouse gas effect

sources.label: PubChem Trichlorofluoromethane summary

471.name: Butylated hydroxytoluene  / BHT
471.description: Synthetic antioxidant used to prevent oxidation in foods, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals.
471.benefits: Effective antioxidant that extends shelf life by preventing rancidity
471.risks: Irritation potential at high concentrations, possible endocrine activity under some conditions, regulatory scrutiny in some jurisdictions

477.name: Oxyfluorfen
477.description: Oxyfluorfen is a pre-emergent herbicide commonly used in agriculture and landscaping to control broadleaf and grassy weeds. It is not a food ingredient and is classified as a synthetic chemical material with potential health and environmental risks. Exposure can occur via inhalation, dermal contact, or ingestion through contaminated food or water. The EPA classifies oxyfluorfen as a possible human carcinogen based on animal studies, with potential toxicity to liver and thyroid. It is not approved for direct food use but residues may be found in treated crops.
477.benefits: Effective weed control in agriculture and landscaping, reduces crop competition
477.risks: Possible carcinogen, liver toxicity, thyroid disruption, environmental toxicity, dermal and respiratory irritation

sources.label: PubChem – Oxyfluorfen Compound Summary
EPA – Oxyfluorfen Pesticide Information Profile

480.name: Tebuconazole
480.description: Tebuconazole is a systemic triazole fungicide primarily used in agriculture to protect crops by inhibiting fungal ergosterol biosynthesis. It is not intended for direct human consumption but residues may occur in food products. The compound is under regulatory scrutiny for potential health and environmental effects including endocrine disruption and toxicity.
480.benefits: Effective fungicide for crop protection, reduces crop losses from fungal diseases
480.risks: Possible endocrine disruption, hepatotoxicity, reproductive toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation

sources.label: Toxicological effects of Tebuconazole on mammals

485.name: Sodium Fluoride
485.description: Inorganic compound used primarily as a fluoridating agent in dental care products to prevent dental caries by enhancing tooth enamel resistance.
485.benefits: Dental caries prevention through enamel remineralization
485.risks: Ingestion toxicity at high doses including acute poisoning, potential skeletal fluorosis with chronic excessive exposure, irritation risk in concentrated topical use

sources.label: Fluoride toxicity and clinical dental applications - PubMed
Fluoride exposure and health risks - PubMed

498.name: Aldicarb
498.description: Aldicarb is a highly toxic carbamate pesticide used to control insects and mites in agriculture. It is not a food ingredient and poses significant health risks due to its ability to inhibit acetylcholinesterase, leading to nervous system toxicity.
498.risks: Neurotoxicity, acetylcholinesterase inhibition, acute poisoning, respiratory failure, environmental contamination

sources.label: PubChem - Aldicarb Chemical Information

513.name: Natural flavors
513.description: Chemical mixtures derived from various natural sources used to impart flavor. Often undisclosed specific composition.
513.risks: Potential presence of undisclosed solvents or processing agents, allergen cross-contact, ultra-processed nature

516.name: Mango puree
516.description: Pureed form of mango fruit providing natural flavor and texture to food products.
516.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamins (especially vitamin C and A precursors), natural flavor

sources.label: Nutritional composition and health benefits of mango fruit

517.name: Orange juice
517.description: Fruit juice derived from oranges, typically containing natural sugars, vitamin C, and other nutrients. Used in food products for flavor and nutrient contribution.
517.benefits: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants, provides flavor and hydration
517.risks: High natural sugar content, potential dental erosion with frequent consumption, possible allergenic reactions in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMC4228663 - Nutritional and health benefits of orange juice
Vitamin C and antioxidant properties of orange juice

518.name: Citric acid
518.description: A weak organic acid naturally found in citrus fruits used as a pH adjuster, preservative, and flavoring agent in food and cosmetic products.
518.benefits: Preservative properties, pH regulation, enhances flavor
518.risks: Irritation potential in high concentrations, dental enamel erosion with excessive ingestion

sources.label: PMID 29212629 - Safety and use of citric acid as a food additive
PMID 28875583 - Dental erosion associated with acid intake

519.name: Hibiscus
519.description: Botanical ingredient derived from Hibiscus flowers, commonly used in beverages and topical products for color and flavor.
519.benefits: Flavoring agent, natural colorant, contains antioxidants
519.risks: Possible allergic reactions or skin irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Antioxidant properties of Hibiscus sabdariffa extract – PMID 30052843
Allergic contact dermatitis from hibiscus – PMID 26103304

520.name: Raspberry puree
520.description: Raspberry puree is a food ingredient made from crushed raspberries, commonly used for flavor and color in foods and beverages. Water is often added to adjust consistency or concentration.
520.benefits: Source of natural flavor, contains dietary fiber and antioxidants

sources.label: PMC Proven Health Benefits of Raspberries

521.name: Raspberry juice
521.description: Juice extracted from raspberries, used primarily as a flavoring or colorant in food and beverage products.
521.benefits: Provides natural flavor and color, contains antioxidants such as vitamin C and polyphenols

522.name: Lime juice
522.description: Lime refers to the citrus fruit Citrus aurantiifolia or Citrus latifolia, used for its juice and flavor. It is a natural source of vitamin C and citric acid.
522.benefits: Provides vitamin C, antioxidant capacity, flavoring agent
522.risks: Irritant potential on skin or mucosa, phototoxicity risk especially with lime oil, ingestion generally safe at dietary levels

sources.label: PMID 21716343 - Phototoxic effects of lime essential oil and furocoumarins
PMID 17250883 - Nutritional and antioxidant properties of citrus fruits

523.name: Natural essence
523.description: Concentrated extracts derived from natural sources such as plants, used primarily for flavoring or fragrance purposes.
523.benefits: Provides natural flavor or fragrance, can enhance sensory properties
523.risks: Potential allergen or sensitizer, variability in composition, possible contamination with solvents or impurities

524.name: Organic cane sugar
524.description: Sucrose extracted from sugarcane, used as a sweetener in foods and beverages.
524.risks: Excessive intake associated with dental caries, weight gain, elevated blood glucose

sources.label: PMC7451191 - Effects of sugar intake on human health

525.name: Organic agave inulin
525.description: Inulin is a fructan-type soluble dietary fiber extracted from organic agave plant. It functions as a prebiotic fiber that resists digestion and promotes beneficial gut bacteria growth.
525.benefits: Prebiotic fiber, supports gut microbiota, may improve bowel regularity
525.risks: Digestive discomfort at high doses such as bloating, gas, flatulence

sources.label: Scientific review on inulin and gut health
Effects of inulin-type fructans on gastrointestinal symptoms

526.name: Apple juice (concentrate)
526.description: Apple juice reconstituted from concentrate, primarily composed of water, sugars (fructose and glucose), and organic acids.
526.benefits: Source of hydration, contains some vitamins and antioxidants from apples
526.risks: High sugar content, potential contribution to dental caries and excess caloric intake

527.name: Organic apple cider vinegar
527.description: Fermented apple juice primarily composed of acetic acid and water, commonly used as a flavoring agent and preservative.
527.benefits: Acetic acid content may support antimicrobial effects and flavor enhancement
527.risks: Irritation risk at high concentrations when applied to skin or mucous membranes, possible enamel erosion with excessive ingestion

sources.label: PMID 24081474 - Antimicrobial properties of vinegar

528.name: Stevia
528.description: Natural non-nutritive sweetener derived from Stevia rebaudiana, used to provide sweetness without calories.
528.benefits: Calorie-free sweetening, low glycemic impact, suitable for diabetic and weight management diets
528.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, potential for rare allergic reactions

sources.label: PMID 29631345 - Safety and efficacy of steviol glycosides

531.name: Phosphorus
531.description: Essential mineral involved in bone formation, energy metabolism, and cellular function.
531.benefits: Supports bone and teeth health, energy production, and cellular signaling
531.risks: Excessive intake may disrupt mineral balance and affect kidney function in vulnerable populations

sources.label: Phosphorus - Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D

542.name: Strontium
542.description: Strontium is an alkaline earth metal element found naturally in small amounts in the environment and in some minerals. In dietary supplements, strontium salts (e.g., strontium ranelate) have been used for bone health, but elemental strontium itself is not a nutrient.
542.benefits: May support bone density when used as specific salts under medical supervision
542.risks: Potential toxicity with excessive ingestion, possible interference with calcium metabolism, contamination risk from radioactive isotopes in certain contexts

543.name: Malic Acid
543.description: A naturally occurring organic acid primarily used as an acidity regulator and flavor enhancer in foods.
543.risks: Mild oral or dermal irritation at high concentrations

sources.label: Safety and uses of malic acid in food products

545.name: Potassium Benzoate
545.description: Potassium benzoate is a potassium salt of benzoic acid used as a preservative to inhibit the growth of mold, yeast, and some bacteria in acidic foods and beverages.
545.benefits: Prevents microbial spoilage, extends shelf life of acidic foods and beverages
545.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, potential formation of benzene under certain conditions, sensitization in rare cases

sources.label: PMID 16214481 - Safety review of benzoates in food products
PMID 18817812 - Benzene formation from benzoate preservatives

546.name: Sucralose
546.description: Sucralose is a non-nutritive artificial sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories.
546.benefits: Calorie-free sweetness, useful for sugar replacement, supports reduced caloric intake
546.risks: Possible gut microbiota alterations, potential digestive discomfort at high doses, heat instability leading to breakdown products

sources.label: PMCID: PMC4919134 - Sucralose and gut microbiota changes
PMID: 23075195 - Safety evaluation of sucralose

547.name: Green Tea Extract
547.description: Concentrated extract from green tea leaves containing polyphenols, primarily catechins like epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Commonly used as an antioxidant and for flavor.
547.benefits: Antioxidant properties, may support skin health and reduce oxidative stress
547.risks: Potential liver toxicity in high doses, possible interference with some medications, mild gastrointestinal irritation

sources.label: PMC3386115 - Safety and efficacy of green tea extract
Green tea catechins: bioavailability and health effects

548.name: Cherry Juice Concentrate
548.description: Concentrated juice derived from cherries, primarily composed of sugars, organic acids, and phytochemicals such as anthocyanins.
548.benefits: Source of antioxidants, phytochemicals like anthocyanins
548.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental caries with excessive consumption

sources.label: Anthocyanins from cherry juice and health effects

549.name: Retinol
549.description: Retinol is a form of vitamin A, a fat-soluble vitamin essential for vision, immune function, and skin health. It is not part of the vitamin B complex. Retinol is recognized by the FDA as a vitamin with established dietary reference intakes.
549.benefits: Supports vision, immune function, cellular growth, skin health, antioxidant activity
549.risks: Hypervitaminosis A, liver toxicity at high intakes, teratogenic effects during pregnancy

sources.label: NIH Vitamin A Fact Sheet
NIH Office of Dietary Supplements – Vitamin A

550.name: Niacinamide
550.description: A form of vitamin B3 used primarily in foods and cosmetics for skin barrier support and metabolic functions.
550.benefits: Supports skin barrier integrity, improves skin appearance, essential nutrient
550.risks: Possible mild skin irritation or sensitization at high concentrations, none at typical use

sources.label: PMC3673383 – Niacinamide and its topical use

551.name: Calcium Pantothenate
551.description: Calcium pantothenate is a stable, calcium salt form of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), a water-soluble vitamin essential for coenzyme A synthesis and energy metabolism.
551.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, necessary for synthesis of coenzyme A, involved in fatty acid and carbohydrate metabolism
551.risks: Rare mild gastrointestinal upset at high doses

sources.label: PMID 24171472 - Review of pantothenic acid's biochemical functions and safety
PMID 23439862 - Safety assessment of pantothenic acid

553.name: Biotin
553.description: Water-soluble B-vitamin (vitamin B7) essential for carboxylase enzyme function in fatty acid synthesis, gluconeogenesis, and amino acid metabolism.
553.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, coenzyme for key metabolic pathways
553.risks: Rare allergic reactions, possible interference with certain laboratory test results

sources.label: PMID 20797836 - Role of biotin in metabolic regulation
PMID 31436633 - Biotin interference in laboratory assays

554.name: Cyanocobalamin
554.description: Synthetic form of vitamin B12 used as a dietary supplement and food fortificant to prevent or treat B12 deficiency.
554.benefits: Prevents and treats vitamin B12 deficiency, supports red blood cell formation and neurological function
554.risks: Rare allergic reactions, potential cyanide exposure in very high doses, generally safe at recommended levels

sources.label: PMC3468949 - Vitamin B12: Physiology, Dietary Sources, and Requirement
PMC3205700 - Safety of vitamin B12 injections compared to cyanide exposure

557.name: Magnesium Malate
557.description: Magnesium malate is a compound of magnesium and malic acid, often used as a dietary supplement to provide bioavailable magnesium.
557.benefits: Source of magnesium, supports muscle and nerve function, involved in energy production
557.risks: Gastrointestinal upset at high doses, laxative effect

558.name: Cane sugar
558.description: Sucrose derived from sugarcane, used as a sweetener and flavor enhancer in food products.
558.benefits: Provides sweetness, energy source through carbohydrates
558.risks: Excessive intake associated with risk of obesity, dental caries, and metabolic disorders

sources.label: Consequences of excessive sugar consumption on health - PubMed 29329891
Health effects of sugars and sweeteners - PubMed 30854843

559.name: Dextrose
559.description: A simple sugar (glucose) commonly used as a sweetener and energy source in food products.
559.benefits: Quick energy source, commonly used for sweetness and fermentation support
559.risks: Excessive intake may contribute to increased blood sugar levels and caloric intake

sources.label: Effects of dietary glucose on glycemic control and energy

560.name: Potassium citrate
560.description: Potassium citrate is a potassium salt of citric acid used as a mineral supplement and alkalinizing agent to maintain electrolyte balance and urinary pH.
560.benefits: Electrolyte replenishment, urinary alkalinizer to reduce kidney stone risk, supports cellular and nerve function
560.risks: Hyperkalemia risk in patients with impaired renal function or excessive intake, gastrointestinal irritation at high doses

sources.label: Effects of potassium citrate on urinary risk factors for kidney stones
Potassium intake and health implications

561.name: Sodium citrate
561.description: Sodium citrate is the trisodium salt of citric acid, used as a water softener and pH buffer in cleaning products. It is classified as an organic salt chelating agent derived from citrus acids.
561.benefits: Water softening, pH buffering, biodegradable, low toxicity
561.risks: Mild skin irritation at very high concentrations, eye irritation if directly contacted

sources.label: ECHA Sodium citrate Skin irritation and eye irritation data
PubChem Sodium citrate toxicity summary
Assessment of sodium citrate safety profile in consumer products

562.name: Silicon dioxide
562.description: An anti-caking agent commonly used in powdered food products and supplements to prevent clumping and improve flow.
562.benefits: Improves powder flow and stability of powdered products
562.risks: Minor inhalation risk in powder form, generally low toxicity

sources.label: PMC1360272 - Safety of silicon dioxide as a food additive

566.name: Organic flavors
566.description: Flavoring agents derived from organic sources, though still subject to extraction and processing methods that may involve solvents or additives. 'Organic' label indicates source material but does not guarantee absence of processing chemicals.
566.benefits: Derived from organic sources, perceived as cleaner by consumers compared to conventional flavors
566.risks: May contain solvent residues, ultra-processed, lack of transparency, no significant nutritional value

567.name: Erythritol
567.description: A sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener that does not raise blood sugar significantly.
567.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, does not affect blood glucose or insulin significantly
567.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, laxative effect

sources.label: PMCID: PMC5372970 – Review of erythritol safety and metabolic effects

568.name: Coconut water concentrate
568.description: Concentrated form of coconut water composed mainly of water, electrolytes, and natural sugars, used for flavor and hydration.

569.name: Acacia gum
569.description: A natural polysaccharide gum obtained from the sap of Acacia trees, used as a glazing agent to provide a protective coating and improve texture in food products.
569.benefits: Edible fiber source, stabilizer, emulsifier, improves texture and shelf-life of food products
569.risks: Possible allergen in sensitive individuals, potential minor gastrointestinal effects at high doses

sources.label: PMCID: PMC3916847 - Acacia gum as a dietary fiber and food additive
PMID: 20925392 - Safety and tolerability of gum arabic (acacia gum)

570.name: Sea salt
570.description: Mineral salt derived from evaporated seawater, containing primarily sodium chloride with trace minerals.
570.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission and fluid balance
570.risks: Excessive sodium intake associated with hypertension and cardiovascular risk

sources.label: Excess salt intake and cardiovascular health

571.name: Tea extract
571.description: Concentrated extract derived from tea leaves, containing polyphenols such as catechins and flavonoids.
571.benefits: Antioxidant properties, potential to reduce oxidative damage, moderate antimicrobial effects
571.risks: Potential skin irritation or sensitization in topical use, caffeine content may cause mild stimulant effects, possible interaction with medications

sources.label: PMC2855614 - Safety and efficacy of tea polyphenols
PMID 24470337 - Topical use of green tea extracts and irritation

572.name: Green coffee bean extract
572.description: Extract derived from unroasted coffee beans containing chlorogenic acids and other polyphenols.
572.benefits: Antioxidant properties, potential mild modulation of glucose metabolism
572.risks: Irritation at high doses, potential mild gastrointestinal upset, caffeine-related effects

573.name: Coffeefruit extract
573.description: Coffeefruit extract is derived from the outer pulp of the coffee cherry, the fruit that surrounds the coffee bean. It is used as a source of polyphenols and antioxidants, and has been investigated for potential neuroprotective and cognitive benefits.
573.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential cognitive support, polyphenol source
573.risks: Possible caffeine content, potential for allergic reaction, insufficient long-term safety data

574.name: D-alpha tocopheryl acetate (Vitamin E)
574.description: Synthetic form of vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol) esterified with acetic acid to enhance stability. Used as an antioxidant and nutrient supplement in food and skincare products.
574.benefits: Antioxidant protecting lipids from oxidation, skin conditioning agent, vitamin E source
574.risks: Low irritation potential, rare allergic sensitization, minimal toxicity at typical use levels

575.name: Agave nectar
575.description: Sweetener derived from the agave plant, primarily composed of fructose and glucose sugars.
575.benefits: Sweetening agent, sweeter than sucrose requiring smaller quantities
575.risks: High fructose content associated with excessive caloric intake, potential contribution to weight gain and metabolic disturbances if consumed in excess

sources.label: Fructose and metabolic health - PMC3820110

576.name: Cassava root fiber
576.description: Dietary fiber derived from the root of the cassava plant (Manihot esculenta), used primarily as a source of insoluble fiber in food products.
576.benefits: Source of insoluble dietary fiber, supports digestive regularity, gluten-free fiber alternative
576.risks: Potential cyanogenic glycoside contamination if improperly processed, mild digestive intolerance in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Dietary Fiber from Cassava and Its Effects on Health (PMC6348784)
Cyanogenic Potential of Cassava Products (PMID:17490999)

577.name: Chicory root inulin
577.description: Dietary fiber extracted from chicory root, classified as a fructan that resists digestion and promotes beneficial gut bacteria growth.
577.benefits: Supports gut microbiota modulation, improves bowel function
577.risks: May cause gastrointestinal discomfort or bloating in sensitive individuals or high doses

579.name: Nopal cactus extract
579.description: Nopal cactus extract is a concentrated form of the pads of the prickly pear cactus (Opuntia ficus-indica), known for its fiber, polyphenols, and antioxidant content. It may be used for its purported glycemic control and anti-inflammatory effects.
579.benefits: May support blood sugar management, provides antioxidants, may support lipid metabolism
579.risks: Mild gastrointestinal upset at high doses, possible drug interactions

580.name: Marshmallow root
580.description: Marshmallow root is derived from the Althaea officinalis plant and has a long history of traditional use as a demulcent, meaning it forms a soothing film over mucous membranes and may help relieve irritation in the throat and digestive tract.
580.benefits: Soothes throat irritation, may reduce cough, potential anti-inflammatory effects, supports digestive comfort
580.risks: Potential allergic reactions, may interact with antidiabetic medications, insufficient safety data in pregnancy

581.name: Calendula flower extract
581.description: Calendula flower extract is derived from the petals of Calendula officinalis and is commonly used for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties in both food and topical products.
581.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, promotes wound healing, antimicrobial effects
581.risks: Rare allergic reactions, potential interaction with sedative medications

582.name: Kudzu root
582.description: Kudzu root is derived from the Pueraria lobata plant and has a long history of use in traditional medicine, especially in East Asia. It contains isoflavones and other phytochemicals that have biological effects in the body, including possible antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.
582.benefits: Potential antioxidant activity, possible reduction of alcohol cravings, may help with menopausal symptoms
582.risks: May interact with medications, possible estrogenic effects, insufficient long-term safety data

583.name: Ginger juice
583.description: Juice extracted from the rhizome of the ginger plant (Zingiber officinale), commonly used as a flavoring agent and in beverages.
583.benefits: Flavor enhancement, natural antioxidant compounds, traditional digestive aid
583.risks: Mild skin and mucous membrane irritation possible in sensitive individuals, potential allergic sensitization

sources.label: PMC3665023 - Ginger's bioactive compounds and effects
PMID 25609279 - Safety and allergenicity of ginger

584.name: Cassava root syrup
584.description: Sweetener derived from the starch of cassava root, used as a natural sugar substitute in foods and beverages. Contains carbohydrates with minimal nutritional micronutrients. Generally regarded as safe for consumption by the FDA.
584.benefits: Natural sweetener alternative to refined sugars, gluten-free, source of energy
584.risks: High glycemic index, potential blood sugar spikes, may contribute to obesity if overconsumed

585.name: Natural ginger flavor
585.description: Extracted or synthesized flavor compounds derived from ginger root commonly used to impart ginger taste in foods and beverages.
585.risks: Irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, potential allergens

588.name: L-Citrulline
588.description: A non-essential amino acid involved in the urea cycle and nitric oxide production.
588.benefits: Supports nitric oxide production, may improve blood flow and exercise performance
588.risks: None at typical dietary or supplemental levels

591.name: Steviol glycosides
591.description: Natural sweetening compounds extracted from the Stevia rebaudiana plant, used as high-intensity sweeteners in foods and beverages.
591.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, suitable for diabetics and weight management
591.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, limited data on long-term high-dose consumption

sources.label: PMID 23107585 - Safety and efficacy of steviol glycosides
PMID 23929708 - Effects of stevia on glucose control in diabetes

592.name: L-theanine
592.description: A non-protein amino acid commonly found in tea leaves, known for its calming and relaxation effects on the central nervous system.
592.benefits: Promotes relaxation without sedation, may improve focus and cognitive performance
592.risks: None at typical dietary or supplemental intake levels

593.name: Ginger Root Extract
593.description: Ginger root extract is a concentrated form of compounds derived from the ginger plant (Zingiber officinale), known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that support digestion, reduce nausea, and may help modulate metabolic and inflammatory pathways.
593.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, reduces nausea, supports digestion, may reduce muscle pain, potential metabolic support
593.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort, potential blood thinning effects, may interact with anticoagulant medications

594.name: Carbonated Purified Water
594.description: Water that has been purified to remove impurities and carbonated by dissolving carbon dioxide gas under pressure. Commonly used as a base in flavored and probiotic beverages.
594.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free base, may aid probiotic delivery
594.risks: Potential dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption of carbonated beverages

595.name: Organic Caffeine
595.description: Organic caffeine is a naturally derived stimulant commonly included in caffeinated flavors to impart alertness and focus. FDA classifies caffeine as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) in typical dietary amounts. When labeled organic, caffeine is sourced from organically grown plants without synthetic pesticides. Used within safe consumption limits, organic caffeine has similar effects and safety profile as conventional caffeine.
595.benefits: Increased alertness, improved cognitive performance, enhanced metabolism, fatigue reduction
595.risks: Insomnia, jitteriness, increased heart rate, potential dependence, anxiety in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Dietary caffeine use and safety

600.name: organic pineapple juice concentrate
600.description: Concentrated juice derived from pineapple, primarily serving as a sweetener and flavoring agent in foods and beverages.
600.benefits: Natural source of vitamins and antioxidants, contributes flavor and sweetness
600.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental erosion with excessive consumption, minor allergenic potential

601.name: Organic guava natural flavor
601.description: A flavoring ingredient derived from organic guava or its components, used to impart guava taste. Classified as a natural flavor but is often a complex mixture created via extraction, distillation, or fermentation. Considered ultra-processed with limited disclosure on specific chemical composition.
601.benefits: Imparts guava flavor, organic sourcing may reduce synthetic pesticide residue
601.risks: Lack of transparency, potential trace solvents or allergens, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

603.name: Carbonated Water
603.description: Water into which carbon dioxide gas has been dissolved under pressure, creating effervescence.

604.name: Taurine
604.description: A sulfur-containing amino acid often used in energy drinks and supplements for its role in cellular function and osmoregulation.
604.benefits: Supports cellular hydration, antioxidant effects, may improve exercise performance
604.risks: Minor gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, potential interaction with stimulant compounds

sources.label: PMID 25637345 - Taurine functions and supplementation

606.name: Sucrose Acetate Isobutyrate
606.description: Sucrose acetate isobutyrate (SAIB) is a synthetic ester used as a stabilizer and emulsifier in food and beverages to maintain uniform dispersion of ingredients.
606.benefits: Enhances stability of emulsions, improves texture and mouthfeel in beverages and food products
606.risks: Potential minor irritant, synthetic processing residues, limited long-term toxicology data

sources.label: Safety evaluation of sucrose acetate isobutyrate as food additive

608.name: Xanthan Gum
608.description: A polysaccharide used as a thickening and stabilizing agent in food and cosmetic products.
608.benefits: Improves texture and stability of products, enhances mouthfeel, acts as a dietary fiber
608.risks: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort at high intake, potential for allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Safety evaluation of xanthan gum as a food additive

609.name: Magnesium Carbonate
609.description: An inorganic salt commonly used as a dietary supplement and antacid, also used as an anti-caking agent and in pharmaceuticals.
609.benefits: Source of magnesium, supports bone health, used as an antacid to neutralize stomach acid
609.risks: None at typical uses, excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal discomfort

sources.label: Magnesium - Dietary Supplement Fact Sheet (NIH)

611.name: Glucose
611.description: Simple sugar (monosaccharide) commonly used as a sweetener and energy source in foods.
611.benefits: Rapid energy source, supports cellular metabolism
611.risks: Excessive intake associated with increased caloric intake and potential weight gain

sources.label: Glucose metabolism and health implications

612.name: Inositol
612.description: A carbohydrate compound often classified as a sugar alcohol, involved in cell membrane signaling and found in various foods.
612.benefits: Supports cell signaling pathways, considered safe as a dietary component

sources.label: PMID 11100003 - Roles of inositol in biology

613.name: Beta carotene
613.description: A carotenoid pigment serving as a provitamin A, converted in the body into vitamin A necessary for vision, immune function, and cellular growth.
613.benefits: Provitamin A activity, antioxidant properties, supports vision and immune health
613.risks: Potential increased lung cancer risk in high-dose supplementation among smokers, skin yellowing at excessive intake

616.name: Ascorbic Acid
616.description: Vitamin C, a water-soluble antioxidant used to maintain color and prevent oxidative degradation in food products.

sources.label: PMC3010673 – Antioxidant role of ascorbic acid in food preservation and health

617.name: Magnesium lactate
617.description: A magnesium salt of lactic acid used as an electrolyte to restore magnesium levels and assist in nerve and muscle function.
617.benefits: Provides bioavailable magnesium, supports electrolyte balance, muscle and nerve function
617.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, excess intake may cause diarrhea

sources.label: Magnesium – Dietary Supplement Fact Sheet

619.name: L-Valine
619.description: L-Valine is an essential branched-chain amino acid important for protein synthesis and muscle metabolism.
619.benefits: Supports muscle protein synthesis, essential amino acid, contributes to nitrogen balance

sources.label: Role of branched-chain amino acids in muscle metabolism and health

620.name: L-Isoleucine
620.description: An essential branched-chain amino acid involved in protein synthesis, energy metabolism, and muscle repair.
620.benefits: Supports protein synthesis, muscle repair, energy metabolism

sources.label: PMID 28232291 - Role of branched-chain amino acids in muscle synthesis and energy metabolism

621.name: L-Glutamine
621.description: An amino acid used as a building block for proteins, involved in nitrogen transport and important for intestinal and immune cell function.
621.benefits: Supports protein synthesis, intestinal health, immune function

sources.label: PMID 14517181 - Role of glutamine in nutrition and intestinal function
PMID 12706917 - Glutamine and immune function in health and disease

622.name: Choline bitartrate
622.description: Choline bitartrate is a salt form of choline, an essential nutrient involved in neurotransmitter synthesis, liver function, and cell membrane integrity.
622.benefits: Supports cognitive function, liver health, and cell membrane structure
622.risks: None at typical supplemental doses, high doses may cause gastrointestinal distress, fishy body odor

623.name: Thiamine Hydrochloride
623.description: Water-soluble vitamin B1 derivative used primarily as a dietary supplement and food additive to prevent or treat thiamine deficiency.
623.benefits: Essential nutrient for energy metabolism, supports nerve function, prevents beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
623.risks: Rare allergic reactions, generally low toxicity at typical doses

sources.label: Thiamine - NIH Office of Dietary Supplements

624.name: Folic acid
624.description: Synthetic form of folate, a B-vitamin involved in DNA synthesis and cellular replication. Used as a dietary supplement and food fortification substance.
624.benefits: Prevents neural tube defects during pregnancy, supports DNA synthesis and red blood cell formation
624.risks: Excessive intake may mask vitamin B12 deficiency effects, potential for unmetabolized folic acid accumulation

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Folate
Safety and efficacy of folic acid supplementation

625.name: Riboflavin (Vitamin B2)
625.description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for energy production, cellular function, and metabolism of fats, drugs, and steroids.
625.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, maintains healthy skin and mucous membranes, contributes to redox reactions
625.risks: None at typical dietary or supplemental levels

sources.label: PMID 24380527 - Riboflavin and its role in health

627.name: Turmeric Extract
627.description: An extract derived from the rhizome of Curcuma longa, containing curcuminoids, mainly curcumin, used primarily for its color and potential bioactive properties.
627.benefits: Antioxidant properties, potential anti-inflammatory effects, culinary use as a spice and colorant
627.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, potential for drug interactions

sources.label: PMID 17569207 - Curcumin: biological and medicinal properties

628.name: Coconut Water
628.description: Clear fluid found inside green coconuts, primarily composed of water with natural sugars, electrolytes, and minor nutrients.
628.benefits: Hydrating, source of electrolytes such as potassium and magnesium
628.risks: Minor risk of gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals, natural sugar content

sources.label: PMID 28785971 - Nutritional and health aspects of coconut water

631.name: Potassium sorbate
631.description: Potassium sorbate is a potassium salt of sorbic acid, commonly used as a preservative to inhibit mold, yeast, and fungal growth in food and personal care products.
631.benefits: Effective preservative against molds and yeasts, extends shelf life of products
631.risks: Skin and eye irritation, sensitization in some individuals, potential for respiratory irritation if inhaled as powder

sources.label: PMID 7294526 - Allergic contact dermatitis from potassium sorbate
PMID 29963262 - Review of safety and efficacy of potassium sorbate as preservative

634.name: Magnesium Citrate
634.description: Magnesium citrate is a magnesium salt of citric acid commonly used as a dietary supplement to supply magnesium, an essential mineral involved in many physiological functions.
634.benefits: Supports magnesium intake, contributes to muscle and nerve function, aids electrolyte balance
634.risks: Digestive upset at high doses, laxative effect with excessive ingestion

sources.label: PubMed 16456837 – Magnesium citrate bioavailability and effects

636.name: Coenzyme Q10
636.description: A fat-soluble compound involved in mitochondrial electron transport and cellular energy production.
636.benefits: Supports cellular energy metabolism, antioxidant properties
636.risks: Mild gastrointestinal upset and rare allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

638.name: Glucuronolactone
638.description: A naturally occurring carbohydrate compound formed from glucose, commonly used in energy drinks and supplements for its purported detoxifying and metabolism support functions.
638.benefits: May support liver detoxification pathways and metabolism, energy metabolism role
638.risks: None at typical dietary or supplemental levels, low toxicity profile

639.name: Chromium chelate
639.description: Chromium chelate is a supplemental form of the essential trace mineral chromium, where chromium is chemically bound to amino acids or other organic molecules to improve absorption. It is often included in dietary supplements for its purported effects on glucose metabolism and insulin sensitivity.
639.benefits: May improve glycemic control in type 2 diabetes, may improve insulin sensitivity in deficient individuals
639.risks: Potential kidney damage at high doses, possible gastrointestinal upset, risk of drug interactions

640.name: Calcium Carbonate
640.description: Inorganic compound commonly used as a calcium supplement and antacid, also utilized as a food additive and filler.
640.benefits: Source of calcium essential for bone health, used as antacid to neutralize stomach acid
640.risks: Possible gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, risk of hypercalcemia with excessive intake

sources.label: PMC4728667 - Calcium carbonate safety and usage

641.name: Caramel color
641.description: Caramel color is a water-soluble food coloring made by controlled heat treatment of carbohydrates. It is widely used to impart brown coloration in foods and beverages.
641.benefits: Provides stable brown color, enhances visual appeal of food and beverages
641.risks: Potential contamination with 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI), a possible carcinogen at high exposure, regulatory limits apply

sources.label: PMID 28769240 - Safety review of caramel color and 4-methylimidazole

642.name: Phosphoric Acid
642.description: Inorganic acid commonly used as a preservative and acidulant in foods and beverages to adjust pH and inhibit microbial growth.
642.benefits: Preservative effect by lowering pH, enhances flavor profile by providing tartness
642.risks: Dental erosion with frequent ingestion, potential to contribute to acid-base imbalance with excessive consumption, possible gastric irritation

sources.label: Dental erosion related to acidic beverages
Use and safety of acidulants in food

643.name: Citicoline
643.description: Citicoline is a naturally occurring compound (CDP-choline) involved in brain metabolism, often used as a supplement to support cognitive function. In the body, it serves as a precursor for the synthesis of phosphatidylcholine, an important component of brain cell membranes, and is thought to support neurotransmitter production and brain health.
643.benefits: May improve cognitive function, supports memory in aging and mild cognitive impairment, may enhance attention, supports brain phospholipid synthesis
643.risks: Mild gastrointestinal upset, headache, insomnia, rarely can cause hypotension

650.name: Nitrate (as NO₃⁻–N)
650.description: An inorganic ion commonly found in soil, water, and certain foods, nitrate is a nutrient for plants and can be ingested through diet or water. It can be converted to nitrite and other nitrogen compounds in the human body.
650.benefits: Dietary nitrate can contribute to nitric oxide production supporting vascular function
650.risks: Potential formation of nitrosamines under acidic conditions, ingestion toxicity at high levels, methemoglobinemia risk in infants, contamination risk in drinking water

sources.label: PMID 23591153 - Dietary nitrate and cardiovascular health
PMID 20298774 - Nitrate and nitrite in drinking water and carcinogenic risk
PMID 17516813 - Nitrate intake and methemoglobinemia

652.name: Calcium lactate
652.description: Calcium lactate is a calcium salt of lactic acid used as a calcium supplement and food additive to provide calcium and improve nutritional content.
652.benefits: Calcium supplementation, supports bone health and muscle function
652.risks: Minor gastrointestinal discomfort at very high doses

sources.label: Calcium supplementation and health effects
