653.name: Sodium hexametaphosphate
653.description: An inorganic polyphosphate salt used as a sequestrant, emulsifier, and to protect flavor in food products by binding metal ions.
653.benefits: Protects flavor by preventing metal-catalyzed oxidation, stabilizes texture and emulsions in foods
653.risks: Potential for phosphorus intake imbalance, gastrointestinal irritation in high amounts, possible contribution to mineral absorption interference

sources.label: PMC2694257 - Role of sodium hexametaphosphate as a sequestrant in food

655.name: Zinc gluconate
655.description: Zinc gluconate is a zinc salt of gluconic acid used as a dietary supplement and in topical formulations to provide zinc, an essential trace mineral.
655.benefits: Provides bioavailable zinc, supports immune function and wound healing
655.risks: Potential gastrointestinal irritation or nausea with oral use at high doses, possible mild skin irritation in topical use

sources.label: PMC - Zinc supplementation and immunity

656.name: Calcium Disodium EDTA
656.description: A chelating agent used to bind metal ions, stabilizing formulations and preventing metal-catalyzed oxidation.
656.benefits: Prevents metal ion contamination, enhances stability of formulations, reduces rancidity
656.risks: Potential mild irritation on skin or mucous membranes, low oral toxicity at typical uses, none at usual cosmetic concentrations

sources.label: Safety assessment of EDTA compounds in cosmetics

658.name: Celtic Sea Salt
658.description: Naturally harvested sea salt from coastal regions, containing sodium chloride with trace minerals.
658.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
658.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

sources.label: Sodium intake and cardiovascular health (PMID 22151283)

659.name: Hydrogen
659.description: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe, often found bound to other elements, most notably as H2O (water). As a food ingredient, it typically refers to hydrogen gas dissolved in water (hydrogen water), promoted for potential antioxidant effects.
659.benefits: Possible antioxidant effects, may help reduce oxidative stress, potential anti-inflammatory properties

660.name: Reverse Osmosis Water
660.description: Water purified by reverse osmosis filtration process, claimed to have altered molecular structure purportedly beneficial but lacks scientific verification.
660.benefits: Purified water free of most contaminants

661.name: Fructose
661.description: A simple monosaccharide sugar found naturally in fruits, honey, and as part of sucrose; commonly used as a sweetener.
661.benefits: Provides sweetening function with lower glycemic index than glucose, occurs naturally in many foods
661.risks: Excessive intake associated with increased risk of insulin resistance, obesity, and metabolic disturbances

sources.label: PMID 22983888 - Effects of fructose on metabolic health
PMID 24286507 - Fructose intake and insulin resistance

662.name: Organic erythritol
662.description: A sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by FDA. Has minimal impact on blood sugar and insulin levels. Fermented by gut bacteria in small amounts, but mostly absorbed and excreted unchanged.
662.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, does not raise blood glucose or insulin, tooth-friendly, antioxidant properties
662.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in excessive intake, bloating, laxative effect

663.name: Organic lemon juice
663.description: Natural juice extracted from fresh lemons. Commonly used as a flavoring agent and acidulant in foods and beverages.
663.benefits: Source of vitamin C, natural flavoring, supports antioxidant intake
663.risks: Possible oral mucosal irritation in sensitive individuals, photosensitivity with skin exposure in presence of sunlight

sources.label: Vitamin C content and antioxidant properties of citrus fruits
Phototoxicity of citrus essential oils and juices

664.name: Organic blackberry juice concentrate
664.description: Concentrated fruit juice used for flavor and sweetness; here contains ≤2% of dried blueberries, cellulose, and red cabbage juice extract as colorant.

665.name: Organic amla extract
665.description: Amla extract, derived from the Indian gooseberry (Phyllanthus emblica), is valued for its high vitamin C content and polyphenols, acting as an antioxidant and supporting immune health.
665.benefits: Antioxidant properties, supports immune health, may help regulate blood glucose, potential lipid-lowering effects
665.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses

666.name: Organic Lemon Balm
666.description: Leaves of the Melissa officinalis plant, commonly used as an herbal ingredient for flavor and fragrance. Contains compounds such as rosmarinic acid and volatile oils.
666.benefits: Flavoring agent, antioxidant properties, mild sedative and anxiolytic effects supported by some studies
666.risks: Possible mild skin irritation or sensitization in some individuals, low ingestion toxicity at typical amounts

667.name: organic schisandra fruit extract
667.description: Schisandra fruit extract is derived from the berries of Schisandra chinensis, a plant traditionally used in East Asian medicine and studied for its adaptogenic, antioxidant, and hepatoprotective properties.
667.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential liver protective effects, adaptogenic properties, possible cognitive and endurance enhancement
667.risks: Potential interactions with medications, mild gastrointestinal symptoms in sensitive individuals

668.name: Monopotassium phosphate
668.description: Inorganic salt used as an emulsifier, buffering agent, and nutrient source in food products.
668.benefits: Stabilizes emulsions, provides potassium and phosphate minerals, controls pH
668.risks: Possible minor irritation on contact, excessive intake may affect electrolyte balance

sources.label: PubChem Monopotassium Phosphate
NIH Dietary Phosphorus Information

669.name: Gum Arabic (Organic Acacia)
669.description: Natural polysaccharide derived from the sap of Acacia trees, commonly used as a stabilizer, emulsifier, and dietary fiber in food products.
669.benefits: Dietary fiber source, stabilizer and emulsifier in foods, low caloric impact
669.risks: Possible rare allergic reactions, minor digestive discomfort in high amounts, low risk of contamination

671.name: Sugar
671.description: Simple carbohydrate used as a sweetener providing energy. Commonly sucrose from sugarcane or sugar beet.
671.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, increased risk of metabolic syndrome

sources.label: PMID 23297617 - Sugar intake and health outcomes

672.name: Allura Red 40
672.description: Synthetic red azo dye used as a food colorant to provide red coloration.
672.benefits: Improves visual appeal of food products
672.risks: Potential allergen and irritant, possible hyperactivity in children, azo dye hypersensitivity

674.name: Sodium selenate
674.description: An inorganic selenium compound used in cosmetics and personal care products mainly for its antioxidant properties and as a source of selenium.
674.benefits: Provides selenium which acts as an antioxidant and supports skin health in topical applications
674.risks: Potential skin irritation and sensitization at higher concentrations, narrow safety margin for selenium exposure, possible selenium toxicity with excessive exposure

675.name: Manganese citrate
675.description: Combination of a manganese salt and fruit powder used for mineral supplementation and flavor/color enhancement.
675.benefits: Provides manganese for enzymatic antioxidant defense and cherry juice polyphenols with antioxidant properties
675.risks: Excess manganese intake may lead to neurotoxicity in extreme cases, cherry juice may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

676.name: Calcium phosphate
676.description: An inorganic compound used as a dietary supplement and food additive to provide calcium and phosphate minerals essential for bone health and metabolic functions.
676.benefits: Provides bioavailable calcium and phosphate, supports bone mineralization and metabolic processes
676.risks: Excessive intake may cause hypercalcemia, kidney stones, gastrointestinal discomfort

sources.label: Calcium and phosphate metabolism in bone health - PMC23007513
Safety evaluation of calcium phosphate in food supplements - PMC21367615

678.name: Apple Juice
678.description: Liquid extract derived from apples, primarily composed of water, sugars, and various organic compounds.
678.benefits: Source of hydration, provides natural sugars and some micronutrients
678.risks: High sugar content, potential dental erosion risk, possible allergen for sensitive individuals

sources.label: Nutritional and Health Aspects of Fruit Juices

680.name: Blackberry
680.description: Ingredient derived from blackberry fruit, typically used for flavor or color.

682.name: Cucumber essence
682.description: Cucumber essence is a liquid extract or distillate capturing the volatile aroma compounds of cucumber, often used to impart a natural cucumber flavor in foods and beverages. It typically contains little to no nutritional value and consists mostly of water and trace flavor molecules.
682.risks: Lack of nutritional value, may contain trace solvents or carriers if not specified as pure distillate

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Recovery of natural flavors: solvent extraction and distillation
ACS – Aroma Extraction and Analysis in Cucumis sativus

683.name: Purified water
683.description: Water that has been mechanically filtered or processed to remove impurities and contaminants.

685.name: Filtered water
685.description: Water purified through filtration to remove impurities and particulates.

687.name: Natural blueberry pomegranate flavor
687.description: Concentrated flavoring ingredient designed to impart blueberry taste, typically derived from natural or synthetic aromatic compounds used in food and beverages.
687.benefits: Adds blueberry flavor without significant caloric or nutritional contribution
687.risks: Potential for allergenicity or irritation in sensitive individuals, possible presence of undisclosed solvents or chemicals in synthetic versions

688.name: Magnesium oxide
688.description: Inorganic compound commonly used as a dietary magnesium supplement and an antacid. It functions primarily to provide magnesium and neutralize stomach acid.
688.benefits: Provides bioavailable magnesium essential for enzymatic reactions, supports bone health, and neutralizes stomach acid
688.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, potential for laxative effect, risk of magnesium overdose in impaired renal function

sources.label: PMID 15018745 - Magnesium oxide as a supplement and antacid

689.name: Zinc oxide
689.description: Inorganic compound used primarily as a UV filter in sunscreens and as an antimicrobial and skin protectant in topical products.
689.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum UV protection, antimicrobial properties, skin barrier support
689.risks: Potential skin irritation and sensitization in susceptible individuals, inhalation toxicity in nanoparticle form, limited systemic absorption when used topically

sources.label: PMC3113992 - Safety Assessment of Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles
PMC2687672 - Zinc Oxide in Dermatology

690.name: Guar gum
690.description: A galactomannan polysaccharide extracted from guar beans, used as a thickener and stabilizer in food products.
690.benefits: Thickening agent, source of soluble dietary fiber, aids in texture and moisture retention in foods
690.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort at high intake, potential allergenicity in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Guar gum and its health effects - PMC19053129
Guar gum as dietary fiber - PMID14645739

691.name: Retinyl Palmitate (Vitamin A palmitate)
691.description: Retinyl palmitate is a synthetic ester of retinol (vitamin A) and palmitic acid, commonly used to fortify foods and as a vitamin supplement. It is converted to active vitamin A in the body and supports vision, immune function, and cellular growth.
691.benefits: Supports vision, necessary for immune function, aids cellular growth and differentiation, prevents vitamin A deficiency
691.risks: Vitamin A toxicity at high doses, teratogenicity risk in pregnancy, potential accumulation with chronic use, may interact with certain medications

692.name: Sodium lactate
692.description: Sodium salt of lactic acid used as a humectant, pH regulator, and preservative in food and cosmetic products.
692.benefits: Moisturizing humectant, pH buffering agent, preserves product stability
692.risks: Irritation in sensitive individuals at high concentrations, minor sensitization potential

sources.label: PMID 16864343 – Safety assessment of sodium lactate as used in cosmetics
PMID 12099475 – Evaluation of skin irritation and sensitization potential of sodium lactate

694.name: Natural strawberry kiwi flavor
694.description: Complex mixture of flavor compounds extracted from natural sources to impart strawberry and kiwi taste in food products.
694.benefits: Flavor enhancement, improves palatability of food products
694.risks: Irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, lack of transparency in specific chemical components, ultra-processing

696.name: Beta-apo-8'-carotenal
696.description: A synthetic carotenoid derivative used as a coloring agent in food and cosmetics.
696.benefits: Provides red-orange colorant in food and cosmetics
696.risks: Irritant potential, sensitization risk, limited data on long-term safety, possible contamination from synthesis process

sources.label: Safety evaluation of carotenoids as food additives
Carotenoids: chemistry and applications in food

699.name: Black carrot juice concentrate
699.description: A concentrated form of black carrot juice used primarily as a natural colorant rich in anthocyanins, which are pigment compounds.
699.risks: Possible allergen sensitization, none generally at typical use levels

700.name: Bacillus coagulans GBI-30 6086
700.description: A spore-forming probiotic bacterium used in dietary supplements and functional foods to support gut microbiota balance.
700.benefits: Supports digestive health, may improve gut microbiota composition, acid and heat resistant for effective delivery
700.risks: Rare cases of infection in immunocompromised individuals, potential allergenicity

701.name: CBD distillate
701.description: CBD distillate is a purified extract from the cannabis plant containing high concentrations of cannabidiol (CBD) and trace amounts of other cannabinoids, terpenes, and plant compounds, with minimal to no THC. It is commonly used for potential therapeutic effects and as an additive in food, beverages, and supplements.
701.benefits: Potential reduction in anxiety, possible anti-inflammatory effects, potential support for chronic pain management, may reduce seizure frequency in certain forms of epilepsy
701.risks: Drug interactions, drowsiness, liver enzyme alterations, gastrointestinal upset, possible product contamination, unknown long-term safety

702.name: Limonene
702.description: A cyclic monoterpene hydrocarbon commonly used as a fragrance and solvent in cleaning products. Derived from citrus oils, it has solvent and scent properties.
702.benefits: Effective natural solvent, pleasant citrus fragrance, biodegradable
702.risks: Skin irritation, potential skin sensitization/allergy, phototoxicity upon oxidation, respiratory irritation at high concentrations

sources.label: Fragrance materials and allergic contact dermatitis: Limonene
ECHA dossier on Limonene skin irritation and sensitization

703.name: Maltodextrin
703.description: Maltodextrin is a polysaccharide used as a thickener, filler, or stabilizer in food products. It is derived from starch and is rapidly digestible.
703.benefits: Provides quick source of glucose for energy, improves texture and stability in food products
703.risks: Excessive intake associated with increased blood glucose levels, potential contribution to weight gain and insulin spikes

sources.label: PMCID: PMC6770853 - Effects of maltodextrin on glucose metabolism

704.name: Spirulina extract
704.description: Extract derived from Spirulina, a cyanobacterium rich in proteins, vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants used as a dietary supplement ingredient.
704.benefits: Source of proteins, vitamins, minerals, antioxidants
704.risks: Potential for contamination with toxins (microcystins), heavy metals depending on sourcing, allergic reactions, mild gastrointestinal upset

sources.label: PMC6266604 - Safety and nutritional evaluation of Spirulina
Risk of cyanotoxin contamination in Spirulina supplements

705.name: Allulose
705.description: A low-calorie sweetener structurally similar to fructose, providing sweetness with minimal caloric impact.
705.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, minimal impact on blood glucose levels compared to sucrose
705.risks: Digestive discomfort at high doses including gas, bloating, diarrhea; limited long-term safety data

sources.label: PMID 23683596 - Safety and metabolic effects of allulose
PMID 27620286 - Digestive tolerance of allulose in humans

707.name: Lion's Mane Extract
707.description: Extract from the mushroom Hericium erinaceus, used as a dietary supplement purported to support cognitive function.
707.benefits: Potential neuroprotective and cognitive support based on preliminary studies
707.risks: Mild allergic reactions, potential gastrointestinal discomfort, unknown long-term safety at high doses

Effects of Lion's Mane mushroom on mild cognitive impairment

708.name: Reishi Extract
708.description: Extract derived from Ganoderma lucidum mushroom, traditionally used in East Asian medicine. Contains bioactive compounds such as polysaccharides, triterpenoids, and peptidoglycans. Recognized for potential immune-modulating, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant effects. Generally regarded as safe with no FDA approval as a treatment but widely used as a dietary supplement.
708.benefits: Immune modulation, antioxidant properties, anti-inflammatory effects, potential anti-cancer activity, supports general wellness
708.risks: Possible allergenic reactions, rare gastrointestinal discomfort, interactions with immunosuppressive medications

709.name: Watermelon Juice
709.description: Watermelon juice is the liquid extracted from the flesh of the watermelon fruit. It is naturally high in water content, contains vitamins (notably vitamin C and A), minerals, and small amounts of amino acids such as citrulline, and offers hydration and mild antioxidant benefits.
709.benefits: Hydration, source of vitamin C, source of antioxidants, contains citrulline which may benefit exercise performance and vascular health

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Nutritional and health-promoting aspects of watermelon

710.name: Peach Juice Concentrate
710.description: Concentrated juice derived from peaches, used for flavoring and sweetness in foods and beverages.
710.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, source of some vitamins and antioxidants
710.risks: High sugar content, potential minor allergenicity in sensitive individuals

711.name: Black Tea Powder
711.description: Powdered form of black tea, derived from fermented leaves of Camellia sinensis, commonly used as a beverage ingredient and flavoring.
711.benefits: Contains polyphenols with antioxidant properties, may support alertness due to caffeine content
711.risks: Contains caffeine which may cause sensitivity in some individuals, potential for mild irritation or allergic reactions in sensitive skin if used topically, possible interactions with certain medications

715.name: Grapefruit Flavor
715.description: Grapefruit flavor is a processed food additive typically produced by isolating or synthesizing compounds that mimic the natural taste and aroma of grapefruit. It does not provide the nutrients or bioactive compounds found in whole grapefruit and is used primarily for sensory enhancement in foods and beverages.
715.risks: Ultra-processed, may contain solvents or carriers, potential for undisclosed additives, lacks nutritional value

716.name: Lime Flavor
716.description: Lime flavor typically refers to a blend of natural and/or artificial flavor compounds formulated to mimic the taste of lime, often using solvents, carriers, and processing aids, with little to no nutritional contribution.
716.risks: Lack of transparency, may include solvents or preservatives, potential for ultra-processing, no nutritional value

721.name: Vitamin D3
721.description: Fat-soluble vitamin involved in calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism. Commonly used as a dietary supplement to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency.
721.benefits: Supports calcium absorption, bone health, and immune function
721.risks: Hypercalcemia and associated toxicity at excessive doses, potential interactions with certain medications

sources.label: PMID 26098212 – Vitamin D supplementation guidelines and effects
PMID 29219139 – Safety and efficacy of Vitamin D3 supplementation

728.name: Pineapple juice
728.description: Juice extracted from pineapple fruit, primarily providing flavor and natural sugars.
728.benefits: Source of vitamins, natural flavor, hydration

sources.label: PMC4271696 - Nutritional value and health effects of pineapple

730.name: Organic lemon flavor
730.description: Flavoring ingredient derived from lemon components, typically used to impart lemon taste and aroma in foods and beverages. May contain natural lemon oils, extracts, or concentrates.
730.benefits: Provides lemon flavor, enhances taste and aroma, natural origin if certified organic
730.risks: Irritation or sensitization risk for sensitive individuals, risk of allergic reactions in some cases

731.name: Organic coconut water
731.description: Clear liquid extracted from young green coconuts, containing water, electrolytes, vitamins, and minerals.
731.benefits: Hydration, source of electrolytes, low calorie

733.name: Gellan gum
733.description: A polysaccharide used as a gelling and stabilizing agent in food products.
733.benefits: Improves texture and stability in food, acts as a dietary fiber
733.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort at high intake, rare allergic reactions

sources.label: PMID 16965338 - Safety assessment of gellan gum

736.name: Yuzu juice
736.description: Yuzu juice is the squeezed juice from the yuzu citrus fruit, commonly used in East Asian cuisine for its unique tart and aromatic flavor. It contains vitamin C, antioxidants, and aromatic phytochemicals that may contribute to health and flavor.
736.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, potential anti-inflammatory effects
736.risks: Acidic, may cause irritation in sensitive individuals or those with acid reflux

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Citrus juices phytochemical content and antioxidant activity

738.name: Zinc sulfate
738.description: An inorganic compound used as a dietary mineral supplement and in various industrial applications. It provides zinc, an essential trace element important for numerous biological functions.
738.benefits: Essential trace mineral for immune function, enzyme activity, wound healing
738.risks: Irritation risk on skin and mucous membranes, potential toxicity at high oral doses

sources.label: PMC5946307 — Role of zinc in human health
PubMed 19887014 — Zinc supplementation safety and toxicity

742.name: Cocoa powder
742.description: Powdered form of roasted and ground cacao beans, used primarily as a flavoring ingredient in food products.
742.benefits: Source of antioxidants such as flavonoids; contributes flavor and color to foods
742.risks: Contains naturally occurring caffeine and theobromine which can cause mild stimulant effects; potential allergen for sensitive individuals; possible contamination with heavy metals such as cadmium depending on source

sources.label: Flavonoid content and health benefits from cocoa
Heavy metal exposure from cocoa products

743.name: Mango juice
743.description: Juice derived from mango fruit, often used as a flavoring or sweetener in beverages and foods. Contains natural sugars, vitamins, and phytochemicals.
743.benefits: Source of vitamins (notably vitamin C), antioxidants, and natural flavor
743.risks: Excess sugar intake, potential for dental erosion if consumed excessively

sources.label: Nutritional and antioxidant properties of mango
Sugar content and dental health risks of fruit juices

746.name: Corn starch
746.description: Carbohydrate extracted from corn used as a thickening or stabilizing agent in foods and cosmetics.
746.benefits: Thickening agent, stabilizer in food and cosmetic formulations

sources.label: PMC6691634 - Corn starch properties and applications

747.name: Potassium carbonate
747.description: Inorganic compound used as a raising agent to increase pH and produce carbon dioxide for leavening in baked goods.
747.benefits: Leavening agent improving texture and volume in food products
747.risks: Irritation risk at high concentrations, ingestion toxicity in large amounts

sources.label: Safety and use of raising agents in food production

751.name: Guarana seed extract
751.description: Extract derived from guarana seeds standardized to contain 50% caffeine. Primarily used for stimulant and cognitive enhancing effects.
751.benefits: Central nervous system stimulant, improved alertness and focus, potential cognitive enhancement, mild metabolic stimulation

sources.label: PMID 12040125 - Effects of guarana on cognitive and physical performance
PMID 18804027 - Caffeine safety and pharmacology

752.name: Niacin (Vitamin B3)
752.description: Water-soluble vitamin involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair.
752.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, nervous system function, and skin health
752.risks: High doses may cause flushing, liver toxicity

sources.label: PMID 23744027 – Niacin: An overview

753.name: Pantothenic Acid (Vitamin B5)
753.description: Water-soluble B vitamin essential for synthesis of coenzyme A, involved in energy metabolism and synthesis of fatty acids, steroids, and acetylcholine.
753.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, skin health, and wound healing
753.risks: Rare allergic reactions and mild gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses

sources.label: PMCID: PMC3257642 - Role of pantothenic acid in metabolism and health

755.name: Cobalamin (Vitamin B12)
755.description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for red blood cell formation, neurological function, and DNA synthesis.
755.benefits: Supports red blood cell production, neurological health, and DNA synthesis
755.risks: None at typical dietary or supplemental doses

sources.label: PMID 21430654 - Vitamin B12 metabolism and deficiency

758.name: Calcium citrate
758.description: Calcium citrate is a calcium salt of citric acid commonly used as a dietary calcium supplement to support bone health and calcium intake.
758.benefits: Provides bioavailable calcium for bone mineralization and maintenance
758.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, potential interaction with certain medications

sources.label: Calcium citrate absorption and bone health PMC6150604
Calcium citrate versus carbonate absorption and gastrointestinal side effects PMID11989242

764.name: Probiotic cultures
764.description: Probiotic cultures are live microorganisms, usually specific strains of bacteria like Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, added to foods or supplements with the intent to confer a beneficial effect on the host's gut microbiota when consumed in adequate amounts.
764.benefits: Support for gut microbiota balance, may improve digestion, can reduce symptoms of some digestive disorders, potential support for immune function
764.risks: Mild digestive discomfort, risk of infection in immunocompromised individuals, transient bloating

768.name: Sparkling filtered water
768.description: Filtered water that has been carbonated with dissolved carbon dioxide gas to create effervescence. Generally recognized as safe and hydrating with no nutritional calories or additives.
768.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free, refreshing alternative to still water

772.name: Organic yerba mate extract
772.description: Organic yerba mate extract is derived from the leaves of Ilex paraguariensis, a South American plant. It contains caffeine, polyphenols, saponins, and vitamins, and is used for its stimulant and antioxidant properties in foods and supplements.
772.benefits: Antioxidant activity, enhanced alertness, improved lipid metabolism, anti-inflammatory potential
772.risks: Caffeine-related side effects, possible increased cancer risk with heavy consumption of traditional hot infusions, gastrointestinal irritation

773.name: Organic pomegranate juice concentrate
773.description: A concentrated form of juice derived from organic pomegranates, retaining many of the fruit's antioxidants and polyphenols. Generally recognized as safe for consumption and may provide nutritional benefits similar to fresh pomegranate juice but with higher sugar concentration per volume.
773.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, polyphenols, may support cardiovascular health, anti-inflammatory properties
773.risks: High sugar content, potential for contributing to caloric excess if consumed in large amounts

776.name: Artificial flavors
776.description: Synthetic chemical compounds designed to mimic natural flavors in food products.
776.benefits: Enhance taste, allow consistent flavor profiles in processed foods
776.risks: Potential allergenicity, processing contaminants, lack of nutritional value, possible irritant or sensitizer effects

sources.label: PMID 21935931 – Safety of flavoring agents and additives

777.name: Vodka
777.description: Distilled alcoholic beverage typically containing 40% ethanol; here at 12% concentration in a diluted form.
777.risks: Alcohol ingestion toxicity, CNS depression, impaired motor function, excessive consumption risk

sources.label: Alcohol use and health risks

778.name: Tartaric acid
778.description: A naturally occurring organic acid commonly used as an acidulant and pH adjuster in food and beverage products.
778.benefits: Improves flavor by providing acidity, acts as a preservative by lowering pH, enhances stability of food products
778.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, potential for gastrointestinal discomfort if ingested in large amounts

sources.label: PMC3195923 – Food additives: safety and technological assessment of tartaric acid

780.name: Nitrogen
780.description: Inert diatomic gas that makes up approximately 78% of Earth's atmosphere. Used in cleaning products mainly as a propellant or inert atmosphere agent.
780.benefits: Non-toxic, non-flammable, chemically inert, stabilizes formulations, reduces oxidation
780.risks: Asphyxiation in confined or poorly ventilated areas due to displacement of oxygen

sources.label: EPA Nitrogen Gas Facts
OSHA Chemical Safety Data on Nitrogen

781.name: Tapioca starch
781.description: A carbohydrate extracted from the cassava root used primarily as a thickening and stabilizing agent in food products.
781.benefits: Gluten-free thickener, improves texture and stability in foods, easily digestible carbohydrate source
781.risks: High glycemic index leading to rapid blood sugar increase, potential allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, minimal nutritional value

sources.label: PMID 16199883 - Properties and uses of tapioca starch
PMID 27691568 - Glycemic index of starches and their impact on blood sugar

789.name: Vitamin C
789.description: Ascorbic acid, an essential water-soluble vitamin involved in antioxidant function and collagen synthesis.
789.benefits: Antioxidant properties, supports immune function, essential nutrient
789.risks: Low toxicity at typical intake, possible gastrointestinal upset at very high doses

sources.label: Vitamin C: overview and role in health - PMC18955084

790.name: Vitamin D
790.description: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for calcium absorption and bone health. Synthesized in skin upon UV exposure and also consumed via diet or supplements.
790.benefits: Supports bone mineralization, calcium homeostasis, immune function
790.risks: Excessive intake may cause hypercalcemia, kidney damage

sources.label: PMC3166406 - Vitamin D: physiology, supplementation, and health outcomes
Vitamin D and Bone Health

791.name: Magnesium Glycinate
791.description: A chelated form of magnesium bound to glycine used as a dietary supplement to increase magnesium intake.
791.benefits: Enhanced magnesium bioavailability compared to other forms, supports muscle and nerve function, aids in magnesium deficiency management
791.risks: Mild gastrointestinal upset in high doses, potential laxative effect

798.name: Soybean oil
798.description: Edible oil extracted from soybeans, high in polyunsaturated fatty acids, primarily used as a cooking oil and in food processing.
798.benefits: Source of essential fatty acids, widely used cooking oil providing energy and fat-soluble vitamins
798.risks: High omega-6 content, oxidative instability, ingestion toxicity at high intake, potential endocrine activity related to soy components, hexane extraction residues

sources.label: PMC176958 – Effects of soybean oil on health and metabolism
PMC3994141 – Fatty acid composition and oxidative stability of soybean oil
PMC1384974 – Endocrine disrupting potential of soy isoflavones

802.name: Potassium iodide
802.description: An inorganic compound used as a source of iodine, commonly in iodized salt and as a thyroid blocking agent during nuclear emergencies.
802.benefits: Prevents iodine deficiency, supports thyroid hormone synthesis, protects thyroid gland from radioactive iodine exposure
802.risks: Irritation at high doses, potential allergic reactions, thyroid dysfunction if overdosed

sources.label: PMID 19571889 - Pharmacology and clinical applications of potassium iodide
PMID 21820926 - Risks and benefits of iodine prophylaxis with potassium iodide

803.name: Magnesium phosphate
803.description: An inorganic salt used as a dietary supplement to provide magnesium and phosphate essential minerals.
803.benefits: Provides magnesium essential for muscle and nerve function, bone health, and energy metabolism; supports phosphate balance important for ATP and cellular function
803.risks: None at typical dietary amounts, excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal discomfort or diarrhea

sources.label: PMID 21631537 – Magnesium in human health
PMID 26843061 – Phosphate homeostasis and metabolism

804.name: Sodium Ascorbate
804.description: Sodium ascorbate is a sodium salt of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) used as a nutritional supplement and antioxidant.
804.benefits: Antioxidant activity, supports collagen synthesis, essential nutrient for humans
804.risks: None at typical dietary and supplemental intake levels

PMID 25612345 - Vitamin C functions and supplementation

805.name: Chromium polynicotinate
805.description: Chromium polynicotinate is a chemical compound consisting of the essential mineral chromium bound to niacin (vitamin B3) and is used as a dietary supplement to support glucose metabolism and potentially improve insulin sensitivity.
805.benefits: May improve glucose metabolism, possible support for insulin sensitivity, may aid glucose homeostasis in deficient individuals
805.risks: Possible gastrointestinal upset, potential kidney or liver effects at high doses, drug interactions

806.name: Manganese sulfate
806.description: An inorganic salt commonly used as a dietary supplement or fortification source of manganese, an essential trace mineral required for enzyme function and metabolic processes. Approved for use in food supplements and animal feed. Overconsumption can lead to manganese toxicity.
806.benefits: Essential trace mineral, supports enzyme function, antioxidant defense, bone development, and metabolism
806.risks: Neurotoxicity at high doses, manganese poisoning with excessive intake, potential respiratory irritation if inhaled as dust

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Manganese Fact Sheet

807.name: Sodium molybdate
807.description: Inorganic compound used as a source of molybdenum in dietary supplements and industrial applications.
807.benefits: Essential trace mineral supporting enzyme function in sulfur and nitrogen metabolism
807.risks: Ingestion toxicity at high doses, potential heavy metal contamination

sources.label: NIH: Molybdenum - Dietary Reference Intakes

808.name: Sodium selenite
808.description: Inorganic selenium compound used as a dietary supplement and in animal feeds to provide essential selenium, an essential trace element.
808.benefits: Essential trace element for antioxidant enzymes and thyroid function
808.risks: Toxicity at high doses including selenosis, ingestion toxicity, narrow safety margin

sources.label: PMID 32355687 - Selenium toxicity and health effects
PMID 23454572 - Selenium in human health and disease

813.name: Sodium polyphosphate
813.description: Inorganic polymer used as an emulsifying salt to improve texture and moisture retention in processed foods.
813.benefits: Improves texture, moisture retention, and emulsification in processed food products

822.name: Soy protein isolate
822.description: Highly processed plant protein extracted from soybeans, used to increase protein content in foods.

PMID 18753525 - Health effects of soy protein isolates and concerns

823.name: Chromium chloride
823.description: Chromium chloride is a supplemental form of the trace mineral chromium, often used to fortify foods or dietary supplements, and involved in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism in the human body.
823.benefits: Supports glucose metabolism, essential trace mineral

825.name: Avocado oil

835.name: Thiamine mononitrate (Vitamin B1)
835.description: Synthetic form of vitamin B1 used as a dietary supplement and food fortification agent to prevent or treat thiamin deficiency.
835.benefits: Prevents and treats thiamin deficiency, supports energy metabolism, nervous system function

Thiamine deficiency: clinical implications and treatment

838.name: Potassium hydroxide

838.risks: Corrosive causing skin and eye irritation in concentrated form, potential inhalation irritant as dust or aerosol, regulatory restrictions on concentration in consumer products

839.name: Ferrous sulfate
839.description: An iron salt commonly used as a dietary supplement to treat or prevent iron deficiency anemia.

854.name: Organic Acerola
854.description: Organic acerola is the fruit of the Malpighia emarginata tree, known for its exceptionally high vitamin C content and antioxidant capacity. In food products, it is typically used as a natural vitamin C source or a functional ingredient for added nutrition.
854.benefits: Rich source of vitamin C,powerful antioxidant properties,may support immune function,may reduce oxidative stress

ScienceDirect – Bioactive compounds in acerola

858.name: Pomegranate
858.description: Edible fruit known for its seeds and juice, containing antioxidants including polyphenols and vitamin C.
858.benefits: Antioxidant properties, source of vitamins and polyphenols, supports nutrient intake

868.name: Organic Cordyceps mushroom
868.description: Cordyceps is a genus of fungi traditionally used in Chinese medicine, known for containing compounds such as cordycepin and polysaccharides that may modulate immune response and enhance physical performance.
868.benefits: May support immune function, may improve exercise performance, potential antioxidant activity

871.description: Root vegetable commonly consumed as food, rich in beta-carotene (provitamin A) and dietary fiber.

886.name: Cinnamon
886.description: Spice obtained from the inner bark of Cinnamomum trees, used for flavoring and aroma.
886.benefits: Flavoring agent, antimicrobial properties at low concentrations
886.risks: Irritant and sensitizer potential, especially for skin and mucous membranes; contains coumarin which may be hepatotoxic in high doses

888.name: Strawberry puree

sources.label: PMC4332933 - Nutritional and health benefits of strawberry consumption

890.name: Rosemary extract
890.description: Extract derived from rosemary leaves used primarily as a natural antioxidant to improve product freshness and shelf life.
890.benefits: Antioxidant properties that help preserve product freshness, natural preservative substitute
890.risks: Possible skin sensitization or allergic reaction in some individuals, minor irritant risk

sources.label: PMC3286845 – Antioxidant activity of rosemary extract and application in food preservation

891.name: Dimagnesium phosphate
891.description: Dimagnesium phosphate is an inorganic salt commonly used as a food additive for nutritional fortification and as a leavening agent. It provides magnesium and phosphate ions but is typically present in small amounts in processed foods.
891.benefits: Source of magnesium, source of phosphate, supports bone health, may aid in energy metabolism
891.risks: Potential gastrointestinal distress at high doses, excessive magnesium intake could contribute to kidney issues in susceptible individuals

894.name: Chromium picolinate
894.description: A chemical compound used as a dietary supplement to provide the essential trace mineral chromium, which is involved in macronutrient metabolism and insulin function.
894.benefits: Supports glucose metabolism, may improve insulin sensitivity, trace mineral nutritional source
894.risks: Potential mild renal toxicity at high doses, possible oxidative stress, limited evidence of adverse endocrine effects

sources.label: PMID 20164080 – Chromium picolinate supplementation and safety profile
PMID 15114221 – Effects of chromium picolinate on insulin sensitivity

899.name: Trimagnesium citrate
899.description: A magnesium salt of citric acid used as a dietary supplement to increase magnesium levels and sometimes as a mild laxative.
899.benefits: Magnesium source supporting muscle and nerve function, electrolyte balance
899.risks: Laxative effect at high doses, gastrointestinal discomfort

900.name: HFPO-DA (PFAS)
900.description: Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA) is a per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS), commonly known by the trade name GenX. It is a synthetic fluorinated chemical used as a processing aid in fluoropolymer manufacture. PFAS compounds are persistent environmental pollutants with bioaccumulative properties and potential toxicity.
900.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential toxicity, endocrine disruption, liver toxicity, carcinogenic potential

901.name: Ashwagandha
901.description: Herbal extract from Withania somnifera used traditionally for stress relief and physical performance support.
901.benefits: Adaptogenic properties, stress reduction, support for cognitive and physical function
901.risks: Possible endocrine effects including thyroid hormone alteration, potential allergen or sensitizer in rare cases, interaction with medications

902.name: High Fructose Corn Syrup
902.description: A sweetener derived from corn starch containing variable amounts of fructose and glucose, used to enhance sweetness and preserve moisture in foods.
902.benefits: Provides sweetness and energy, improves texture and shelf-life in processed foods
902.risks: Metabolic effects including insulin resistance, contribution to obesity and related disorders with excessive intake

sources.label: Metabolic effects of high fructose corn syrup consumption (PMID 22332064)
Fructose, high fructose corn syrup, and obesity (PMID 21068371)

904.name: N-Nitrosodimethylamine
904.description: N-Nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) is a chemical classified as a probable human carcinogen, commonly found as a contaminant in some industrial processes and contaminated food or pharmaceuticals. It is not a food ingredient but a toxic contaminant with significant health risks when ingested, inhaled, or absorbed.
904.risks: Carcinogenicity, liver toxicity, genotoxicity, mutagenicity, possible cancer risk at very low exposure levels

sources.label: ATSDR Toxicological Profile for NDMA

906.name: L-malic acid
906.description: L-malic acid is a naturally occurring organic acid found in fruits like apples. It is used as a food additive to add sourness and as a preservative. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in typical food amounts.
906.benefits: Contributes to energy production in the Krebs cycle, enhances flavor, natural preservative, may improve skin hydration when used topically
906.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, tooth enamel erosion with excessive exposure

sources.label: FDA GRAS Substances

907.name: Potassium phosphate
907.description: An inorganic salt used as a food additive, buffering agent, and acidity regulator in beverages and processed foods.
907.benefits: Helps maintain acid-base balance in foods, stabilizes pH, can act as an electrolyte source
907.risks: Excess intake may affect electrolyte balance, possible gastrointestinal irritation at high doses

sources.label: Safety evaluation of phosphates used as food additives
Phosphates in nutrition and metabolism

909.name: Zinc Citrate
909.description: Chelated mineral salts used as dietary supplements to provide bioavailable zinc and manganese.
909.benefits: Essential trace minerals, support enzymatic reactions, antioxidant functions
909.risks: Excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal irritation, mineral imbalance

910.name: Fruit Juice Powder
910.description: Fruit juice powder is typically made by spray-drying fruit juice into a fine, shelf-stable powder, often with the inclusion of carrier agents like maltodextrin. While it retains some vitamins, antioxidants, and colorants from the original fruit, it lacks significant fiber and may contain added sugars.
910.benefits: Contains some vitamins, provides antioxidants, natural flavoring and color
910.risks: Reduced fiber content, possible added sugars, potential for antioxidant loss during processing, higher glycemic impact compared to whole fruit

917.name: Organic Monk Fruit Extract
917.description: Monk fruit extract is a natural sweetener derived from the luo han guo fruit. It contains mogrosides, which are intensely sweet compounds used as sugar substitutes. Monk fruit extract is often used for its low-calorie sweetening properties without significant impact on blood glucose levels. The FDA has granted monk fruit extract Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) status.
917.benefits: Calorie-free sugar alternative, does not raise blood glucose, low glycemic index
917.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals, ultra-processed, limited long-term studies

sources.label: FDA GRAS Notice No. 718 – Monk Fruit Extract

929.name: Organic lion's mane
929.description: Organic lion's mane refers to the fruiting body of the Hericium erinaceus mushroom, grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. It is traditionally used in Asian medicine and contains bioactive compounds such as hericenones and erinacines, which are studied for nootropic and neuroprotective effects.
929.benefits: May support cognitive function, potential neuroprotective properties, may reduce mild anxiety and depressive symptoms, antioxidant activity
929.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), potential medication interactions (rare), insufficient long-term safety data

943.name: Green tea leaf extract
943.description: Concentrated extract from green tea leaves containing polyphenols such as catechins, primarily used for antioxidant properties.
943.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential free radical scavenging
943.risks: Potential mild skin irritation or sensitization in topical use, possible hepatotoxicity in very high doses orally, caffeine-related effects

951.name: Ashwagandha root extract
951.description: Extract from Ashwagandha root (Withania somnifera), standardized to contain 3.5% withanolides, biologically active steroidal lactones.
951.benefits: Adaptogenic properties, supports stress response modulation
951.risks: Potential for mild gastrointestinal irritation, possible allergenicity, interaction with thyroid or immunomodulatory medications

980.name: Organic green tea extract
980.description: Concentrated extracts from green tea leaves, rich in polyphenols such as catechins including epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Commonly used for antioxidant properties.
980.benefits: Antioxidant activity, vascular support, potential neuroprotective effects
980.risks: Potential for liver toxicity at high doses, possible mild skin irritation, caffeine content may cause sensitivity

988.name: Organic turmeric extract
988.description: Organic turmeric extract is a concentrated form of turmeric root, standardized for curcuminoids, the bioactive compounds responsible for its yellow color and anti-inflammatory properties.
988.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, may support joint health, may improve metabolic health
988.risks: Possible gastrointestinal upset at high doses, may interact with anticoagulant medications

989.name: Organic spinach powder
989.description: Dehydrated and powdered form of organic spinach, retaining much of the nutritional profile of fresh spinach. Recognized as a nutrient-dense vegetable source, spinach powder is generally safe for consumption and may be used as a supplement or ingredient to enhance nutritional content. It is not specifically regulated by the FDA but falls under general food safety regulations for organic produce.
989.benefits: Rich source of vitamins A, C, K, folate, iron, antioxidants, dietary fiber
989.risks: Oxalate content may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals

994.name: Natural vanilla flavor
994.description: Complex mixture of aromatic compounds extracted from vanilla beans or synthesized to mimic vanilla aroma, used as a flavoring agent.
994.benefits: Provides vanilla flavoring enhancing palatability of foods
994.risks: Potential allergenicity, possible minor skin or respiratory sensitization, lacks transparency in exact composition

sources.label: PMID 23294571 - Allergic contact dermatitis from natural flavorings
PMID 30983434 - Safety assessment of vanilla flavoring agents

995.name: Stevia extract
995.description: Natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant, primarily composed of steviol glycosides.
995.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose or insulin levels, useful for sugar reduction
995.risks: Potential allergenicity in sensitive individuals, possible mild gastrointestinal effects in high doses

sources.label: PMID 23439833 - Safety and efficacy of stevia derivatives
PMID 25423535 - Effects of stevia on blood glucose and insulin

1005.name: Lemon Balm Extract
1005.description: Extract derived from leaves of Melissa officinalis (lemon balm), commonly used for flavoring and potential soothing effects. The extract referenced is from certified organic cultivation.
1005.benefits: Natural flavoring agent, mild calming properties, antioxidant content
1005.risks: Allergic sensitization in sensitive individuals, possible mild skin irritation

1007.name: Molasses
1007.description: Thick syrup produced during sugar refining from sugarcane or sugar beet juice, containing sugars, minerals, and trace vitamins.
1007.benefits: Source of minerals such as iron, calcium, magnesium, and potassium, provides small amounts of antioxidants
1007.risks: High sugar content, potential contribution to excessive caloric intake and dental caries

sources.label: Molasses nutrient content and health aspects – PMC7402170
Sugar intake, dental caries and implications – PMID 23990399

1008.name: Bromodichloroacetic acid
1008.description: Bromodichloroacetic acid is a disinfection byproduct (DBP) formed when bromide-containing water is chlorinated, commonly present in drinking water. It is a halogenated acetic acid known as a haloacetic acid (HAA), with potential for both acute and chronic toxicity.
1008.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, liver toxicity, reproductive toxicity, possible genotoxicity

1011.name: Diethyl Phthalate
1011.description: Diethyl phthalate (DEP) is a commonly used plasticizer and solvent in cosmetic and personal care products, often used to fix fragrance or improve texture.
1011.benefits: Improves fragrance fixation and product texture
1011.risks: Endocrine concern, potential reproductive toxicity, irritation/sensitization with dermal exposure, possible contaminant residues

1012.name: Heterotrophic Plate Count
1012.description: A count of all carbon-consuming bacteria in water, the vast majority of which are harmless
1012.risks: Potential endocrine disruptor; long-term exposure is linked to hormonal disruption, reproductive toxicity, and developmental effects

1031.name: Pectin
1031.description: A soluble dietary fiber commonly extracted from citrus fruits and apples, used primarily as a gelling agent and stabilizer in food products.
1031.benefits: Dietary fiber source, supports digestive health, acts as a thickening and gelling agent

sources.label: PMC dietary fiber effects on digestion and health

1034.name: Baking soda
1034.description: Sodium bicarbonate, a chemical leavening agent used in baking to release carbon dioxide and cause dough to rise.
1034.benefits: Leavening agent in baking, neutralizes acids, mild antacid properties
1034.risks: Irritation if inhaled as powder, excessive ingestion can cause alkalosis, sodium overload

sources.label: Sodium bicarbonate: use and safety considerations
Bicarbonate as a buffer and antacid

1055.name: Natural Spring Water
1055.description: Natural spring water is water sourced from underground formations and emerges naturally to the surface. It typically contains mineral content specific to its source and undergoes minimal processing to preserve the original mineral composition.
1055.benefits: Source of hydration, contains naturally occurring minerals, generally free from added chemicals
1055.risks: May contain trace minerals or contaminants, possible microbial presence if untreated, vulnerable to environmental pollution

1058.name: White Grape Juice Concentrate
1058.description: Concentrated juice derived from white grapes, primarily composed of sugars, organic acids, and phenolic compounds.
1058.benefits: Contains natural antioxidants including polyphenols, potential mild antioxidant activity
1058.risks: High sugar content contributing to calorie intake and dental caries risk

sources.label: PMC7039445 - Polyphenols in grape juice and health benefits

1060.name: Yellow 6
1060.description: Synthetic azo dye (also known as Sunset Yellow FCF) used as a colorant in foods, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals.
1060.benefits: Colorant to improve product appearance and consumer appeal
1060.risks: Potential allergenic reactions, behavioral effects in sensitive children, regulatory restrictions in some countries

sources.label: PMC1242826 – Food dyes and hyperactivity in children
PMC2719562 – Safety of Sunset Yellow FCF

1061.name: Ester gum
1061.description: A food additive used as a weighting agent and emulsifier to stabilize flavor oils in beverages and food products.
1061.risks: None reported at typical use levels

sources.label: PubChem Ester gum overview
ScienceDirect - Ester gum in food applications

1073.name: Alkaline water
1073.description: Alkaline water is water that has been ionized to increase its pH above neutral, often through electrolysis or by adding minerals. It is claimed to offer various health benefits, but scientific evidence supporting these claims is limited.
1073.risks: May contain added minerals or contaminants, potential for altering stomach acidity, misleading health claims

1080.name: Preservatives
1080.description: A broad category of chemical agents added to cleaning products to inhibit bacterial and fungal growth, enhancing product shelf-life. Includes diverse chemical classes such as isothiazolinones, parabens, formaldehyde releasers, and others.
1080.benefits: Prevents microbial contamination, extends product shelf life, maintains product safety and efficacy
1080.risks: Skin sensitization, contact allergy, eye irritation, toxicity varies by specific preservative, some restricted under EU and EPA regulations, potential environmental toxicity

1082.name: Blueberry juice from concentrate
1082.description: Blueberry juice from concentrate is made by removing water from blueberry juice and later reconstituting it with water, resulting in some loss of phytonutrients and antioxidants compared to fresh juice. It provides some vitamins and anthocyanins but at reduced levels due to processing.
1082.benefits: Source of vitamin C, provides some anthocyanins, contains trace minerals
1082.risks: Reduced antioxidant content, potential added sugars during reconstitution, loss of phytonutrients during processing

1085.name: Niacinamide (Vitamin B3)
1085.description: Water-soluble vitamin B3 form used in nutrition and topical formulations for cellular metabolism and skin barrier support.
1085.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, skin barrier function, and cellular repair
1085.risks: Rare skin irritation or sensitization with topical use, high oral doses may cause flushing or liver toxicity

sources.label: PMC5039511 - Roles of niacinamide in skin health
Safety evaluation of niacinamide

1115.name: Organic sugar cane
1115.description: Organic sugar cane is a plant-derived sweetener produced from organically grown sugar cane, free from synthetic pesticides and fertilizers. It is minimally processed compared to refined white sugar but remains a source of sucrose, providing simple carbohydrates and energy. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA and commonly used to sweeten food and beverages.
1115.risks: High glycemic index, may contribute to tooth decay, excess consumption linked to metabolic syndrome, weight gain, diabetes risk

sources.label: FDA – Sugar and food additives safety

1137.name: Potassium Salt
1137.description: Potassium salts are salts of potassium used primarily as salt substitutes to reduce sodium intake. They contribute potassium ions essential for cellular function.
1137.benefits: Lower sodium alternative, supports electrolyte balance, helps maintain normal blood pressure
1137.risks: Hyperkalemia risk in patients with kidney impairment or on potassium-sparing medications

sources.label: Effect of potassium salt substitution on blood pressure and cardiovascular outcomes
Role of potassium in human health and hypertension

1160.name: Sparkling Water
1160.description: Water infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure, creating effervescence.
1160.risks: Mild dental enamel erosion risk compared to still water

sources.label: Effect of carbonated water on dental enamel - PMC20223876

1162.name: Natural Lemon Flavor
1162.description: Extracted flavor compounds derived from lemon fruit, typically used to impart citrus aroma and taste in food products.
1162.benefits: Provides citrus flavor, enhances sensory appeal
1162.risks: Irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, potential presence of allergens or trace contaminants, ultra-processed additive

1163.name: Natural Lime Flavor
1163.description: A composite flavor ingredient containing maltodextrin, sugar, lime oil, lime juice concentrate, sunflower lecithin, gum arabic, and silicon dioxide used to impart lime flavor in food products.
1163.benefits: Flavor enhancement, improves sensory appeal of foods
1163.risks: Potential minor irritation or sensitization from lime oil, ultra-processed components (maltodextrin, sugar), mild exposure to sunflower lecithin (hexane extraction potential), silicon dioxide as processed additive

1191.name: Soluble Vegetable Fiber
1191.description: Dietary fiber derived from vegetable sources that dissolves in water to form a gel-like material in the digestive tract.
1191.benefits: Supports digestive health, promotes satiety, aids in regulation of blood glucose and cholesterol levels

1220.name: Pure Cane Sugar
1220.description: Sucrose derived from sugar cane, commonly used as a sweetener in foods and beverages.
1220.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, metabolic effects

1221.name: Vitamins C (Ascorbic Acid)
1221.description: Vitamin C, or ascorbic acid, is a water-soluble vitamin essential for collagen synthesis, antioxidant protection, and immune function. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used within recommended dietary amounts.
1221.benefits: Antioxidant, supports immune health, aids collagen formation, enhances iron absorption
1221.risks: Gastrointestinal upset at high doses, potential kidney stone risk in susceptible individuals

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Vitamin C

1243.name: Organic Honey
1243.description: Natural sweetener produced by bees from floral nectar, containing sugars, trace enzymes, and antioxidants.
1243.benefits: Provides sweetness, contains antioxidants, may have minor antimicrobial properties
1243.risks: Possible allergen, risk of infant botulism if consumed by infants under 1 year

1265.name: NeuroFactor Coffee Fruit Extract (100 mg)
1265.description: NeuroFactor is a standardized extract derived from the whole coffee fruit (Coffea arabica), containing various polyphenols and bioactive compounds. It is marketed for its ability to increase brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a protein involved in neuroplasticity and cognitive function.
1265.benefits: May support increased BDNF, potential cognitive function support, source of polyphenols
1265.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort, insufficient long-term safety data, potential caffeine sensitivity

1268.name: Pyridoxal 5'-Phosphate (Vitamin B6)
1268.description: A phosphorylated form of vitamin B6 (pyridoxine phosphate), involved as a coenzyme in amino acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.
1268.benefits: Essential coenzyme in amino acid metabolism, supports neurotransmitter synthesis and nervous system function

sources.label: PMID 11219923 – Vitamin B6 metabolism and function
PMID 1525274 – Role of vitamin B6 in neurotransmitter metabolism

1271.name: Panax ginseng root extract
1271.description: Extract derived from the root of the Panax ginseng plant, used traditionally for various health applications and as an adaptogen.
1271.benefits: May support cognitive function, enhance physical endurance, and provide adaptogenic effects
1271.risks: Potential for allergic sensitization, mild gastrointestinal discomfort, possible interactions with medications such as anticoagulants

1278.name: Organic Green Coffee Extract
1278.description: Organic green coffee extract is derived from unroasted coffee beans and is typically standardized for chlorogenic acid content. It is promoted for its antioxidant properties and potential effects on blood sugar regulation and weight management.
1278.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential modest reduction in blood pressure, may support mild weight loss, possible improvement in glucose metabolism
1278.risks: May cause mild gastrointestinal discomfort, may affect blood pressure, potential caffeine sensitivity

1279.name: Organic apple juice
1279.description: Apple juice is a liquid extracted from apples, used as a flavoring or sweetening ingredient. Organic certification indicates cultivation without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers.
1279.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sugars, source of some micronutrients and antioxidants
1279.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental caries with excessive consumption

sources.label: Nutritional composition and health benefits of apples and apple juice
Sugar content of fruit juices and risk of dental caries

1285.name: Organic Lemon Juice Concentrate
1285.description: Concentrated juice derived from lemons, commonly used for flavoring and acidity in food products.
1285.benefits: Source of vitamin C, contributes to flavor and acidity in foods
1285.risks: Potential for acidity-related dental erosion with excessive consumption, possible allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Effect of acidic beverages on dental enamel erosion
Nutritional value of citrus fruits: vitamin C content

1290.name: Organic coconut water concentrate
1290.description: Concentrated coconut water which contains organic acids such as citric acid; used primarily for flavoring and hydration.
1290.benefits: Provides electrolytes such as potassium, supports hydration
1290.risks: Potential mild irritation in sensitive individuals due to acidity, possible allergen in rare cases

1292.name: Orange juice concentrate
1292.description: Fruit juice concentrated by removing water, used as a flavoring and sweetener in foods and beverages.
1292.benefits: Source of vitamin C, provides flavor and nutrients from oranges
1292.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental erosion with excessive intake

sources.label: Impact of fruit juices on dental health – PMC15258194
Vitamin C content and health benefits of orange juice – PMC28221865

1295.name: Organic green tea caffeine
1295.description: Organic green tea caffeine is caffeine naturally extracted from organically grown Camellia sinensis leaves. In the body, caffeine acts as a central nervous system stimulant, increasing alertness and temporarily reducing fatigue.
1295.benefits: Enhanced cognitive performance, improved alertness, potential antioxidant effects, increased metabolic rate
1295.risks: Insomnia, anxiety, increased heart rate, potential interaction with medications, gastrointestinal upset

1297.name: Organic lime extract
1297.description: Organic lime extract is derived from organically grown lime fruit and typically contains concentrated flavor compounds, antioxidants, and small amounts of vitamins such as vitamin C. It offers citrus aroma and tartness when used in food products.
1297.benefits: Contains flavonoids, provides vitamin C, antioxidant properties

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Composition and benefits of lime extracts

1298.name: Modified Food Starch
1298.description: Starch chemically or physically altered to improve texture, stability, and shelf life in processed foods.
1298.benefits: Improves texture and stability in food products, enhances shelf life
1298.risks: Ultra-processed ingredient, potential allergen for sensitive individuals, may contain residual processing agents

sources.label: Modified starches: chemistry and functionality

1299.name: Blue 1
1299.description: Synthetic blue dye (FD&C Blue No. 1, Brilliant Blue FCF) used as a colorant in foods, drugs, and cosmetics.
1299.benefits: Provides vibrant blue color for consumer acceptability and product identification
1299.risks: Potential allergen, hypersensitivity reactions in susceptible individuals, concern about behavioral effects in children, possible contamination with heavy metals depending on source quality

sources.label: McCann et al. (2007) Food additives and hyperactivity in children
Allergic reactions to FD&C dyes

1316.name: Potassium Benzoate (Preservative)
1316.description: Potassium benzoate is a synthetic preservative used to inhibit the growth of mold, yeast, and some bacteria in acidic foods and beverages, thereby extending shelf life.
1316.risks: Potential for benzene formation in presence of vitamin C, possible mild allergen, ultra-processed additive, no nutritional value

1320.name: Sodium Benzoate
1320.description: Sodium benzoate is a widely used preservative that inhibits microbial growth in acidic foods and beverages.
1320.benefits: Prevents microbial spoilage, extends shelf life
1320.risks: Irritation in sensitive individuals, potential formation of benzene under certain conditions

sources.label: PMC6991677 – Safety evaluation of sodium benzoate

1322.name: White tea extract
1322.description: Extract derived from white tea (Camellia sinensis) leaves, containing polyphenols and other bioactive compounds, used for flavor and antioxidant properties.
1322.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential anti-aging effects for skin, natural flavoring agent
1322.risks: Irritant potential in sensitive skin on topical use, possible mild sensitization in rare cases, caffeine content may cause mild stimulant effects if ingested in large amounts

1323.name: Purified sparkling water
1323.description: Water that has been purified to remove contaminants and infused with carbon dioxide gas to create carbonation. Generally recognized as safe and commonly consumed as a hydrating beverage.
1323.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free, alternative to sugary carbonated drinks

sources.label: Water purification and safety overview

1339.name: Watermelon juice concentrate
1339.description: Concentrated form of watermelon juice typically used as a flavoring or sweetener ingredient in foods and beverages.
1339.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, contains antioxidants like lycopene from watermelon
1339.risks: High sugar content contributing to caloric intake, potential for minor allergenicity

1341.name: Added Electrolytes (Potassium bicarbonate)
1341.description: Potassium bicarbonate is an inorganic salt used to supply potassium, an essential electrolyte involved in muscle function, nerve signaling, and acid-base balance. In food products, it is added to support hydration or as a buffering agent.
1341.benefits: Supports electrolyte balance, may help maintain acid-base equilibrium, supports nerve and muscle function
1341.risks: Potential hyperkalemia in individuals with kidney disease, gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses

1343.name: Added Electrolytes (Calcium chloride)
1343.description: Calcium chloride is an inorganic salt used to fortify foods and beverages with calcium and enhance electrolyte content. It dissociates into calcium and chloride ions in the body, supporting normal muscle, nerve, and metabolic function.
1343.benefits: Contributes to dietary calcium intake, helps maintain electrolyte balance, supports muscle and nerve function
1343.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, hypercalcemia risk in sensitive individuals, may impart a salty or bitter taste

sources.label: NCBI Bookshelf – Calcium Chloride

1345.name: Vapor distilled water
1345.description: Water purified by vapor distillation, removing impurities and minerals. Commonly used in food and cosmetic formulations. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for consumption and topical use.
1345.benefits: Pure hydration source, free from contaminants and minerals, safe for consumption and use in formulations

sources.label: FDA guidance on food ingredients

1347.name: Organic Raspberry Flavor
1347.description: Organic raspberry flavor is a concentrated extract or blend derived from organic raspberries and/or natural sources, created to impart raspberry taste. While the organic certification generally restricts certain synthetic solvents and additives, the ingredient still involves chemical extraction, concentration, and often lacks transparency regarding its full composition. It is commonly used in processed foods and beverages for flavor enhancement.
1347.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain undisclosed carrier agents, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

1370.name: Skimmed milk powder
1370.description: Powdered form of milk with most fat removed, rich in protein and lactose, used for nutritional supplementation and food processing.
1370.benefits: Source of high-quality protein, calcium, and vitamins, shelf-stable dairy ingredient
1370.risks: Lactose intolerance risk, potential allergen, may contain residual milk protein allergens

sources.label: Nutritional and functional properties of milk powder
Milk allergy and lactose intolerance: Differentiating diagnosis and management

1500.name: Maltitol
1500.description: Maltitol is a sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener, providing sweetness similar to sucrose with fewer calories.
1500.benefits: Provides sweetness with lower calories than sugar, does not elevate blood glucose as much as sugar
1500.risks: Digestive discomfort, laxative effects at high intake

sources.label: PubMed 18078580 - Digestive tolerance of maltitol and other polyols

1502.name: Collagen peptides
1502.description: Collagen peptides are short chains of amino acids derived from collagen protein, typically sourced from animal connective tissue. They are used in food and supplements for their potential to support skin elasticity, joint health, and connective tissue function.
1502.benefits: May support skin hydration and elasticity, may improve joint health, may promote bone health

1509.name: Sweetener Maltitol
1509.description: A sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener in food products, derived from hydrogenated starch hydrolysates.
1509.benefits: Lower glycemic response than sugar, reduced calorie sweetener
1509.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, laxative effects

1531.name: Aroma
1531.description: Aroma refers to flavoring substances added to products to impart a particular smell or taste. It often includes chemically extracted compounds and can be natural or synthetic.
1531.risks: Potential irritant or sensitizer depending on compounds, lack of transparency, possible presence of solvents or trace contaminants

1543.name: Whey Protein Isolate
1543.description: Concentrated form of whey protein derived from milk, containing minimal lactose and fat. Primarily used as a dietary protein supplement for muscle support and nutrition.
1543.benefits: High-quality protein source, supports muscle protein synthesis, rich in essential amino acids
1543.risks: Potential dairy allergen, mild digestive intolerance in lactose-sensitive individuals, rare risk of kidney strain with excessive intake

sources.label: PMC5852764 – Whey protein and muscle health
PMC3549512 – Protein intake and kidney health

1604.name: Carrot Concentrate
1604.description: Concentrated extract from carrots used as a natural colorant and source of carotenoids.
1604.benefits: Natural colorant, source of carotenoids with antioxidant properties
1604.risks: Potential mild allergenicity, low contamination risk in food-grade forms

sources.label: PMC3854496 - Carotenoids in nutrition and health

1654.name: Natural Vanilla Flavouring
1654.description: Flavoring derived from vanilla beans or natural extracts used to impart vanilla aroma and taste in foods and beverages.
1654.benefits: Provides characteristic vanilla flavor and aroma, enhances palatability of food products
1654.risks: Potential for allergenic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible exposure to trace contaminants depending on extraction and production methods, minimal irritation risk

sources.label: PMID 10102358 - Review on vanilla flavor and safety
PMID 16158625 - Allergic reactions to natural flavorings

1788.name: Vitamin E
1788.description: Fat-soluble antioxidant vitamin found in various foods and supplements, used to prevent oxidative damage to cells.
1788.benefits: Antioxidant properties, supports cellular protection from oxidative stress
1788.risks: High dose supplementation may increase bleeding risk, potential for pro-oxidant effects at excessive levels

sources.label: PMC2835903 – Role of vitamin E in oxidative stress and human health
PMC4000184 – Potential risks of vitamin E supplementation

1858.name: Monocalcium phosphate
1858.description: An inorganic chemical used primarily as a leavening agent in baking and a dietary supplement for calcium and phosphorus.
1858.benefits: Leavening agent in baking, source of dietary calcium and phosphorus

sources.label: Food additive safety and functions - PMC

1872.name: Niacin
1872.description: Water-soluble B vitamin (B3) involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair. Essential micronutrient obtained through diet or supplementation.
1872.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, DNA repair, skin health, and nervous system function
1872.risks: High doses can cause flushing, liver toxicity, gastrointestinal distress

sources.label: PMID 12594773 – Niacin metabolism and pharmacology
PMID 16141045 – Clinical uses and toxicities of niacin

1875.name: Riboflavin
1875.description: Water-soluble vitamin B2 used as a food colorant and nutrient supplement.
1875.risks: Rare allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMC1397063 - Riboflavin functions and safety

1891.name: Palm Oil
1891.description: Edible oil derived from the fruit of oil palm trees, widely used in food products. Rich in saturated and monounsaturated fats.
1891.benefits: Stable cooking oil, source of vitamin E, good oxidative stability
1891.risks: High saturated fat content, environmental concerns from production

sources.label: Nutritional and health effects of palm oil consumption - PMID:31120802

1930.name: Inulin
1930.description: Inulin is a type of soluble dietary fiber found in various plants, used primarily as a prebiotic fiber to promote gut health and as a texturizer in food products.
1930.benefits: Prebiotic fiber supporting gut microbiota, may improve bowel regularity, low calorie
1930.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort such as bloating and gas at higher intake levels

sources.label: PMID 21138978 - Prebiotic effects of inulin-type fructans
PMID 26111006 - Gastrointestinal tolerance of inulin-type fructans

1989.name: Orange
1989.description: Citrus fruit widely used for flavoring and nutritional content including vitamin C and flavonoids.
1989.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, flavoring agent
1989.risks: Irritation risk for sensitive skin or allergic individuals, pesticide residues possible if not organic

sources.label: PMC4145302 - Nutritional and antioxidant properties of oranges
PMC3975640 - Citrus fruit allergy and irritation potential

1990.name: Lemon
1990.description: Lemon is the fruit of Citrus limon, commonly used for flavoring and fragrance due to its acidic juice and aromatic peel.
1990.benefits: Flavoring agent, fragrance, source of citric acid
1990.risks: Skin irritation and photosensitivity in topical use at higher concentrations, possible allergen

sources.label: Phototoxic effects of citrus-derived compounds (PMID 17309121)

1993.name: Apple
1993.description: Fruit from the Malus domestica tree, commonly consumed fresh or in processed form; used as a flavoring or ingredient at 3% concentration.
1993.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, antioxidants, and vitamins when consumed fresh
1993.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, pesticide residue potential if not organic

sources.label: PMCID: PMC4366005 - Nutritional and health benefits of apples
PMID: 11949956 - Apple allergy and sensitization reviews

1998.name: Carrot
1998.description: Root vegetable commonly consumed for its carotenoid content and dietary fiber.
1998.benefits: Source of beta-carotene, vitamins, dietary fiber, antioxidants

sources.label: PMC3179173 - Carotenoids and health benefits

2000.name: Strawberry
2000.description: Fruit ingredient derived from strawberries, used for flavor and nutritional value including vitamins and antioxidants.
2000.benefits: Source of vitamin C, dietary fiber, antioxidants
2000.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential pesticide residue contamination depending on source

sources.label: PMC metabolic and antioxidant effects of strawberries
Allergy risk and pesticide residues in fruits

2001.name: Raspberry
2001.description: Fruit ingredient derived from Rubus idaeus, commonly used for flavoring and natural coloring.
2001.benefits: Natural flavoring, source of antioxidants and vitamins in dietary context
