2001.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible pesticide residues if not organic

sources.label: Antioxidant properties of raspberry
Raspberry allergy overview

2013.name: Coriander
2013.description: Herb derived from Coriandrum sativum seeds, often used as a spice or flavoring agent.
2013.risks: Possible skin sensitization or allergic reactions in some individuals

sources.label: PMC4003790 – Coriander: chemical and pharmacological aspects

2024.name: Natural Watermelon Flavor
2024.description: Extracted flavor compounds derived from watermelon, used to impart watermelon taste in food and beverages.
2024.benefits: Provides watermelon flavoring for palatability and sensory appeal
2024.risks: Potential for allergens, may contain trace solvents or processing residues, ultra-processed ingredient

2030.name: Natural Citrus Flavors
2030.description: Complex mixture of volatile compounds derived from citrus fruits, used to impart citrus and lemon-lime aroma and taste in foods and beverages.
2030.benefits: Provides citrus aroma and flavor, enhances palatability of food and beverages
2030.risks: Potential skin and respiratory sensitization, possible residual solvents or contaminants from extraction, variable composition due to natural sources

2066.name: L-Tryptophan
2066.description: An essential amino acid required for protein synthesis and precursor to neurotransmitters such as serotonin and melatonin.
2066.benefits: Supports protein synthesis, precursor to serotonin and melatonin, may aid mood regulation and sleep
2066.risks: Allergic reactions or sensitization in rare cases, risk of eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome from contaminated supplements, none at typical dietary intake

sources.label: PMID 12895487 - Safety of L-tryptophan supplementation
PMID 27986476 - Tryptophan metabolism and physiological roles

2070.name: Organic Agave Syrup
2070.description: A natural sweetener derived from the agave plant, composed primarily of fructose and glucose.
2070.benefits: Sweetening agent, provides sugars for energy
2070.risks: High fructose content associated with excessive caloric intake, potential weight gain with overconsumption

2096.name: Natural Grapefruit Essence
2096.description: Natural grapefruit essence is typically a volatile aromatic extract obtained from the peel or juice of grapefruits, used to impart flavor and aroma to foods and beverages. It contains concentrated grapefruit-derived compounds but lacks significant nutritional value.
2096.risks: Potential allergen, lack of transparency in processing, may contain trace solvents or carriers, no nutritional value

2101.name: D-Alpha-Tocopherol Acetate
2101.description: D-Alpha-Tocopherol Acetate is a synthetic ester form of vitamin E commonly used as a dietary supplement and antioxidant in food products. It is converted to the biologically active form of vitamin E in the body, supporting cellular membranes and acting as a free radical scavenger.
2101.benefits: Antioxidant activity, supports immune function, protects cell membranes
2101.risks: Digestive upset at high doses, potential anticoagulant effect at high intake, possible interaction with anticoagulant medications

2102.name: Beta-carotene
2102.description: A carotenoid pigment functioning as a provitamin A, convertible to vitamin A in the body, commonly found in fruits and vegetables.
2102.benefits: Antioxidant properties, source of vitamin A, supports vision and immune function
2102.risks: Potential lung cancer risk with high-dose supplementation in smokers, skin discoloration with excessive intake

sources.label: Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study Group, 1994
Role of beta-carotene in human health: A review

2104.name: Brewed Black Tea
2104.description: Brewed infusion of fermented tea leaves containing polyphenols, caffeine, and trace nutrients.
2104.benefits: Source of antioxidants (polyphenols), mild stimulant (caffeine), potential antimicrobial properties
2104.risks: Caffeine sensitivity, potential moderate irritant to sensitive skin, possible mild staining of teeth

2112.name: Invert Sugar
2112.description: A mixture of glucose and fructose produced by hydrolyzing sucrose, commonly used as a sweetener and humectant in foods.
2112.benefits: Provides sweetness, retains moisture, improves texture in food products
2112.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries risk, metabolic impact in high amounts

sources.label: PMCID: PMC3257692 - Effects of dietary sugars on metabolic health
PMCID: PMC4425174 - Sugar intake and dental caries

2144.name: Modified Corn Starch
2144.description: Chemically or physically treated starch derived from corn used as a thickener, stabilizer, or emulsifier in food products.
2144.benefits: Improves texture, stabilizes emulsions, thickening agent
2144.risks: Possible allergenicity, processing residues, ultra-processed ingredient

sources.label: PMID 25209389 - Modified starches in food applications and digestion

2154.name: Apple Powder
2154.description: Apple powder is made by dehydrating and grinding whole apples or apple flesh into a fine powder. It retains some of the fiber, polyphenols, and micronutrients found in fresh apples, but nutrient content and bioavailability may vary based on processing.
2154.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, contains polyphenols with antioxidant activity, provides some vitamins and minerals
2154.risks: Possible loss of heat-sensitive nutrients during processing, may contain added preservatives or anti-caking agents depending on source

2188.name: Glycerin
2188.description: A simple polyol compound commonly used as a humectant, solvent, and sweetener in foods and cosmetics.
2188.benefits: Moisturizing agent, humectant properties, enhances texture in formulations
2188.risks: None at typical use levels, potential mild skin irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMC4884799 – Glycerin's role in skin hydration and safety

2235.name: Tripotassium Citrate
2235.description: Potassium salt of citric acid used as a buffering agent, alkalizing agent, and food additive to regulate acidity and preserve products.
2235.benefits: Regulates acidity, acts as a potassium source, preserves food stability
2235.risks: Potential gastrointestinal irritation at high oral doses, electrolyte imbalance if consumed excessively

sources.label: Potassium citrate clinical uses and effects

2242.name: Vanilla Beans
2242.description: Natural pods from the vanilla orchid containing vanillin and other aromatic compounds used primarily for flavoring.
2242.benefits: Flavoring agent, natural aromatic compounds, culinary and fragrance uses
2242.risks: Possible mild skin irritation or sensitization in rare cases, minimal ingestion toxicity at typical culinary use

sources.label: Vanillin compound summary, PubChem

2262.name: Lycopene
2262.description: A red carotenoid pigment found in tomatoes and other red fruits, used as a food colorant and antioxidant.
2262.benefits: Antioxidant activity, may contribute to reduced oxidative damage

sources.label: PMC3854496 – Lycopene and health outcomes: a review

2274.name: Clarified Lemon Juice Concentrate
2274.description: Concentrated lemon juice with reduced pulp and particulates, primarily used as a flavoring and acidity regulator.
2274.benefits: Provides natural lemon flavor, acidity regulation in food products
2274.risks: Irritant to skin or mucous membranes in some individuals, potential for allergic reaction

2290.name: Betaine Hydrochloride
2290.description: Betaine hydrochloride (Betaine HCl) is a synthetic compound used as a dietary supplement to increase stomach acidity and support digestive function, particularly in cases of low gastric acid production.
2290.benefits: May improve digestion in people with low stomach acid, supports protein breakdown in specific cases of hypochlorhydria
2290.risks: Potential gastrointestinal irritation, may cause heartburn, rare risk of esophageal injury, not recommended for people with peptic ulcers

sources.label: NCBI – Betaine and Betaine Hydrochloride

2293.name: Magnesium Stearate
2293.description: A magnesium salt of stearic acid used as a lubricant and flow agent in pharmaceutical and supplement manufacturing.
2293.benefits: Improves powder flow, prevents ingredient clumping, aids manufacturing consistency
2293.risks: Potential minor irritation in sensitive individuals, possible interference with absorption at high doses

sources.label: PMID 16450810 – Effects of magnesium stearate on drug dissolution
PMID 15622079 – Evaluation of magnesium stearate in pharmaceutical formulations

2313.name: Black Currant
2313.description: Edible berries from the Ribes species, known for their high vitamin C content, antioxidants, and phytochemicals.
2313.benefits: Rich source of vitamin C, antioxidants, may support immune function
2313.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential interaction with anticoagulant medications

2315.name: Elderberry Extract
2315.description: Concentrated extract derived from Sambucus nigra berries, commonly used for flavoring, antioxidant properties, and topical application.
2315.benefits: Antioxidant properties, source of flavonoids, used for flavor and as a traditional botanical extract
2315.risks: Potential for allergic reactions, possible irritation in sensitive individuals, limited data on ingestion safety at high doses

sources.label: PMC5749447 - Antioxidant activity of elderberry extract
Elderberry extract and safety overview

2321.name: Banana
2321.description: Edible fruit providing carbohydrates, dietary fiber, and micronutrients such as potassium and vitamin C.
2321.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, potassium, vitamins, natural sugars for energy
2321.risks: Allergic reactions rare but possible, potential for spoilage if improperly stored

sources.label: Nutritional and health-promoting properties of bananas (PMID:25685853)

2322.name: Mango
2322.description: Edible fruit from the Mangifera indica tree, rich in vitamins, fiber, and antioxidants.
2322.benefits: Source of vitamins A and C, dietary fiber, antioxidants
2322.risks: Possible allergen for sensitive individuals, potential mild oral irritation in some

sources.label: PMCID: PMC4284105 - Nutritional and health-promoting aspects of mango fruit

2324.name: Pineapple
2324.description: Tropical fruit known for its sweet, tangy flavor, primarily composed of water, sugars, fiber, and micronutrients.
2324.benefits: Source of vitamin C, dietary fiber, and digestive enzyme bromelain
2324.risks: Potential allergen for some individuals, mild oral irritation due to bromelain enzyme

sources.label: PMC3883548 – Nutritional and health benefits of Pineapple
PMC121062 – Bromelain: Pharmacology and Therapeutic Applications

2331.name: Chaga Mushroom (Inonotus obliquus)
2331.description: Chaga mushroom is a parasitic fungus found mainly on birch trees, used traditionally in folk medicine. It contains polysaccharides, phenolic compounds, and antioxidants, and is being studied for its immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory properties.
2331.benefits: Antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory effects, immune modulation, potential anticancer properties
2331.risks: Risk of oxalate kidney stones, may interact with anticoagulant medications, potential hypoglycemic effects, allergic reactions

2334.name: Plum
2334.description: Plum is a whole fruit from the Prunus genus, providing dietary fiber, vitamins (notably vitamin C and K), potassium, and various polyphenol antioxidants. Plums can contribute to gastrointestinal health, antioxidant defense, and metabolic wellness when consumed as part of a balanced diet.
2334.benefits: Dietary fiber, vitamin C, antioxidant polyphenols, supports gut health, may help regulate blood sugar, potential cardiovascular benefits
2334.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort if overeaten, mild allergen for sensitive individuals

2344.name: Lemongrass
2344.description: Lemongrass is an essential oil extracted from the leaves and stalks of the Cymbopogon plant, commonly used for its fragrance and flavor.
2344.benefits: Natural fragrance, antimicrobial properties, flavoring agent
2344.risks: Skin irritation, allergic sensitization in susceptible individuals, phototoxicity in some preparations

sources.label: PMID 28918211 - Allergic contact dermatitis to essential oils including lemongrass
PMID 32672337 - Chemical composition and biological activities of lemongrass essential oil

2404.name: Black Cherry
2404.description: Black cherry is a fruit rich in vitamins, antioxidants, and anti-inflammatory compounds. It contains anthocyanins which may support cardiovascular health and reduce oxidative stress. Generally recognized as safe and nutritious when consumed as whole fruit or juice.
2404.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, anti-inflammatory, supports heart health, may reduce muscle soreness
2404.risks: Rare allergic reactions, potential interaction with blood-thinning medications

2522.name: Matcha
2522.description: Powdered green tea leaves primarily used for flavoring and antioxidant content.
2522.benefits: Antioxidant properties, contains polyphenols, enhances flavor
2522.risks: Caffeine content may cause mild stimulant effects, potential for allergic reactions

sources.label: PMC2686662 - Health effects of green tea catechins

2544.name: Blueberry Extract
2544.description: Blueberry extract is a concentrated form of compounds derived from blueberries, rich in polyphenols, particularly anthocyanins, known for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects in the body.
2544.benefits: Antioxidant activity, supports cognitive function, may reduce inflammation, potential cardiovascular benefits

2548.name: Kombucha Culture
2548.description: Kombucha culture refers to a symbiotic colony of bacteria and yeast (SCOBY) used to ferment sweetened tea to make kombucha, a lightly effervescent drink. Known for its probiotic content, kombucha may promote gut health and support digestion. It is generally considered safe and is acknowledged by health authorities as having some potential health benefits.
2548.benefits: May provide probiotics, may support gut microbiome balance, source of organic acids
2548.risks: Possible contamination risk if improperly fermented, digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals

2552.name: Organic Black Tea
2552.description: Organic black tea is derived from the fully oxidized leaves of the Camellia sinensis plant, cultivated without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. It contains bioactive compounds, notably flavonoids and caffeine, that may influence cardiovascular health, antioxidant status, and cognitive performance.
2552.benefits: Source of polyphenols, antioxidant effects, may support cardiovascular health, may improve cognitive function
2552.risks: Caffeine sensitivity, may interfere with iron absorption, potential pesticide contamination in non-organic forms

2553.name: Organic Evaporated Cane Juice
2553.description: Organic evaporated cane juice is a minimally processed sweetener derived from sugar cane, often used as an alternative to refined white sugar but with similar calorie and sucrose content.
2553.risks: High glycemic index, contributes to metabolic syndrome, risk of obesity, dental caries, cardiovascular risk

2561.name: Black Tea Leaves
2561.description: Processed leaves of Camellia sinensis, commonly used to prepare black tea. Contains polyphenols, caffeine, and flavor compounds.
2561.benefits: Contains antioxidants (polyphenols), supports hydration with stimulant effect, commonly consumed beverage
2561.risks: Caffeine-related sensitivity, potential pesticide residues depending on source

2564.name: Natural Raspberry Flavor
2564.description: Concentrated flavoring derived from raspberry fruit compounds, used to impart raspberry taste in food and beverages.
2564.benefits: Provides raspberry flavor without added sugars or calories, enhances palatability
2564.risks: Potential irritant or sensitizer in sensitive individuals, may contain trace solvents from extraction, lack of transparency in specific constituents

2577.name: Organic Blueberry Juice
2577.description: Juice derived from blueberries rich in anthocyanins and antioxidants.

2582.name: Organic Kaffir Lime Leaves
2582.description: Kaffir lime leaves are aromatic leaves from the kaffir lime tree, commonly used in Southeast Asian cuisine for their distinct citrus flavor. They contain essential oils and bioactive compounds that have antioxidant and antimicrobial properties.
2582.benefits: Antioxidant properties, antimicrobial activity, source of essential oils

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Volatile Compounds and Bioactivity in Kaffir Lime Leaves

2584.name: Organic Hibiscus
2584.description: Organic hibiscus refers to the dried petals of Hibiscus sabdariffa, cultivated without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. In food products, it provides a tart flavor and red color, and in the body, it is known for its antioxidant and potential antihypertensive properties.
2584.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, supports cardiovascular health, may lower blood pressure, anti-inflammatory properties
2584.risks: Possible drug interactions (with antihypertensive medications), mild gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals

2586.name: Guava Puree
2586.description: Purée made from guava fruit, used as a flavor and nutrient source in food products.
2586.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamins (notably vitamin C), antioxidants

2594.name: Rose Water
2594.description: Rose water is a flavored water made by steeping or distilling rose petals. It is used in foods, cosmetics, and traditional medicine, typically for its fragrance and subtle floral flavor. In food, it acts mainly as a flavoring agent and does not contribute significant nutrients or bioactive compounds in dietary amounts.
2594.risks: Rare allergic reactions, potential contamination if not properly processed

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Rose extracts and their functional food uses

2600.name: Chamomile
2600.description: Herbal extract from dried flowers of the Matricaria recutita plant, commonly used for its calming properties and mild anti-inflammatory effects.
2600.benefits: Mild anti-inflammatory effects, soothing properties, used topically and in teas for calming effects
2600.risks: Allergic reactions and skin sensitization in sensitive individuals, possible cross-reactivity with related plants (e.g. ragweed), rare contact dermatitis

2601.name: Hibiscus Flower
2601.description: Hibiscus flower, often used as a herbal tea or extract, is rich in polyphenols and anthocyanins, compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, and has been studied for its effects on blood pressure and metabolic health.
2601.benefits: Antioxidant activity, blood pressure reduction, lipid profile improvement, anti-inflammatory effects
2601.risks: Potential interaction with antihypertensive drugs, mild gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Pharmacological effects of Hibiscus sabdariffa

2620.name: Lemon Juice Powder
2620.description: Dehydrated powder form of lemon juice, primarily used for flavoring and as a source of organic acids and bioactive compounds such as vitamin C and flavonoids.
2620.benefits: Provides natural flavoring, source of vitamin C and antioxidants, shelf-stable compared to fresh lemon juice
2620.risks: Potential for mild irritation in high concentrations, sensitivity reactions in some individuals, possible residual pesticides if not properly processed

2626.name: Organic Inulin
2626.description: A soluble dietary fiber commonly extracted from chicory root, used as a prebiotic fiber to support gut health.
2626.benefits: Prebiotic fiber promoting beneficial gut microbiota, aids digestive health
2626.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses including bloating, gas, and diarrhea

2627.name: Pure Filtered Water
2627.description: Pure filtered water refers to water that has undergone mechanical or chemical filtration to remove impurities and contaminants; however, certain filtration processes may not eliminate all toxins and can strip beneficial minerals.
2627.risks: Potential residual contaminants, loss of minerals, may contain disinfection byproducts

2633.name: Organic Ashwagandha Extract
2633.description: Extract from the root of Withania somnifera standardized to 0.5% withanolides, commonly used as a botanical supplement.
2633.benefits: Botanical source of withanolides, potential adaptogenic effects supporting stress response
2633.risks: Irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, potential interactions with medications, limited data on long-term safety

sources.label: PMC4270108 – Ashwagandha safety and pharmacology overview

2635.name: Organic Reishi Mushroom Extract
2635.description: Organic Reishi Mushroom Extract is derived from the fruiting body or mycelium of the Ganoderma lucidum mushroom using water or alcohol extraction. It is used in supplements for its potential immunomodulatory and adaptogenic properties.
2635.benefits: Immune system modulation, potential anti-inflammatory effects, antioxidant activity
2635.risks: Rare allergic reactions, possible interaction with anticoagulant medications, mild digestive upset

2636.name: Organic Nutmeg
2636.description: Nutmeg is a spice derived from the seed of Myristica fragrans, used primarily for flavoring in food.
2636.risks: Irritant and sensitizer at high doses, ingestion toxicity due to myristicin content which can cause hallucinations or poisoning in large amounts

2659.name: Cottonseed Oil
2659.description: Edible oil extracted from cotton seeds, primarily composed of polyunsaturated fatty acids with significant omega-6 content.
2659.benefits: Source of vitamin E, culinary uses as cooking oil
2659.risks: High omega-6 fatty acid content, oxidative instability, potential pesticide residue, hexane extraction processing, moderate ingestion toxicity risk as dietary fat

sources.label: PMID 21858552 - Effects of cottonseed oil on lipid profiles and oxidative stress
PMID 23749032 - Cottonseed oil oxidation stability and contaminants

2680.name: Digestion-Resistant Maltodextrin
2680.description: A type of soluble dietary fiber derived from maltodextrin that resists digestion in the small intestine and ferments in the colon.
2680.benefits: Dietary fiber source, promotes gut health, aids bowel regularity
2680.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high intake, possible bloating or gas

2685.name: Molybdenum Yeast
2685.description: Molybdenum yeast is a form of the essential trace mineral molybdenum, biofortified into yeast cells to enhance absorption. In the body, molybdenum acts as a cofactor for several enzymes essential for the metabolism of sulfur-containing amino acids and certain drugs and toxins.
2685.benefits: Supports sulfur amino acid metabolism, essential trace mineral, cofactor for detoxification enzymes
2685.risks: Potential toxicity at high doses, may interact with copper metabolism if consumed in excess, rare hypersensitivity

sources.label: NIH ODS – Molybdenum Fact Sheet

2686.name: Manganese Gluconate
2686.description: Manganese gluconate is a manganese salt of gluconic acid used as a dietary supplement to provide manganese, an essential trace mineral involved in enzyme function and metabolism.
2686.benefits: Essential trace mineral, cofactor for enzymes, supports metabolism, bone formation, antioxidant defense
2686.risks: Potential for manganese toxicity with excessive intake, neurotoxicity in high doses, limited risk at typical supplementation levels

2691.name: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)
2691.description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for energy metabolism and cellular function, commonly used in dietary supplements and fortified foods.
2691.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, antioxidant functions, and normal cellular processes
2691.risks: Rare allergic reactions or hypersensitivity in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMC5579659 - Riboflavin (Vitamin B2) functions and safety
PMID 10468596 - Allergic reactions associated with riboflavin

2694.name: Tangerine Juice
2694.description: Tangerine juice is a liquid extracted from tangerines, a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C, flavonoids, and various phytonutrients. It provides antioxidant activity and supports immune function in the body.
2694.benefits: High vitamin C content, antioxidant effects, potential support for immune health, source of potassium, contains phytonutrients
2694.risks: High in natural sugars, potential oral acidity, may interact with certain medications

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Phenolic profile and antioxidant activity of tangerine juice

2704.name: Carob Bean Gum
2704.description: Natural polysaccharide extracted from the seeds of the carob tree, used as a thickening and stabilizing agent in foods.
2704.benefits: Thickening, stabilizing, emulsifying properties, soluble dietary fiber
2704.risks: Potential mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, rare allergenic potential

sources.label: PMC3872229 – Functional properties and applications of carob gum
PubMed 10840735 – Safety evaluation of locust bean gum

2711.name: Alpha-Tocopheryl Acetate
2711.description: A synthetic form of vitamin E used as an antioxidant in foods and cosmetics to protect oils and fats from oxidation.
2711.benefits: Antioxidant properties, helps prevent oxidative damage in formulations, supports vitamin E nutritional intake
2711.risks: Rare skin irritation or sensitization in topical use, low toxicity at typical intake levels

sources.label: Vitamin E - Fact Sheet for Health Professionals (NIH)

2713.name: Orange Juice from Concentrate
2713.description: Juice reconstituted from concentrated orange juice, providing flavor and nutritional components such as vitamin C and natural sugars.
2713.benefits: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants, hydration, natural flavoring
2713.risks: High sugar content leading to excessive calorie intake if consumed in large amounts, potential dental erosion risk from acidity

sources.label: Health benefits of citrus fruit consumption and vitamin C
Dental erosion and citrus fruit juices

2714.name: Orange Pulp
2714.description: Fibrous material derived from the edible part of oranges, primarily composed of dietary fiber, water, and residual sugars.
2714.benefits: Dietary fiber source, supports digestive health, contains natural vitamins and antioxidants

2716.name: Strawberry Juice from Concentrate
2716.description: Juice derived from strawberries concentrated by removing water, then reconstituted for use in foods and beverages.
2716.benefits: Source of natural flavor and color, contains some vitamins and antioxidants from strawberries
2716.risks: Potential allergen for sensitive individuals, high natural sugar content, possible processing residues

sources.label: PMC4932306 – Nutritional and health benefits of strawberries

2721.name: Pear Juice from Concentrate
2721.description: Pear juice from concentrate is made by extracting pear juice, removing most of its water to create a concentrate, then reconstituting it with water for use in foods and beverages. It provides natural fruit sugars and some vitamins, but processing removes most fiber and micronutrients.
2721.benefits: Provides hydration, contains some vitamin C and potassium
2721.risks: High in free sugars, low in fiber, possible spike in blood glucose, loss of polyphenols and micronutrients due to processing

2722.name: Passion Fruit Juice from Concentrate
2722.description: Juice derived from the concentration and reconstitution of passion fruit, commonly used as a flavoring and beverage ingredient.
2722.benefits: Source of vitamins and antioxidants, provides natural flavor and sweetness
2722.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible pesticide residues depending on agricultural practices, high natural sugar content

2723.name: Pineapple Juice from Concentrate
2723.description: Reconstituted juice made by adding water to pineapple juice concentrate, containing natural fruit sugars and organic acids.
2723.benefits: Source of vitamins (notably vitamin C), natural flavor and hydration
2723.risks: High sugar content, potential dental erosion from acidity

sources.label: Nutritional and health aspects of fruit juices
Dietary sugars and dental health

2725.name: Peach Purée
2725.description: A processed fruit ingredient made by mashing or blending ripe peaches into a thick, sauce-like consistency, primarily used for flavoring or as a sweetener in foods.
2725.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, source of dietary fiber and micronutrients such as vitamins A and C
2725.risks: Possible allergen for sensitive individuals, potential microbial contamination if improperly processed or stored

sources.label: Nutritional and health benefits of fruits — PubMed
Foodborne risk factors and microbial contamination in fruit purees

2742.name: Organic Strawberry Puree
2742.description: Pureed strawberries, usually used as a flavoring or ingredient in foods and beverages. Contains natural sugars, fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants.
2742.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, antioxidants
2742.risks: Possible allergen for strawberry-sensitive individuals, sugar content when consumed in excess

sources.label: PMC4192979 - Nutritional and health effects of strawberries
PubMed 19597535 - Strawberry intake and antioxidant status

2748.name: Natural Grape Strawberry Flavor
2748.description: This ingredient refers to a blend of chemical extracts and concentrates derived from grape, strawberry, or similar natural sources, intended to mimic the taste of those fruits. It often contains solvents, carriers, and minor additives, and its use in foods is primarily for taste enhancement rather than nutrition.
2748.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents or preservatives, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

2755.name: Magnesium hydroxide
2755.description: An inorganic compound used primarily as an antacid and laxative, also utilized in water treatment and as a flame retardant.
2755.benefits: Antacid properties, laxative effect, flame retardant, pH neutralizer
2755.risks: Mild gastrointestinal irritation at high doses, possible laxative effect, minimal dermal or inhalation toxicity

sources.label: PubChem Magnesium Hydroxide Summary

2766.name: Organic Coconut Water from Concentrate
2766.description: Coconut water from concentrate is reconstituted by adding water to previously dehydrated coconut water. It contains electrolytes such as potassium and sodium, but the concentration process can reduce or alter some phytonutrients compared to fresh coconut water.
2766.benefits: Provides hydration, contains electrolytes, source of minerals
2766.risks: Potential loss of nutrients during processing, possible presence of contaminants from water used for reconstitution

2767.name: D-alpha-tocopheryl Acetate
2767.description: D-alpha-tocopheryl acetate is a synthetic form of vitamin E, commonly used as an antioxidant and dietary supplement to prevent oxidation in foods and enhance shelf life. It is the most bioavailable form of vitamin E, providing antioxidant activity in the body.
2767.benefits: Antioxidant, supports immune function, protects cell membranes from oxidative damage
2767.risks: High-dose supplementation risks (e.g., increased bleeding risk), possible gastrointestinal discomfort at large intakes

2778.name: Orange zest
2778.description: Orange zest is the outer colorful layer of the orange peel, rich in essential oils such as limonene and containing various phytonutrients and antioxidants. It is commonly used to add flavor, aroma, and small amounts of micronutrients to foods.
2778.benefits: Antioxidant properties, source of vitamin C, contains flavonoids, contributes dietary fiber, provides natural essential oils with anti-inflammatory effects
2778.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), pesticide residues (if not organic)

2779.name: L-Tyrosine
2779.description: Non-essential amino acid used as a precursor for proteins and neurotransmitters such as dopamine and norepinephrine.
2779.benefits: Supports protein synthesis, precursor for neurotransmitter production, may support cognitive function under stress
2779.risks: Minor gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, potential interaction with thyroid or catecholamine medications

2781.name: Acetyl L-Tyrosine
2781.description: Acetyl L-Tyrosine is an acetylated form of the amino acid L-tyrosine, often used in dietary supplements for improved solubility and potential cognitive and neurological support due to its role as a precursor for neurotransmitters like dopamine and norepinephrine.
2781.benefits: Precursor to catecholamine neurotransmitters, may support cognitive function under stress, may aid in mental performance
2781.risks: Mild gastrointestinal upset, possible interactions with thyroid or antidepressant medications

2791.name: Licorice Root Extract
2791.description: Extract derived from the root of Glycyrrhiza glabra, commonly used as a flavoring agent in foods and beverages.
2791.benefits: Flavor enhancer, provides characteristic sweet and anise-like taste
2791.risks: Potential for endocrine disruption via mineralocorticoid effects leading to hypertension and hypokalemia with excessive intake, possible irritant in high concentrations

2802.name: Copper Sulfate
2802.description: Copper sulfate is an inorganic compound frequently used as a supplement in animal and plant nutrition, as well as an additive in some processed foods for its essential trace mineral copper content. In the human body, copper is necessary in small amounts for enzymatic reactions and iron metabolism.
2802.benefits: Provides copper, an essential trace mineral for enzymatic function, iron metabolism, and antioxidant defense
2802.risks: Potential toxicity at high doses, gastrointestinal irritation, liver and kidney damage with chronic exposure, not recommended for direct human supplementation without medical oversight

2808.name: Natural Mineral Water
2808.description: Water sourced from natural springs containing various dissolved minerals. Primarily used for hydration.
2808.benefits: Hydration, source of minerals such as calcium, magnesium, and bicarbonates
2808.risks: Potential contamination with heavy metals or microbiological agents depending on source quality

2830.name: Bacillus subtilis DE111
2830.description: A probiotic bacterial strain used to support gut microbiota balance and digestive health.
2830.benefits: Supports gut microbiome, aids digestion, may enhance immune function
2830.risks: Rare risk of infection in immunocompromised individuals, possible allergic reactions

sources.label: PMC5440521 - Safety and efficacy of Bacillus subtilis probiotics
PMID 29498239 - Effects of Bacillus subtilis DE111 on gut health and immune response

2836.name: Phosphatidylserine
2836.description: Phosphatidylserine is a phospholipid component naturally found in cell membranes, especially in brain tissue, and is involved in cellular signaling and maintenance of membrane fluidity. It is commonly used as a dietary supplement for cognitive health.
2836.benefits: May support cognitive function, may improve memory in older adults, may reduce exercise-induced stress
2836.risks: Potential GI upset, possible insomnia, use with caution in those on anticoagulants or with bleeding disorders

sources.label: FDA GRAS Notice Inventory

2855.name: Trace Minerals
2855.description: Minerals present in small amounts obtained from purified seawater, including elements such as magnesium, calcium, potassium, and others needed in trace quantities.
2855.benefits: Provides essential minerals for physiological functions at trace levels, supports electrolyte balance and metabolic processes
2855.risks: Contamination potential if purification is incomplete, intake of heavy metals if sourced improperly, irritation potential if used topically in high concentration

2873.name: Deionized Water
2873.description: Purified water from which ions and minerals have been removed. Used as a solvent and diluent in cleaning formulations.
2873.benefits: Non-toxic, non-irritating, solvent and carrier for other ingredients

sources.label: PubChem Water
REACH Chemical Safety Assessment

2876.name: Calcium Hydroxide
2876.description: An inorganic compound used as a raising agent in foods to leaven or modify texture.
2876.benefits: Leavening agent, improves texture and processing in food products
2876.risks: Irritation risk if ingested in large quantities, high pH causing mucosal irritation

sources.label: PMID 21172317 - Use and safety of calcium hydroxide in food
PMID 31021639 - Food additive safety assessment

2913.name: Blueberry Puree
2913.description: Blueberry puree is made by mashing whole blueberries into a thick liquid or paste, retaining much of the fruit's natural nutrients and bioactive compounds.
2913.benefits: Source of dietary antioxidants, vitamins, and dietary fiber

2914.name: Blackberry Puree
2914.description: Pureed form of blackberry fruit containing water, fiber, natural sugars, vitamins, and antioxidants.
2914.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamins, antioxidants
2914.risks: Minimal risk at typical use levels, potential for microbial contamination if not properly processed

sources.label: PMC6313444 – Nutritional and health benefits of blackberries

2944.name: Niacin (Nicotinic Acid)
2944.description: Niacin, also known as nicotinic acid, is a water-soluble B vitamin (B3) essential for energy metabolism, DNA repair, and cell signaling. It is required for the formation of NAD and NADP, which are crucial coenzymes in cellular redox reactions.
2944.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, reduces LDL cholesterol, increases HDL cholesterol, supports DNA repair, essential nutrient
2944.risks: Flushing at high doses, liver toxicity with excessive supplementation, gastrointestinal upset

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements – Niacin

2955.name: Non-GMO Citric Acid
2955.description: Organic acid commonly used as a flavoring and acidulant in food and beverages to add sour taste and preserve products.
2955.benefits: Flavor enhancement, pH control, preservative effects
2955.risks: Irritation potential (skin, eyes, mucous membranes) at high concentrations, dental enamel erosion with excessive ingestion

2980.name: Carbonated Filtered Water
2980.description: Water that has been filtered for impurities and infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure to create carbonation. Widely consumed and generally recognized as safe for consumption.
2980.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free beverage, alternative to sugary sodas

2982.name: Ginger Extract
2982.description: Ginger extract is a concentrated form of bioactive compounds from the ginger root (Zingiber officinale), commonly used for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties in both food products and supplements.
2982.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, may reduce nausea, may support digestion
2982.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort, may interact with anticoagulant medications

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Review on the health benefits and side effects of ginger

3024.name: Vanadium (as Vanadium Amino Acid Chelate)
3024.description: Vanadium is a trace mineral sometimes added to supplements in chelated forms to potentially improve absorption. In the body, vanadium is not considered essential and is poorly understood in terms of human health; it has been studied largely for its insulin-mimetic effects.
3024.benefits: Possible mild insulin-mimetic activity, potential effect on blood glucose regulation (limited and inconsistent evidence)
3024.risks: Potential for toxicity at supplemental doses, kidney toxicity, gastrointestinal irritation, insufficient evidence for safety and efficacy, possible DNA damage at high doses

3102.name: Brilliant Blue FCF
3102.description: Synthetic blue dye used as a colorant in foods, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals to impart blue coloration.
3102.benefits: Adds blue color for aesthetic purposes in food and cosmetic products
3102.risks: Potential allergen, possible hypersensitivity reactions, regulatory restrictions in some regions

sources.label: PubChem - Brilliant Blue FCF
EFSA Journal - Scientific Opinion on Brilliant Blue FCF

3142.name: Blueberry Concentrate
3142.description: A concentrated form of blueberry fruit juice containing anthocyanins and other polyphenols.
3142.benefits: Source of antioxidants and polyphenols, used for color and potential nutritional benefits in foods
3142.risks: Low risk of irritation or sensitization, potential pesticide residues depending on source, minor contamination risk

sources.label: PMC - Antioxidant properties of blueberries

3154.name: ConcenTrace® Trace Mineral Complex
3154.description: A concentrated liquid mineral supplement derived from seawater, containing multiple trace minerals like magnesium, sulfate, potassium, and others at low concentrations.
3154.benefits: Provides bioavailable trace minerals, supports electrolyte balance, may contribute to mineral nutrition
3154.risks: Possible contamination with heavy metals if not purified, ingestion toxicity unlikely at typical supplemental doses, minimal irritation risk, potential cumulative mineral imbalance if overconsumed

sources.label: PMC6722952 - Trace minerals in human health and nutrition
PubMed 29914982 - Benefits and risks of trace mineral supplementation

3186.name: Organic Whole Lemon Puree
3186.description: Organic whole lemon puree is made from the entire lemon fruit, including the peel, pulp, and juice, and is processed without synthetic pesticides or additives. It provides vitamin C, flavonoids, fiber, and other phytonutrients that support antioxidant defenses and digestive health.
3186.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, source of fiber, contains flavonoids and polyphenols, antioxidant activity, potential cardiovascular support
3186.risks: Acidic irritation in sensitive individuals, potential for dental enamel erosion

3194.name: Resistant Dextrin
3194.description: A type of soluble dietary fiber derived from starch through enzymatic treatment, resistant to digestion in the small intestine.
3194.benefits: Prebiotic effects, supports gut health, may improve bowel regularity, aids blood glucose regulation
3194.risks: Digestive discomfort at high doses including bloating, gas, mild laxative effect

3246.name: Monk Fruit Extract
3246.description: Sweetener derived from monk fruit (Siraitia grosvenorii) containing natural glycosides like mogrosides responsible for sweetness.
3246.benefits: Zero-calorie natural sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, alternative to sugar
3246.risks: Rare sensitization potential, lack of long-term safety data in large populations

3276.name: Natural Aroma
3276.description: A general term for flavoring substances derived from natural sources, often a complex mixture of volatile compounds. May contain trace allergens such as milk.
3276.risks: Allergen cross-contamination (milk), lack of transparency, potential sensitizer, ultra-processed

3282.name: Orange Peel
3282.description: Dried or processed rind of orange fruit used for flavoring and aroma.
3282.benefits: Provides natural citrus flavor, source of dietary fiber and antioxidant compounds
3282.risks: Potential for mild skin or mucous membrane irritation, pesticide residue contamination if not organic, ingestion generally safe in food amounts

sources.label: PMC antioxidants and compounds in citrus peel
Safety and risks of citrus peel consumption

3289.name: Organic Mango Purée
3289.description: Fruit purée made from organic mango, used as a flavoring and sweetening ingredient in food products.
3289.benefits: Source of vitamins (notably vitamin C), natural sugars, flavor enhancer

3294.name: DL-Alpha Tocopheryl Acetate (Vitamin E)
3294.description: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin important for vision, immune function, and cellular communication. Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative damage.
3294.benefits: Supports vision and immune health (vitamin A), antioxidant protection (vitamin E)
3294.risks: Excessive intake of vitamin A can cause toxicity including liver damage and teratogenic effects; excessive vitamin E intake may increase bleeding risk

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Vitamin A
NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Vitamin E

3305.name: Natural Mango Flavor
3305.description: Complex mixture of volatile compounds derived from mango or mango extracts used to impart mango scent or taste in food products.
3305.benefits: Provides mango flavoring in foods and beverages, enhances sensory appeal
3305.risks: Possible irritant or sensitizer due to complex natural compounds, variability in composition, potential for allergenic reactions, ultra-processed ingredient

3307.name: Sulfur Dioxide
3307.description: Sulfur dioxide is a preservative commonly used in food and beverages to prevent microbial growth and oxidation.
3307.risks: Respiratory irritant especially for sensitive individuals, potential allergen, may cause bronchospasm in asthmatics

sources.label: PMID 19649267 – Sulfur dioxide and respiratory effects

3327.name: Raspberry Juice Concentrate
3327.description: Fruit juice derived from raspberries, concentrated to remove water then reconstituted; primarily provides flavor and some nutritional components such as vitamins and antioxidants.
3327.benefits: Source of antioxidants, vitamins, natural flavor
3327.risks: Potential allergen for sensitive individuals, contains natural sugars

3328.name: Safflower Concentrate
3328.description: Concentrated extract or oil derived from safflower seeds, primarily a source of polyunsaturated fatty acids, notably linoleic acid (omega-6). Commonly used as an edible oil or ingredient in food products.
3328.benefits: Source of polyunsaturated fatty acids, contributes essential fatty acids
3328.risks: High omega-6 fatty acid content associated with oxidative instability, potential pro-inflammatory effects with excessive intake

3338.name: Elderberry Concentrate
3338.description: Elderberry concentrate is produced by reducing the juice of the elderberry fruit (Sambucus nigra), concentrating its natural polyphenols, anthocyanins, and vitamins. It is often used for its perceived immune-supporting properties and as a natural colorant in food and beverages.
3338.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, may support immune function, potential antiviral effects, contains vitamins and polyphenols
3338.risks: Potential allergen in sensitive individuals, gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses

3340.name: Blackcurrant Concentrate
3340.description: Concentrated extract of blackcurrant fruit, often used for flavoring and as a source of anthocyanins and vitamin C.
3340.benefits: Source of antioxidants (anthocyanins), vitamin C, potential support for vascular health
3340.risks: Possible allergic reactions, potential for high sugar content if not unsweetened, minor gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals

3351.name: Lemon Concentrate
3351.description: Concentrated juice derived from lemons, containing primarily citric acid, vitamin C, and natural flavor compounds.
3351.benefits: Source of vitamin C, flavor enhancer, natural acidulant
3351.risks: Irritation to skin or mucous membranes in concentrated form, potential for acid damage to tooth enamel if ingested in large amounts

sources.label: PMC6267451 – Vitamin C and Lemon Juice Properties

3367.name: Calcium D-Pantothenate
3367.description: Calcium D-pantothenate is the calcium salt of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), used as a nutritional supplement and fortifier to support metabolic functions.
3367.benefits: Supports coenzyme A synthesis, aids energy metabolism, essential vitamin

sources.label: Pantothenic Acid - Dietary Supplement Fact Sheet - NIH

3381.name: Lemon Extract
3381.description: Concentrated preparation derived from lemon fruit, containing flavor and aroma compounds primarily used for flavoring purposes.
3381.benefits: Provides natural citrus flavor and aroma
3381.risks: Irritation or sensitization risk for some individuals upon skin contact or ingestion in high amounts

sources.label: Citrus extracts properties and uses - PMID 21377665

3393.name: Niacinamide (Niacin)
3393.description: Niacinamide is a form of vitamin B3 (niacin), an essential water-soluble vitamin involved in numerous cellular processes including energy metabolism and DNA repair. It is commonly added to fortified foods and supplements to prevent vitamin B3 deficiency.
3393.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, helps maintain healthy skin and nervous system, prevents pellagra (niacin deficiency disease), supports DNA repair
3393.risks: Flushing at high doses, GI irritation at very high intakes, rare liver toxicity with prolonged large doses

3399.name: Passionfruit Juice (from Concentrate)
3399.description: Fruit juice derived from passionfruit concentrate, typically used as a flavoring or minor nutritional component in food products.
3399.benefits: Provides natural flavor, contains small amounts of vitamins and antioxidants
3399.risks: Low risk at trace levels, potential allergen in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Nutritional and antioxidant properties of passionfruit juice
Food allergenicity and fruit juices

3416.name: Organic Beet Root Powder (for color)
3416.description: Powdered form of beet root used primarily as a natural colorant and source of dietary nitrates.
3416.benefits: Natural colorant, dietary nitrates may support vascular function
3416.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal upset, beeturia (harmless red urine discoloration)

sources.label: PMC4386576 - Beetroot juice and vascular health

3441.name: Organic Apple Juice Concentrate
3441.description: Concentrated juice derived from organic apples used primarily as a sweetener or flavor enhancer in food products.
3441.benefits: Natural source of sugars, provides flavor and sweetness
3441.risks: High sugar content, excessive intake associated with weight gain and dental caries

3494.name: Suiker
3494.description: Sugar is a carbohydrate used primarily as a sweetener. Dextrose is a simple sugar (glucose) often used as a sweetener and energy source.
3494.benefits: Provides quick energy as a carbohydrate source
3494.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, and increased risk of metabolic disorders

3510.name: Fumaric Acid
3510.description: Fumaric acid is an organic acid used primarily as an acidity regulator in food products to control pH and act as a preservative.
3510.benefits: Acidity regulation, food preservation, pH control
3510.risks: Irritation risk at high concentrations, potential gastrointestinal discomfort with excessive ingestion

sources.label: PMID 27933545 - Safety evaluation of food additives including fumaric acid

3511.name: Paprika Oleoresin
3511.description: A natural color additive derived from paprika peppers, containing carotenoids such as capsanthin and capsorubin used for coloring food and cosmetic products.
3511.benefits: Provides natural red-orange color, antioxidant carotenoids present
3511.risks: Irritation and sensitization potential in sensitive individuals, possible contamination with pesticide residues depending on source

sources.label: Safety assessment and health benefits of carotenoids – PMC26415994
Skin and respiratory allergy potential of paprika oleoresin – PMC21512509

3523.name: Organic Ginger Extract
3523.description: Organic ginger extract is a concentrated form of the bioactive compounds found in ginger (Zingiber officinale), commonly used for its flavor, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and digestive properties.
3523.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, supports digestive health, may reduce nausea, may aid in blood sugar regulation
3523.risks: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort, possible interaction with anticoagulant medications, potential allergic reactions

3536.name: Tapioca Dextrin
3536.description: A carbohydrate derived from tapioca starch, used as a thickener, stabilizer, or filler in food products.
3536.benefits: Provides texture and stability in foods, gluten-free carbohydrate source
3536.risks: Minor digestive intolerance in sensitive individuals, generally low concern

3541.name: Cold pressed Meyer lemon juice
3541.description: Cold pressed Meyer lemon juice is made by mechanically extracting juice from Meyer lemons without heat or solvents, preserving vitamin C, flavonoids, and aromatic compounds.
3541.benefits: High in vitamin C, provides flavonoids, antioxidant properties, may support immune function
3541.risks: Possible dental enamel erosion if consumed excessively, potential allergic reactions

3547.name: Tea Infusion (0.1%)
3547.description: Tea infusion is a water-based extract made by steeping tea leaves (Camellia sinensis) in hot water, resulting in the transfer of polyphenols, caffeine, amino acids, and other phytochemicals into the liquid. At 0.1%, the concentration is very low compared to typical brewed tea.

3548.name: Peach juice (0.1%) from concentrate
3548.description: Peach juice from concentrate is made by extracting the water from peach juice to form a concentrate, which is then reconstituted with water before use; the low percentage indicates minimal peach-derived nutrients in the final product.
3548.risks: Ultra-processed, minimal phytonutrients, potential residual processing compounds

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Nutritional properties of peach juice and effects of processing

3820.name: Galactomannan Prebiotic Fiber
3820.description: Galactomannan is a soluble dietary fiber found in the cell walls of certain legumes, notably guar beans and fenugreek. As a prebiotic fiber, it can be slowly fermented by gut microbiota, potentially supporting beneficial bacteria growth and aiding digestive health.
3820.benefits: May improve gut microbiota composition, may reduce blood cholesterol, may aid glycemic control, can increase stool bulk
3820.risks: Potential gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, rare allergy risk

3822.name: Natural Caffeine (From Green Coffee Bean Extract)
3822.description: Caffeine is a stimulant found naturally in green coffee bean extract, primarily used to increase alertness and reduce fatigue.
3822.benefits: Stimulant effects, increases alertness and cognitive function at typical doses
3822.risks: Irritation at high doses, potential for nervous system overstimulation, sleep disruption, possible dependence with excessive intake

3826.name: Patented Lychee Fruit Extract & Green Tea Leaf Extract
3826.description: A proprietary blend typically marketed for its high antioxidant content, combining lychee fruit extract (rich in polyphenols) and green tea leaf extract (notably containing catechins like EGCG), both studied for their possible effects on oxidative stress and metabolic health.
3826.benefits: Antioxidant properties, mild anti-inflammatory effects, possible support of metabolic health, potential cardiovascular benefits
3826.risks: Potential liver toxicity at high doses, caffeine sensitivity, possible drug interactions

3827.name: Patented Lychee Fruit Extract
3827.description: Extract derived from the fruit of Litchi chinensis, commonly used in foods and cosmetics for flavor, antioxidant properties, and fragrance.
3827.benefits: Antioxidant activity, source of vitamin C and flavonoids

3828.name: Pyridoxine HCl (Vitamin B6)
3828.description: Water-soluble vitamin important for amino acid metabolism and neurological function. Often used in supplements as pyridoxine hydrochloride.
3828.benefits: Supports metabolism, neurotransmitter synthesis, immune function
3828.risks: Possible sensory neuropathy in high doses, rare allergic reactions

3900.name: Dl-Alpha-Tocopheryl Acetate
3900.description: Synthetic form of vitamin E, used as an antioxidant and skin conditioning agent in foods and cosmetics.
3900.benefits: Antioxidant properties, protects against oxidative damage in formulations, supports skin barrier function
3900.risks: Irritant or sensitizer in some individuals, mild toxicity at very high doses, low oral bioavailability compared to natural vitamin E

3965.name: Potassium Chloride (Electrolyte)
3965.description: Potassium chloride is a mineral salt commonly used as a dietary electrolyte and as a salt substitute to help maintain normal cellular function and fluid balance. In food products, it is often added to replace sodium or support electrolyte content.
3965.benefits: Essential for nerve and muscle function, helps maintain fluid and electrolyte balance, may help reduce high blood pressure as sodium substitute
3965.risks: Hyperkalemia in susceptible individuals, gastrointestinal irritation in large doses, contraindicated in kidney disease

3980.name: Natürliches Mineralwasser
3980.description: Natürliches Mineralwasser (natural mineral water) is water sourced from underground reservoirs, containing naturally occurring minerals and trace elements. It is bottled at the source and is typically free from chemical processing, making it a common beverage in many countries.
3980.benefits: Source of hydration, provides trace minerals, generally free from artificial additives
3980.risks: Potential for residual contaminants, possible heavy metal content, may lack essential electrolytes depending on mineral composition

4000.name: Organic Agave Nectar
4000.description: Organic agave nectar is a natural sweetener derived from the agave plant. It is primarily composed of fructose and is used as an alternative to table sugar or honey in foods and beverages. Its high fructose content makes it sweeter than sucrose, allowing for smaller quantities to be used for the same level of sweetness.
4000.benefits: Low glycemic index compared to table sugar
4000.risks: High fructose content, may contribute to insulin resistance, risk of fatty liver, potential to disrupt gut microbiota, not nutritionally superior to table sugar

4002.name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
4002.description: A water-soluble vitamin involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair. Exists as niacin and niacinamide forms.
4002.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, helps maintain healthy skin and nervous system, involved in DNA repair
4002.risks: High dose supplementation may cause skin flushing, liver toxicity, gastrointestinal upset

sources.label: PMID 12584112 – Niacin in clinical practice
PMID 21404560 – Role of niacin in human health

4005.name: Filtered Carbonated Water
4005.description: Water purified through filtration and infused with carbon dioxide gas to create effervescence.
4005.risks: Mild acidity that may cause dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption

sources.label: PMC5562979 - Effects of carbonated beverages on dental enamel
PUBMED 29590697 - Carbonated water: health effects and hydration potential

4012.name: Pristine Water
4012.description: Frozen pure water applied as a protective ice glaze on frozen seafood to prevent dehydration and oxidation during storage.
4012.benefits: Protects product quality by reducing dehydration and oxidation during frozen storage
4012.risks: None at typical use, potential for microbial contamination if water quality is poor

4024.name: Organic Lime Juice Concentrate
4024.description: Concentrated juice from limes, used primarily for flavoring and as an acidulant in foods and beverages.
4024.benefits: Provides vitamin C, natural flavoring, acidic preservative properties
4024.risks: Irritation to skin and mucous membranes in sensitive individuals, potential oral sensitivity with excessive consumption

sources.label: PMC3396197 - Citrus fruits and bioactive compounds
Citrus fruit consumption and human health

4029.name: Organic Lime Flavor
4029.description: Organic lime flavor is a natural flavoring derived from organic limes or lime oils, used to impart a citrus taste to foods and beverages. Despite being labeled 'organic,' it is often processed, and exact composition is rarely disclosed to consumers.
4029.risks: Lack of transparency, potential for solvent residues, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

4030.name: L-Carnitine L-Tartrate
4030.description: L-Carnitine L-Tartrate is a supplemental form of L-carnitine, an amino-acid-derived compound involved in the transport of fatty acids into mitochondria for energy production. It is often used for exercise recovery and performance enhancement, as L-tartrate salt allows faster absorption.
4030.benefits: May reduce muscle soreness, could aid recovery from exercise, supports fat metabolism
4030.risks: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, rare fishy body odor, not recommended for individuals with epilepsy, may interact with some medications

4113.name: Organic Orange Extract
4113.description: Organic orange extract is a concentrated flavoring derived from organic oranges, typically capturing volatile aromatic compounds such as limonene and other citrus oils. It is primarily used for flavoring foods and beverages and contains minimal nutrients.

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Citrus essential oils: Extraction, composition and applications

4114.name: Natural Green Tea Caffeine
4114.description: Caffeine is a stimulant found in green tea that acts on the central nervous system to increase alertness and reduce fatigue.
4114.benefits: Cognitive alertness, mild stimulant effects, possible antioxidant properties due to associated green tea compounds
4114.risks: Irritation/sensitization risk at high doses, potential for jitteriness, increased heart rate, sleep disturbances, possible interactions with certain medications

4115.name: Organic L-Theanine (from Green Tea)
4115.description: L-Theanine is an amino acid found primarily in green tea leaves. It is known for its calming effects, modulation of brain neurotransmitters, and ability to promote relaxation without drowsiness.
4115.benefits: May improve relaxation, may reduce stress, may enhance focus, may help with mild anxiety

4120.name: Organic Cranberry Juice Concentrate
4120.description: Concentrated cranberry juice reconstituted with water, used as a flavoring and source of natural phytochemicals.
4120.benefits: Source of antioxidants and phytochemicals, provides natural flavor and nutrients
4120.risks: High natural sugar content, potential digestive upset with excessive intake

4144.name: Organic Blueberry Flavor
4144.description: Flavoring derived from organic blueberries or their extracts, used to impart blueberry taste in foods. Typically considered a food ingredient; organic designation implies avoidance of synthetic pesticides.
4144.benefits: Provides natural blueberry aroma and taste, may contain trace antioxidants from blueberries

sources.label: Flavor compounds in blueberries

4218.name: Mushroom Glycolipids
4218.description: Mushroom glycolipids are lipid molecules derived from fungi, primarily consisting of a carbohydrate (glyco-) moiety linked to a lipid (fat) component. They are studied for their potential use as natural emulsifiers and bioactive compounds in food products due to their amphiphilic properties.
4218.benefits: Potential antioxidant properties, possible cholesterol-lowering effects, natural emulsifier
4218.risks: Insufficient human safety data, possible allergenicity, unknown long-term effects

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Mushrooms as a source of glycolipids with health potential

4289.name: Arginine Nitrate
4289.description: Inorganic compound commonly found in vegetables, water, and as a food additive; used as a preservative and color fixative in processed meats.
4289.benefits: Preserves food by inhibiting microbial growth, extends shelf life, and maintains color in cured meats
4289.risks: Potential formation of carcinogenic nitrosamines under acidic or high-heat conditions, contamination in drinking water leading to methemoglobinemia especially in infants

4346.name: Organic Pomegranate Flavor
4346.description: Flavoring additive derived to mimic or enhance pomegranate taste, may be natural or artificial compounds designed for food and beverage applications.
4346.benefits: Flavor enhancement, improves palatability of products
4346.risks: Potential allergen, possible irritant or sensitizer in sensitive individuals, lack of transparency in chemical composition

4357.name: Black Carrot Concentrate (Color)
4357.description: Natural colorants derived from grape and black carrot, rich in anthocyanin pigments used for food coloring.
4357.benefits: Natural coloring agent, antioxidant properties, derived from food sources
4357.risks: Potential allergic sensitization in sensitive individuals, possible contamination depending on extraction process

4375.name: Black Carrot Extract
4375.description: Extract derived from black carrots, primarily containing anthocyanins and other phenolic compounds used as natural colorants and antioxidants.
4375.risks: Low irritation potential, possible allergen in sensitive individuals, minimal contamination risk at typical use levels

4416.name: Purified Carbonated Water
4416.description: Purified carbonated water is water into which carbon dioxide gas under pressure has been dissolved. It's commonly used as a base in soft drinks and some other beverages. Purified means that the water has undergone processes to remove impurities, ensuring a higher level of cleanliness.
4416.risks: May leach minerals from the body, ultra-processed, associated with microplastic exposure

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Benefits and Risks of Carbonated Water

4428.name: Guayusa (Ilex Guayusa) Leaf Extract
4428.description: Guayusa is a caffeinated leaf from the holly tree native to the Amazon rainforest, traditionally consumed as a tea. The extract is concentrated in caffeine, polyphenols, and other bioactive compounds, often used in energy drinks or supplements for its stimulating effects.
4428.benefits: Antioxidant effects, mild cognitive enhancement, increased alertness, potential anti-inflammatory effects
4428.risks: Caffeine-related side effects (anxiety, heart palpitations, insomnia), possible elevated blood pressure, insufficient long-term safety studies

sources.label: Toxicological and Pharmacological Profile of Ilex guayusa

4452.name: Organic Gum Acacia
4452.description: Gum Acacia, also known as gum arabic, is a natural gum derived from the hardened sap of the Acacia tree. It is commonly used as an emulsifier, thickening agent, and stabilizer in food products. It's considered a prebiotic fiber, supporting gut health, and is Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by the FDA.
4452.benefits: Prebiotic fiber, supports gut microbiota, may improve satiety, well-tolerated in moderate amounts
4452.risks: Possible mild digestive discomfort at high intakes, rare allergic reactions

4567.name: Carbonated Spring Water
4567.description: Water sourced from a natural spring, infused with carbon dioxide gas for carbonation.
4567.benefits: Hydration, alternative to still water with sensory variation

4568.name: Trisodium citrate
4568.description: Trisodium citrate is the trisodium salt of citric acid used primarily as an acidity regulator and buffering agent in food products.
4568.benefits: Regulates acidity, acts as a buffering agent, stabilizes pH in food and beverages
4568.risks: Low irritation potential, excessive intake may affect electrolyte balance

sources.label: PMID 10866609 - Safety and use of citrate salts as food additives
PMID 22901939 - Food additives: Trisodium citrate as an acidity regulator

4569.name: Dextrose Monohydrate
4569.description: Dextrose monohydrate is a crystalline form of glucose used primarily as a sweetener and energy source in foods and pharmaceuticals.
4569.benefits: Rapidly absorbed carbohydrate source providing quick energy
4569.risks: Excessive intake associated with elevated blood glucose, potential contribution to weight gain and metabolic imbalance

4579.name: Calcium lactate gluconate
4579.description: Calcium lactate gluconate is a calcium salt compound used primarily as a calcium supplement and food additive to fortify calcium content.
4579.benefits: Calcium source, supports bone health and calcium homeostasis
4579.risks: None at typical dietary supplementation levels

sources.label: Calcium - Dietary Supplements Fact Sheet - NIH

4583.name: Concord Grape Juice Concentrate
4583.description: Concord grape juice concentrate is created by removing a portion of the water from Concord grape juice, resulting in a syrup-like product used as a natural sweetener and flavoring in foods. It contains natural sugars, polyphenols, and antioxidants, but is more calorie-dense than whole grapes and lacks significant fiber.
4583.benefits: Contains antioxidants, polyphenols, potential cardiovascular benefits, source of vitamins
4583.risks: High sugar content, increased glycemic load compared to whole fruit, potential contribution to dental caries

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Cardiometabolic health effects of Concord grape

4588.name: Natural Orange Flavor
4588.description: Flavoring derived from orange, used to impart citrus aroma and taste.
4588.risks: Possible mild irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, lack of transparency in composition

4601.name: Vitamin B5 (Pantothenic Acid)
4601.description: Water-soluble B vitamin essential for synthesizing coenzyme A, involved in energy metabolism and synthesis of fatty acids and hormones.
4601.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, synthesis of fatty acids, steroids, and neurotransmitters
4601.risks: None at typical dietary intake; high doses may cause minor gastrointestinal discomfort

sources.label: PMC4273027 – Role of Vitamin B5 in human nutrition and metabolism
Pantothenic acid: nutritional role and safety

4603.name: Vegan Vitashine Vitamin D3
4603.description: Vitamin D3 is a fat-soluble vitamin essential for calcium homeostasis and bone health. Vegan sources are typically derived from lichen or synthetic processes rather than animal sources.
4603.benefits: Supports bone health, calcium absorption, immune function
4603.risks: Excessive intake can cause hypercalcemia, potential toxicity at very high doses

4611.name: Carbonated Coconut Water
4611.description: Coconut water is a clear liquid from young coconuts, naturally rich in electrolytes including potassium, magnesium, and sodium. Carbonation refers to the addition of dissolved carbon dioxide gas, giving it a fizzy texture but not significantly altering the base nutritional profile.
4611.benefits: Hydration, provides electrolytes (potassium, magnesium), low calorie
4611.risks: Potential digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals (from carbonation), rarely high potassium in kidney disease

4613.name: Organic Watermelon Juice
4613.description: Juice extracted from organically grown watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), containing water, natural sugars, vitamins A and C, antioxidants, and the amino acid citrulline. Typically consumed for its hydrating and nutritional properties.
4613.benefits: Hydration, source of antioxidants, contains vitamins A and C, provides citrulline which may support vascular health

4627.name: Potassium Metabisulfite
4627.description: An inorganic compound used as a preservative and antioxidant in food and beverages to prevent spoilage and discoloration.
4627.benefits: Preservative, antioxidant, prevents microbial growth and spoilage
4627.risks: Irritation, sulfite sensitivity including allergic reactions and asthma exacerbation, potential respiratory sensitizer

sources.label: Sulfite sensitivity and allergic reactions - PubMed 11139778
Use of sulfites as preservatives - PubMed 17693978

4629.name: Organic Elderberry Juice from Concentrate
4629.description: Elderberry juice is derived from the fruit of the Sambucus nigra plant and is used for its antioxidant content and potential immune-supporting properties. When labeled 'from concentrate,' water is removed and then added back, often involving heat processing.
4629.benefits: Rich in anthocyanins, antioxidant activity, may support immune function
4629.risks: Possible allergic reactions, mild gastrointestinal discomfort

4645.name: Organic Raw Honey
4645.description: Natural sweetener produced by bees from nectar, minimally processed to retain enzymes and bioactive compounds.
4645.benefits: Natural sweetener, contains trace antioxidants and enzymes, minimal processing preserves some bioactive compounds
4645.risks: Potential for botulism in infants under 1 year, high sugar content leading to dental caries and elevated calorie intake

4658.name: Organic Hibiscus Flower
4658.description: Organic hibiscus flower refers to the dried petals of Hibiscus sabdariffa, grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. It's used in teas, beverages, and supplements, recognized for its deep red color and tart flavor. In the body, hibiscus has been studied for its antioxidant properties and effects on blood pressure regulation.
4658.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, may support healthy blood pressure, potential cholesterol-lowering effects, anti-inflammatory properties
4658.risks: Potential interaction with antihypertensive drugs, may lower blood pressure excessively at high doses, possible allergic reactions

4667.name: Sour Cherry Juice Concentrate
4667.description: Sour cherry juice concentrate is a reduced, highly concentrated form of sour cherry juice, commonly used as a flavoring, sweetener, or coloring in foods and beverages. It retains many of the bioactive compounds found in whole sour cherries, including polyphenols and anthocyanins, which have antioxidant properties.
4667.benefits: Antioxidant properties, anti-inflammatory effects, may improve recovery after exercise, may benefit sleep quality
4667.risks: High natural sugar content, possible dental caries risk if consumed in excess

4739.name: Organic Ashwagandha Root Extract (KSM-66)
4739.description: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) root extract is a traditional adaptogenic herb used in Ayurvedic medicine. It is valued for its potential to reduce stress, improve cognitive function, and support immune health. Organic certification indicates cultivation without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Generally recognized as safe for consumption in recommended doses.
4739.benefits: Stress reduction, anti-anxiety effects, improved cognitive function, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant support, potential immune modulation
4739.risks: Mild gastrointestinal upset, potential interactions with sedatives, thyroid medications, or immunosuppressants

4750.name: Partially Hydrogenated Soybean Oil
4750.description: Soybean oil that has undergone partial hydrogenation to increase shelf life and stability, resulting in trans fat formation.
4750.benefits: Improved shelf life and stability compared to native soybean oil
4750.risks: Contains trans fatty acids associated with increased cardiovascular disease risk, regulatory restrictions on use

sources.label: PMC3650507 - Health effects of trans fatty acids
FDA Regulatory Action on PHOs

4764.name: BHA (Butylated Hydroxyanisole)
4764.description: Synthetic antioxidant used as a preservative to prevent oxidation and rancidity in fats and oils.
4764.benefits: Prevents oxidation and spoilage of fats, extends shelf life of food products
4764.risks: Potential carcinogenicity in rodents, endocrine disruption, allergic sensitization

sources.label: PMID 28227951 - Health effects and safety of food antioxidants including BHA
PMID 15769104 - Carcinogenicity and endocrine activity of BHA

4906.name: Artificial Flavor
4906.description: Synthetic chemical compounds added to foods to mimic natural flavors and enhance taste.
4906.benefits: Enhances flavor and palatability of food products
4906.risks: Possible allergic reactions, irritant or sensitizer potential, ultra-processed, may contain solvents or byproducts

sources.label: PMC6543468 - Safety assessment of flavoring substances

4926.name: Organic Shiitake Mushroom Extract
4926.description: Shiitake mushroom extract is a concentrated form derived from Lentinula edodes, commonly known as shiitake mushrooms. It contains bioactive compounds such as polysaccharides (notably lentinan), eritadenine, sterols, and various micronutrients, and is used for its potential immunomodulatory, antioxidant, and lipid-lowering properties.
4926.benefits: Immune modulation, antioxidant effects, cholesterol-lowering, potential anti-inflammatory properties
4926.risks: Allergic reaction (rare), possible digestive discomfort at high doses

4936.name: Himalayan Salt
4936.description: A form of rock salt mined from regions near the Himalayas, chemically similar to regular salt (sodium chloride) and used as a seasoning or preservative.
4936.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission and fluid balance
4936.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake, potential contamination with trace minerals but generally low levels

4981.name: Raspberry Extract
4981.description: Raspberry extract is a concentrated solution made from raspberries, often containing bioactive compounds such as ellagic acid, anthocyanins, and flavonoids. It is used both as a flavoring agent and as a potential health supplement.
4981.benefits: Antioxidant properties, anti-inflammatory potential, may support metabolic health (preliminary evidence)
4981.risks: Potential for allergic reaction in sensitive individuals, limited data on high-dose supplementation

4988.name: Carrot Powder
4988.description: Powdered form of dried carrots, used primarily as a natural colorant and flavoring agent with nutritional content including beta-carotene.
4988.benefits: Source of beta-carotene and antioxidants, natural colorant, provides some nutrients
4988.risks: Low irritation potential, possible allergen for sensitive individuals

5018.name: Organic Lion's Mane Extract
5018.description: Lion's mane (Hericium erinaceus) is a medicinal mushroom used in traditional medicine, known for its potential neuroprotective properties. Lion's mane extract is derived from the fruiting body or mycelium and is commonly marketed as a nootropic or cognitive-support supplement. The 'organic' label indicates it is grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Classified as GRAS (Generally Recognized As Safe) in supplemental use, but long-term safety data are limited.
5018.benefits: Neuroprotective effects, potential cognitive enhancement, anti-inflammatory properties, antioxidant activity
5018.risks: Rare allergic reactions, insufficient long-term safety data

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Hericium erinaceus review
Springer – Review on clinical effects of Lion's Mane mushroom

5031.name: Organic Stevia
5031.description: Organic stevia refers to extracts from the Stevia rebaudiana plant, typically processed into a calorie-free sweetener. It is used as a sugar substitute in food and beverage products, providing sweetness without raising blood glucose.
5031.benefits: Calorie-free, does not spike blood sugar, may support glucose management in diabetics
5031.risks: Possible bitter aftertaste, potential gut microbiome effects at high doses, may alter insulin sensitivity in select cases

5052.name: Retinyl Palmitate
5052.description: A synthetic ester of retinol (vitamin A) used in skincare for its provitamin A activity and skin renewal properties.
5052.benefits: Supports skin cell turnover and collagen production
5052.risks: Skin irritation, photosensitivity, potential teratogenicity at high systemic exposure, instability to light and air

sources.label: PMID 15685359 - Safety assessment of retinyl palmitate
PMID 18718926 - Retinyl esters and skin effects

5054.name: Cholecalciferol
5054.description: Cholecalciferol is Vitamin D3, a fat-soluble vitamin important for calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism.
