9284.risks: Caffeine-related side effects, potential liver toxicity in very high doses

9290.name: Niacinamide (B3)
9290.description: Niacinamide, also known as nicotinamide, is a water-soluble form of vitamin B3. It functions as a precursor for NAD+/NADP+ in the body, playing a critical role in cellular energy metabolism and DNA repair.
9290.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, essential nutrient, supports DNA repair, may improve skin health, may reduce inflammation
9290.risks: High-dose supplementation may cause liver toxicity, mild gastrointestinal discomfort, potential interactions with certain medications

sources.label: NCBI – Niacinamide Overview

9318.name: Prickly Pear Puree
9318.description: Prickly pear puree is made from the fruit of the Opuntia cactus. It is rich in antioxidants, dietary fiber, and vitamin C. Traditionally consumed in various cultures, it is noted for its phytochemicals and potential anti-inflammatory properties.
9318.benefits: High in antioxidants, source of vitamin C, supports immune function, anti-inflammatory effects, dietary fiber

9411.name: White Grape Juice from Concentrate
9411.description: Concentrated juice derived from white grapes, used as a sweetener and flavoring agent in food and beverages.
9411.benefits: Source of natural sugars for energy, contains small amounts of antioxidants and vitamins
9411.risks: High sugar content, potential dental caries risk, possible contribution to caloric excess

9525.name: Pumpkin
9525.description: Edible fruit commonly used as food, rich in fiber, vitamins (notably vitamin A), and minerals.
9525.benefits: Rich in dietary fiber, vitamin A precursors (beta-carotene), supports eye health and digestion
9525.risks: Rare allergic reactions, low risk of foodborne contamination if improperly handled

sources.label: Nutritional and health-promoting aspects of pumpkin fruit

9546.name: Beetroot Powder
9546.description: Powdered form of beetroot commonly used as a natural colorant in foods and beverages. Derived from red beet roots.
9546.benefits: Natural coloring agent, source of dietary nitrates which can support vascular function, contains antioxidants
9546.risks: Low allergenic potential, possible beeturia (pink urine) in some individuals, high nitrate content may affect sensitive individuals

sources.label: Clancy et al. 2009 - Dietary nitrate supplementation and vascular health
Rao et al. 2013 - Beetroot and beetroot juice: An antioxidant-rich functional food

9548.name: Hibiscus Extract
9548.description: Concentrated extract from Hibiscus sabdariffa flowers, used for flavoring and antioxidant properties.
9548.benefits: Contains antioxidants, may support cardiovascular health, used as natural colorant and flavor enhancer
9548.risks: Potential mild skin irritation or sensitization, possible hypotensive effect with excessive oral intake

sources.label: PMC5648960 - Hibiscus sabdariffa in the treatment of hypertension and hyperlipidemia: a review
PubMed 29064124 - Hibiscus sabdariffa L., an ancient functional food in therapeutic applications

9584.name: Natural Flavor (Grapefruit)
9584.description: Natural grapefruit flavor refers to chemically extracted compounds from grapefruit or substances synthesized to mimic grapefruit’s flavor, used as additives in foods and beverages. The specific formulation is proprietary and can include solvents, carriers, and preservatives alongside aromatic compounds.
9584.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents or preservatives, ultra-processed, possible undisclosed allergens, no nutritional value

9660.name: Organic Cordyceps Mushroom Extract
9660.description: Cordyceps Mushroom extract is derived from the Cordyceps genus of fungi, traditionally used in Chinese medicine. Its extracts contain bioactive compounds like cordycepin and polysaccharides, which may influence energy metabolism, immune function, and inflammation.
9660.benefits: Potential antioxidant properties, possible immune system support, may improve exercise performance, anti-inflammatory effects
9660.risks: Rare allergic reactions, limited safety data for long-term use, may interact with immunosuppressant drugs

9690.name: Mushroom Extract (to Protect Quality)
9690.description: Mushroom extract refers to a concentrated solution obtained from edible mushrooms, often used for its antioxidant and antimicrobial properties to extend the shelf life and maintain the quality of food products. The specific mushroom species is typically not listed, but common choices include shiitake or reishi due to their bioactive compounds.
9690.benefits: Antioxidant properties,potential antimicrobial activity,mild shelf-life extension

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Antimicrobial and antioxidant activities of mushroom extracts

9696.name: Passionfruit
9696.description: Passionfruit is the fruit of Passiflora edulis, commonly used for flavoring and as a source of vitamins and antioxidants.
9696.benefits: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants, natural flavoring agent
9696.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible irritation in high concentrations

sources.label: PMC study on antioxidant and nutritional properties of passionfruit
Allergy potential of passionfruit and related plants

9710.name: Lion's Mane
9710.description: Edible mushroom (Hericium erinaceus) used as a food and supplement ingredient. Contains bioactive compounds such as hericenones and erinacines.
9710.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, bioactive compounds with neuroprotective and cognitive support potential
9710.risks: Mild allergenic potential, possible gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals

9796.name: Passion Fruit Juice Concentrate
9796.description: Concentrated juice derived from passion fruit, used primarily as a flavoring and sweetening agent.
9796.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, contains some vitamins and antioxidants typical of passion fruit
9796.risks: Potential allergen for sensitive individuals, high sugar content if consumed in large amounts

9797.name: Mandarin Juice Concentrate
9797.description: Mandarin juice concentrate is made by removing water from mandarin orange juice, resulting in a thicker, sweeter product often used in processed foods and beverages. It retains most nutrients and bioactive compounds from mandarins, though concentration can mildly affect antioxidant content and flavor.
9797.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, flavonoids
9797.risks: High sugar content, caloric density, potential loss of heat-sensitive vitamins

9889.name: Natural Flavorings
9889.description: Likely a typographical variant of 'natural flavoring', which refers to flavor compounds derived from natural sources through various extraction and processing methods.
9889.risks: Lack of transparency, potential allergenicity, may contain residual solvents or processing chemicals, ultra-processed

sources.label: Study on safety and regulation of natural flavorings

9896.name: Additives
9896.description: \"Additives\" is a broad, non-specific term referring to substances added to food to modify its properties, such as taste, appearance, shelf life, or texture. Examples include preservatives, colorants, flavor enhancers, emulsifiers, and stabilizers. The safety and health impact of additives varies wildly depending on the specific compound. The lack of specificity in this label raises concerns regarding transparency and the possibility of including ingredients with potential health risks.
9896.risks: Lack of transparency, may include synthetic chemicals, potential for gut irritation, possible allergenic reactions, ultra-processed

9898.name: Organic Strawberry Juice from Concentrate
9898.description: Juice obtained by concentrating strawberry juice and then reconstituted to original concentration. Used as flavor and colorant ingredient in foods.
9898.benefits: Provides natural flavor, color, and some vitamins and antioxidants
9898.risks: Potential allergen for sensitive individuals, minimal risk at typical use levels

9912.name: Organic Lemon Juice from Concentrate
9912.description: Lemon juice concentrated by removal of water, reconstituted to achieve desired acidity and flavor.
9912.benefits: Provides vitamin C, organic acids, and flavoring
9912.risks: Acidic pH may cause dental enamel erosion with excessive exposure, potential minor allergen for citrus-sensitive individuals

9925.name: Natural Flavoring
9925.description: Complex mixture of volatile compounds extracted or synthesized to provide aroma and taste, derived from natural sources.
9925.benefits: Enhances flavor and aroma in food products
9925.risks: Potential allergenicity, lack of transparency, possible trace contaminants or solvents

sources.label: PMID 29843394 - Safety and regulatory aspects of natural flavorings

9942.name: Alpinia Galanga Root Extract
9942.description: Extract derived from the rhizome of Alpinia galanga, a plant in the ginger family, commonly used in traditional medicine and cosmetics.
9942.benefits: Antioxidant properties, antimicrobial effects, potential anti-inflammatory effects
9942.risks: Mild skin irritation, potential sensitization in sensitive individuals

9943.name: Natural Cola Flavor
9943.description: A complex mixture of natural extracts and essential oils designed to impart cola flavor in food and beverages.
9943.benefits: Provides flavor enhancement, improves taste profile of foods and beverages
9943.risks: Potential allergen or sensitizer for sensitive individuals, possible presence of trace contaminants from natural extracts, ultra-processed additive

9944.name: Natural Caramel Flavor
9944.description: Natural caramel flavor is a flavor additive produced by heating carbohydrates (typically sugars) and processing them to create a caramel-like taste. It may include additional natural or artificial compounds, solvents, and processing aids. Used to impart a sweet, caramelized flavor in processed foods and beverages.
9944.risks: Ultra-processed, lack of transparency, may contain additives or solvents, no nutritional value

9945.name: Cinnamon Extract
9945.description: Cinnamon extract is a concentrated form of the active compounds found in cinnamon bark, such as cinnamaldehyde and polyphenols. It is used in food and supplements for flavor and potential health effects, including blood sugar regulation and antioxidant activity.
9945.benefits: Antioxidant properties, potential blood sugar regulation, anti-inflammatory effects
9945.risks: Possible liver toxicity at high doses, allergic reactions, drug interactions

10119.name: Natural Flavourings
10119.description: Complex mixtures of aroma compounds extracted from natural sources used to enhance food flavor.
10119.benefits: Flavor enhancement at low usage levels
10119.risks: Allergenic potential, lack of transparency, possible contamination with allergens, ultra-processed

sources.label: PMC8026810 – Health implications of natural flavorings

10120.name: Pink Grapefruit Juice
10120.description: Pink grapefruit juice is the liquid extracted from the fruit of the pink grapefruit (Citrus × paradisi), known for its distinctive tart-sweet flavor and pink hue due to the presence of lycopene. It is a source of vitamin C, potassium, antioxidants, and other phytonutrients. In the body, it supports hydration, immune function, and acts as an antioxidant.
10120.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, source of antioxidants, may support immune system, hydration, contains potassium, contains lycopene
10120.risks: Interacts with certain medications, potential for high sugar content, acid can erode tooth enamel

10138.name: Black Carrot Juice
10138.description: Juice derived from black carrots, rich in anthocyanins used as a natural food colorant.
10138.risks: Possible allergenicity in sensitive individuals, mild irritation in rare cases

sources.label: Anthocyanin content and antioxidant potential of black carrot juice

10181.name: Natural Peach Flavor with Other Natural Flavors
10181.description: This ingredient refers to a blend of chemically extracted flavor compounds derived from peaches and other unspecified natural sources. The process often includes solvents, carriers, and additives not disclosed to consumers. While 'natural flavors' must be sourced from plants or animals, they are purified and manipulated, resulting in an ultra-processed product that provides no nutritional value. The formulation lacks transparency, and the specific sources and processing methods are rarely specified to consumers.
10181.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents or preservatives, ultra-processed, possible allergen exposure, no nutritional value

10199.name: Natural Flavours
10199.description: Complex mixtures of flavor compounds extracted from natural sources and/or synthesized, used to impart specific tastes and aromas in food and beverages.
10199.benefits: Enhances flavor and palatability of food and beverages
10199.risks: Lack of transparency, potential presence of solvent residues, possible allergens, ultra-processed nature, no nutritional value

sources.label: PMC8026810 – Health implications of flavor additives

10230.name: Apple Extract
10230.description: Concentrated preparation derived from apples, used primarily for flavor and aroma enhancement in food products.

10280.name: Natural Grapefruit Flavor
10280.description: Natural grapefruit flavor is a chemically extracted concentrate derived from grapefruit and/or its essential oils, used to impart citrus flavor to food products. The production process typically involves the use of solvents and processing aids, and the final composition may contain a mix of volatile compounds. This ingredient is regulated by the FDA as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS), but the exact formulation is usually proprietary and may include undisclosed additives.
10280.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents or preservatives, ultra-processed, potential allergenicity, no nutritional value

10468.name: Citra Hops
10468.description: Citra hops are a variety of hop (Humulus lupulus) commonly used in brewing to impart strong citrus and tropical fruit flavors and aromas to beverages, especially craft beers. They provide flavor, aroma, and some natural preservation due to their polyphenols and essential oils. Hops are generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA for use in foods and beverages.
10468.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, anti-inflammatory properties, potential mild antimicrobial effects
10468.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), estrogenic effects (very high intake), possible mild digestive discomfort

10470.name: Mosaic Hops
10470.description: Dried flower cones from the Humulus lupulus plant variety 'Mosaic,' used primarily as a flavoring and bittering agent in beer production.
10470.benefits: Natural flavoring and bittering agent in alcoholic beverages, contains bioactive compounds with antioxidant properties
10470.risks: Allergic sensitization, contact dermatitis, respiratory irritation from inhalation of dust

10519.name: Red Amaranth
10519.description: Red amaranth (Amaranthus cruentus or Amaranthus dubius) is a leafy green vegetable, known for its vibrant red or purple leaves. It is traditionally consumed as a food in many cultures and is valued for its nutrient density, offering high levels of vitamins (such as vitamin C, vitamin A), minerals (like calcium and iron), antioxidants, and dietary fiber. Red amaranth is minimally processed when used as a fresh green, and it is regarded as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) by the FDA when consumed as a food.
10519.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, high in vitamins and minerals, good source of dietary fiber, supports eye health, supports immune health, potential anti-inflammatory properties

10543.name: Indian Gooseberry
10543.description: Indian Gooseberry, also known as Amla (Emblica officinalis), is a fruit widely used in traditional medicine and as a dietary supplement. It is rich in vitamin C, polyphenols, and antioxidants. Amla is considered a whole food and is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) in food products.
10543.benefits: Antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory properties, supports immune function, may improve cholesterol profile, supports blood sugar regulation

10609.name: Natural Butter Flavor
10609.description: Complex mixture of flavor compounds derived from dairy to replicate butter taste, often combined with maltodextrin as a carrier or filler.
10609.benefits: Provides butter flavor without fat, used in flavor enhancement
10609.risks: Potential allergens from dairy source, processed additive, possible irritant, ultra-processed ingredient

sources.label: Maltodextrin: Properties and uses

10631.name: Natural Cucumber Flavor
10631.description: Natural cucumber flavor refers to flavoring compounds derived from cucumber or synthesized to mimic cucumber's taste, labeled as 'natural' according to FDA regulations. This ingredient is typically produced using extraction and purification processes, and can include added solvents or carriers. Its exact composition is not disclosed, leading to lack of transparency and potential inclusion of unlisted additives.
10631.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain added solvents or preservatives, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

10711.name: Red Grape Juice from Concentrate
10711.description: Grape juice concentrated by removing water, then reconstituted; primarily composed of sugars, organic acids, and phytochemicals from grapes.
10711.benefits: Provides hydration, source of antioxidants such as polyphenols, contains vitamins and minerals
10711.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental caries, lacks fiber, possible oxidation of sensitive compounds

sources.label: PMC5613902 - Health Benefits of Grape Polyphenols
Effects of Fruit Juice Consumption on Dental Health
Evaluation of Nutrient Composition in Fruit Juices from Concentrate

10751.name: Organic Peach Juice Concentrate
10751.description: Organic peach juice concentrate is a fruit-derived liquid produced by removing water from the juice of organically grown peaches. It is commonly used in foods and beverages as a natural sweetener and flavoring. The concentrate retains some vitamins and antioxidants present in peaches but is higher in sugar concentration and lower in fiber compared to whole fruit. As an organic product, it is produced without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers, and is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used as intended.
10751.benefits: Contains vitamins (such as vitamin C), provides antioxidants, natural source of some phytonutrients
10751.risks: High sugar content, lower fiber than whole fruit

sources.label: NCBI Bookshelf – Fruit Juice Concentrates and Health

10820.name: Hemp Seed Oil
10820.description: Hemp seed oil is a vegetable oil extracted from the seeds of the hemp plant. It contains a balanced ratio of omega-6 to omega-3 fatty acids and is rich in polyunsaturated fats. It is generally regarded as safe for food consumption and is valued for its nutritional profile.
10820.benefits: Rich in omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids, anti-inflammatory properties, supports cardiovascular health, contains vitamin E and antioxidants
10820.risks: Possible oxidation if highly processed, mild allergenicity in sensitive individuals

10844.name: Organic Acerola Extract
10844.description: Acerola extract is derived from the acerola cherry (Malpighia emarginata), a fruit known for its exceptionally high vitamin C content and antioxidant compounds. Organic acerola extract refers to the extract obtained from acerola cherries grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. It is commonly used as a natural source of vitamin C fortification in foods and supplements. The FDA generally recognizes acerola cherry as safe (GRAS) when used in food.
10844.benefits: Rich source of vitamin C, provides antioxidants, may support immune function

10845.name: Natural Pomegranate Flavor
10845.description: Natural pomegranate flavor is a proprietary blend of flavoring compounds derived from or made to resemble pomegranate, often using natural origin chemicals, solvents, and additives. It is highly processed and typically added to foods and beverages to impart a fruit-like flavor, but contains little to no actual pomegranate or its nutrients. Regulatory agencies such as the FDA consider 'natural flavors' generally recognized as safe (GRAS), but the disclosure of exact components is often lacking.
10845.risks: Lack of transparency, ultra-processed, may contain solvents or preservatives, no nutritional value

10870.name: Black Tea Essence
10870.description: Concentrated extract derived from organic black tea leaves, used for flavoring. Black tea contains bioactive compounds such as polyphenols and flavonoids which have antioxidant properties. It is generally recognized as safe for consumption and is valued for its flavor and mild stimulant effects due to caffeine content.
10870.benefits: Antioxidant properties, may improve cardiovascular health, provides mild cognitive stimulation
10870.risks: Caffeine sensitivity, potential for mild stimulant-related side effects such as insomnia and jitteriness

11018.name: Natural Black Cherry Flavor
11018.description: Natural Black Cherry Flavor is a flavoring made from natural sources, designed to mimic or enhance the taste of black cherries. While labeled 'natural,' these flavors are commonly manufactured using chemical extraction and may contain numerous undisclosed compounds, solvents, or preservatives. The production process is highly industrial, and the ingredient is considered ultra-processed. The FDA classifies natural flavors as GRAS (Generally Recognized As Safe), but their specific composition remains largely unregulated and undisclosed.
11018.risks: Lack of transparency, ultra-processed, may contain solvents or preservatives, no nutritional value

11196.name: Pink Himalayan Rock Salt
11196.description: Pink Himalayan rock salt is a type of salt mined from the Khewra Salt Mine near the Himalayas in Pakistan. It contains trace minerals like potassium, magnesium, and calcium, which impart its pink color. Its primary function is as a seasoning and preservative, much like regular table salt. The U.S. FDA considers salt (sodium chloride) generally recognized as safe (GRAS) when used in food.
11196.benefits: Source of trace minerals, essential for electrolyte balance, necessary for nerve and muscle function
11196.risks: High sodium intake can increase blood pressure, excessive consumption may contribute to cardiovascular risk

sources.label: USDA Nutrition Data – Salt, Himalayan

11270.name: Clementine Juice Concentrate
11270.description: Clementine juice concentrate is produced by removing water from clementine juice to create a denser, shelf-stable product. Used mainly as a flavoring or sweetening ingredient, juice concentrates are more processed than fresh juice but retain many of the original juice's nutrients, such as vitamin C. The process may reduce certain phytonutrients and can increase sugar concentration per serving. Generally regarded as safe (GRAS) by the FDA.
11270.benefits: Source of vitamin C, provides antioxidants, natural flavor
11270.risks: Higher sugar concentration, potential loss of some phytonutrients through processing

11300.name: Dark Sweet Cherry Juice Concentrate
11300.description: Dark sweet cherry juice concentrate is produced by removing water from the juice of dark sweet cherries (Prunus avium), typically to increase shelf life and sweetness. It contains naturally occurring sugars, vitamins, minerals, and polyphenols such as anthocyanins, which are responsible for the deep red color. It is sometimes used as a natural flavoring or sweetener in foods and beverages. The ingredient is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used as intended.
11300.benefits: Contains polyphenols, antioxidant activity, source of vitamin C, potential support for inflammation reduction, possible support for muscle recovery
11300.risks: High sugar content, potential for elevated blood glucose, caloric density

11397.name: Clarified Pineapple Juice Concentrate
11397.description: Pineapple juice concentrate that has been filtered to remove solids and impurities, resulting in a clear liquid with concentrated sugars and flavor compounds.
11397.benefits: Provides natural sugars and flavor, source of some vitamins and antioxidants from pineapple
11397.risks: High sugar content, potential for dental caries with excessive consumption, possible minor allergenicity

11435.name: Non-GMO Digestion Resistant Maltodextrin
11435.description: A modified polysaccharide used as a soluble dietary fiber and bulking agent, derived from starch and resistant to digestion in the small intestine.
11435.benefits: Source of soluble fiber, supports digestive health, may improve bowel regularity
11435.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort (bloating, gas) at high intake, ultra-processed carbohydrate

11484.name: Natural Orange Extract
11484.description: Natural orange extract is a flavoring made by extracting aromatic compounds from orange peel or oil, typically using alcohol or other solvents. It is used as a flavor enhancer in food products, providing a citrus aroma and taste. As a flavoring, it is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA, though its composition can be variable depending on the extraction process and may involve minor undisclosed additives.
11484.benefits: Flavor enhancement, may contain trace antioxidants
11484.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain undisclosed solvents or carriers, potential for ultra-processing

11558.name: Elderflower Extract
11558.description: Elderflower extract is derived from the blossoms of the Sambucus nigra plant. Traditionally used in herbal medicine, elderflower is valued for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and potential immune-supporting properties. In food products, it is mainly used for its floral flavor and aromatic qualities. Elderflower extract is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) when used according to intended food applications.
11558.benefits: Antioxidant activity, potential anti-inflammatory properties, mild immune support
11558.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), mild gastrointestinal upset (in large quantities)

11561.name: Lime Peel Extract
11561.description: Lime peel extract is derived from the outer skin of the lime (Citrus aurantiifolia or Citrus latifolia). It is rich in antioxidants, flavonoids, and essential oils such as limonene. In food applications, it is used as a flavoring or preservative due to its aromatic compounds and natural antimicrobial properties. There is no FDA GRAS (Generally Recognized As Safe) status specifically for lime peel extract, but limonene and natural citrus oils are generally considered safe for consumption in typical amounts.
11561.benefits: Antioxidant activity, antimicrobial properties, potential anti-inflammatory effect
11561.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible phototoxicity in large amounts

11596.name: Natural Pineapple Flavor
11596.description: Natural pineapple flavor refers to flavor compounds derived from pineapples or created from other plant or animal sources to mimic pineapple's taste. While labeled 'natural,' such flavors are often obtained through extraction, concentration, or enzymatic processes, and may contain carrier solvents, emulsifiers, or preservatives. The FDA generally recognizes natural flavors as GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe), but the exact composition is not required to be disclosed, leading to potential transparency concerns.
11596.risks: Lack of transparency, ultra-processed, may contain solvents or preservatives, possible allergens

11629.name: Patented Liquid Silica
11629.description: Patented liquid silica refers to a proprietary, soluble formulation of silicon (often as orthosilicic acid or stabilized silica), marketed for potential health benefits such as supporting skin, hair, nails, and connective tissues. Silica is naturally found in foods and is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in its purified forms (e.g. silicon dioxide) as a food additive. However, 'patented' formulations may contain undisclosed additives and their bioavailability and efficacy can vary by brand.
11629.benefits: Essential trace mineral, supports connective tissue, may improve skin, hair, nail strength
11629.risks: Possible contamination with additives or preservatives, unsubstantiated health claims, overconsumption may lead to mild kidney issues

11630.name: Purified Spring Water
11630.description: Purified spring water is water sourced from a spring and then processed to remove impurities and contaminants such as bacteria, viruses, and chemical pollutants. It is commonly used as a base ingredient in beverages and processed foods. While it must meet safety standards and is considered safe for general consumption, it contains no nutrients and offers no particular health benefit beyond hydration.

sources.label: FDA – Bottled Water: Everything You Need to Know

11700.name: Natural Lemon and Lime Flavourings
11700.description: Flavoring derived from lemon or its components, used to impart lemon aroma and taste in food and beverages.
11700.benefits: Provides natural lemon aroma and taste, enhances flavor profile in food and beverages
11700.risks: Potential for allergic reactions, possible irritation in sensitive individuals, variability in composition due to manufacturing processes

sources.label: Chemical composition and sensory evaluation of lemon flavorings

11907.name: Isobutane
11907.description: A branched alkane hydrocarbon used primarily as a propellant in aerosol cleaning products. Classified as a flammable gas with low acute toxicity but potential inhalation hazard at high concentrations.
11907.benefits: Effective propellant for aerosol products, low toxicity under normal use concentrations
11907.risks: Flammability, asphyxiation risk in confined spaces, mild respiratory irritation at high concentrations

sources.label: ECHA Isobutane Registration Dossier - Eye and Skin Irritation
Assessment of inhalation risks from hydrocarbon propellants

11927.name: Organic Reishi Extract
11927.description: Organic Reishi extract is a concentrated preparation derived from the fruiting body or mycelium of Ganoderma lucidum, commonly known as Reishi or Lingzhi mushroom. It is used in traditional medicine and marketed for its potential health-promoting properties, including immunomodulation and antioxidant activity. The ‘organic’ designation means the mushrooms are grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. There is no FDA GRAS status, but it is widely consumed as a supplement.
11927.benefits: Immunomodulatory effects, anti-inflammatory properties, antioxidant activity, possible support for liver health
11927.risks: Possible interaction with anticoagulants, mild digestive upset, allergic reactions

11957.name: White Sugar
11957.description: Refined sucrose commonly used as a sweetener in food and beverages.
11957.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain and dental caries

12081.name: Raspberry Juice from Concentrate
12081.description: Raspberry juice concentrated and reconstituted; used as flavor and color additive in foods and beverages.
12081.benefits: Source of natural flavor compounds and antioxidants

sources.label: Antioxidant properties of raspberry juice concentrate

12294.name: Humic Acid
12294.description: Complex mixture of organic acids derived from the decomposition of plant and microbial material in soil, often used as a soil conditioner or dietary supplement.
12294.benefits: May improve nutrient absorption in soil applications, proposed benefits in gut health though evidence limited
12294.risks: Potential contamination with heavy metals or toxins depending on source, ingestion toxicity at high doses not well studied

sources.label: PMC7273734 - Humic substances: structures, properties, and potential applications
PubMed 31432242 - Overview on humic substances and their role in agriculture and environment

12358.name: L-Cysteine Hydrochloride
12358.description: A derivative of the amino acid cysteine used primarily as a food additive to improve dough conditioning and texture in bakery products.
12358.benefits: Improves dough elasticity and texture, enhances baking performance
12358.risks: Irritation risk to eyes, skin, respiratory tract upon exposure, potential allergen, contamination risk from manufacturing processes

sources.label: Safety assessment of amino acid-derived food additives
Occupational exposure and sensitization to cysteine derivatives

12378.name: Quinine
12378.description: Quinine is an alkaloid used primarily as a bitter flavoring agent in tonic water beverages. It has historical medicinal use for malaria but is now consumed mainly in beverages at low doses.
12378.benefits: Provides bitter flavor characteristic of tonic water
12378.risks: Potential for hypersensitivity reactions and rare serious adverse effects at high doses, photosensitivity, possible cardiac effects in overdose, ingestion toxicity at supratherapeutic levels

12471.name: Black Tea Extract
12471.description: Concentrated extract derived from black tea leaves containing polyphenols and caffeine.
12471.benefits: Source of antioxidants, may support antioxidant activity
12471.risks: Irritation or sensitization on skin contact in sensitive individuals, potential caffeine-related effects if ingested in large amounts

sources.label: PMC6313445 - Overview of black tea polyphenols and health
PubMed 29927287 - Skin sensitization potential of tea extracts

12897.name: Natural Flavourings including Quinine
12897.description: Natural flavourings are chemically extracted compounds derived from plant or animal sources, labeled as 'natural' but often highly processed and non-specific. Quinine is a bitter alkaloid extracted from the bark of the cinchona tree, commonly used as a flavoring in tonic water and classified as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) by the FDA for limited use in beverages.
12897.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain undisclosed solvents or carriers, possible allergenic compounds, excessive quinine intake may cause cinchonism (nausea, tinnitus, visual disturbances), not suitable for pregnancy in high doses

12898.name: Sodium Saccharin
12898.description: Synthetic non-nutritive sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories.
12898.benefits: Calorie-free sweetness, useful for sugar reduction and diabetes management
12898.risks: Potential allergenic reactions, controversies about carcinogenicity though low risk at approved levels, not metabolized by body

sources.label: NTP Report on Saccharin Carcinogenicity
Review on Safety of Artificial Sweeteners

12938.name: Cardamom Extract
12938.description: Cardamom extract is derived from the seeds of Elettaria cardamomum, a spice widely used for flavoring and medicinal purposes. It contains volatile oils like cineole, terpinene, and limonene, and is known for its strong aromatic properties. Cardamom extract is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in typical food quantities.
12938.benefits: Antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory effects, possible blood pressure reduction, digestive health support, potential antimicrobial properties

12986.name: Calcium beta-Hydroxy-beta-Methylbutyrate Monohydrate (HMB-Ca)
12986.description: Calcium is an essential mineral important for bone health, muscle function, and nerve transmission. Present at 2 mg/L concentration.
12986.benefits: Supports bone mineralization, muscle contraction, nerve signaling
12986.risks: None at typical dietary or environmental concentrations

13192.name: Orange Blossom
13192.description: Orange blossom refers to the fragrant flower of the orange tree (Citrus aurantium), commonly used in culinary applications as a flavoring or garnish, and in traditional medicine and aromatherapy. Orange blossom water is also a byproduct of distilling these flowers. As a minimally processed, plant-based ingredient, it is generally considered safe for food use and is not classified as an additive requiring FDA GRAS status when used in traditional forms.
13192.benefits: Contains flavonoids and antioxidants, aromatic compounds may support relaxation
13192.risks: Rare allergic reaction, potential pesticide exposure if not organic

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Essential oils from Citrus aurantium flowers: composition and therapeutic properties
FDA – Substances Generally Recognized as Safe

13257.name: Seedless Raspberry Purée
13257.description: Purée made from raspberries, containing natural sugars, dietary fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants.
13257.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, antioxidants, natural flavoring
13257.risks: Irritation possible in sensitive individuals due to acidity, potential allergen in rare cases

13322.name: Organic Blackberry Flavor
13322.description: Organic blackberry flavor is a food ingredient comprised of volatile aromatic compounds isolated or synthesized to mimic the taste and aroma of blackberries. Even when labeled 'organic,' this ingredient is typically processed and lacks meaningful nutritional content. The 'flavor' designation means it could include multiple substances besides direct extracts, often utilizing organic carriers and solvents.
13322.risks: Lack of transparency, ultra-processed, may mask use of synthetic carriers, no nutritional value

13357.name: INS 331iii (Trisodium Citrate)
13357.description: Trisodium citrate, designated as INS 331(iii), is the trisodium salt of citric acid. It is widely used as a food additive for its buffering, anticoagulant, and preservative properties. Recognized as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) by the FDA, it is commonly found in processed foods and beverages for pH regulation and flavor enhancement.
13357.benefits: Regulates acidity, enhances stability, extends shelf life, generally recognized as safe
13357.risks: Excessive intake may cause mild gastrointestinal upset, very rare allergic reactions

sources.label: NCBI – Trisodium Citrate
EFSA – Re-evaluation of citric acid and its salts

13396.name: Organic Blood Orange Juice from Concentrate
13396.description: Organic blood orange juice from concentrate is produced by removing water from organic blood orange juice and later reconstituting it with water, allowing for easier storage and transport. Blood oranges are a variety of citrus known for their high vitamin C and antioxidant anthocyanin content. The concentrate process may slightly reduce some volatile compounds and nutrient density compared to fresh juice, but it generally retains most of its nutritional value. 'Organic' labeling indicates production without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. This ingredient is regarded as safe (GRAS) by the FDA.

13400.name: Organic Black Carrot Juice from Concentrate
13400.description: Juice derived from black carrots concentrated by removal of water; contains anthocyanins and natural sugars.
13400.benefits: Source of anthocyanin antioxidants, natural colorant, provides vitamins and minerals found in black carrots
13400.risks: Potential allergenicity, natural sugars contributing to caloric intake, risk of oxidative instability due to anthocyanins

sources.label: Anthocyanins in black carrot: Composition and health effects
Safety and beneficial properties of anthocyanins from black carrots

13425.name: Grapefruit Juice Concentrate
13425.description: Concentrated form of grapefruit juice obtained by removing water content, used for flavor and sweetness.
13425.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, source of vitamin C and antioxidants
13425.risks: Potential interaction with certain medications due to furanocoumarins, possible allergen, minor irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Drug interactions with grapefruit juice: Clinical implications
Grapefruit Juice and its Potential Health Effects

13549.name: Di(2-ethylhexyl) Adipate (DEHA)
13549.description: DEHA is a plasticizer commonly used in plastics and food contact materials to enhance flexibility. It is not a food ingredient itself but may migrate into foods from packaging. DEHA has been evaluated for safety and is generally considered safe at low exposure levels, but high exposures may present health concerns.
13549.risks: Potential endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity at high doses, liver effects in animal studies, accumulation from packaging migration

sources.label: EFSA assessment on adipates migration from food contact materials

13551.name: Benzyl Butyl Phthalate (BBP)
13551.description: Benzyl Butyl Phthalate (BBP) is a synthetic plasticizer used primarily in plastics and personal care products to increase flexibility. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material due to its endocrine-disrupting properties and potential toxicity upon exposure, including via inhalation or skin contact.
13551.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, potential carcinogen, harmful to aquatic life, suspected developmental toxicant

13556.name: Dimethyl Phthalate (DMP)
13556.description: Dimethyl Phthalate is a synthetic chemical commonly used as a plasticizer and solvent in fragrances and personal care products. It is not a food ingredient. DMP is known for its role in making materials more flexible and as a fixative in perfumes.
13556.benefits: Effective plasticizer, solvent, and fragrance fixative
13556.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, developmental toxicity, potential carcinogenicity, environmental persistence

sources.label: Toxicity of dimethyl phthalate and exposure risks

13560.name: Di-n-butyl Phthalate (DBP)
13560.description: Di-n-butyl Phthalate (DBP) is a synthetic chemical used primarily as a plasticizer in various consumer products, including cosmetics and fragrances. It is not a food ingredient. DBP is known to be endocrine-disrupting and has been banned or heavily restricted in many countries for certain uses due to reproductive and developmental toxicity risks.
13560.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, developmental toxicity, potential carcinogen, environmental pollutant

13628.name: Pasteurized 100% Carbonated Apple Juice from U.S. Grown Fresh Apples
13628.description: A beverage made by juicing fresh apples grown in the United States, then pasteurizing the juice to kill pathogens, and infusing it with carbon dioxide to create carbonation. Pasteurization preserves food safety while carbonation provides effervescence. Contains natural fruit sugars, minor vitamins, and antioxidants from the apples.
13628.benefits: Source of vitamin C (if not heat-degraded), contains polyphenols and antioxidants, hydrating, provides natural fruit flavor
13628.risks: Natural sugar content, may cause dental erosion if consumed excessively, potential for mild digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals

13666.name: Natural Raspberry Flavour
13666.description: Synthetic or natural flavoring compounds designed to mimic the taste of raspberry, used to enhance flavor in food products.
13666.benefits: Enhances flavor and consumer acceptance of food products
13666.risks: Possible irritant or sensitizer in susceptible individuals, potential processing with solvents, limited transparency on exact chemical composition

sources.label: PMCID: PMC3860165 – Safety evaluation of food flavorings

14069.name: Mandarin Flavor
14069.description: Mandarin flavor typically refers to an artificial or natural flavoring compound formulated to mimic the taste of mandarin oranges. Most commercial products use a combination of natural extracts and synthetic chemicals that are not disclosed in detail. These flavors are highly processed, can contain solvents or carriers, and are regulated by agencies such as the FDA but do not provide nutritional value. Labeling is often vague, and the actual source and formulation are rarely transparent to consumers.
14069.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents or preservatives, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

14148.name: Melon Juice Concentrate
14148.description: Juice derived from melon fruit, concentrated to reduce water content, used as a flavoring or sweetening agent in foods and beverages.
14148.benefits: Provides flavor, natural sweetness, contains some vitamins and antioxidants
14148.risks: Potential allergen for sensitive individuals, sugar content contributing to caloric intake

14171.name: Soursop Juice
14171.description: Juice extracted from the fruit of Annona muricata (soursop), consumed as a beverage.
14171.benefits: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants, hydrating beverage
14171.risks: Potential neurotoxicity from annonacin with excessive consumption, possible allergic reactions, microbial contamination risk if not pasteurized

14193.name: Potassium Gluconate
14193.description: Potassium salt of gluconic acid used primarily as a mineral supplement to provide potassium.
14193.benefits: Provides potassium which is essential for electrolyte balance, nerve transmission, and muscle function
14193.risks: Excessive intake can cause hyperkalemia especially in individuals with kidney impairment

sources.label: PMID 160273 – Role of potassium in human health
PMID 25636782 – Potassium supplements and safety

14196.name: Kale Powder
14196.description: Dehydrated and powdered form of kale, a leafy green vegetable rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.
14196.benefits: High in vitamins A, C, K, antioxidants, dietary fiber, supports nutrient intake
14196.risks: Potential oxalate content affecting kidney stone risk in susceptible individuals, possible pesticide residues depending on cultivation

14209.name: Organic Red Beet Juice Concentrate
14209.description: A natural coloring agent derived from red beets, used to impart red/purple color in food products. Contains betalains and other antioxidants. Recognized as safe by FDA as a color additive exempt from certification.
14209.benefits: Natural colorant, contains antioxidants like betalains, may have anti-inflammatory properties, improves food appeal
14209.risks: Possible allergic reaction in rare cases, beeturia (red urine) which is harmless

sources.label: FDA Organic Red Beet Concentrate Color Additive Status

14234.name: Anthocyanins
14234.description: Water-soluble pigments found in many fruits and vegetables responsible for red, purple, and blue colors.
14234.risks: Rare allergenicity, generally low irritation potential

sources.label: PMC4144270 - Anthocyanins: antioxidant and health benefits

14311.name: Quinine Hydrochloride
14311.description: Quinine hydrochloride is a synthetically derived salt form of quinine, originally extracted from the bark of the cinchona tree. It is used as a flavoring agent in food and beverages, notably tonic water, to provide a bitter taste. Quinine is also a well-known antimalarial drug, but in foods and drinks, its use is heavily regulated. The FDA restricts the amount of quinine allowed in beverages due to potential toxicity at high doses; it is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) in low concentrations.
14311.risks: Cinchonism (nausea, headache, tinnitus, visual disturbances at higher doses), allergic reactions, hemolytic anemia (in susceptible individuals), potential drug interactions, risk for arrhythmia

sources.label: FDA – Quinine and quinine salts in food

14316.name: Natural Caffeine (Green Coffee Beans)
14316.description: Caffeine is a central nervous system stimulant naturally found in green coffee beans. It is used to increase alertness and reduce fatigue.
14316.benefits: Increased alertness, cognitive performance enhancement, mild metabolic stimulation
14316.risks: Irritation at high doses, potential for dependence, sleep disruption with excessive intake

14334.name: Natural Identical Soursop Flavor
14334.description: Natural identical soursop flavor refers to flavor compounds chemically synthesized to be molecularly identical to those found in natural soursop fruit (Annona muricata). Used in processed foods and beverages to mimic the taste of soursop, these are not extracted directly from the fruit but rather created from other natural or synthetic sources. Often grouped with flavor additives, these undergo processing and may include solvents, carriers, or emulsifiers.
14334.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain ultra-processed compounds, potential presence of solvents or carriers, no nutritional value

14347.name: Pineapple Syrup
14347.description: Pineapple syrup is a sweetened liquid made by combining pineapple juice or concentrate with added sugar and sometimes preservatives or stabilizers. It is used as a sweetener and flavor enhancer in beverages, desserts, and processed foods. Pineapple syrup is not considered a whole food and is typically a source of added sugars. It is regarded as safe for consumption (GRAS) by the FDA when used in typical food amounts.
14347.risks: High in added sugars, may contribute to increased calorie intake, potential for increased risk of obesity and metabolic disease when consumed in excess

sources.label: FDA – Additives Affirmed as GRAS

14382.name: Organic Black Currant Juice Concentrate
14382.description: Concentrated extract of black currant fruit, typically rich in vitamin C, anthocyanins, and other antioxidants.

14427.name: Zinc Lactate
14427.description: Zinc lactate is a zinc salt of lactic acid used primarily as a dietary supplement and food additive to provide zinc, an essential trace mineral.
14427.benefits: Provides bioavailable zinc, supports immune function and enzymatic processes
14427.risks: Irritation at high doses, potential gastrointestinal discomfort with excessive ingestion

sources.label: PMID 23967368 - Zinc supplementation and immune function
PMID 23651578 - Safety and bioavailability of zinc compounds

14445.name: Nature Identical Flavouring Substances
14445.description: Synthetic or semi-synthetic compounds chemically identical to natural flavor molecules, used for imparting peach and passion fruit flavors.
14445.benefits: Consistent flavor profile, cost-effective alternative to natural extracts
14445.risks: Possible sensitization or allergic reactions, ultra-processed, lack of transparency in constituent chemicals

14449.name: Ammonium Hydrogen Carbonate
14449.description: Ammonium hydrogen carbonate is a leavening agent used in baking to release carbon dioxide and cause dough to rise.
14449.benefits: Effective leavening agent that promotes dough rising
14449.risks: Irritation to respiratory tract and mucous membranes from inhalation of dust, potential allergen cross-contact with sesame traces

14450.name: Natural and Nature Identical Flavouring Substances
14450.description: Compounds used to impart flavor, either extracted from natural sources or chemically synthesized to be identical to natural flavors.
14450.risks: Potential allergenicity, irritation, lack of transparency, ultra-processed, unknown solvents or additives

14490.name: Potato Protein
14490.description: Protein extracted from potatoes, used as a plant-based protein source in food products.
14490.benefits: Provides plant-based protein, supports muscle maintenance and repair
14490.risks: Potential allergenicity, limited data on sensitization

14495.name: Natural Flavor Identical to Passion Fruit
14495.description: This term refers to a chemically synthesized flavoring compound that replicates the taste profile of passion fruit. Although labeled 'natural', such flavors may be produced via chemical processes and may include solvents, preservatives, or carrier agents. These ingredients are regulated for safety (FDA GRAS) but lack transparency regarding their precise composition and source.
14495.risks: Lack of transparency, may include solvents or preservatives, ultra-processed, potential for allergic reactions, no nutritional value

14537.name: Orange Flavour
14537.description: A mixture of natural and/or synthetic flavoring compounds designed to impart an orange citrus taste and aroma, typically used at low concentrations in food products.
14537.benefits: Improves palatability and sensory appeal of food and beverage products
14537.risks: Potential dermal or respiratory sensitization, ingestion toxicity generally low at typical use levels, possibility of synthetic additive contaminants, ultra-processing

14547.name: Plant-Based Mineral Calcium
14547.description: Calcium is a mineral essential for bone structure, muscle function, nerve transmission, and intracellular signaling.
14547.benefits: Supports bone health, muscle function, nerve transmission
14547.risks: Excessive intake can lead to kidney stones or impaired absorption of other minerals

sources.label: Role of Calcium in Human Health; PMC7000495

14568.name: Organic Vegetable Juice Color
14568.description: Coloring agent derived from concentrated organic vegetable juices, used to impart natural color to food products.
14568.benefits: Natural source of color, minimal processing, may contain minor nutrients
14568.risks: Allergic reactions possible in sensitive individuals, potential for variability in color stability

14586.name: Shiitake (Lentinula edodes)
14586.description: An edible mushroom widely used in Asian cuisine (also spelled “shiitake”). It contains beta-glucans (notably lentinan) and the alkaloid eritadenine, as well as B vitamins and minerals. UV-exposed shiitake can be a dietary source of vitamin D2. As a conventional food, shiitake is generally recognized as safe when properly cooked.
14586.benefits: Rich in polysaccharides which may support immune function, antioxidant properties, source of B vitamins and copper, contains lentinan with potential anti-inflammatory and antitumor effects
14586.risks: Rare allergic reactions, rare shiitake dermatitis (skin rash when consumed raw or undercooked)

14667.name: Blackcurrant
14667.description: Blackcurrant is a berry fruit known for high levels of vitamin C, polyphenols, and anthocyanins. It is consumed as fresh fruit, juice, or extracts.
14667.benefits: Rich source of antioxidants, vitamin C, may support immune function, provides dietary fiber
14667.risks: Potential allergen, possible gastrointestinal irritation with excessive consumption

sources.label: PMC1722412 - Polyphenols in blackcurrant and antioxidant effects
PMC3725499 - Blackcurrant anthocyanins and health benefits

14691.name: Hexachlorocyclopentadiene
14691.description: A synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon intermediate used in the manufacture of pesticides, flame retardants, and other industrial chemicals. Not intended for food use and considered hazardous due to its toxicity and environmental persistence.
14691.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, environmental persistence, respiratory irritation, neurotoxicity, bioaccumulation

sources.label: PubChem: Hexachlorocyclopentadiene
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Hexachlorocyclopentadiene

14845.name: Organic Mango Flavor
14845.description: Organic mango flavor is a manufactured flavoring derived from natural mango extracts and other plant-based components, certified organic to meet certain agricultural standards. Despite the 'organic' label, the term 'flavor' still refers to an ultra-processed additive designed to impart mango-like taste, sometimes using solvents or carriers that, while organic, are not always disclosed. It contributes only sensory appeal and does not provide nutritional or functional value.
14845.risks: Lack of transparency, ultra-processed, potential for allergenic compounds, no nutritional value

14912.name: Lychee Juice
14912.description: Lychee juice is the liquid extracted from the lychee fruit (Litchi chinensis), typically consumed as a beverage or used in culinary applications. It is rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, and provides natural sugars. Lychee and its juice are considered generally safe and are recognized as food worldwide, with no GRAS (Generally Recognized As Safe) issues according to the FDA for traditional fruit juice use.
14912.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, contains polyphenols and antioxidants, may support immune function
14912.risks: High in natural sugars, possible allergic reactions (rare), potential hypoglycin A toxicity from unripe fruit (rare in juice)

14961.name: Lauryl Glucoside
14961.description: Non-ionic surfactant derived from glucose and lauryl alcohol. Mild and biodegradable surfactant commonly used in cleaning products and personal care formulations.
14961.benefits: Mild cleansing agent, biodegradable, low irritancy, good foaming properties, suitable for sensitive skin
14961.risks: Mild skin irritation, possible eye irritation at high concentrations, minimal sensitization potential

sources.label: ECHA Substance Information
Safety assessment of alkyl glucoside surfactants
Surfactant irritation potential study

15085.name: Polypropylene
15085.description: Thermoplastic polymer widely used in packaging, textiles, automotive components, and consumer goods.
15085.benefits: Durable, chemical resistant, lightweight, low cost material with broad industrial and consumer applications
15085.risks: Potential inhalation of microplastics or degradation fumes during high heat processing, very low dermal and ingestion toxicity in typical use, environmental persistence

sources.label: Microplastics and human health: inhalation and ingestion exposure
Overview of polypropylene properties and applications

15139.name: Argania Spinosa Kernel Oil
15139.description: Argania spinosa kernel oil, commonly known as argan oil, is a plant oil extracted from the kernels of the argan tree native to Morocco. It is rich in unsaturated fatty acids (mainly oleic and linoleic acids), tocopherols (vitamin E), and polyphenols. In food products, argan oil is used for its nutty flavor and potential antioxidant properties. It is considered GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe) by the FDA when used as a food ingredient.
15139.benefits: Rich in monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats, source of vitamin E, antioxidant properties, may support cardiovascular health

sources.label: FDA GRAS Notice for Argan Oil

15251.name: Dehydroacetic Acid
15251.description: Dehydroacetate is a preservative agent known for antimicrobial properties, commonly used as dehydroacetic acid or its salts.
15251.benefits: Antimicrobial preservative that helps prevent spoilage
15251.risks: Possible skin irritation or sensitization at high levels, regulatory limits apply

sources.label: PMC Review on dehydroacetic acid safety and use

15254.name: Lime Juice from Concentrate
15254.description: Juice from limes that has been evaporated to remove water, concentrating flavor and acidity. Used primarily for flavoring and acidification.
15254.benefits: Provides natural acidity and flavor, source of vitamin C and flavonoids with antioxidant properties
15254.risks: Irritation risk to skin and mucous membranes in concentrated form, possible allergen. Potential dental enamel erosion with excessive ingestion.

15295.name: Full Cream Goat Milk Powder
15295.description: Powdered form of goat milk, providing proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals similar to fresh goat milk.
15295.benefits: Source of protein, calcium, vitamin D, and other nutrients, alternative to cow milk for some with sensitivities
15295.risks: Potential allergenicity in individuals allergic to milk proteins, lactose intolerance symptoms in sensitive individuals

15348.name: Pantothensäure
15348.description: Pantothensäure, also known as vitamin B5, is a water-soluble vitamin essential for synthesizing coenzyme A and metabolizing carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.
15348.benefits: Essential nutrient for energy metabolism, supports skin health, aids wound healing
15348.risks: Rare mild irritation or sensitization in topical use, generally safe at typical intake levels

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Pantothenic acid

15416.name: Dilinoleic Acid/Propanediol
15416.description: Dilinoleic acid/propanediol is a synthetic compound made by combining dilinoleic acid (a dimer of linoleic acid, a fatty acid) and propanediol (a type of glycol). It is rarely used as a direct food ingredient and is more commonly found in cosmetics, polymers, or technical applications. There is limited evidence for its use or safety as a food ingredient, and it is not on the FDA's list of Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) food substances.
15416.risks: Lack of safety data, potential for gut irritation, not established as a food ingredient, possible synthetic processing byproducts

sources.label: PubChem – Dilinoleic Acid
NCBI Bookshelf – Polyols in Food Products
FDA – Food Additive Status List

15433.name: Polyurethane
15433.description: A synthetic polymer used in coatings, adhesives, foams, and elastomers for its durability and flexibility.
15433.benefits: Strong, flexible, durable material with wide industrial application
15433.risks: Potential irritant and sensitizer on skin contact, respiratory sensitization risk during aerosol or dust exposure, possible contamination with residual isocyanates during manufacturing

sources.label: NBK513307 – Occupational exposure and health hazards of polyurethane

15528.name: Natural Orange Flavouring
15528.description: Flavoring derived from orange peel or juice, used to impart citrus aroma and taste. Typically contains complex mixtures of volatile compounds.
15528.risks: Irritant/sensitizer potential, allergen risk especially in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMID 19139795 - Citrus peel allergens and irritant potential

15636.name: Organic Watermelon Juice Concentrate
15636.description: Organic watermelon juice concentrate is produced by removing water from organic watermelon juice, resulting in a denser, sweeter liquid often used as a natural sweetener or flavoring in foods and beverages. It provides natural sugars, some vitamins, and phytonutrients like lycopene. As a concentrate from organic watermelon, it retains many beneficial plant compounds but is more calorie-dense and less hydrating than fresh watermelon. Recognized as safe for consumption by regulatory agencies such as the FDA when derived from safe handling and organic sources.
15636.benefits: Contains natural antioxidants, source of vitamins (notably vitamin C), contains lycopene and citrulline, organic source with less exposure to synthetic pesticides
15636.risks: High natural sugar content, increased calorie density when overconsumed

15638.name: Mushroom Fiber Extract
15638.description: Dietary fiber derived from the cell walls of mushrooms, often used as a functional food ingredient and prebiotic fiber source.
15638.benefits: Dietary fiber source, supports gut health, prebiotic effects
15638.risks: Rare digestive discomfort at high intake, potential allergenicity in sensitive individuals

15639.name: Organic Elderflower Extract
15639.description: Organic elderflower extract is derived from the flowers of the Sambucus nigra plant, produced without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Traditionally used for flavor and in herbal remedies, elderflower contains bioactive compounds, including flavonoids and phenolic acids, and is recognized for its antioxidant and mild anti-inflammatory properties. It is considered Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in conventional amounts for flavoring.
15639.benefits: Antioxidant properties, anti-inflammatory effects, potential mild immune support
15639.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), potential interaction with some medications if consumed excessively

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Elderflower (Sambucus nigra L.): Recent advances and perspectives

15662.name: Permitted Class II Preservatives (INS 211)
15662.description: Also known as sodium benzoate, a widely used food preservative to inhibit microbial growth and extend shelf life.
15662.benefits: Effective antimicrobial preservative, extends shelf life of food products
15662.risks: Potential irritant, possible formation of benzene under certain conditions, concerns about hyperactivity in children, ingestion toxicity at high doses

sources.label: PMC3034917 - Sodium benzoate potential risks and benefits
PMC4085340 - Benzene formation from sodium benzoate in beverages

15693.name: Organic Ashwagandha extract KSM-66 (Withania somnifera) root
15693.description: Extract derived from the root of Withania somnifera, used traditionally in herbal medicine. Contains withanolides and other bioactive compounds.
15693.benefits: Adaptogenic properties supporting stress response, potential cognitive and fatigue support, traditional use in immune modulation
15693.risks: Potential for allergic reactions, gastrointestinal discomfort, possible interactions with medications including sedatives and thyroid hormone, irritation risk in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMC3573577 - Adaptogenic effects of Ashwagandha
PMC6832878 - Safety and efficacy profile of Ashwagandha

15782.name: Coconut Acid
15782.description: Mixture of fatty acids derived from coconut oil, commonly used as a mild surfactant or cleansing agent in cleaning products.
15782.benefits: Biodegradable, effective mild surfactant, derived from natural sources, low toxicity
15782.risks: Mild skin irritation in sensitive individuals, eye irritation at concentrated exposure

sources.label: ECHA Registration Info on Fatty Acids from Coconut Oil

15783.name: Parfum
15783.description: A generic term for fragrance mixtures used in cleaning products. Composed of many chemicals which may vary widely; commonly known to cause skin sensitization and irritation depending on individual components and concentration.
15783.benefits: Improves product scent, enhances consumer acceptance
15783.risks: Skin sensitization, allergic contact dermatitis, respiratory irritation, potential for phototoxicity

sources.label: Fragrance allergy and sensitization review (PMID 29225260)
ECHA Substance Restriction Registry - Fragrance allergens

15808.name: Vegetable Juices
15808.description: Liquid extracts obtained from one or more vegetables, used for flavoring, coloring, or nutritional enhancement in food products.
15808.benefits: Source of natural pigments, vitamins, and minerals, contributes flavor and color, may add micronutrients
15808.risks: Potential allergenicity depending on vegetable source, possible pesticide residues if not organic, minor irritation risk in sensitive individuals

15839.name: Natural Orange Mango Flavor
15839.description: Natural Orange Mango Flavor refers to flavoring compounds derived or synthesized to mimic the taste and aroma of orange and mango. These are typically mixtures of extracts, oils, or chemically isolated aromatic compounds, which may include a wide range of undisclosed carriers, solvents, or preservatives. While 'natural' indicates origin from plant or animal sources, processing often involves physical and chemical extraction steps. The FDA considers natural flavors as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS), but their ingredient transparency and nutritional value are minimal.
15839.risks: Lack of transparency, ultra-processed, may contain solvents or preservatives, potential for allergenic byproducts, no nutritional value

15850.name: Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Extract
15850.description: Aloe barbadensis leaf extract, commonly known as aloe vera extract, is derived from the leaves of the aloe vera plant. Used in both food and cosmetics, it contains bioactive compounds including vitamins, polysaccharides, and antioxidants. In the food context, it is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used within recommended limits.
15850.benefits: May support digestion, contains antioxidants, possible mild anti-inflammatory effects
15850.risks: Possible gastrointestinal upset at high doses, rare allergic reactions, contamination risk if unpurified

sources.label: FDA – Food Additive Status List

16129.name: Beta-Caryophyllene
16129.description: A bicyclic sesquiterpene found in essential oils of plants such as black pepper, cloves, and cannabis. Commonly used for flavoring and fragrance.
16129.benefits: Flavoring agent, may have anti-inflammatory properties demonstrated in preclinical studies
16129.risks: Possible skin sensitizer, respiratory irritant in concentrated inhalation, low toxicity at typical exposure

16154.name: Polymethyl Methacrylate
16154.description: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) is a synthetic polymer commonly used as a plastic and resin, also known as acrylic, acrylic glass, or Plexiglas. In the context of food and nutrition, PMMA is not a food ingredient but has occasional use in non-edible applications such as food packaging, medical devices, and dental materials. It is not recognized as safe for human ingestion and is not listed as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by the FDA for food use.
16154.risks: Not intended for ingestion, potential toxicity if ingested, chemical contamination, not GRAS for food use

sources.label: FDA – Food Contact Substances Inventory

16224.name: Hydroxyacetophenone
16224.description: An aromatic organic compound used primarily as an antioxidant and stabilizer in cosmetic and personal care formulations.
16224.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, sensitization potential in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Safety assessment and use of hydroxyacetophenone in cosmetics

16235.name: Pear Juice
16235.description: Juice extracted from pears, commonly used as a flavoring and sweetener in food and beverage products.
16235.benefits: Source of natural sugars, provides flavor enhancement

16405.name: Peach Juice from Concentrate
16405.description: Fruit juice derived from concentrated peach extract, commonly used as a sweetener or flavoring agent in beverages and foods.
16405.benefits: Natural flavoring, source of vitamins and antioxidants present in peaches
16405.risks: Sugar content contributing to caloric intake, potential for minor irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Bioactive compounds and antioxidant capacities of peach fruits
Fruit juice intake and health effects

16479.name: Acidity Regulator (E330) / Citric Acid
16479.description: Citric acid is a weak organic acid commonly used to adjust acidity in foods and beverages.
16479.benefits: Preserves product stability, controls pH, enhances flavor
16479.risks: Dental erosion at high consumption, minor gastrointestinal irritation

sources.label: Citric acid and dental erosion: PMID 20396479
Role of acidity regulators in food stability: PMID 22895381

16527.name: Coffee Flavor
16527.description: Coffee flavor is a flavoring agent formulated to mimic or enhance the taste and aroma of coffee. In food products, 'coffee flavor' usually refers to a composite of natural or artificial flavor compounds and does not necessarily contain real coffee or caffeine. It is often composed of solvent-extracted aroma chemicals and may include additional carriers or preservatives. Its vague labeling reduces ingredient transparency, making it difficult for consumers to discern its exact content. In the U.S., such flavorings are generally classified as 'Generally Recognized As Safe' (GRAS) by the FDA, but the specific composition is not always disclosed.
16527.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents or preservatives, potential allergenic compounds, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

16532.name: Ethylene Vinyl Acetate
16532.description: Ethylene Vinyl Acetate (EVA) is a synthetic copolymer often used in food processing equipment, packaging, and sometimes as a coating for food-contact surfaces. It is not a food ingredient but may migrate into foods from packaging materials. EVA is evaluated by food safety authorities for its use in indirect food contact, and the FDA recognizes certain forms of EVA as generally safe under specific conditions, but concerns remain over potential leaching of additives or monomers.
16532.risks: Potential migration of chemical additives, possible exposure to vinyl acetate monomer, ultra-processed, not a food ingredient

sources.label: EFSA – Safety assessment of substances used in plastic food contact materials
Hong Kong CFS – Chemical safety of food packaging materials

16545.name: Organic Sugar Cane Alcohol Denat.
16545.description: Denatured alcohol, ethanol with additives to make it unsuitable for consumption, used as a solvent and preservative in cosmetics and personal care products.
16545.benefits: Effective solvent, antimicrobial preservative, enhances product texture and absorption
16545.risks: Skin irritation, dryness, sensitization, potential inhalation irritation, drying effect on skin barrier

sources.label: NCBI Bookshelf - Cosmetic Ingredient Review on Alcohols

16558.name: Rhabarbersaft (Rhubarb Juice)
16558.description: Rhubarb juice derived from concentrated rhubarb juice, used for flavor and color.
16558.benefits: Natural flavor and source of antioxidants
16558.risks: Oxalate content may contribute to kidney burden in high intake, allergen potential in rare cases

16560.name: Wasser
16560.description: Water, essential for hydration and a universal solvent in food preparation.
16560.benefits: Hydration, solvent for food ingredients, essential for life

16614.name: Vinyl (Polyvinyl Chloride, PVC)
16614.description: Vinyl, commonly known as polyvinyl chloride (PVC), is a synthetic plastic polymer widely used in seating and trim applications for vehicles due to its durability, water resistance, and low cost. In food and nutrition contexts, vinyl is not an edible substance and is not approved for use as a food ingredient or additive. Chronic exposure in occupational, industrial, or environmental settings carries health risks, but typical consumer contact (such as car seats) is unrelated to nutrition or food safety.
16614.risks: May emit volatile organic compounds (VOCs), potential exposure to plasticizers like phthalates, not intended for ingestion

sources.label: CDC – Vinyl Chloride: Health Effects

16655.name: Organic Lemon Balm Leaf Extract
16655.description: Organic lemon balm leaf extract is derived from the leaves of Melissa officinalis, a perennial herb in the mint family. It is commonly used for its mild calming effects and pleasant lemon aroma. The extract contains bioactive compounds such as rosmarinic acid, flavonoids, and essential oils. It is considered Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) by the FDA for use in foods and supplements.
16655.benefits: Mild anxiety reduction, potential cognitive support, antioxidant properties, sleep aid
16655.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), mild gastrointestinal upset (rare), potential drug interactions (sedatives, thyroid medication)

16679.name: Organic Passionfruit Flavor
16679.description: Flavoring derived from natural sources of passion fruit, used to impart fruity taste.
16679.risks: Possible sensitization or allergenicity in some individuals, possible residual solvents or contaminants from processing

16687.name: Alkyl Dimethyl Benzyl Ammonium Saccharinate
16687.description: A quaternary ammonium compound commonly used as a disinfectant or antimicrobial agent. Not a food ingredient; primarily used in surface sanitizers. Safety concerns arise from potential skin irritation and respiratory effects during use. Not intended for ingestion.
16687.risks: Skin irritation, respiratory irritation, potential toxic effects if ingested

16859.name: Beech Tree Spirit Essence
16859.description: A 'flower essence' preparation typically made by sun-infusing beech (Fagus sylvatica) blossoms in water and preserving the dilute solution with ethanol (brandy). Marketed within Bach flower remedies, it contains negligible measurable phytochemicals and is not a nutrient. It is not FDA GRAS for use as a food ingredient and is sold as a homeopathic/alternative remedy; randomized trials and systematic reviews find no efficacy beyond placebo.
16859.risks: Lack of proven efficacy, misleading or non-evidence-based claims, ethanol exposure (concern for children, pregnancy, alcohol-sensitive individuals), potential delay of effective treatment

sources.label: Swiss Med Wkly (2010) – Bach flower remedies: systematic review of RCTs
BMC Complement Altern Med (2009) – Bach flower remedies for psychological problems and pain: systematic review
FDA – Drug Products Labeled as Homeopathic (regulatory status/oversight)

16936.name: Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)
16936.description: PET is a synthetic thermoplastic polyester used for food and beverage packaging (bottles, containers). It is not a food ingredient but an FDA- and EFSA-approved food-contact material (indirect additive). Under typical use, overall migration is low and within regulatory limits, though heat and prolonged storage can increase migration of certain compounds.
16936.risks: Potential antimony migration from catalyst, increased leaching with heat and prolonged storage, possible estrogenic activity signals in bottled water (inconsistent evidence), microplastic/nanoplastic shedding and exposure (health effects under investigation), potential taste/odor from acetaldehyde at high temperatures

sources.label: 21 CFR 177.1630 – Poly(ethylene terephthalate) for food-contact use (FDA)
FDA – Polyethylene Terephthalate

16952.name: Rum
16952.description: Fermented and distilled alcoholic beverage typically made from sugarcane byproducts, containing ethanol.
16952.benefits: None at typical use levels for non-beverage applications
16952.risks: Ingestion toxicity due to ethanol, potential for acute and chronic alcohol-related harm, risk of addiction

16986.name: Citrus aurantium dulcis peel oil
16986.description: Essential oil extracted from the peel of the sweet orange fruit, primarily used as a fragrance ingredient in cosmetics and cleaning products.

17165.name: Cherry Puree
17165.description: Purée made from cherries, providing flavor and natural fruit solids typically used as a food ingredient.
17165.benefits: Source of natural sugars, antioxidants such as anthocyanins, and vitamins
17165.risks: Low risk of allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential for mild gastrointestinal upset in excessive amounts

sources.label: PMC3321287 – Health effects of cherries and anthocyanins
PMID 27855245 – Nutritional composition of cherry products

17370.name: Calcium Acetate
17370.description: Calcium acetate is a calcium salt of acetic acid used as a buffering agent, sequestrant, and stabilizer in cleaning products. It is generally considered safe with low toxicity and mild irritant potential.
17370.benefits: Buffering agent, calcium source for stability, low toxicity, biodegradable
17370.risks: Mild skin irritation at high concentrations, eye irritation in concentrated form

sources.label: ECHA Substance Information on Calcium Acetate
Toxicological Profile for Acetates

17473.name: Organic Peach Flavor
17473.description: Organic peach flavor refers to flavoring derived from organic peaches. It is used to impart the taste and aroma of peaches in food products. Though labeled as organic, these flavors can still go through extensive processing, including extraction and concentration.
17473.risks: Ultra-processed, potential lack of transparency in ingredient sourcing and processing

17527.name: Niacin (Vitamin B-3)
17527.description: Niacin, also known as vitamin B3, essential nutrient involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair.
17527.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, skin health, and nervous system function
17527.risks: High doses may cause flushing and gastrointestinal discomfort

sources.label: PMID 12615781 – Niacin role and safety

17575.name: Cetrimonium Bromide
17575.description: A quaternary ammonium compound used primarily as a cationic surfactant and conditioning agent in personal care products such as hair conditioners and creams.
17575.benefits: Effective conditioning agent, reduces static and improves hair manageability
