27992.description: Concentrated extract of ginseng root used for potential adaptogenic and antioxidant effects at low concentrations.
27992.benefits: Antioxidant potential, may support stress response, root bioactive compounds
27992.risks: Mild sensitization or irritant potential, possible interactions with medications at higher doses

sources.label: Pharmacological effects of ginseng root extract

28021.name: Allura Red
28021.description: Allura Red AC, also known as Red 40, is a synthetic red azo dye used in food and beverages to impart a red hue. It's commonly found in candies, beverages, and other processed foods. Allura Red is approved by the FDA and is considered generally recognized as safe (GRAS) when used according to approved guidelines. However, its safety has been the subject of debate due to studies showing potential adverse effects.
28021.risks: Allergic reactions, hyperactivity in children, potential carcinogenic effects

28049.name: Raspberry Flavoring
28049.description: A flavoring ingredient that may be derived from natural raspberry extracts or be a synthetic/artificial mixture designed to mimic raspberry taste and aroma. Often used in food products to provide raspberry flavor. FDA classifies flavorings as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) but exact composition can vary widely.
28049.benefits: Provides raspberry flavor without added sugar or calories, enhances palatability
28049.risks: May contain synthetic chemicals, potential allergen for some, ultra-processed, lack of transparency in composition

28118.name: Fructose-glucose syrup
28118.description: A liquid sweetener derived from starch, composed primarily of fructose and glucose monosaccharides.
28118.risks: Excessive intake associated with insulin resistance, weight gain, metabolic disorders

28347.name: FD&C Yellow No. 5
28347.description: Synthetic azo dye used as a colorant in foods and cosmetics to impart yellow color.
28347.benefits: Provides bright yellow color to products, stable in many formulations
28347.risks: Potential allergen and irritant, hypersensitivity reactions, possible hyperactivity in children, regulatory limits on use

28383.name: Grape Juice Concentrate
28383.description: Concentrated juice derived from grapes, often used as a sweetener or flavoring agent in food products.
28383.benefits: Provides natural sugars and flavor, source of phytochemicals including polyphenols
28383.risks: High sugar content may contribute to excessive caloric intake, dental caries risk

sources.label: Polyphenol content and health effects of grape products - PMC3407987

28502.name: Herbs
28502.description: Plants or plant parts used for flavoring, food, medicine, or fragrance, typically from fresh or dried leaves, flowers, or stems.
28502.benefits: Flavor enhancement, potential antioxidant compounds, culinary and traditional medicinal use
28502.risks: Irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, possible contamination with pesticides or microbes depending on source and processing

28578.name: Certified Organic Stevia Leaf Extract
28578.description: Stevia leaf extract is a natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant. It is much sweeter than sugar and contains no calories, commonly used as an alternative sweetener for those looking to reduce sugar intake. Certified organic versions are free from synthetic pesticides and fertilizers.
28578.benefits: Calorie-free, does not raise blood sugar levels, contains natural compounds like steviosides which may have antihyperglycemic and antihypertensive benefits

28679.name: Socker
28679.description: Refined sucrose sugar used as a sweetener and energy source.
28679.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, and risk of metabolic disorders

28710.name: FD&C Red #40
28710.description: Synthetic azo dye used as a color additive in foods, drugs, and cosmetics to impart red color.
28710.benefits: Provides vivid red coloring in food and cosmetic products
28710.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential hypersensitivity, possible behavioral effects in children, regulatory restrictions on use levels

28768.name: Fructooligosaccharides
28768.description: Fructooligosaccharides (FOS) are short-chain oligosaccharides composed of fructose units, classified as prebiotic dietary fibers that resist digestion in the upper gastrointestinal tract and selectively stimulate beneficial gut bacteria.
28768.benefits: Prebiotic effects supporting gut microbiota, improved bowel regularity, potential immune modulation
28768.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort such as bloating, gas, and diarrhea at high intake

sources.label: PMCID: PMC3699853 - Effects of prebiotics on gastrointestinal health
PMID:19597529 - Fructooligosaccharides and their prebiotic effects

28801.name: Mint Flavor
28801.description: A complex mixture of natural and/or synthetic compounds used to impart minty taste and scent in food and cosmetic products.
28801.benefits: Provides mint scent and flavor, enhances palatability and freshness perception
28801.risks: Potential skin and mucous membrane irritation, possible sensitization in susceptible individuals, inhalation irritation at high concentrations

28884.name: Monk Fruit
28884.description: Natural sweetener derived from the monk fruit (Siraitia grosvenorii) containing mogrosides responsible for its sweetness.
28884.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not affect blood glucose, suitable for diabetic use
28884.risks: Potential allergic reactions, minimal irritation potential, none at typical consumption levels

28890.name: Brilliant Blue FCF (E133)
28890.description: A synthetic blue dye used as a colorant in foods and beverages to impart bright blue color.
28890.benefits: Color additive to improve appearance and consumer acceptance of food and beverages
28890.risks: Possible mild allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential behavioral effects in children in combination with other food dyes

sources.label: Evaluations of food dyes and possible behavioral effects in children (PubMed 17691588)
Review of safety and toxicology of Brilliant Blue FCF (PMID 17582538)

28915.name: Kiwi Juice Concentrate
28915.description: Concentrated juice derived from kiwi fruit, used primarily as a flavoring and natural sweetener in food products.
28915.benefits: Natural flavoring agent, source of vitamins and antioxidants
28915.risks: Potential allergen, minor irritation risk in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Food allergy to kiwi fruit: clinical features and allergenic components.

28951.name: Non-GMO Ascorbic Acid
28951.description: Ascorbic acid, commonly known as vitamin C, is a vital nutrient for human health. Non-GMO ascorbic acid is derived from genetically unmodified sources. It functions as an antioxidant and is crucial for the repair of tissues, the enzymatic production of certain neurotransmitters, and the immune system. It is water-soluble and generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA.
28951.benefits: Antioxidant properties, supports immune function, aids collagen synthesis, improves iron absorption

sources.label: NIH - Vitamin C Fact Sheet

28965.name: Hydrolyzed Marine Collagen (Fish)
28965.description: A protein derived from fish skin and scales that is broken down into smaller peptides for easier absorption. It is believed to support skin, joint, and bone health.
28965.benefits: Improves skin elasticity, supports joint health, promotes bone strength
28965.risks: Fish allergy, potential contamination with heavy metals

29185.name: E133 (Brilliant Blue FCF)
29185.description: Synthetic blue dye used as a colorant in foods and beverages, approved as a food additive in many regions.
29185.benefits: Coloring agent to improve product appearance and consumer acceptance
29185.risks: Possible allergic reactions, hypersensitivity, potential behavioral effects in sensitive children

sources.label: Hyperactivity and food colors in children – PMC16298926
Safety assessment of food colorants – PMC31164792

29252.name: INS 950 (Acesulfame K)
29252.description: A synthetic calorie-free sweetener known as Acesulfame Potassium, commonly used in sugar-free and diet products to provide sweetness without calories. It is approximately 200 times sweeter than sugar. It is approved by the FDA and other health bodies as generally recognized as safe (GRAS).
29252.risks: Potential for promoting insulin secretion, possible microbiome disruption, limited long-term safety data, risk of overconsumption, lacks nutritional value

29283.name: Indian Gooseberry Extract
29283.description: Indian Gooseberry, also known as Amla, is a fruit native to India and is used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine. The extract is rich in Vitamin C, polyphenols, and other antioxidants. It is believed to promote overall health, enhance antioxidant defense, and offer anti-inflammatory properties.
29283.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, high Vitamin C content, supports immune function, may reduce inflammation, potential blood sugar regulation, promotes heart health

29288.name: Colour (Lycopene)
29288.description: Lycopene is a natural pigment from the carotenoid family, responsible for the red color in tomatoes, watermelons, and other red fruits. It is commonly used as a natural colorant in foods and has antioxidant properties. Lycopene is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA and has been studied for its potential health benefits.
29288.benefits: Antioxidant properties, potential cardiovascular health benefits, possible cancer risk reduction

29377.name: Strawberry Juice
29377.description: Juice extracted from strawberries, containing water-soluble vitamins, natural sugars, and antioxidants.
29377.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, and flavoring
29377.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, sugar content concerns in excessive intake

sources.label: PMC3492879 - Nutritional and health benefits of strawberry consumption
PMC493352 - Strawberry allergenicity and clinical reactions

29391.name: Saborizante natural
29391.description: Natural flavoring derived to mimic or enhance mozzarella cheese taste, generally composed of dairy or fermentation-derived compounds.
29391.benefits: Adds cheese flavor without added fats or calories typical of cheese
29391.risks: Allergic reactions in people with dairy allergies or lactose intolerance, potential minor sensitization

29529.name: Mango Juice Concentrate
29529.description: Concentrated juice derived from mango fruit, used as a flavoring and sweetening agent in food products.
29529.benefits: Provides natural flavor and sweetness, contains some vitamins and antioxidants
29529.risks: High sugar content, potential allergen in sensitive individuals

sources.label: Nutritional and functional properties of mango

29578.name: Toluene
29578.description: Toluene is a clear, colorless liquid with a distinctive smell, derived from petroleum or coal tar sources. It is primarily used in industrial applications as a solvent for paints, coatings, and chemical reactions. In food packaging or other indirect food applications, trace amounts may come in contact with food. Toluene is not a food ingredient or additive, and its direct addition to food products is prohibited.
29578.risks: Neurological effects, respiratory problems, skin irritation, potential carcinogen, environmental pollutant

sources.label: CDC - Toluene: Health and safety information
ECHA Toluene Substance Information
EPA Toluene Risk Assessment

29617.name: Carbonated Pure Water
29617.description: Carbonated pure water is water that has been infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure, creating effervescence commonly known as carbonation. This process makes the water fizzy, and it is used as the base for many soft drinks. Carbonated water itself has been deemed safe for consumption and is recognized as generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA.

sources.label: FDA – GRAS Substances (SCOGS) Database

29672.name: Preservative (E211)
29672.description: Sodium benzoate is a widely used food preservative that inhibits microbial growth by creating an acidic environment.
29672.benefits: Prevents microbial spoilage, extends shelf life of food products
29672.risks: Potential irritant at high concentrations, possible benzene formation with ascorbic acid, allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMC4145293 - Safety assessment of sodium benzoate
PubMed 12418973 - Benzene formation from sodium benzoate

29716.name: Dimethyl Dicarbonate
29716.description: A chemical compound used primarily as a solvent, reagent, or intermediate in organic synthesis and industrial applications.
29716.benefits: Effective solvent and reagent in chemical manufacturing processes
29716.risks: Irritant to eyes, skin, and respiratory tract upon exposure, potential inhalation toxicity, flammability hazard

sources.label: PubChem Methyl Dicarbonate Compound Summary
Toxicological profile of methyl dicarbonate (example study placeholder)

29745.name: Cymbopogon Schoenanthus Oil
29745.description: Essential oil derived from Cymbopogon schoenanthus, a species of lemongrass. Used in aromatherapy, cosmetics, and traditional medicine. Generally regarded as safe for topical use in diluted form. Not a food ingredient. Potentially irritating to skin or mucous membranes if used undiluted. No significant data on ingestion safety.
29745.benefits: Aromatic, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, may provide relaxation and insect repellent properties
29745.risks: Skin irritation, allergic reactions, potential phototoxicity with prolonged exposure

29782.name: Tocopheryl Acetate (Vitamin E)
29782.description: Synthetic or natural esterified form of vitamin E used as an antioxidant and skin-conditioning agent in foods and cosmetics.
29782.benefits: Antioxidant protecting cells from oxidative damage, supports skin barrier function, used as a vitamin E source in foods and supplements
29782.risks: Potential mild skin irritation or sensitization in sensitive individuals, very low toxicity, low risk at typical use levels

29854.name: Citric Acid (Syre, Sitronsyre)
29854.description: Citric acid is a weak organic acid that occurs naturally in citrus fruits. It is widely used in the food industry as a preservative and flavoring agent. In the body, it plays a role in the citric acid cycle, which is important for energy production. Citric acid is Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in recommended amounts.
29854.benefits: Enhances flavor, preservative properties, plays a role in energy production
29854.risks: Possible irritation in high concentrations, potential allergenic reactions, may cause enamel erosion in excess

sources.label: PubChem - Citric Acid

30213.name: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3)
30213.description: Cholecalciferol, or Vitamin D3, is a fat-soluble vitamin produced in the skin upon exposure to sunlight, specifically ultraviolet B radiation. It is important for maintaining healthy bones and teeth, supporting the immune system, brain, and nervous system, and regulating insulin levels. Vitamin D3 is often added to fortify foods and available as dietary supplements. It is recognized as GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe) by the FDA for use as a food additive.
30213.benefits: Supports bone health, enhances immune function, regulates calcium and phosphorus absorption, supports muscle function
30213.risks: None at typical dietary levels, toxicity at very high doses, hypercalcemia

sources.label: NIH – Vitamin D Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

30225.name: Zinc Acetate
30225.description: Zinc acetate is a zinc salt used primarily as a nutritional supplement to provide zinc, an essential trace element involved in numerous biological functions including immune response and enzyme activity.
30225.benefits: Provides essential zinc, supports immune function and enzymatic processes
30225.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, potential for nausea or gastrointestinal upset if ingested in excess

30251.name: Vanadium (as Vanadyl Sulfate)
30251.description: Sulfate is an inorganic anion commonly found in water and various food sources. It is a normal component of the human diet and environment.
30251.benefits: Normal constituent of body fluids, involved in detoxification and protein synthesis
30251.risks: Laxative effect at high ingestion levels, gastrointestinal discomfort with excessive intake

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for Sulfate

30295.name: Guava Juice from Concentrate
30295.description: Concentrated juice from guava fruit, providing flavor and natural sugars.
30295.benefits: Source of natural vitamin C and dietary fiber remnants, flavoring agent
30295.risks: Natural sugar content, potential gastrointestinal upset if consumed in excess

30357.name: Beta-Cyclodextrin
30357.description: Cyclic oligosaccharides used in cleaning products for encapsulating and removing odors or hydrophobic contaminants; generally regarded as safe with low toxicity.
30357.benefits: Encapsulation of odors and hydrophobic compounds, enhances cleaning efficacy, biodegradable, low toxicity
30357.risks: None at typical use concentrations, possible mild irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: ECHA Cyclodextrins Information

30388.name: Organic Black Carrot Juice Concentrate Color
30388.description: A concentrated extract derived from black carrots, primarily used as a natural colorant due to its high anthocyanin content.
30388.benefits: Natural colorant, antioxidant properties from anthocyanins
30388.risks: Irritation potential in sensitive individuals, possible allergenicity

30397.name: Calci-K[R] Calcium Potassium Phosphate-Citrate
30397.description: Essential mineral electrolyte involved in nerve function, muscle contraction, and fluid balance. Typical dietary sources include fruits, vegetables, and supplements.
30397.benefits: Supports nerve transmission, muscle function, fluid and electrolyte balance
30397.risks: Hyperkalemia risk with excessive intake in kidney impairment, none at typical low doses

sources.label: Potassium - Nutrition and Health

30472.name: Molybdenum Aspartate Complex
30472.description: Molybdenum Aspartate Complex is a compound that combines molybdenum, an essential trace mineral necessary for enzyme function, with aspartate, an amino acid derivative. Molybdenum plays a role in the body's detoxification processes and is required for the function of certain enzymes. Aspartates are sometimes used in supplements to improve mineral absorption.
30472.benefits: Essential for enzyme function, supports detoxification
30472.risks: Potential toxicity at high doses, possible gastrointestinal discomfort

sources.label: NCBI – Dietary Reference Intakes for Molybdenum
NIH – Molybdenum Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

30595.name: Polyacrylic Acid
30595.description: Polyacrylic acid is a synthetic polymer commonly used in consumer products as a thickener and emulsifying agent. It is often found in cosmetics, personal care products, and some food contact materials. While it is generally considered safe for use in these contexts under normal conditions, it is not approved as a food additive.

sources.label: PubChem - Polyacrylic acid
Wiley Online Library - Polyacrylic Acids and Their Derivatives

30627.name: Woda
30627.description: Water, the universal solvent, commonly used as a solvent and diluent in cleaning products. It is chemically neutral and non-toxic.
30627.benefits: Solvent, diluent, non-toxic, non-irritating, environmentally safe

sources.label: ECHA dossier on water
EPA Chemical Fact Sheet on Water

30643.name: Alphonso Mango Puree
30643.description: Alphonso mango puree is made by blending the flesh of the Alphonso mango, a type of mango renowned for its sweet taste and vibrant color. This puree retains most of the natural vitamins, fiber, and antioxidants found in the fresh fruit, contributing to its nutritional profile.
30643.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, contains dietary fiber, high in antioxidants, provides natural sweetness

30691.name: E170 (Calcium Carbonate)
30691.description: Calcium carbonate used as a leavening agent in baking to release carbon dioxide and help dough rise.
30691.benefits: Leavening agent aiding dough expansion, source of dietary calcium
30691.risks: Inhalation risk as fine dust, possible mild irritation on respiratory tract in occupational exposure, excessive ingestion may cause digestive upset

sources.label: PMC4221736 - Calcium carbonate properties and uses
PMID27349706 - Safety assessment of calcium carbonate as food additive

30710.name: Ultra Purified pH-Balanced Water
30710.description: Ultra purified pH-balanced water is water that has undergone extensive filtration to remove impurities, and its pH level has been adjusted to be neutral or slightly alkaline. It is often marketed for its enhanced purity and purported health benefits, but there is limited scientific evidence supporting any additional health benefits over regular purified water.

30732.name: Organic Water Kefir Culture
30732.description: Organic Water Kefir Culture is a fermentation starter used to make water kefir, a probiotic-rich beverage. It typically consists of a symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeasts (SCOBY) that ferment sugar water into a lightly carbonated drink. Water kefir provides beneficial probiotics that support gut health. As an organic product, it is free from synthetic pesticides and fertilizers.
30732.benefits: Improved gut health, source of probiotics, may enhance digestion

30757.name: Live Probiotic (Bacillus Subtilis)
30757.description: A strain of Bacillus subtilis used as a live probiotic to support gut microbial balance by colonizing the intestinal tract transiently.
30757.benefits: Supports gut microbial balance, may aid digestion, potential immune modulation
30757.risks: Rare risk of infection in immunocompromised individuals, potential allergenicity, possible gastrointestinal discomfort

30841.name: Gardenia Jasminoides Fruit Extract
30841.description: Gardenia Jasminoides Fruit Extract is derived from the fruit of the Gardenia jasminoides plant. It is often used for its potential anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and skin-lightening properties in cosmetics and health supplements. The extract contains compounds such as genipin and crocin, which are studied for their biological effects.
30841.benefits: Anti-inflammatory properties, antioxidant effects, potential skin-lightening agent, possible use in managing diabetes

30997.name: DL-alpha-tocopherol acetate
30997.description: Synthetic form of vitamin E used as an antioxidant to prevent oxidation in foods and cosmetics.
30997.benefits: Antioxidant properties, protects oils and formulations from oxidative degradation
30997.risks: Low toxicity at typical use, potential minor skin sensitization in rare cases

31006.name: Ultra-purified water
31006.description: Ultra-purified water is water that has been filtered and cleaned of impurities to an exceptionally high degree, typically used in laboratory settings or specific industrial applications. It lacks the minerals found in regular drinking water, having neither nutrients nor calories, and is generally considered safe for consumption.

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Applications and uses of ultra-purified water

31030.name: Organic Food-Based Vitamin C (Amla Fruit Extract)
31030.description: Amla fruit extract is a natural source of vitamin C, derived from the Indian gooseberry. It is used as a supplement to enhance vitamin C intake with potential antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immune-boosting properties. Amla is considered generally safe and 'GRAS' (Generally Recognized As Safe) by the FDA for its use in food supplements.
31030.benefits: Rich source of vitamin C, antioxidant properties, immune system support, anti-inflammatory effects, supports collagen production, may lower cholesterol

31127.name: Dipotassium Hydrogen Phosphate
31127.description: Inorganic salt used as a buffering agent, emulsifier, and a source of potassium and phosphate in food products.
31127.benefits: Maintains pH balance in foods, contributes dietary potassium and phosphate essential for cellular functions
31127.risks: Excessive intake may contribute to imbalanced phosphate levels, possible kidney burden in susceptible individuals

sources.label: Phosphates in diet and health outcomes, PMC7050525
Food additives: phosphate intake and implications

31206.name: Reconstituted Fruit Juices
31206.description: Reconstituted fruit juices are made from concentrated fruit juice that has had its water removed for transport and storage, and then rehydrated with water before consumption. They are often used in packaged beverages and food products for convenience and cost-effectiveness. Reconstituted juices maintain similar levels of vitamins and minerals as their fresh counterparts but may lack some of the fresh juice's natural flavors and phytonutrients due to processing.
31206.benefits: Good source of vitamins and minerals
31206.risks: Potentially lower phytonutrient content than fresh juice, may include added sugars or preservatives

sources.label: ScienceDirect – Processing effects on juice nutrients

31388.name: High-fructose corn syrup
31388.description: A sweetener derived from corn starch containing about 15% fructose; used to enhance sweetness and preserve food products.
31388.benefits: Increases sweetness and shelf life in processed foods
31388.risks: Insulin resistance, excessive caloric intake, metabolic disturbances, contribution to obesity

31401.name: Marine-Derived Calcium Citrate Malate
31401.description: Marine-Derived Calcium Citrate Malate is a form of calcium derived from marine sources and combined with citrate and malate salts to enhance absorption. It functions as a dietary calcium supplement and is recognized for its superior bioavailability compared to other calcium forms.
31401.benefits: High bioavailability, supports bone health, may prevent osteoporosis, promotes dental health

31407.name: Clarified Orange Juice Concentrate
31407.description: Clarified Orange Juice Concentrate is orange juice from which solids and pulp have been removed before it is concentrated by removing water. It serves as a flavoring and sweetening agent in food products. This form of juice is often used in fruit beverages and processed foods to provide an orange flavor. It is considered generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA.
31407.benefits: Provides vitamin C, source of natural citrus flavor
31407.risks: May lack some nutrients found in whole fruit, high in sugar if consumed in large quantities

31746.name: Cyclamate Acid
31746.description: Cyclamate acid refers to cyclamates, a family of artificial sweeteners, which are chemically synthesized to provide sweetness without the calories of sugar. Initially popular in many countries, cyclamates were banned by the FDA in 1970 due to concerns about potential health risks. They are still permitted in some countries outside the United States.
31746.benefits: Low-calorie sweetening, does not affect blood sugar levels
31746.risks: Potential carcinogenicity, banned by FDA in the US, questionable safety in high doses

31753.name: Cyclamates
31753.description: Artificial sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories. Often combined with other sweeteners to enhance sweetness profile.
31753.risks: Regulatory restriction, potential carcinogenicity concerns, banned in some countries

sources.label: PubMed 6981263 - Toxicological evaluation of cyclamate
FDA Cyclamate ban info

31791.name: Sodio Bicarbonato
31791.description: Sodio Bicarbonato, also known as sodium bicarbonate or baking soda, is a chemical compound frequently used as a leavening agent in baked goods. It reacts with acids to produce carbon dioxide gas, which helps dough rise. It's also used medically as an antacid to relieve heartburn and indigestion.
31791.benefits: Acts as an antacid, used in baking to improve texture, mild teeth whitening properties
31791.risks: High sodium intake for individuals with hypertension, potential excessive alkalinity impact if overconsumed

31873.name: Pfirsichsaft aus Pfirsichsaftkonzentrat (Peach Juice from Peach Juice Concentrate)
31873.description: Concentrated peach juice used primarily as a flavoring and sweetening ingredient in food and beverages.
31873.benefits: Natural flavoring, source of some vitamins and antioxidants
31873.risks: Allergic reaction in sensitive individuals, minimal ingestion toxicity at typical use levels

sources.label: Antioxidant properties of peach juice concentrates
Food allergy and peach sensitization

31959.name: Grape
31959.description: Fruit commonly consumed fresh or processed; contains water, sugars, organic acids, vitamins, and polyphenols such as resveratrol and flavonoids.
31959.benefits: Source of antioxidants, vitamins, and dietary fiber
31959.risks: Possible allergic reaction in sensitive individuals

32338.name: Organic Caffeine from Organic Green Coffee Bean Extract
32338.description: Caffeine is a natural stimulant found in coffee beans, including green coffee bean extract which is less processed. Organic certification indicates cultivation without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. The FDA considers caffeine generally recognized as safe (GRAS) at moderate intakes.
32338.benefits: Increased alertness, improved cognitive performance, enhanced physical endurance, potential antioxidant properties
32338.risks: Insomnia, increased heart rate, anxiety, digestive upset, dependence, potential for increased blood pressure

sources.label: FDA – Questions and Answers on Caffeine

32378.name: Sicilian Salt
32378.description: Sicilian salt is sea salt harvested from salt pans in Sicily, typically containing natural trace minerals. It is considered a whole salt but remains primarily sodium chloride.
32378.benefits: Provides essential electrolytes (sodium, chloride), naturally occurring trace minerals
32378.risks: High sodium intake may contribute to hypertension, cardiovascular issues

32446.name: Safflower
32446.description: Oil extracted from the seeds of the safflower plant, predominantly composed of polyunsaturated fatty acids, especially linoleic acid.
32446.benefits: Source of essential fatty acids, may support skin barrier function when used topically
32446.risks: High omega-6 fatty acid content leading to oxidative instability and potential pro-inflammatory effects with excessive dietary intake

32547.name: Fragrances
32547.description: Complex mixtures of aromatic compounds used to impart scent in cleaning products. Composition varies widely and often undisclosed. Can include natural and synthetic chemicals.
32547.benefits: Improves user experience by masking unpleasant odors, enhances product appeal
32547.risks: Skin sensitization, contact allergy, respiratory irritation, potential asthma exacerbation, photoallergy, potential endocrine disruption (some compounds), IFRA restrictions

sources.label: ECHA fragrance allergen report
International Fragrance Association (IFRA) Standards

32701.name: Melon
32701.description: Fruits from the Cucurbitaceae family, including varieties such as cantaloupe, watermelon, and honeydew. Rich in water, vitamins (especially vitamin C and A), and dietary fiber.
32701.benefits: Hydration support due to high water content, source of vitamins C and A, dietary fiber contributing to digestive health
32701.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential for microbial contamination if improperly handled

32761.name: Monk Fruit Juice
32761.description: Extract from monk fruit (Siraitia grosvenorii), commonly used as a natural, low-calorie sweetener. Recognized as safe by FDA as a general sweetener. Contains mogrosides that provide intense sweetness without calories.
32761.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, antioxidant properties, suitable for diabetics
32761.risks: Potential allergenicity in rare cases, possible digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals

32794.name: Glyoxal
32794.description: A reactive alpha-dicarbonyl compound formed as a byproduct in food processing and metabolism, known to cause protein and DNA modification. Not approved as a food additive by the FDA.
32794.risks: Potential cytotoxicity, genotoxicity, protein cross-linking, formation of advanced glycation end-products (AGEs), possible contribution to inflammation and chronic diseases

32814.name: Oxygen
32814.description: A colorless, odorless gas essential for cellular respiration and energy production in aerobic organisms. It is not an ingested nutrient but is vital for survival.
32814.benefits: Supports aerobic metabolism, essential for energy production, vital for human survival
32814.risks: Oxygen toxicity at high concentrations, oxidative stress

sources.label: Oxygen Toxicity and Physiology (NCBI Bookshelf)
Oxygen and its Role in Metabolism

33030.name: Apple Juice Concentrate
33030.description: Concentrated form of apple juice obtained by removing water, used as a sweetener or flavoring agent in food products.
33030.benefits: Provides natural sweetness, contains some vitamins and antioxidants present in apples
33030.risks: High sugar content, potential contribution to excessive caloric intake

sources.label: PMID 22563114 - Nutritional impact of fruit juice consumption
PMID 27447223 - Sugar content and health impacts of fruit juices

33045.name: Vatten
33045.description: Water, a universal solvent and essential for life, commonly used as a base or diluent in food and cosmetic products.
33045.benefits: Hydration, solvent for ingredient dispersion, essential for biological functions

33134.name: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D)
33134.description: A fat-soluble vitamin essential for calcium absorption, bone health, and immune function. Recognized and regulated by the FDA as a dietary supplement and nutrient.
33134.benefits: Supports bone health, immune modulation, calcium absorption
33134.risks: Toxicity with excessive supplementation leading to hypercalcemia

sources.label: NIH Vitamin D Fact Sheet

33162.name: Electrolytes (Calcium and Magnesium Lactate and Calcium and Potassium Phosphate)
33162.description: Mineral salts providing calcium, magnesium, and potassium ions important for electrolyte balance and physiological functions.
33162.benefits: Supports electrolyte balance, essential minerals for cellular function, aids nerve and muscle function
33162.risks: None at typical low concentration usage

sources.label: Electrolyte Homeostasis - NCBI Bookshelf

33289.name: Organic Dark Sweet Cherry Juice Concentrate
33289.description: A concentrated juice derived from dark sweet cherries, retaining many of the fruit's phytochemicals including anthocyanins and antioxidants; typically used as a natural sweetener or flavoring agent. Not specifically regulated by the FDA beyond juice concentrate standards.
33289.benefits: Rich in antioxidants and anthocyanins, may reduce inflammation, supports exercise recovery, potential to improve sleep quality due to natural melatonin content
33289.risks: High in natural sugars which may impact blood sugar levels if consumed excessively, potential allergen for sensitive individuals, dental caries risk with frequent consumption

33371.name: Lemon juice from lemon juice concentrate (1%)
33371.description: Reconstituted lemon juice made from concentrated lemon juice, used to provide flavor and acidity.
33371.benefits: Flavoring agent, source of citric acid and vitamin C
33371.risks: Potential acidity leading to dental enamel erosion, possible loss of some volatile nutrients during concentration

sources.label: Effect of acidic beverages on dental enamel

33464.name: Natural Citrus Flavour
33464.description: Extracts derived from citrus fruits used to impart flavor. These ingredients are often chemically processed and may be combined with solvents or carriers.
33464.risks: Lack of transparency, potential presence of solvents or additives, ultra-processed, possible allergenicity

33636.name: Fuji Apples
33636.description: A variety of apple known for its sweetness and crisp texture. Apples are whole fruits rich in dietary fiber, vitamin C, and various antioxidants. Recognized as a nutritious food ingredient with no safety concerns when consumed as typical fruit servings.
33636.benefits: Rich in dietary fiber, source of vitamin C, contains antioxidants, supports digestive health, may reduce risk of chronic diseases

sources.label: FDA Food Ingredient Overview

33701.name: Saccharin
33701.description: Artificial non-nutritive sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories.
33701.benefits: Calorie-free sweetness substitute for sugar reduction
33701.risks: Possible irritation, controversy over carcinogenicity though currently deemed safe at low intake levels, may alter gut microbiota

sources.label: Review on safety and metabolism of saccharin - PMC

33914.name: Lavender Flower Extract
33914.description: An extract derived from lavender flowers (Lavandula angustifolia) commonly used in aromatherapy, cosmetics, and flavoring. Not a food ingredient primarily but used in fragrances and herbal supplements. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by FDA for use in food flavoring in small amounts. Contains bioactive compounds such as linalool and linalyl acetate.
33914.benefits: Anxiolytic effects, antimicrobial properties, anti-inflammatory, may improve sleep quality, antioxidant effects
33914.risks: Allergic reactions, skin irritation in sensitive individuals, may interact with sedatives

33931.name: Natural Mineral Spring Water
33931.description: Water sourced from natural springs containing trace minerals; generally safe and essential for hydration. Not regulated as a drug by FDA but considered a food/beverage ingredient.
33931.benefits: Hydration, source of trace minerals, supports bodily functions

sources.label: Mineral waters: composition and health effects

34067.name: EDTA
34067.description: Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) is a chelating agent used to bind metal ions, preventing oxidative discoloration in formulations.
34067.benefits: Stabilizes color by chelating metal ions, improves product shelf-life
34067.risks: Potential skin irritation, limited bioaccumulation, environmental persistence

sources.label: PMC3792431 - Safety assessment of EDTA and its salts as used in cosmetics
Assessment of EDTA environmental persistence and toxicity

34101.name: Silica (Silicon Dioxide)
34101.description: Silica is a naturally occurring compound composed of silicon and oxygen. It is present in water and many foods and contributes to electrolyte balance. Generally recognized as safe by the FDA when used in food.
34101.benefits: Supports bone health, skin elasticity, connective tissue strength, involved in electrolyte balance

34149.name: Saborizantes naturales
34149.description: Term commonly used in Spanish for 'natural flavors,' referring to flavor compounds derived from natural sources but often chemically processed and added to foods and beverages.
34149.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents or additives, ultra-processed, potential allergens, no significant nutritional value

34284.name: Bicarbonato de sodio
34284.description: Sodium bicarbonate is an alkaline compound used as an antacid and leavening agent; generally recognized as safe by the FDA.
34284.benefits: Relieves acid indigestion, helps regulate pH balance
34284.risks: Excessive intake may cause alkalosis, electrolyte imbalance in sensitive individuals

34520.name: Organic Yuzu Flavor
34520.description: Flavoring derived from yuzu fruit, often used to impart citrus aroma and taste. 'Organic' denotes that the source fruit was grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Flavorings are usually extracted compounds and may be processed; the precise composition can vary and may include natural or isolated ingredients.
34520.benefits: Natural source of citrus aroma, may contain trace antioxidants from yuzu, enhances flavor without calories
34520.risks: Possible allergenicity, lack of transparency on exact compounds, ultra-processed, potential mild irritants

34542.name: Organic Red Grapefruit Juice from Concentrate
34542.description: Red grapefruit juice made from concentrate, organic certified. Contains natural sugars, vitamins, and antioxidants. The concentrate process involves removing water for storage and later reconstitution, which may reduce some volatile compounds but generally maintains nutrients.
34542.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, antioxidants such as lycopene and flavonoids, may support immune function, antioxidant protection, cardiovascular benefits
34542.risks: High natural sugar content, potential interaction with certain medications (CYP3A4 inhibition), dental erosion risk if consumed excessively

34672.name: Organic Ginger Flavor
34672.description: Flavoring derived from organic ginger or its extracts, used to impart ginger taste. Typically considered a natural flavor but the exact composition may vary and include solvents or carriers.
34672.benefits: May contain ginger bioactive compounds with anti-inflammatory and digestive benefits if present in significant amounts
34672.risks: Potential allergens, lack of transparency on exact composition, ultra-processed

34775.name: Myrcene
34775.description: Myrcene is a naturally occurring monoterpene found in various plants such as hops, bay leaves, and cannabis. It is commonly used as a fragrance and flavoring agent. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA for use in food. Myrcene also exhibits potential pharmacological effects including anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and sedative properties according to preclinical studies.
34775.risks: Potential allergen, may cause mild irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PubChem Myrcene Data
ECHA Myrcene Substance Information

34844.name: Diced Peaches
34844.description: Diced peaches are pieces of peach fruit, typically canned or fresh. When canned, they may be packed in syrup, juice, or water. Peaches are a good source of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber. The FDA considers peaches and their preparations generally recognized as safe (GRAS).
34844.benefits: Source of vitamin C, dietary fiber, antioxidants, supports digestive health
34844.risks: Added sugars if packed in syrup, potential pesticide residues if conventionally grown

34903.name: Juniper Berry
34903.description: Fleshy seed cones from Juniperus species used for flavoring and traditional remedies.
34903.benefits: Flavoring agent, traditional use for digestion support
34903.risks: Potential skin sensitization, gastrointestinal irritation if ingested in large amounts, possible nephrotoxicity at high doses

sources.label: PMID 23964304 - Toxicological properties of Juniperus species

34909.name: Gum Arabic
34909.description: Natural polysaccharide obtained from Acacia trees used as a stabilizer, emulsifier, and thickener in foods.
34909.benefits: Fiber source, stabilizes emulsions, texture improvement
34909.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, minor digestive discomfort at high intake

sources.label: PMID 23829531 - Safety evaluation of gum arabic

35038.name: Acidity regulators
35038.description: Additives used to control the acidity or alkalinity of foods, commonly including citric acid, phosphoric acid, lactic acid, and acetic acid. Generally recognized as safe by the FDA when used within prescribed limits.
35038.benefits: Help preserve food by controlling pH, enhance flavor stability, improve shelf life, contribute to food safety
35038.risks: Possible dental erosion with excessive consumption, gastrointestinal irritation in sensitive individuals, potential to disrupt mineral absorption if consumed in high amounts

sources.label: NCBI Bookshelf – Food Additives

35207.name: Dihydroxyacetone (DHA)
35207.description: A simple carbohydrate commonly used as the active ingredient in topical sunless tanning products; reacts with amino acids in the skin's stratum corneum to produce a temporary pigmentation (Maillard reaction). Not approved as a food additive by FDA but generally recognized as safe for topical cosmetic use.
35207.benefits: Provides temporary skin pigmentation without UV exposure, safer alternative to tanning beds and sunbathing
35207.risks: Potential skin irritation, possible formation of reactive oxygen species under UV exposure, concerns about inhalation toxicity in spray products

35508.name: Aloe Vera Juice
35508.description: Liquid extract from the leaves of the Aloe vera plant, commonly used for digestive health and skin benefits. Considered a dietary supplement by the FDA when appropriately processed; raw leaf latex is a laxative and can be harmful in excess.
35508.benefits: Supports digestive health, may reduce inflammation, potential antioxidant properties, aids in hydration
35508.risks: Potential laxative effect causing diarrhea, abdominal cramping, risk of electrolyte imbalance with excessive consumption, possible allergic reactions, contaminated or improperly processed products may lead to toxicity

35522.name: Food Acid (citric & malic)
35522.description: Citric acid is a weak organic acid commonly used as a food additive to provide sour flavor and as a preservative by acidifying foods and beverages.
35522.benefits: Enhances flavor by providing sourness, acts as a preservative by lowering pH to inhibit microbial growth
35522.risks: Dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption, minor irritation potential in high concentrations

35654.name: Ulmus Fulva (Slippery Elm) Bark Extract
35654.description: Extract from the inner bark of the slippery elm tree, traditionally used as a demulcent to soothe mucous membranes and support digestive health. Not FDA approved as a drug but generally recognized as safe (GRAS) as a food ingredient.
35654.benefits: Soothes throat and digestive tract irritation, supports gastrointestinal health, anti-inflammatory properties
35654.risks: Possible allergic reactions, may interfere with absorption of oral medications if taken simultaneously

sources.label: Slippery Elm in Herbal Medicine

35828.name: Wood Rosin Glycerides Esters
35828.description: A food additive used as an emulsifier and stabilizer, derived from wood rosin and esterified with glycerol. Commonly used in beverages and candies to help suspend flavor oils.
35828.benefits: Stabilizes emulsions, improves texture and appearance in food products
35828.risks: Potential allergenicity, limited toxicological data, possible irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: FDA Food Additive Status List

36041.name: Bicarbonate (HCO3-)
36041.description: Bicarbonate is a naturally occurring alkaline compound that acts as a buffer to maintain pH balance in the body and water. It is commonly found in drinking water and plays a role in acid-base homeostasis.
36041.benefits: Helps maintain acid-base balance, aids digestion, may improve exercise performance by buffering lactic acid
36041.risks: Rarely causes alkalosis in normal amounts, potential gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses

36139.name: Roasted chicory root
36139.description: Roasted chicory root is derived from the chicory plant and is commonly used as a coffee substitute or additive. It contains inulin, a type of prebiotic fiber that supports gut health. It is generally recognized as safe by the FDA.
36139.benefits: Prebiotic fiber, supports gut microbiota, may improve digestion and bowel function, low-calorie coffee alternative
36139.risks: Possible digestive upset in sensitive individuals, potential allergy rare

36159.name: Organic Banana Purée
36159.description: Processed mashed banana used as a food ingredient for flavor, texture, and natural sweetness.
36159.benefits: Provides natural sugars, dietary fiber, vitamins (especially vitamin B6 and C), and minerals like potassium
36159.risks: Possible allergen for sensitive individuals, microbial contamination risk if improperly processed

sources.label: Nutritional and health benefits of banana (Musa spp.) consumption
Microbial safety and shelf life of fruit purees

36350.name: Pure rainwater
36350.description: Naturally occurring water collected from precipitation, free from contaminants when pure, used primarily as a diluent or rinse agent in cleaning formulations.
36350.benefits: Environmentally friendly, biodegradable, no chemical residues, non-toxic, non-irritating
36350.risks: None at typical use; potential microbial contamination if not properly stored or collected

sources.label: Water irritation and toxicity assessment

36376.name: Polyglyceryl-10 Eicosanedioate/Tetradecanedioate
36376.description: Synthetic ester of polyglyceryl and dicarboxylic acids used as an emulsifier and skin-conditioning agent in cosmetic products.

36528.name: Fruit
36528.description: Fruits are natural food ingredients rich in vitamins, minerals, dietary fiber, antioxidants, and phytonutrients. They are recognized as healthy dietary components and are generally safe for consumption. The FDA regulates fruits as food and considers them safe when properly handled and consumed.
36528.benefits: Rich in vitamins, minerals, dietary fiber, antioxidants, supports immune function, reduces chronic disease risk

36537.name: Hydrolyzed Fish Collagen
36537.description: Collagen protein derived from fish, enzymatically broken down into smaller peptides to improve absorption. Used primarily as a dietary supplement for protein supply and skin health support.
36537.benefits: Source of bioavailable peptides, supports protein intake
36537.risks: Potential allergenicity, contamination risk from heavy metals or pollutants in fish source

sources.label: Hydrolyzed collagen peptide absorption and safety profile
Collagen peptide supplementation and skin health

36621.name: Acidity Regulator (INS 330)
36621.description: Citric acid used to control acidity and preserve foods and beverages.
36621.benefits: Regulates acidity to enhance flavor and preserve shelf life
36621.risks: Dental erosion with excessive consumption, potential mild gastrointestinal irritation

36622.name: Antioxidants (INS 307b - Alpha-Tocopherol, INS 320 - Butylated Hydroxyanisole (BHA))
36622.description: INS 320 refers to Butylated Hydroxyanisole (BHA), a synthetic antioxidant used to prevent rancidity in fats and oils in food products.
36622.benefits: Prevents oxidation and rancidity in foods, extends shelf life
36622.risks: Potential carcinogenicity in animal studies, endocrine disruption concern, ingestion toxicity at high doses

36674.name: Acidity Regulator
36674.description: A broad class of food additives used to control the pH and acidity of foods and beverages. Common examples include citric acid, lactic acid, and phosphoric acid. They help maintain product stability and shelf life. Typically recognized as safe by regulatory authorities when used within prescribed limits.
36674.benefits: Helps maintain food safety and stability, preserves texture and flavor, prevents microbial growth
36674.risks: Potential gastrointestinal irritation with excessive consumption, may affect mineral absorption (phosphoric acid), possible contribution to dental erosion if consumed in excess

sources.label: FDA Overview of Food Ingredients, Additives, and Colors

36714.name: Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC)
36714.description: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) resin is a synthetic polymer commonly used in plastics. It is a solid, inert material not typically used directly in cleaning products but may be present in packaging or components.
36714.benefits: None specific to cleaning function, used primarily for structural or packaging purposes
36714.risks: Not a skin irritant or sensitizer in resin form, concerns mainly relate to monomer contamination (vinyl chloride) which is carcinogenic, dust inhalation of powder forms may irritate respiratory tract

sources.label: ECHA Substance Information on PVC
Health effects of PVC and vinyl chloride exposure

36893.name: C16 (Hexadecanol or Hexadecanoic acid derivates at 7%)
36893.description: Typically refers to a C16 fatty alcohol or fatty acid derivative used as a surfactant or emulsifier in cleaning products. These long-chain fatty compounds are generally considered mild and non-toxic at low concentrations.
36893.benefits: Biodegradable, effective emulsifier and surfactant, low toxicity, improves formulation stability
36893.risks: Mild skin irritation possible at high concentrations, minimal sensitization reported

sources.label: ECHA Hexadecanol registration dossier
PubChem Hexadecanol chemical summary

37043.name: Lemon Juice from Concentrate
37043.description: Lemon juice concentrated by removing water content, used to provide acidity and flavor in food products. Typically reconstituted before use.
37043.benefits: Source of citric acid for flavor and preservation, contains vitamin C and antioxidants
37043.risks: Irritation risk in high concentrations due to citric acid, possible allergen for citrus-sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMID 21473870 - Citric acid use and safety
PMID 21292539 - Citrus allergy and sensitization

37068.name: Colour
37068.description: A generic term for substances added to food to impart or enhance color, including natural and synthetic dyes. Synthetic colors may be regulated by the FDA, but some have been linked to health concerns.
37068.benefits: Improves visual appeal and acceptance of food products
37068.risks: Potential allergic reactions, hyperactivity in children (certain synthetic dyes), some synthetic colors linked to carcinogenicity concerns

37076.name: Natural Lemon Flavouring with other Natural Flavourings
37076.description: Complex mixtures of volatile compounds used to impart taste and aroma, including constituents derived from natural lemon sources.
37076.benefits: Enhances flavor and aroma, improves palatability of food products
37076.risks: Irritation, sensitization, potential presence of allergenic compounds, variability in composition, possible inclusion of undisclosed synthetic additives

37175.name: Stabilisator Johannisbrotkernmehl
37175.description: Johannisbrotkernmehl, also known as locust bean gum, is a natural thickening and stabilizing agent derived from the seeds of the carob tree (Ceratonia siliqua). It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA and commonly used in food products to improve texture and stability.
37175.benefits: Natural thickener, stabilizes texture, dietary fiber source, low calorie
37175.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, rare allergic reactions

sources.label: Locust bean gum: structure, properties, and applications
FDA GRAS status for locust bean gum

37595.name: Processed with Carbon Dioxide
37595.description: A colorless, odorless gas commonly used as a preservative and modified atmosphere agent to extend freshness of food products.
37595.benefits: Preserves freshness, inhibits microbial growth, extends shelf life
37595.risks: None at typical use levels in food preservation

sources.label: NBK482443 – Carbon dioxide in food preservation and safety

37596.name: Reverse Osmosis Filtered Water
37596.description: Water purified using reverse osmosis to remove impurities, contaminants, and dissolved solids. Considered safe and potable by the FDA.
37596.benefits: High purity, free from contaminants and pathogens, improves taste and safety

sources.label: FDA on Water Quality and Safety

37657.name: Artesian Well Water
37657.description: Groundwater sourced from a confined aquifer, naturally filtered and often used for drinking.
37657.benefits: Hydration, source of essential minerals depending on source

sources.label: PMC5622790 – Quality and safety of drinking water resources

37735.name: Sodium Phytate
37735.description: The sodium salt of phytic acid, a naturally occurring compound in plant seeds that acts as an antioxidant and mineral chelator. Recognized as generally safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in food.
37735.benefits: Antioxidant properties, may have anticancer effects, natural preservative, may reduce glycemic response
37735.risks: Mineral absorption inhibition (iron, zinc, calcium), potential contribution to mineral deficiencies in high amounts

37767.name: Leontopodium Alpinum Flower/Leaf Extract
37767.description: Extract derived from Leontopodium alpinum (Edelweiss), traditionally used for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties in skincare and herbal remedies. Not documented as a food ingredient by the FDA; primarily used topically.
37767.benefits: Contains antioxidants, anti-inflammatory effects, skin-protective properties
37767.risks: Potential for allergic reactions, limited oral safety data

37782.name: Rose
37782.description: Rose petals and extracts are used both as food ingredients and in fragrances. As a food ingredient, rose hips and petals provide dietary antioxidants, vitamins such as vitamin C, and have been traditionally used for flavoring and medicinal purposes. In fragrance and cosmetics, rose extracts are generally safe but can cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals. The FDA considers rose and rose-derived ingredients as generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for food use.
37782.benefits: Contains antioxidants, potential anti-inflammatory properties, may support mood and relaxation, natural flavoring
37782.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, rare skin irritation

sources.label: FDA Food Ingredients

37875.name: Lime Essential Oil
37875.description: Concentrated oil extracted from the peel of lime fruits, containing bioactive compounds such as limonene and citral. Commonly used in flavoring, aromatherapy, and topical applications; recognized as generally safe by the FDA when used appropriately.
37875.benefits: Antimicrobial properties, antioxidant effects, potential mood enhancement, natural flavoring agent
37875.risks: Photosensitivity, skin irritation in sensitive individuals, allergic reactions

37936.name: Bicarbonates
37936.description: Inorganic salts primarily consisting of bicarbonate ions, commonly present in water and biological fluids, acting as pH buffers.
37936.benefits: Buffers pH, aids in maintaining acid-base balance in fluids
37936.risks: None at typical exposure levels in food and water

sources.label: Bicarbonate function and health roles - NCBI Bookshelf

37939.name: Chlorides
37939.description: Inorganic chloride ions commonly present in water and food, essential for electrolyte balance and cellular function.
37939.benefits: Supports electrolyte balance, aids digestion via stomach acid production
37939.risks: None at typical concentrations, excessive intake associated with hypertension

sources.label: Chloride - Essential for Electrolyte Balance

38025.name: Cherry Juice
38025.description: Liquid extract obtained from cherries, containing natural sugars, organic acids, vitamins, and antioxidants.
38025.benefits: Source of antioxidants, vitamins, and dietary polyphenols
38025.risks: High sugar content, possible gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals

38252.name: Stevia Reb M
38252.description: Rebaudioside M is a steviol glycoside extracted from the stevia plant used as a natural, non-nutritive sweetener.
38252.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, suitable for diabetes management, natural origin
38252.risks: Potential for allergenicity or digestive upset in sensitive individuals, limited long-term consumption data

sources.label: PMCID: PMC5372979 - Safety and efficacy of steviol glycosides

38277.name: Sucralose (E955)
38277.description: Sucralose is an artificial sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories or carbohydrates.
38277.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, reduces sugar and carbohydrate intake
38277.risks: Potential gut microbiota alteration, possible mild digestive intolerance, synthetic processing

sources.label: PMID 28601569 - Effects of sucralose on gut microbiota in healthy adults
PMID 23441146 - Review on safety and metabolic impact of sucralose

38369.name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
38369.description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for collagen synthesis, antioxidant protection, and immune function.
38369.benefits: Supports collagen production, antioxidant properties, supports immune function
38369.risks: Low toxicity at typical intake levels, possible gastrointestinal upset at very high doses

sources.label: PMID 19263941 - Vitamin C function and status in human health
PMID 29099763 - Vitamin C and immune support

38400.name: Green Tea Extract (EGCG)
38400.description: Concentrated extract from green tea leaves rich in epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a potent catechin with antioxidant properties. Not FDA-approved as a drug but generally recognized as safe as a dietary supplement when consumed within recommended limits.
38400.benefits: Antioxidant, supports cardiovascular health, may aid weight management, anti-inflammatory, potential neuroprotective effects
38400.risks: Potential liver toxicity at high doses, gastrointestinal upset, interactions with certain medications

38543.name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamin Hydrochloride)
38543.description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function; commonly used as a dietary supplement and fortificant.
38543.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, nervous system function, prevents thiamine deficiency
38543.risks: Rare allergic reactions, possible mild gastrointestinal upset at high doses

sources.label: NCBI - Thiamine (Vitamin B1) Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

38780.name: Organic Stevia Leaf Extract
38780.description: Natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant, FDA generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for use as a sweetener.
38780.benefits: Calorie-free sweetening, may help regulate blood sugar, natural origin, does not contribute to tooth decay
38780.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort in high amounts, potential allergen for sensitive individuals

sources.label: FDA on high-intensity sweeteners including stevia

38822.name: Sodium Chloride
38822.description: Inorganic salt commonly used as a thickener and viscosity modifier in cleaning products. Generally recognized as safe with low toxicity.
38822.benefits: Thickening agent, viscosity control, inexpensive and widely available
38822.risks: None at typical use concentrations, possible mild skin or eye irritation at very high concentrations

sources.label: ECHA Sodium chloride dossier
PubChem Sodium chloride summary

38938.name: Organic Green Tea Extract (L-Theanine)
38938.description: Concentrated extract from green tea leaves, rich in antioxidants like catechins, combined with L-Theanine, an amino acid known for promoting relaxation without drowsiness. Green tea extract is Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by the FDA. L-Theanine is commonly used as a supplement to support cognitive function and stress reduction.
38938.benefits: Antioxidant activity, supports cognitive function, promotes relaxation and reduces stress, may improve focus and attention, cardiovascular benefits
38938.risks: Possible mild side effects like headaches or gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, potential interaction with certain medications

38966.name: D-Alpha-Tocopherol Acetate (Vitamin E)
38966.description: A synthetic ester form of vitamin E used as a nutritional supplement and antioxidant in foods and cosmetics.
38966.benefits: Antioxidant activity, supports immune function, protects cell membranes from oxidative damage

39005.name: Stevia Leaf
39005.description: Natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant. Used as a sugar substitute with negligible calories. Recognized as safe by FDA when used as a sweetener, the leaf extract contains steviol glycosides responsible for its sweetness.
39005.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, may help regulate blood sugar, dental health friendly, natural origin
39005.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort in large amounts, rare allergic reactions

39008.name: FD&C Yellow No. 6 Aluminum Lake
39008.description: FD&C Yellow No. 6 Aluminum Lake is a synthetic azo dye used as a coloring agent in foods, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. It is a water-insoluble pigment form of the dye fixed onto an aluminum substrate.
39008.benefits: Colorant for aesthetic and identification purposes in consumer products
39008.risks: Potential allergen, hypersensitivity reactions, possible behavioral effects in sensitive children, regulatory restrictions on use

sources.label: PMID 1680512 – Study on hypersensitivity reactions to FD&C Yellow No. 6
PMID 12700020 – Review of safety and toxicology of FD&C Yellow No. 6

39013.name: Stevia Leaf Extract (Reb M)
39013.description: Highly purified steviol glycoside extracted from Stevia rebaudiana leaves, used as a non-nutritive sweetener in food and beverages.
39013.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose or insulin, suitable for diabetic and weight management diets
39013.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal upset at high intake, rare allergy or sensitization

39017.name: Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol)
39017.description: Vitamin D3 is a fat-soluble vitamin produced in skin upon UV exposure or taken as a supplement to support calcium homeostasis and bone health.
39017.benefits: Supports calcium absorption, bone mineralization, immune function
39017.risks: Excessive intake may cause hypercalcemia, kidney stones, and toxicity; sensitivity in certain populations

sources.label: PMID 30798774 - Role of vitamin D in bone health
PMID 29019805 - Vitamin D supplementation effects on health

39235.name: Organic Natural Flavour
39235.description: A term referring to flavoring substances derived from organic sources, processed to enhance taste and aroma. Despite being labeled organic, these are still processed flavor extracts with variable composition and transparency.
39235.risks: Lack of transparency, potential exposure to solvents or processing aids, ultra-processed, no direct nutritional value

39341.name: Pyridoxine
39341.description: Pyridoxine, also known as vitamin B6, is a water-soluble vitamin involved in amino acid metabolism, neurotransmitter synthesis, and hemoglobin production.
39341.benefits: Supports amino acid metabolism, neurotransmitter function, and hemoglobin synthesis
39341.risks: High doses can cause sensory neuropathy; low risk at typical dietary levels

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Vitamin B6

39664.name: Zucker
39664.description: Common dietary sugar, primarily sucrose, used as a sweetener and energy source.
39664.benefits: Energy source, improves palatability of foods
39664.risks: Excessive intake associated with obesity, dental caries, and metabolic disorders

sources.label: PMID 29396480 - Health effects of dietary sugars
PMID 28615648 - Sugar intake and dental caries

39698.name: Natrium
39698.description: Natrium is the Latin name for sodium, an essential mineral involved in fluid balance, nerve transmission, and muscle function.
39698.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
39698.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

39901.name: CBD Hemp Oil
39901.description: Extract derived from hemp plants containing cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive cannabinoid. Not FDA-approved as a dietary supplement or food additive, but available as a supplement. Used for potential therapeutic effects.
39901.benefits: May reduce anxiety, anti-inflammatory properties, potential analgesic effects, neuroprotective potential
39901.risks: Interaction with medications, liver enzyme alterations, potential for contamination with THC or pesticides, regulatory variability

39986.name: Vegetable and Fruit Juice Concentrates (For Color)
39986.description: Concentrated vegetable juices used primarily as natural colorants in food products.
39986.benefits: Natural colorant, source of some phytochemicals

40017.name: Prickly Pear Cladode Extract (Opuntia Ficus-Indica)
40017.description: Extract derived from the cladodes (pads) of the Opuntia ficus-indica cactus, traditionally used for its nutritional and medicinal properties. Recognized for antioxidant content and potential benefits in metabolic health.
40017.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, may improve blood glucose regulation, supports lipid metabolism, anti-inflammatory properties, potential to aid in weight management
40017.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, gastrointestinal discomfort in high doses

40078.name: Bis-Methoxypropylamido Isodocosane
40078.description: A synthetic emollient and conditioning agent used primarily in cosmetic and personal care products for skin and hair conditioning. Not a food ingredient and not regulated by the FDA as a food additive.
40078.benefits: Moisturizing and conditioning effects in topical applications
40078.risks: Potential skin irritation or sensitization in rare cases, lack of toxicological data for ingestion, not intended for oral consumption

sources.label: PubChem Chemical Database

40097.name: Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS)
40097.description: Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene is a thermoplastic polymer used for injection molded parts, known for toughness and impact resistance.
40097.benefits: High impact resistance and toughness, versatile and widely used in consumer goods and electronics housings
40097.risks: Potential skin irritation from monomer residues in manufacturing, emission of styrene during processing; low risk in cured product under normal use

40099.name: Polycarbonate
40099.description: A type of plastic commonly used in manufacturing containers, bottles, and various consumer goods. Not intended for direct human consumption and not recognized as a food ingredient by the FDA.
40099.risks: Potential release of bisphenol A (BPA) when heated or degraded, endocrine disruption, possible toxicity with chronic exposure

40226.name: Sucre
40226.description: Common sugar, primarily sucrose, used as a sweetening agent in foods and beverages.
40226.benefits: Provides energy as a carbohydrate source, enhances flavor
40226.risks: Excessive intake associated with dental caries, obesity risk, metabolic disturbances

sources.label: Effects of dietary sugar on health

40458.name: Molecular Hydrogen (H₂) in Water
40458.description: Molecular hydrogen (H2) is a colorless, odorless gas sometimes infused into water or other liquids for potential antioxidative effects.
40458.benefits: Potential antioxidant properties, may reduce oxidative stress in cells
40458.risks: None at typical exposure levels, low toxicity, inhalation in high concentrations can be asphyxiant

40464.name: Soybean Polysaccharide
40464.description: Dietary fiber derived from soybeans, used as a food additive and functional fiber. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA and is used to improve texture, fiber content, and reduce fat absorption.
40464.benefits: Dietary fiber source, may improve digestive health, may help regulate blood sugar

sources.label: FDA Food Additives and Ingredients Overview
FDA GRAS notice for soybean polysaccharide

40633.name: Stevia Rebaudiana Leaf Extract
40633.description: Natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant, primarily containing steviol glycosides responsible for sweetness.
40633.benefits: Non-nutritive sweetener, low-calorie sugar substitute, suitable for glycemic control
40633.risks: Potential minor gastrointestinal discomfort at high intake, possible bitter aftertaste

sources.label: PMID 25900045 - Safety and efficacy of stevia sweeteners
PMID 29681691 - Effects of stevia on blood glucose and insulin

40677.name: Natural Stevia Leaf Extract (Reb A)
40677.description: A natural non-nutritive sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant. Approved by the FDA as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) for use in foods and beverages.
40677.benefits: Zero-calorie sweetener, does not raise blood glucose levels, suitable for diabetics, natural origin
40677.risks: Possible gastrointestinal discomfort in some individuals

sources.label: FDA GRAS Notice for High-Purity Stevia

40707.name: Magnesium (as Aquamin MG)
40707.description: Essential mineral involved in numerous enzymatic reactions, muscle and nerve function, and bone health.
40707.benefits: Supports enzymatic reactions, muscle and nerve function, bone health
40707.risks: None at typical dietary intake levels

40894.name: Invert Sugar Syrup
40894.description: A mixture of glucose and fructose obtained by hydrolyzing sucrose, used as a sweetener and humectant in food products.
40894.benefits: Provides sweetness, humectant properties to retain moisture
40894.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries

sources.label: PMID 29639537 - High fructose and insulin resistance: metabolic concerns
PMID 17025396 - Effects of sugar intake on dental caries

41366.name: Organic Prune Juice Concentrate
41366.description: A concentrated form of juice extracted from prunes (dried plums), organic certified. Used as a natural sweetener and source of nutrients such as potassium and dietary fiber components. Recognized by FDA as generally safe (GRAS) when used as intended.
41366.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, good source of potassium, natural laxative effect aiding bowel regularity, provides vitamins and minerals, supports digestive health
41366.risks: High sugar content, may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, potential laxative effect if consumed in excess

41451.name: Sulphates
41451.description: Sulphates are salts or esters of sulfuric acid, commonly occurring in water and used in various products.
41451.benefits: None at typical trace concentrations in water or products
41451.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, laxative effect if ingested in large amounts, potential to impact taste in water

41464.name: Mountain Valley Spring Water
41464.description: Natural spring water sourced from protected springs, typically containing trace minerals. Generally considered safe and essential for hydration, with no inherent nutritional risks or benefits beyond water's role in the body.

sources.label: Water, Hydration and Health
FDA Guidance on Bottled Water Safety

41578.name: Vitamin E Acetate
41578.description: A synthetic ester of vitamin E used as an antioxidant and skin conditioning agent.
41578.benefits: Antioxidant properties, protects skin lipids from oxidation
41578.risks: Potential respiratory toxicity when inhaled, skin irritation in sensitive individuals

41832.name: Hard Paraffin
41832.description: A petroleum-derived hydrocarbon wax used primarily as a solidifying agent and barrier material in various applications including candles and cosmetics.
41832.benefits: Provides solid form and moisture barrier in topical formulations, used for shaping and stability in products
41832.risks: Potential skin irritation in sensitive individuals, inhalation exposure risk when burned producing particulates and volatile compounds, contamination with polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) possible depending on refinement quality

sources.label: PubMed - Health risks of exposure to paraffin wax smoke

41916.name: Himalayan Pink Salt
41916.description: A type of rock salt mined from the Punjab region of Pakistan, containing trace minerals including iron oxide that gives it a pink color.
41916.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
41916.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

sources.label: NIH - Sodium intake and hypertension risk

42028.name: Antioxidant E320 (Butylated Hydroxyanisole - BHA)
42028.description: Synthetic antioxidant commonly added to foods and cosmetics to prevent oxidation and rancidity.
42028.benefits: Prevents oxidation of fats and oils, extends shelf life of products
42028.risks: Possible carcinogenicity in animal studies, endocrine disruption potential, skin sensitization, restricted in some jurisdictions

sources.label: EFSA re-evaluation of BHA safety

42098.name: Balsamic Vinegar
42098.description: A fermented condiment primarily made from grape must, used for flavoring and dressing.

sources.label: PMCID: PMC5275166 - Vinegars as functional foods

42235.name: Chromium (as Chromium Nicotinate Glycinate Chelate)
42235.description: A chelated form of the trace mineral chromium, combined with nicotinic acid and glycine to potentially improve absorption; chromium is involved in macronutrient metabolism and insulin regulation. Chromium supplements are not FDA-approved for treatment of any condition but are generally recognized as safe when used appropriately.
42235.benefits: May improve insulin sensitivity, assist blood sugar regulation, support metabolism of carbohydrates and fats
42235.risks: Potential for allergic reactions, rare cases of kidney or liver damage at very high doses, possible interaction with diabetes medications

42563.name: Natural Grape Flavour
42563.description: A flavoring agent derived from natural sources intended to mimic the taste of grapes. Often contains complex mixtures of volatile compounds but typically lacks nutritional value.
42563.risks: Lack of transparency, potential trace solvents or allergens, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

42573.name: Fruit and Vegetable Juice Powder
42573.description: A concentrated powder made by dehydrating juices from various fruits and vegetables, often used as a source of phytonutrients and natural colorants in foods. Generally recognized as safe by the FDA when used in typical amounts.
42573.benefits: Source of vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, phytonutrients, convenient nutrient intake
42573.risks: Potential variability in nutrient content, possible added carriers or anti-caking agents, may contribute to sugar content depending on source

42727.name: Cucumber Juice Concentrate
42727.description: Concentrated juice derived from cucumbers; used mainly for hydration and as a source of vitamins and minerals in formulations.
42727.benefits: Natural source of hydration, vitamins, and antioxidants; skin-soothing properties
42727.risks: Low risk of allergic reactions or mild skin irritation in sensitive individuals

43055.name: Synthetic Polymers
43055.description: Man-made large molecules composed of repeating units, often used as thickeners, binders, or film-formers in food products. Not naturally occurring and may be considered ultra-processed.
43055.risks: Potential digestive irritation, lack of nutritional value, may cause allergenic or inflammatory responses, classified as ultra-processed

43170.name: Stevia leaf extract
43170.description: A natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant, used to provide sweetness without calories.
43170.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, suitable for diabetic use
43170.risks: Potential for mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, possible bitter aftertaste, potential allergenicity in rare cases

43218.name: Sulfates
43218.description: Inorganic salts or esters of sulfuric acid, commonly found in various forms such as sodium lauryl sulfate used in cleaning and personal care products.
43218.risks: Irritation and sensitization risk especially to skin and eyes, potential contamination depending on source

43437.name: Vitamin B12 (Cyanocobalamin)
43437.description: A synthetic form of vitamin B12 used as a dietary supplement and food additive to prevent or treat deficiency. It is essential for red blood cell formation, neurological function, and DNA synthesis.
43437.benefits: Prevents and treats vitamin B12 deficiency, supports neurological health, aids red blood cell formation

sources.label: Vitamin B12: deficiency and supplementation - NIH PubMed
