sources.label: FDA GRAS Notice for high-purity steviol glycosides

68508.name: Vitamina A (beta-caroteno)
68508.description: Beta-carotene is a provitamin A carotenoid found in many fruits and vegetables. It is converted in the body to retinol (active vitamin A), essential for vision, immune function, and skin health. Recognized as safe by the FDA when consumed in typical dietary amounts.
68508.benefits: Antioxidant, supports eye health, boosts immune function, skin maintenance
68508.risks: High-dose supplementation may cause carotenemia (benign discoloration), potential risk of lung cancer in smokers with high-dose supplements

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Vitamin A

68717.name: Fruit (6%) strawberry (3.5%)
68717.description: Strawberries are edible fruits containing vitamins, antioxidants, and dietary fiber. Used at 3.5% concentration, typically as a flavor or natural additive in foods or cosmetics.
68717.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, natural flavoring
68717.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible pesticide residue contamination depending on source

sources.label: PMCID: PMC5465813 - Nutritional and health benefits of strawberries
PMID: 30481452 - Strawberry allergy and allergenicity

68756.name: Silicato de calcio
68756.description: Calcium silicate is an inorganic compound commonly used as an anti-caking agent and food additive to prevent clumping. It is recognized as safe by regulatory agencies such as the FDA when used in accordance with good manufacturing practices.
68756.benefits: Prevents caking, maintains food quality and texture

68767.name: Aspartame
68767.description: Artificial sweetener commonly used in food and beverages as a low-calorie sugar substitute. Contains a source of phenylalanine.
68767.benefits: Provides sweetness with low caloric content, useful for sugar reduction
68767.risks: Phenylalanine source harmful to individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU), potential mild headache or sensitivity reactions in some individuals

sources.label: PMID 15191513 - Safety evaluation of aspartame
PMID 19967482 - Review of aspartame safety and metabolism
PMID 17417064 - Phenylketonuria and phenylalanine in diet

68814.name: Strawberry 20%
68814.description: Strawberry used as a food ingredient, likely in a processed or concentrated form at 20% content. Strawberries are a fruit rich in vitamins, antioxidants, and dietary fiber. When used in food products, they provide nutritional benefits related to vitamin C and polyphenols. The '20%' indicates partial strawberry content, suggesting dilution with other ingredients, which may affect overall nutritional value.

68867.name: Dióxido de carbono
68867.description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a colorless, odorless gas naturally present in the atmosphere. It is not a food ingredient but is commonly used in food processing, such as carbonation of beverages and modified atmosphere packaging to preserve freshness. As a material, exposure to high concentrations can cause respiratory issues, but its use in food contexts is generally safe.
68867.benefits: Used to carbonate beverages, preserve food freshness, inert and non-toxic at typical food use levels
68867.risks: Respiratory irritation at high concentrations, suffocation risk in confined spaces

sources.label: NIOSH Carbon Dioxide Exposure

68877.name: Água
68877.description: Chemical substance composed of hydrogen and oxygen; essential for all known forms of life, used primarily as a solvent and hydration agent.
68877.benefits: Essential for hydration, solvent in numerous biological and chemical processes

sources.label: Water: Essential Nutrient in Nutrition

68915.name: Agua mineral
68915.description: Mineral water is water from a mineral spring containing various minerals, such as salts and sulfur compounds. It is generally safe to consume and often used for hydration and sometimes therapeutic benefits due to mineral content. Approved as safe by food authorities when sourced and processed properly.
68915.benefits: Hydration, source of essential minerals like calcium, magnesium

68987.name: Zitronensaft aus Zitronensaftkonzentrat
68987.description: Concentrated lemon juice derived from citrus fruits, primarily used as a flavoring or acidulant in food and beverages.
68987.benefits: Natural flavor enhancer, source of citric acid and vitamin C, preservative effect in foods
68987.risks: Irritation potential in high concentrations, acidity may contribute to dental enamel erosion

68988.name: Natürliche Aromen
68988.description: Natural flavors derived from various natural sources; exact composition often proprietary and may include solvents or carriers.
68988.risks: Potential allergens, possible traces of gluten-containing grains, lack of transparency, possible solvent residues

sources.label: Health implications of flavor additives (PMC8026810)

69203.name: Apfelsäure (Malic Acid)
69203.description: Organic acid used as acidulant to provide tartness and regulate pH in foods.
69203.benefits: Improves flavor and acidity control in food products
69203.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, minor gastrointestinal discomfort possible

sources.label: Safety evaluation of malic acid as a food additive

69331.name: Alpha-Tocopheryl Acetate [Vitamin E]
69331.description: Fat-soluble vitamin E ester commonly used for antioxidant properties after metabolic conversion to alpha-tocopherol.
69331.benefits: Antioxidant, protects cell membranes from oxidative damage
69331.risks: Excess intake associated with bleeding risk, generally safe at normal doses

sources.label: PMID 17538030 - Vitamin E antioxidant functions

69400.name: Beta carotene [color]
69400.description: Beta carotene is a carotenoid pigment used as a natural colorant and a precursor to vitamin A in the human diet.
69400.benefits: Antioxidant properties, vitamin A precursor, used as natural colorant
69400.risks: Excessive intake can lead to carotenodermia (skin discoloration), possible increased risk in smokers for lung cancer at very high supplemental doses

sources.label: PMID 10972885 - Beta-carotene safety and metabolism

69421.name: Natural Rosemary Flavouring
69421.description: Extracted aromatic compounds from rosemary (Rosmarinus officinalis) used as flavoring agents in food and cosmetics.
69421.benefits: Provides natural flavor, contains antioxidant compounds
69421.risks: Potential allergen, skin and respiratory sensitization, may cause irritation in sensitive individuals

69773.name: Antioxidant (E385) - Calcium Disodium EDTA
69773.description: E385 is calcium disodium EDTA, a chelating agent used as an antioxidant to bind metal ions and prevent oxidation in foods.
69773.benefits: Prevents oxidation of fats and color loss in food, extends shelf life
69773.risks: Low risk at permitted levels, potential for mild gastrointestinal irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: EFSA scientific opinion on calcium disodium EDTA (E385)

69777.name: Aqua
69777.description: Refers to purified water used as a solvent or diluent in formulations, with Q.S indicating quantity sufficient to complete the formulation volume.
69777.benefits: Widely used as a non-toxic solvent and carrier

69875.name: Acrylates
69875.description: Acrylates are a group of synthetic polymers derived from acrylic acid, commonly used in adhesives, coatings, cosmetics, and some consumer products. They are not food ingredients and primarily classified as materials. Some acrylate compounds can cause skin irritation and allergic reactions upon contact; inhalation or ingestion can be harmful depending on the specific acrylate compound and exposure level. Safe use depends on formulation and exposure controls.
69875.benefits: Useful in adhesives, coatings, cosmetics for flexibility and durability
69875.risks: Skin irritation, allergic contact dermatitis, respiratory irritation with inhalation exposure, potential toxicity if ingested

sources.label: PubChem Acrylates Chemical Overview

70061.name: Wortel
70061.description: Carrot content representing 35% of the product; carrots are root vegetables rich in beta-carotene and dietary fiber.
70061.benefits: Source of beta-carotene, dietary fiber, vitamins

sources.label: Health benefits of carrots and beta-carotene

70261.name: Extrait de fruit de framboise
70261.description: Raspberry fruit extract derived from Rubus idaeus, used as a flavoring and antioxidant source in food products. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used appropriately.
70261.benefits: Contains antioxidants, vitamins, supports potential anti-inflammatory effects, natural flavoring

70321.name: Organic Beta Carotene
70321.description: Beta carotene is a provitamin A carotenoid found naturally in fruits and vegetables. It is an antioxidant and is converted by the body into vitamin A, essential for vision, immune function, and skin health. The 'organic' designation refers to its cultivation without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. The FDA considers beta carotene safe as a food ingredient and dietary supplement.
70321.benefits: Antioxidant, vitamin A precursor, supports vision, immune health, skin health
70321.risks: Overconsumption may cause carotenodermia (skin discoloration), potential risk in smokers for increased lung cancer at high supplemental doses

sources.label: NIH Vitamin A Fact Sheet

70493.name: Natural raspberry aroma
70493.description: Natural raspberry aroma refers to flavoring compounds derived from raspberry fruits or their natural extracts, used to impart raspberry scent and taste. Despite the 'natural' label, these aromas can be highly processed and may contain multiple chemical constituents. The FDA classifies natural flavors as generally recognized as safe (GRAS) but does not require disclosure of specific components.
70493.benefits: Provides raspberry flavor without added sugars or calories
70493.risks: Lack of transparency, potential allergens, ultra-processed, possible solvents or preservatives

70779.name: Agua carbonatada
70779.description: Water infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure, creating carbonated or sparkling water.
70779.benefits: Hydration, can improve palatability of water for increased intake
70779.risks: Mild dental enamel erosion risk with excessive consumption, minor gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals

71035.name: Yellow 5
71035.description: Synthetic azo dye used as a color additive in food, drugs, and cosmetics.
71035.benefits: Provides bright yellow color, improves product appearance and consumer appeal
71035.risks: Irritant/sensitizer potential, allergy and hypersensitivity reactions including urticaria and asthma, possible behavioral effects in sensitive children, regulatory limits on use concentration

sources.label: PMID 23056311 – Adverse reactions to food additives including Yellow 5
PMID 22995317 – Behavioral effects of synthetic food dyes in children

71069.name: Zucchero
71069.description: Sucrose, a common sugar used as a sweetener and energy source in foods.
71069.benefits: Provides energy as a carbohydrate source
71069.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain and dental caries

sources.label: Sweeteners and Health Risks – PMC4266947

71108.name: Dye beta-carotene
71108.description: A red-orange pigment found in plants and fruits, beta carotene is a precursor to vitamin A and functions as an antioxidant.
71108.benefits: Precursor to vitamin A, antioxidant properties supporting eye and immune health
71108.risks: High-dose supplementation linked to increased lung cancer risk in smokers, potential skin discoloration (carotenodermia) at high intake

71316.name: Açúcar
71316.description: Sucrose, a disaccharide sugar commonly used as a sweetener in foods and beverages.
71316.benefits: Provides caloric energy, enhances flavor and palatability
71316.risks: Excessive intake associated with increased risk of obesity, dental caries, and metabolic disorders

sources.label: PMC6363521 – Health effects of dietary sugars

71339.name: Zinkcitrat
71339.description: Zinkcitrat (Zinc citrate) is a zinc salt commonly used as a dietary supplement to provide bioavailable zinc, an essential trace element important for immune function, enzymatic reactions, and cellular metabolism. It is generally recognized as safe by regulatory authorities when used within recommended dosages.
71339.benefits: Supports immune system, aids wound healing, antioxidant properties, supports enzymatic functions
71339.risks: High doses can cause nausea, gastrointestinal upset, copper deficiency with long-term excessive intake

sources.label: NIH Zinc Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

71354.name: Natural Panax Ginseng Extract
71354.description: Panax ginseng extract is derived from the root of the Panax ginseng plant. It is widely used in traditional medicine and dietary supplements for its adaptogenic properties. The FDA categorizes it as a dietary supplement ingredient but does not approve it as a drug. It contains bioactive compounds called ginsenosides thought to provide health benefits.
71354.benefits: May improve cognitive function, reduce fatigue, enhance immune response, provide antioxidant effects, support blood sugar regulation
71354.risks: Possible allergic reactions, interactions with blood thinners and stimulants, may cause insomnia or gastrointestinal upset in some individuals

71453.name: Dried Mint
71453.description: Dried leaves of the mint plant, used primarily as a flavoring and aromatic herb in food and beverages.
71453.benefits: Flavor enhancement, aromatic properties, mild digestive aid
71453.risks: Irritation risk in high concentration, potential for allergic sensitization in sensitive individuals

71810.name: Pink Grapefruit
71810.description: Natural juice concentrate from pink grapefruit, used for flavor and aroma and contains natural sugars and bioactive compounds.
71810.benefits: Contains vitamin C, antioxidants, natural flavoring
71810.risks: Photosensitization risk in sensitive skin, potential drug interaction risks when ingested in large amounts, allergic reactions

71824.name: Fat
71824.description: Macronutrient composed of triglycerides; provides energy, supports cell structure, and aids absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
71824.benefits: Energy source, supports cell membrane integrity, aids absorption of fat-soluble vitamins
71824.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain and cardiovascular risk depending on fat type

71927.name: Artificial Sweetener (Sucralose)
71927.description: Sucralose is a non-nutritive artificial sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute. It is FDA-approved and considered safe for general consumption, but emerging evidence raises concerns about possible negative effects on gut microbiota and glucose metabolism.
71927.benefits: Zero-calorie sugar substitute, helps reduce caloric intake, does not raise blood glucose levels
71927.risks: Potential disruption of gut microbiota, possible effects on glucose metabolism, may contribute to metabolic syndrome in some individuals

72402.name: Volvic Natural Mineral Water
72402.description: Volvic natural mineral water is sourced from volcanic regions in France, containing minerals such as calcium, magnesium, and potassium. It is purified and safe for regular consumption, meeting FDA and EU standards for mineral water.
72402.benefits: Hydration, provides essential minerals like calcium and magnesium, supports electrolyte balance

sources.label: FDA Mineral Water Regulations

72632.name: Ascorbic Acid [Vitamin C]
72632.description: Water-soluble vitamin functioning as an antioxidant and cofactor in collagen synthesis.
72632.benefits: Antioxidant, supports immune function, aids collagen synthesis
72632.risks: High doses may cause gastrointestinal discomfort or kidney stones in susceptible individuals

sources.label: PMC: Role of Vitamin C in Skin Health
PMC: Vitamin C and Immune Function

72633.name: Calcium D-Pantothenate [Vitamin B5]
72633.description: Calcium D-Pantothenate is the calcium salt of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), essential for Coenzyme A synthesis and energy metabolism.
72633.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, skin health, and synthesis of coenzyme A
72633.risks: None at typical use levels, rare allergic reaction possible

sources.label: Biological role of vitamin B5

72722.name: Sicilian Lemon Juice from Concentrate
72722.description: Lemon juice obtained by reconstituting concentrated lemon juice derived from Sicilian lemons. Contains natural organic acids, primarily citric acid, with vitamin C and flavonoids. The concentrate process involves removal of water and later rehydration, which may slightly reduce some volatile compounds but maintains nutritional and flavor properties. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by FDA as a food ingredient.
72722.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidant properties, enhances flavor, supports immune function
72722.risks: Potential acidity-related dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption

sources.label: FDA food additive status list

73328.name: Glyceryl Abietate
73328.description: Ester of glycerol and abietic acid derived from rosin, used as a film-former, stabilizer, or thickener in cosmetics and topical products.
73328.benefits: Film forming, stabilizing, thickening agent in topical formulations
73328.risks: Irritation, sensitization potential especially in sensitive skin, possible impurities from rosin derivatives

sources.label: Use of rosin derivatives in cosmetic formulations

73376.name: Limettensaft aus Limettensaftkonzentrat
73376.description: Concentrated lime juice used primarily for flavoring and acidity adjustment in foods.
73376.benefits: Provides flavor and acidity, source of vitamin C and antioxidants
73376.risks: Mild oral irritation possible in sensitive individuals, acidity may contribute to dental erosion with frequent consumption

sources.label: PMC2812829 - Citrus fruit antioxidants and health benefits

73686.name: Organic Natural Lime Flavor
73686.description: Flavoring derived from organic lime, used to impart lime taste in foods and beverages. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) when used in typical food amounts. The term 'natural flavor' can be vague, indicating a mixture of flavor compounds extracted from natural sources, sometimes chemically processed.
73686.benefits: Provides natural lime aroma and taste, enhances food palatability
73686.risks: Possible presence of trace solvents or processing chemicals, lack of transparency about specific compounds, potential allergenicity in sensitive individuals

73730.name: Azúcar
73730.description: Sucrose, a disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose, commonly used as a sweetener in foods and beverages.
73730.benefits: Provides energy as a carbohydrate source
73730.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, and increased risk of metabolic diseases

sources.label: PMID 23463986 - Dietary sugars and obesity
PMID 20675614 - Sugars, dental caries, and health risks

74283.name: Pure Water
74283.description: Essential for life, pure water contains no contaminants or additives. It is critical for hydration, metabolic processes, and maintaining physiological homeostasis. Recognized as safe and necessary by all health authorities.
74283.benefits: Hydration, supports metabolic processes, detoxification, essential nutrient carrier

sources.label: Water, hydration, and health - NCBI Bookshelf

74378.name: Sodium (from Sodium Chloride and Sodium Bicarbonate)
74378.description: Sodium is an essential electrolyte involved in fluid balance, nerve transmission, and muscle function. Sodium chloride (table salt) is the primary dietary source, while sodium bicarbonate is used as an antacid and leavening agent. Normal intake supports physiological functions; excessive intake may increase risk of hypertension and cardiovascular disease.
74378.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance, muscle contraction
74378.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

74396.name: 100% Natural Spring Water
74396.description: Water sourced from natural springs, typically containing minerals in trace amounts. Recognized as safe and essential for hydration and bodily functions. FDA classifies water as a food ingredient when consumed.
74396.benefits: Hydration, essential for life, contains trace minerals

sources.label: Water: Essential Nutrient for Life
FDA Food Labeling - water as a food ingredient

74498.name: Mandarin Juice
74498.description: Juice extracted from mandarins, commonly used as a flavoring agent and source of natural sugars and vitamin C.
74498.benefits: Provides natural flavor, source of vitamin C and antioxidants
74498.risks: Potential for allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, sugar content contributing to caloric intake

sources.label: PMC3257681 - Nutritional and antioxidant properties of citrus juices

74710.name: Fresh golden yuzu juice
74710.description: Fresh juice extracted from the golden yuzu fruit, a citrus fruit native to East Asia. It is rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) when consumed as a food ingredient.
74710.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, supports immune function, adds natural flavor
74710.risks: Potential citrus allergy in sensitive individuals, may cause photosensitivity in rare cases

75005.name: Ácido cítrico
75005.description: Organic acid used primarily as an antioxidant and pH adjuster in food and cosmetic products.
75005.benefits: Prevents oxidation, preserves freshness, enhances flavor stability
75005.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, potential dentin erosion with excessive consumption

sources.label: PMC4005367 - Use and safety of citric acid in foods

75007.name: Zumo de limón a partir de concentrado
75007.description: Lemon juice reconstituted from concentrate, commonly used as a flavoring and acidulant in foods and beverages. Contains vitamin C and citric acid. Regarded as safe for consumption by the FDA when produced hygienically.
75007.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidant properties, enhances flavor, natural acidulant
75007.risks: May contain added sugars or preservatives depending on processing, potential acidity may cause dental erosion in excessive amounts

sources.label: FDA Guidance on Food Ingredients

75247.name: Cukor
75247.description: "Cukor" is the Hungarian word for sugar, a carbohydrate used as a sweetener and energy source. Commonly refers to sucrose derived from sugar cane or sugar beets. Recognized by the FDA as safe for consumption but offers no essential nutrients beyond calories.
75247.benefits: Provides quick energy, enhances flavor of foods and beverages
75247.risks: Metabolic syndrome, obesity, dental caries, insulin resistance, increased cardiovascular risk with excessive consumption

75479.name: Aromatizante
75479.description: Spanish term for 'flavorings' or 'flavor additives,' typically referring to added substances to impart flavor in foods or fragrances. Often vague, may include natural or artificial chemical compounds.
75479.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain synthetic chemicals, potential allergens, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

75680.name: Sanguinello Blood Orange Juice
75680.description: Juice extracted from Sanguinello blood oranges, a variety known for its deep red flesh and high content of vitamin C, antioxidants, and flavonoids. Recognized as a natural food ingredient with no safety concerns when consumed in typical dietary amounts.
75680.benefits: Rich source of vitamin C, antioxidants (anthocyanins, flavonoids), supports immune health, anti-inflammatory properties, may aid cardiovascular health
75680.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential acidity-related dental erosion if consumed excessively

75890.name: Natural Mint Aroma
75890.description: A flavoring ingredient derived from natural mint sources, typically used to impart mint flavor in foods and beverages. The exact composition is often proprietary and may include distilled mint oils and natural extracts. Considered generally safe by the FDA when used as intended in food products.
75890.benefits: Provides mint flavor, derived from natural sources, enhances palatability
75890.risks: Potential allergen, flavor sensitivity, ultra-processed, lack of full transparency

75906.name: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
75906.description: Water-soluble vitamin involved in collagen synthesis, antioxidant activity, and immune function support.
75906.benefits: Antioxidant, supports collagen production, aids immune defense, enhances iron absorption
75906.risks: High doses may cause gastrointestinal discomfort, potential pro-oxidant effects in presence of metal ions at excessive levels

sources.label: PMID 18296328 - Role of Vitamin C in health
PMID 29101323 - Safety of Vitamin C supplementation

76016.name: Food Preservatives E202 (Potassium Sorbate)
76016.description: Potassium sorbate (E202) is a widely used food preservative effective in inhibiting molds, yeasts, and some bacteria. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used within recommended levels in foods and beverages.
76016.benefits: Prevents microbial spoilage, extends shelf life, reduces foodborne illness risk
76016.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, mild gastrointestinal discomfort in large amounts, possible skin irritation on direct contact

sources.label: FDA Food Additive Status List

76300.name: Şeker (Sugar)
76300.description: Sucrose, commonly used as a sweetener in foods and beverages.
76300.benefits: Provides energy as carbohydrate source, enhances flavor
76300.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, increased risk of metabolic disorders

76455.name: Apfelsaft
76455.description: Apple juice, a beverage derived from pressed apples containing natural sugars, organic acids, and micronutrients.
76455.benefits: Source of natural vitamins (such as vitamin C), hydration, contains antioxidants
76455.risks: High sugar content, potential contribution to dental caries, excessive caloric intake if consumed in large amounts

sources.label: PMC3775240 - Nutritional and health benefits of apple juice
PubMed 20725369 - Apple and apple juice impact on dental health

76473.name: Beta-Carotene Color
76473.description: Beta-carotene is a carotenoid pigment used primarily as a natural colorant in foods and cosmetics. It is a precursor to vitamin A.
76473.benefits: Colorant properties, provitamin A activity, antioxidant potential
76473.risks: Rare irritation or sensitization on skin contact, excessive intake may cause carotenodermia, no major toxicity at typical use levels

sources.label: Dietary carotenoids and health

77079.name: Malic Acid (Äpfelsäure)
77079.description: A naturally occurring organic acid used as an acidulant to impart sour taste and adjust pH in food products.
77079.benefits: Enhances flavor by adding sourness, acts as pH regulator
77079.risks: Irritation at high concentrations, dental enamel erosion with excessive intake

sources.label: PMID 20024628 - Safety assessment of malic acid

77161.name: Folsäure
77161.description: Folic acid is the synthetic form of folate, a water-soluble B-vitamin (B9) essential for DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and prevention of neural tube defects during pregnancy. Widely used in dietary supplements and food fortification. Recognized as safe and essential by FDA and other health authorities.
77161.benefits: Prevention of neural tube defects, supports DNA synthesis, reduces risk of some anemias
77161.risks: Excess intake may mask vitamin B12 deficiency, possible interaction with certain medications

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Folate

77182.name: Oleoresin Paprika [Color]
77182.description: Oleoresin paprika is a concentrated extract derived from paprika peppers primarily used as a natural colorant in food products.
77182.benefits: Natural colorant, source of carotenoids providing red-orange color
77182.risks: Possible skin and eye irritation, potential allergen for sensitive individuals

sources.label: Safety and efficacy of paprika oleoresins as food colorants

77313.name: Yuzu extract
77313.description: Yuzu extract is derived from the citrus fruit Yuzu (Citrus junos), commonly used as a flavoring agent in food and beverages. It contains vitamin C, antioxidants, and aromatic compounds. Generally recognized as safe for consumption, Yuzu extract offers flavor enhancement and potential health benefits associated with citrus bioactives.
77313.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, antioxidant properties, flavor enhancement, potential anti-inflammatory effects
77313.risks: Possible allergic reactions in citrus-sensitive individuals, photosensitivity in rare cases

78025.name: Natural Colour Black Carrot Concentrate
78025.description: A natural food colorant derived from black carrots rich in anthocyanins, used to impart purple to black hues in foods. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) and used as a natural alternative to synthetic dyes.
78025.benefits: Natural colorant, antioxidant properties, no synthetic additives, safe for consumption

sources.label: FDA Color Additives Overview

78372.name: Prepared drinking water
78372.description: Water that has undergone some form of treatment or purification to remove contaminants and improve safety or taste.
78372.benefits: Hydration, solvent for ingredients, supports metabolic processes
78372.risks: None at typical use, possible contamination if improperly handled or stored

78536.name: Eau gazéifiée
78536.description: Carbonated water, typically water infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure. Generally recognized as safe for consumption without nutritional value.
78536.benefits: Hydration, alternative to still water, may aid digestion for some individuals
78536.risks: Dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption due to acidity

78975.name: Acidity regulator (E331)
78975.description: E331 refers to sodium citrates, commonly used as acidity regulators and preservatives in food products to control pH and enhance stability. It is considered safe for consumption by the FDA and EFSA.
78975.benefits: Controls acidity, preserves food stability, may enhance mineral absorption
78975.risks: Rare allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible laxative effect in very high amounts

sources.label: EFSA Scientific Opinion on the safety of sodium citrates (E331)

79025.name: Rebaudioside A (from stevia)
79025.description: Rebaudioside A is a major steviol glycoside extracted from the stevia plant, used as a natural non-caloric sweetener. It is FDA approved as Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) for use in foods and beverages. It has minimal impact on blood glucose and is considered safe for consumption at typical levels.
79025.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood sugar, suitable for diabetics, natural origin
79025.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, rare allergic reactions

sources.label: FDA GRAS Notice for Steviol Glycosides

79175.name: Cypermethrin
79175.description: Synthetic pyrethroid insecticide occasionally found in pest-control related cleaning products. Acts on insect nervous system disrupting nerve function.
79175.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, potential neurotoxicity on prolonged exposure, possible respiratory sensitization, environmental toxicity especially aquatic organisms

sources.label: ECHA Cypermethrin Brief Profile
Review on Pyrethroid Toxicity and Safety

79201.name: Organic Lemon Pulp
79201.description: Organic lemon pulp consists of the fibrous, fleshy part of the lemon fruit, rich in dietary fiber, vitamins, and bioactive compounds. Generally recognized as safe and consumed as a whole food ingredient.
79201.benefits: Rich source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, antioxidants, supports digestion, immune health

79306.name: Ginger Powder
79306.description: Dried and ground form of ginger root used as a spice and flavoring agent.
79306.benefits: Flavoring agent, contains bioactive compounds with antioxidant properties
79306.risks: Mild irritation possible in sensitive individuals, potential allergen

79383.name: CBD from Broad-Spectrum Hemp Extract
79383.description: Cannabidiol (CBD) is a non-intoxicating cannabinoid derived from hemp. Broad-spectrum hemp extract contains multiple cannabinoids and terpenes except THC, which is removed or undetectable. Used widely for potential therapeutic effects including anxiety relief, anti-inflammatory, and pain management. Not FDA-approved as a food additive or dietary supplement ingredient, with regulatory status evolving.
79383.benefits: Anxiolytic, anti-inflammatory, analgesic, neuroprotective, seizure reduction in certain conditions
79383.risks: Potential drug interactions, liver enzyme alterations, drowsiness, gastrointestinal discomfort, variability in product purity and labeling accuracy

sources.label: FDA regulation of CBD products

79477.name: Glukózo-fruktózový sirup
79477.description: Glukózo-fruktózový sirup is the Czech term for glucose-fructose syrup, a sweetener derived from starch hydrolysis, similar to high fructose corn syrup (HFCS). It contains varying ratios of glucose and fructose. Commonly used as a sweetener in processed foods and beverages. Not recognized as essential in diet and associated with metabolic health concerns.
79477.risks: Metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, obesity, type 2 diabetes, dental caries, increased inflammation

79568.name: Édulcorant (glycoside de stéviol)
79568.description: Steviol glycosides are natural sweeteners extracted from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant. Recognized as safe by the FDA and EFSA for use as non-nutritive sweeteners, they provide sweet taste without calories or impact on blood sugar.
79568.benefits: Calorie-free sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, tooth-friendly, natural origin
79568.risks: Possible mild digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals, rare allergenic reactions

sources.label: FDA Overview on Stevia Sweeteners

79953.name: Aspartame and Neohesperidin DC
79953.description: Aspartame is a widely used artificial sweetener approved by FDA, commonly used as a low-calorie sugar substitute. Neohesperidin DC is a sweetener derived from citrus flavonoid neohesperidin, used as a flavor enhancer and sweetness modifier. Both are synthetic additives used in food and beverages to provide sweetness without calories.
79953.benefits: Provides sweetness with low or no calories, useful for weight management and diabetics
79953.risks: Aspartame may cause mild side effects in sensitive individuals, possible headaches, phenylketonuria risk, debated controversy over long-term safety; Neohesperidin DC may have limited safety data but generally considered safe at approved levels

79997.name: Caffeine
79997.description: A central nervous system stimulant commonly found in coffee, tea, and various beverages. It is used primarily to increase alertness and reduce fatigue.
79997.risks: Stimulant effects including increased heart rate, potential for insomnia, anxiety, dependence with chronic high intake

sources.label: PMID 25295675 – Caffeine: cognitive and physical performance effects
PMID 24659174 – Safety and efficacy of caffeine

80089.name: Cyclamate
80089.description: Cyclamate is an artificial sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories.
80089.risks: Potential carcinogenicity noted in rodent studies leading to regulatory restrictions, ingestion toxicity concern

sources.label: NCI Carcinogenesis studies on cyclamate
FDA regulatory stance on cyclamate
EFSA re-evaluation of cyclamate safety

80526.name: Dioxyde de carbone
80526.description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a colorless gas naturally present in the atmosphere. In food industry, it is commonly used as a carbonation agent and preservative. It is safe for consumption at regulated levels and is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA.
80526.benefits: Used in carbonation, preservative properties, inert and non-toxic at regulated amounts

sources.label: FDA GRAS status and CO2 uses

80823.name: Natural Citrus Aroma
80823.description: A flavoring ingredient derived from natural citrus sources such as orange, lemon, or grapefruit. Typically used to impart citrus flavor in foods and beverages. While labeled 'natural,' it may undergo extraction and processing methods that include solvents and carriers. It does not provide nutritional value and is primarily used for sensory enhancement.
80823.benefits: Imparts pleasant natural citrus flavor, may enhance palatability of foods and beverages
80823.risks: Possible exposure to extraction solvents, lack of full ingredient transparency, potential allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, ultra-processed additive

80838.name: Mineraalwater
80838.description: Mineraalwater (mineral water) is water from a natural mineral spring containing various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, and bicarbonates. It is generally safe for consumption and can contribute to hydration and intake of essential minerals. The FDA considers natural mineral water to be safe if it meets regulatory standards.
80838.benefits: Hydration, source of essential minerals like calcium and magnesium

sources.label: FDA guidance on mineral water

81056.name: Hibiscus Sabdariffa (Hibiscus)
81056.description: Hibiscus Sabdariffa is a plant whose calyces are commonly used to make herbal teas and food products. It is rich in antioxidants, particularly anthocyanins, and has been studied for cardiovascular and metabolic benefits. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for consumption.
81056.benefits: Antioxidant-rich, may reduce blood pressure, supports cardiovascular health, anti-inflammatory effects, source of vitamin C
81056.risks: May lower blood pressure excessively in hypertensive individuals, potential allergic reactions (rare)

81125.name: Orange 2
81125.description: Orange 2 is a synthetic azo dye formerly used as a food colorant and in cosmetics. It is not approved for use in foods by the FDA due to concerns over its safety and carcinogenic potential. The compound has been associated with mutagenic effects in animal studies and is considered a potential human carcinogen.
81125.risks: Carcinogenic potential, mutagenicity, allergenic reactions, regulatory disapproval for food use

sources.label: FDA - Cosmetic ingredient status of Orange 2

81128.name: Colorants (caroténoïdes)
81128.description: Carotenoids are pigmented compounds with antioxidant properties commonly extracted from natural sources; vanilla extract contains vanillin compounds used as a flavoring.
81128.benefits: Provides antioxidant activity, natural colorant effects (carotenoids), and flavoring (vanilla extract)
81128.risks: None at typical use levels; rare sensitization possible from vanilla in topical exposures

81129.name: Antioxydant (acide ascorbique)
81129.description: Acide ascorbique, ou vitamine C, est un agent de traitement de la farine utilisé comme oxydant pour améliorer les propriétés de panification.
81129.benefits: Améliore la qualité de la pâte, agent oxydant, contribue à la résistance et élasticité de la pâte
81129.risks: Irritation possible à des concentrations élevées, rares cas d’allergie

sources.label: Ascorbic Acid - Food Additives

81202.name: Citronensäure
81202.description: Organic acid commonly used as a food additive for acidity regulation and as a preservative.
81202.benefits: Acidity regulator, preservative, enhances flavor stability
81202.risks: Irritation to skin, eyes, and respiratory tract in concentrated form; may cause mild digestive upset if consumed in large amounts

sources.label: PMID 15785773 – Safety and applications of citric acid

81203.name: Natriumsulfat
81203.description: Sodium sulfate is an inorganic salt commonly used as a filler or bulking agent in cleaning products. It is generally considered chemically inert and low in toxicity.
81203.benefits: Inert filler, helps improve product texture and viscosity, non-toxic, environmentally benign
81203.risks: Possible mild skin and eye irritation at high concentrations

sources.label: ECHA Sodium sulfate substance information
PubChem Sodium sulfate

81314.name: Amidon modifié
81314.description: Modified starch derived from natural starches treated physically, enzymatically, or chemically to alter properties such as thickening, stability, and texture in foods.
81314.benefits: Improved texture, stability, thickening agent in food formulations

81356.name: 6:2 FTSA
81356.description: 6:2 Fluorotelomer Sulfonic Acid (6:2 FTSA) is a synthetic surfactant and a type of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS). It is used primarily in industrial and manufacturing applications such as textile treatment, paper coatings, and firefighting foams. Not approved for food use and is considered an environmental contaminant with bioaccumulative properties.
81356.benefits: Effective surfactant and stain resistant properties in industrial applications
81356.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, developmental toxicity, carcinogenic potential

81357.name: 4:2 FTSA
81357.description: 4:2 Fluorotelomer sulfonic acid (4:2 FTSA) is a perfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) used as a degradation product and precursor to longer-chain PFAS compounds. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical material often detected as an environmental contaminant with persistence and bioaccumulative potential.
81357.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential toxicity, endocrine disruption, carcinogenicity concerns

81358.name: ADONA
81358.description: ADONA, also known as 1,3-Dimethylbutylamine or dimethylpentylamine, is a stimulant structurally related to methylhexanamine (DMAA). It is sometimes used in dietary supplements for purported energy and performance enhancement. Not approved by the FDA as a food additive or dietary ingredient, ADONA's safety profile is not well established. It has potential stimulant effects but lacks extensive peer-reviewed safety data.
81358.benefits: Potential stimulant and energy enhancement (anecdotal, not well-established)
81358.risks: Cardiovascular effects, increased heart rate, blood pressure elevation, potential toxicity, lack of regulatory approval, possible stimulant-related adverse events

81359.name: Perfluorododecanoic acid PFDoA
81359.description: A man-made perfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) used in industrial applications for its water and oil repellant properties. Not approved for food use. Known to be environmentally persistent and bioaccumulative.
81359.risks: Toxicity to liver and kidneys, endocrine disruption, bioaccumulation, environmental persistence, potential carcinogenicity

81360.name: Perfluoropentane sulfonic acid PFPeS
81360.description: PFPeS is a synthetic per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) used in industrial applications for its water, oil, and stain-resistant properties. It is persistent in the environment and resistant to degradation.
81360.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential toxicity, endocrine disruption, potential carcinogenicity, reproductive and developmental toxicity

sources.label: Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry - PFAS Toxicological Profile

81361.name: Perfluoroundecanoic acid PFUnA
81361.description: A synthetic perfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) used in industrial applications for its chemical stability and resistance to heat, water, and oil. Not a food ingredient; primarily an environmental contaminant with persistence and bioaccumulation potential.
81361.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, developmental toxicity, immunotoxicity, possible carcinogenic effects

81362.name: 11Cl-PF3OUdS
81362.description: Tap water contaminant (EWG): 11Cl-PF3OUdS. Add description/guidelines in admin.

81363.name: NMeFOSAA
81363.description: A synthetic perfluoroalkyl substance related to PFAS chemicals, often found as a degradation product from certain stain-resistant coatings and firefighting foams. Not a food ingredient; it is an environmental contaminant with potential bioaccumulative and toxic properties.
81363.risks: Persistent environmental pollutant, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, liver toxicity, carcinogenicity concerns

81364.name: N-EtFOSAA
81364.description: N-Ethyl perfluorooctane sulfonamidoacetic acid (N-EtFOSAA) is a per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) and a degradation precursor to PFOS (perfluorooctane sulfonate). It is an environmental contaminant known for persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity. Not a food ingredient; poses health risks primarily via environmental and human exposure rather than direct consumption.
81364.risks: Persistent organic pollutant, bioaccumulative, endocrine disruption, developmental toxicity, potential carcinogen

81365.name: Perfluoroheptane sulfonic acid PFHpS
81365.description: A perfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS), used in industrial applications for its stain-resistant and water-repellent properties. It is persistent in the environment and bioaccumulative. Not a food ingredient; relevant for material contamination assessment and environmental health.
81365.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, toxicity, immune system effects, carcinogenic potential

81366.name: Perfluorotridecanoic acid PFTrDA
81366.description: A long-chain perfluoroalkyl acid belonging to the PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) family. Not a food ingredient but an environmental contaminant and industrial chemical with persistence and bioaccumulation concerns.
81366.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, toxicity to liver and immune system, carcinogenic potential

81367.name: Perfluorotetradecanoic acid PFTA
81367.description: A perfluorinated carboxylic acid belonging to the PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) family, used in various industrial applications for its water and oil repellent properties. Not a food ingredient. Known environmental persistent pollutant with bioaccumulative and toxic properties. Concerns exist related to human exposure through contaminated water, food, and consumer products.
81367.benefits: Industrial applications in creating stain-resistant coatings and surfactants
81367.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, hepatotoxicity, immunotoxicity, developmental toxicity, carcinogenic potential

sources.label: ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Perfluoroalkyls

81368.name: 9Cl-PF3ONS
81368.description: 9Cl-PF3ONS is a perfluoroalkyl sulfonate compound, part of the PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) class. PFAS are synthetic chemicals widely used for their water- and stain-resistant properties but are persistent environmental pollutants with potential adverse health effects. This compound is not a food ingredient but a synthetic chemical material with concerns related to toxicity and bioaccumulation.
81368.risks: Persistent environmental pollutant, bioaccumulative, potential endocrine disruption, toxicological concerns including liver toxicity, immunotoxicity, developmental toxicity

sources.label: PubChem - 9Cl-PF3ONS chemical information

81369.name: 2-methyl-1-propene
81369.description: Also known as isobutylene, a volatile organic compound primarily used as a chemical intermediate in the production of polymers and fuels. Not a food ingredient and not intended for consumption. Used in industrial applications and can be a component of fuels or synthetic resins.
81369.benefits: None (no nutritional or beneficial use in foods or personal care)
81369.risks: Inhalation toxicity, respiratory irritation, flammability, potential environmental pollutant

sources.label: PubChem Isobutylene
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Hydrocarbon Fuels

81370.name: 2-Methoxyethanol
81370.description: A solvent commonly used in industrial applications and manufacturing. Not a food ingredient. Known for its toxicity and potential to cause reproductive harm and organ toxicity upon inhalation or dermal exposure.
81370.risks: Reproductive toxicity, developmental toxicity, organ damage (especially testes), mutagenicity, carcinogenic potential, inhalation hazard, skin absorption hazard

sources.label: PubChem 2-Methoxyethanol Toxicity
NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards - 2-Methoxyethanol

81371.name: n-Nitrosomorpholine
81371.description: n-Nitrosomorpholine is a member of the nitrosamine chemical class, known primarily as a contaminant and a potent carcinogen in food and industrial settings. It is not a food ingredient but a harmful chemical compound often formed by nitrosation of secondary amines under certain conditions.
81371.risks: Carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, potential presence in contaminated food and tobacco products, toxic

81372.name: 2-propen-1-ol
81372.description: Also known as allyl alcohol, it is an industrial chemical used primarily as an intermediate in organic synthesis, not a food ingredient. It is a volatile, reactive alcohol with known toxicity.
81372.risks: Toxicity, hepatotoxicity, respiratory irritation, potential mutagenicity, harmful if ingested or inhaled

sources.label: PubChem Allyl Alcohol Toxicity and Properties

81373.name: Trichlorotrifluoroethane
81373.description: A synthetic chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) historically used as a refrigerant and solvent. Not a food ingredient; significant environmental and health concerns have led to phase-out under international agreements.
81373.risks: Ozone depletion, respiratory toxicity, central nervous system effects, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation

sources.label: PubChem - Trichlorotrifluoroethane
EPA - Ozone Layer Depletion

81388.name: Organic Fruit Juice
81388.description: Liquid extracted from fruits grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers. Contains natural sugars, vitamins, minerals, and phytochemicals. Organic certification indicates no synthetic chemicals used in cultivation. Nutritional value varies based on fruit type. Consumption in moderate amounts is generally safe, though high sugar content can affect metabolic health.
81388.benefits: Source of vitamins (e.g., vitamin C), minerals, antioxidants, and phytochemicals; organic status reduces exposure to synthetic pesticide residues
81388.risks: High natural sugar content, potential contribution to dental caries, possible impact on blood sugar regulation if consumed in excess

81424.name: Bubble Gum Flavor
81424.description: Artificial flavoring compound created to mimic the sweet, fruity taste of bubble gum. Typically a mixture of various synthetic chemicals and natural extracts classified as food additives by the FDA.
81424.benefits: Enhances palatability and flavor appeal in food products
81424.risks: Artificial flavor-related hypersensitivity, potential allergenicity, ultra-processed additive, lack of transparency in components

81453.name: 1,1-Dichloroethane
81453.description: A chlorinated hydrocarbon solvent mainly used industrially as a chemical intermediate and in adhesives. Not a food ingredient and not intended for consumption.
81453.risks: Toxic if inhaled or ingested, possible carcinogen, central nervous system depression, respiratory irritation, environmental pollutant

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary for 1,1-Dichloroethane
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for 1,1-Dichloroethane

81455.name: Simazine
81455.description: Simazine is a synthetic triazine herbicide used primarily to control broadleaf and grassy weeds in crops and non-crop areas. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a material (chemical pesticide). It is known for environmental persistence and potential toxicological concerns.
81455.benefits: Effective herbicide for weed control in agriculture and non-crop areas
81455.risks: Environmental toxicity, potential endocrine disruption, possible carcinogenicity, water contamination, soil persistence, toxicity to aquatic life

sources.label: Simazine-induced oxidative stress and endocrine disruption study
EPA Simazine Pesticide Information

81456.name: 1,1-Dichloroethylene
81456.description: 1,1-Dichloroethylene (also known as vinylidene chloride) is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon used primarily in the production of polymers and as an industrial chemical. It is not a food ingredient and is considered a hazardous material with toxicity concerns. Exposure typically occurs via inhalation or skin contact in industrial settings. It is not approved for food use.
81456.risks: Toxicity, carcinogenic potential, respiratory irritation, central nervous system effects, environmental pollutant

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary
NTP Report on Vinylidene Chloride

81457.name: 1,1,1-Trichloroethane
81457.description: A synthetic chlorinated solvent formerly used industrially as a degreasing agent and in aerosol formulations. It is not a food ingredient and is hazardous for human health and the environment. Its use is heavily restricted due to ozone depletion potential and toxic effects.
81457.risks: Neurotoxicity, respiratory irritation, central nervous system depression, liver toxicity, ozone depletion, environmental persistence

sources.label: PubChem - 1,1,1-Trichloroethane
WHO IPCS Concise International Chemical Assessment Document 38
EPA Ozone-Depleting Substances Phaseout

81462.name: Alpha-hexachlorocyclohexane
81462.description: Alpha-hexachlorocyclohexane (α-HCH) is an isomer of hexachlorocyclohexane, a synthetic organochlorine pesticide. It is a persistent environmental pollutant with bioaccumulative properties and is considered toxic to humans and wildlife. It is not used as a food ingredient and is primarily a contaminant or pollutant.
81462.risks: Toxicity, neurotoxicity, carcinogenic potential, endocrine disruption, bioaccumulation, environmental persistence

81463.name: 1,2-Dichloroethylene
81463.description: A synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon solvent used industrially and as a chemical intermediate; not used as a food ingredient. Exposure primarily occurs via inhalation or skin contact, with potential toxicity concerns.
81463.risks: Toxicity to the liver and kidneys, potential carcinogenicity, respiratory irritation, neurotoxicity, environmental contaminant

81465.name: Ethanethiol
81465.description: Ethanethiol (ethyl mercaptan) is a sulfur-containing organic compound with a strong, unpleasant odor used as an odorant additive in natural gas for leak detection; not a food ingredient and not intended for ingestion.
81465.benefits: Effective odorant for safety detection of natural gas leaks
81465.risks: Toxic if inhaled or ingested in significant amounts, respiratory irritation, skin and eye irritation, potential central nervous system effects in high exposure

sources.label: PubChem Ethanethiol Summary
OSHA Ethanethiol Information

81472.name: Cyanogen chloride
81472.description: A highly toxic chemical compound used historically as a chemical warfare agent and industrial chemical. Not a food ingredient and poses significant inhalation, ingestion, and skin contact hazards.
81472.risks: Highly toxic, respiratory failure, cyanide poisoning, fatal if inhaled or ingested, skin and eye irritation

sources.label: PubChem - Cyanogen chloride toxicity and hazards
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Cyanogen chloride

81495.name: Phenanthrene
81495.description: Phenanthrene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) commonly found in fossil fuels, tobacco smoke, and as a byproduct of incomplete combustion. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical compound often encountered in environmental exposure and industrial contexts.
81495.risks: Carcinogenic potential, mutagenicity, respiratory toxicity, environmental pollutant

81528.name: Erucylamide
81528.description: Erucylamide is a synthetic fatty acid amide, often used as a slip agent in plastic food packaging materials and occasionally detected as a contaminant migrated into food. It is not a food ingredient per se but a material-related compound arising from materials in contact with food. Its presence in food is unintended and associated with polymer additives rather than direct consumption.
81528.risks: Potential migration contaminant, limited toxicity data, possible low-level exposure concerns via food contact materials

sources.label: Migrants from plastic food packaging and their health effects

81529.name: Methylcyclohexane
81529.description: Methylcyclohexane is a hydrocarbon solvent primarily used in industrial applications such as paints and coatings. It is not a food ingredient and is not safe for ingestion. Exposure mainly occurs via inhalation or skin contact in occupational settings.
81529.risks: Inhalation toxicity, skin irritation, central nervous system effects, flammability, possible acute poisoning

sources.label: PubChem - Methylcyclohexane
NLM TOXNET - Chemical Safety

81598.name: Naturliga aromer
81598.description: The term 'Naturliga aromämnen' translates to 'natural flavorings' in English and refers to flavor compounds derived from natural sources. However, these are often processed extracts that may contain solvents or preservatives, and the exact composition is usually undisclosed.
81598.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain residual solvents, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

81661.name: Citric Acid (Regulator kwasowości, kwas cytrynowy)
81661.description: Citric acid is an organic acid naturally present in citrus fruits, commonly used to control pH and preserve flavor and stability in foods.
81661.benefits: Regulates acidity in foods, acts as preservative preventing microbial growth, enhances flavor
81661.risks: Irritation to skin and eyes in concentrated form, potential dental enamel erosion with excessive ingestion

81705.name: Édulcorants
81705.description: The French term for sweeteners, encompassing both natural and artificial types used to provide sweetness in foods and beverages without or with fewer calories than sugar. Artificial sweeteners such as aspartame, sucralose, and saccharin are synthetic compounds. Natural sweeteners include stevia and allulose.
81705.benefits: Reduce caloric intake, aid glycemic control in diabetics, dental health benefits compared to sugar
81705.risks: Potential metabolic effects, altered gut microbiota, possible increased appetite, artificial sweeteners linked to mild adverse effects in some studies

82218.name: Peach Extract
82218.description: Peach extract is a concentrated substance derived from peaches, commonly used for flavoring in foods and beverages. It contains natural compounds such as antioxidants, vitamins, and phenolics, though typically in small amounts depending on processing. The FDA generally recognizes peach extract as safe when used as a flavoring agent.
82218.benefits: Contains antioxidants, may provide natural flavoring, source of vitamins A and C
82218.risks: Possible allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential pesticide residue depending on source

sources.label: FDA Overview of Food Ingredients and Additives

82758.name: Jus de citron vert concentré
82758.description: Lime juice, natural source of acidity and vitamin C used for flavor enhancement.
82758.risks: Oral mucosal irritation due to acidity, potential citrus allergy reactions

82810.name: Ácido tartárico
82810.description: Organic acid commonly used as an antioxidant and acidulant to stabilize pH and prevent oxidation in foods.
82810.benefits: Antioxidant properties help preserve food quality, pH regulator
82810.risks: Irritation risk if ingested in large amounts, potential mild gastrointestinal upset

82888.name: Potassium Tallate
82888.description: A potassium salt of tall oil fatty acids used primarily in soap and cosmetic formulations as a surfactant and emulsifier. Not typically a food ingredient and mainly considered a material.
82888.benefits: Effective emulsifier and cleansing agent, biodegradable, derived from natural tall oil
82888.risks: Irritation to skin or eyes upon contact, potential for sensitization in some individuals

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary Potassium Tallate

83059.name: Ferments lactiques naturels
83059.description: Natural lactic acid bacteria used as ferments in food products like yogurt and fermented vegetables. Recognized as probiotics that can improve gut health and aid digestion. Generally considered safe and beneficial for consumption.
83059.benefits: Supports gut microbiota, aids digestion, may improve immune function, natural preservation
83059.risks: Rare allergic reactions, potential for contamination if improperly processed

83257.name: Natural Lemon and Strawberry Flavors
83257.description: Blend of extracted flavor compounds derived from strawberry and lemon sources used to impart fruit flavor in foods.
83257.benefits: Provides fruit flavor enhancement, improves sensory appeal
83257.risks: Possible allergenicity, potential for minor irritation or sensitization, ultra-processed, lack of transparency in constituents

83550.name: Aromă
83550.description: Aroma refers to flavoring agents used to impart specific smells or tastes to food products. These can be natural or synthetic compounds added in small amounts.
83550.benefits: Enhances sensory appeal of food products, improves palatability
83550.risks: Potential for allergenicity, contamination with synthetic chemicals depending on source and purity

sources.label: PMC7355186 - Food Flavorings and their Impact on Health

83743.name: Preservative [INS 200]
83743.description: INS 200 refers to Sorbic Acid, a widely used food preservative approved by regulatory bodies like the FDA and EFSA. It inhibits the growth of molds, yeasts, and fungi, extending shelf life in various food products.
83743.benefits: Effective mold and yeast inhibitor, extends food shelf life, prevents food spoilage
83743.risks: Possible mild allergic reactions or skin irritation in sensitive individuals, potential gastrointestinal discomfort in high amounts

sources.label: EFSA Scientific Opinion on Sorbic Acid and Potassium Sorbate

83760.name: Ácido málico
83760.description: Organic acid used primarily as an acidity regulator and flavor enhancer in food products.
83760.benefits: Regulates acidity, enhances flavor, participates in natural metabolic pathways
83760.risks: Irritation at high concentrations if ingested or in contact with skin, minimal systemic toxicity at typical food levels

sources.label: PMC11543732 - Safety assessment of malic acid

83883.name: Natural Passion Fruit Flavouring
83883.description: Flavoring derived from natural sources of passion fruit, often extracted using solvents or other processing methods. Used to impart passion fruit aroma and taste in foods and beverages. Classified as a natural flavor but the exact composition and safety depend on manufacturing and source.
83883.benefits: Provides natural fruit flavoring, enhances sensory appeal of foods
83883.risks: May contain residual solvents, ultra-processed, lack of transparency in composition, potential allergenicity in sensitive individuals

84201.name: Chardonnay
84201.description: Fermented alcoholic beverage made from Chardonnay grapes, used in cooking to enhance flavor.
84201.benefits: Adds flavor to dishes, contains some antioxidants from grapes but minimal in cooked form
84201.risks: Alcohol content may cause intoxication if consumed in large amounts, potential sulfite sensitivity

84292.name: Lime Tea Infusion
84292.description: A beverage infusion made from lime (citrus fruit) and tea leaves, typically black or green tea. Lime provides vitamin C and antioxidants, while tea contributes polyphenols and caffeine. Generally safe for consumption with hydrating and antioxidant properties.
84292.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, vitamin C source, may support hydration, potential anti-inflammatory and metabolic benefits from tea polyphenols
84292.risks: Possible acidity causing tooth enamel erosion if consumed excessively, caffeine sensitivity

84508.name: Malic Acid (Acide malique)
84508.description: Malic acid is a naturally occurring dicarboxylic acid used primarily as an acidulant in foods and beverages.
84508.benefits: Improves flavor by providing sour taste, acts as acidulant to control pH
84508.risks: Mild irritation at high concentrations, negligible ingestion toxicity at typical use levels

sources.label: PMC Malic acid safety and usage

84649.name: Šećer
84649.description: Common sugar (sucrose) used as a sweetener in food products.
84649.benefits: Provides energy as a carbohydrate source
84649.risks: Excessive intake associated with dental caries, weight gain, increased risk of metabolic disorders

84655.name: Kieselsäure (Silicic Acid)
84655.description: Kieselsäure, or silicic acid, is a form of silicon oxide commonly used as an anti-caking agent in food products and dietary supplements. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by FDA for use as a food additive. Silicic acid is also naturally present in various plant foods and contributes to dietary silicon intake, which may support bone and connective tissue health. In non-food contexts, it is used in industrial and cosmetic applications.
84655.benefits: Anti-caking agent, source of dietary silicon, supports bone and connective tissue health

sources.label: FDA GRAS affirmation for silicic acid

84667.name: Oxid uhličitý
84667.description: Carbon dioxide (CO2), a colorless, odorless gas naturally present in the atmosphere. Used in food and beverage industry primarily as a carbonation agent and preservative. Recognized as safe by FDA when used appropriately.
84667.benefits: Used for carbonation in beverages, inert atmosphere in food packaging to extend shelf life, non-toxic at typical exposure levels

sources.label: FDA Food Additive Status for Carbon Dioxide

84668.name: Minerální voda
84668.description: Mineral water is water containing dissolved minerals and trace elements, sourced from natural springs. It is generally safe for consumption and can contribute to hydration and mineral intake. The FDA considers mineral water a type of bottled water with specific mineral content standards.
84668.benefits: Hydration, source of essential minerals such as calcium, magnesium, and potassium

sources.label: FDA regulation of bottled and mineral water

84899.name: Preservatives (E202 & E211)
84899.description: E202 (Potassium sorbate) is a common food preservative that inhibits mold and yeast growth. E211 (Sodium benzoate) is used to prevent microbial growth, particularly in acidic foods and beverages. Both are approved by FDA but have some concerns regarding potential adverse effects.
84899.benefits: Effective microbial growth inhibition, extends shelf life, prevents food spoilage
84899.risks: Potential allergenicity, hyperactivity in children (especially E211), formation of benzene (carcinogen) under certain conditions with E211, mild gastrointestinal irritation

85288.name: L-Phenylalanine Compound
85288.description: Essential amino acid used in protein synthesis and as a dietary supplement. Present naturally in many protein-containing foods.
85288.benefits: Supports protein synthesis, precursor to neurotransmitters such as dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine
85288.risks: Not safe for individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU) due to risk of neurotoxicity

sources.label: NCBI - Phenylalanine metabolism

85945.name: Nitrates
85945.description: Inorganic compounds commonly found in water and foods, mainly used as preservatives and fertilizers.
85945.benefits: Preservative properties in processed meats, natural occurrence in vegetables
85945.risks: Potential formation of nitrosamines (carcinogenic), methemoglobinemia risk in infants, contamination risk from agricultural runoff

86008.name: Tamarind Juice Concentrate
86008.description: A concentrated extract from tamarind fruit pulp, used as a food ingredient for flavor and acidity. Tamarind is a source of vitamins, antioxidants, and dietary fiber. The concentrate delivers the characteristic tangy flavor and nutritional components in a concentrated form.
86008.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, contains vitamin C and B vitamins, supports digestion, natural flavoring agent
86008.risks: May cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, high acidity may affect dental enamel with excessive consumption

86146.name: Citric Acid (Antioxidante ácido cítrico)
86146.description: Organic acid commonly used as a pH adjuster and preservative in food and cosmetic products.
86146.risks: Mild irritant to skin and eyes at high concentrations

sources.label: PMID 10695371 – Safety and uses of citric acid

86281.name: Colorantes E102 (Tartrazine)
86281.description: Synthetic lemon yellow azo dye used as a colorant in foods, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals.
86281.benefits: Colorant for visual appeal in products
86281.risks: Irritation/sensitization potential, allergic reactions, hyperactivity in children, regulatory restrictions in some countries

86710.name: Agua purificada
86710.description: Purified water diluted with an acidic substance to achieve 5% acidity; commonly used as a solvent or vehicle in formulations.
86710.benefits: Solvent and diluent, facilitates formulation stability and delivery
86710.risks: Low risk at typical exposure; potential mild irritation if strong acid used for acidification

sources.label: NCBI - Purified Water Uses and Safety

86784.name: Pectin (Stabilisator)
86784.description: Pectins are polysaccharides primarily used as gelling agents, stabilizers, and thickening agents in food products.
86784.benefits: Dietary fiber, supports digestive health, stabilizing and gelling functionality

sources.label: PMC5372966 - Pectin and its application

87044.name: Cis-Trans-Cypermethrin
87044.description: Synthetic pyrethroid insecticide commonly used in pest control and sometimes in cleaning products for antimicrobial and insecticidal properties. It is a mixture of isomers of cypermethrin.
87044.benefits: Effective insecticidal action, pest control aid
87044.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, neurotoxicity with high exposure, potential aquatic toxicity, possible respiratory sensitization

sources.label: ECHA Cypermethrin Skin and Eye Irritation
PubChem Cypermethrin Profile
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Pyrethrins and Pyrethroids

87351.name: Natural Lemon Aroma
87351.description: A fragrance ingredient derived from lemon essential oils or citrus extracts used for flavoring or scent. Despite the term 'natural,' it often involves chemical extraction and can contain multiple volatile compounds. Not regulated as food additive but commonly used in food products and fragrances.
87351.benefits: Provides natural lemon flavor or scent, generally recognized as safe in food when used in typical amounts
87351.risks: Allergic reactions, skin irritation (in direct topical use), potential respiratory sensitization, possible trace solvent residues, lack of transparency in composition

sources.label: Limonene safety and use summary

87623.name: Stinging Nettle Root
87623.description: Herbal ingredient derived from the root of Urtica dioica (stinging nettle) often used in traditional medicine for urinary and prostate health. It contains bioactive compounds such as lignans, polysaccharides, and phenolics with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Not an FDA-approved drug but commonly used as a dietary supplement.
87623.benefits: Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, potential benefits for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), supports urinary tract health
87623.risks: Possible allergic reactions, mild gastrointestinal discomfort in some individuals

87643.name: Blueberry or Lemon-Lime Natural Aroma
87643.description: A flavoring ingredient derived from natural sources to impart blueberry or lemon-lime taste in foods and beverages. These natural aromas are typically extracted using solvents or steam distillation methods, but the exact chemical composition may vary and sometimes include minor processing aids. The FDA considers natural flavors generally safe, but lack of transparency and potential allergens may be concerns.
87643.benefits: Provides natural fruit flavor, enhances palatability and consumer appeal
87643.risks: Possible allergenic compounds, lack of transparency in composition, may contain trace solvents or processing aids

87785.name: Vitamins
87785.description: Organic compounds essential in small amounts for normal metabolism and health. They must be obtained from diet or supplements. Different vitamins have varied functions including antioxidant roles, energy metabolism, and immune support.
87785.benefits: Supports normal metabolic functions, antioxidant protection, immune support, prevents deficiency diseases
87785.risks: Hypervitaminosis with excessive intake of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), possible interactions with medications

87878.name: Citronensäuremonohydrat (Citric Acid Monohydrate)
87878.description: Citric acid monohydrate is a natural organic acid commonly used as a food additive and preservative to enhance flavor and shelf life. It is recognized as safe by the FDA and commonly derived from citrus fruits or microbial fermentation. It is water-soluble and widely used in beverages, candies, and processed foods.
87878.benefits: Enhances flavor, acts as a natural preservative, improves mineral absorption, antioxidant properties
87878.risks: May cause mild irritation in sensitive individuals when consumed in large amounts, potential dental erosion with excessive intake

87894.name: Sugar (apple juice concentrate)
87894.description: Sugar derived from concentrated apple juice, used as a sweetener in foods and beverages. Provides calories without significant nutrients. Considered a form of added sugar by FDA standards.
87894.benefits: Energy source, naturally derived sweetener alternative to refined sucrose
87894.risks: Metabolic syndrome, obesity, insulin resistance, dental caries, increased cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

88053.name: Sugar colorant IV
88053.description: A caramel coloring agent produced by controlled heat treatment of sugars, commonly used in foods and beverages as a color additive. Classified as Caramel Color IV, it is produced with ammonium compounds and may contain 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI). It is approved by the FDA but has raised some health concerns.
88053.benefits: Provides color and aesthetic appeal in foods and beverages, generally recognized as safe at typical consumption levels
88053.risks: Contains 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) which has potential carcinogenic effects based on animal studies, possible association with cancer risk upon high chronic exposure

88142.name: Apples
88142.description: Fruit from Malus domestica providing dietary fiber, vitamins, and phytochemicals.
88142.benefits: Source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, antioxidants, and flavonoids
88142.risks: Possible pesticide residues if not organic, allergen risk in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMID 23538915 - Nutritional and health-related effects of apples.
PMID 20478669 - Apples and cardiovascular health: a review.

88175.name: Natural Blackberry Flavouring
88175.description: A flavoring derived from blackberry extracts or compounds intended to mimic blackberry taste. Classified as a natural flavor but often involves chemical isolation and processing. Used primarily to impart fruit aroma and taste in foods.
88175.benefits: Provides natural fruit flavor, enhances palatability of food products
88175.risks: May contain chemical solvents or preservatives, lack of transparency in composition, potential allergenicity

88219.name: Stabiliser E415
88219.description: A polysaccharide used as a stabilizer and thickening agent in food products.
88219.benefits: Improves texture and stability in food formulations
88219.risks: Minor digestive discomfort at high intake, potential for rare allergic reactions

88226.name: Organic Natural Pumpkin Spice Flavor
88226.description: A flavoring blend typically derived from natural extracts of spices such as cinnamon, nutmeg, clove, and ginger, used to impart pumpkin pie-like aroma and taste; 'organic' implies sourcing from organically grown ingredients. The composition is generally safe for consumption and recognized as GRAS (Generally Recognized As Safe) though exact formulations vary and may include minor processing aids or solvents.
88226.benefits: Provides natural spice flavoring, may contain bioactive compounds with antioxidant properties
88226.risks: Possible allergic reactions to spice components, potential trace solvents from extraction, ultra-processed additive with little nutritional value

sources.label: FDA Overview of Food Ingredients and Additives

88461.name: Water
88461.description: Pure H2O used as a filler or solvent in products.
88461.benefits: Universal solvent, supports hydration and formulation stability

88551.name: Zitronensaftpulver
88551.description: Lemon juice powder is a dehydrated form of lemon juice, containing concentrated citric acid, vitamin C, and aromatic compounds. It is used as a flavoring and acidity regulator in foods. Generally recognized as safe for consumption by the FDA when used appropriately.
88551.benefits: Source of vitamin C, natural antioxidant, enhances flavor, acidity regulation
88551.risks: Potential dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption, possible citrus allergy in sensitive individuals

sources.label: FDA overview on food additives

88662.name: Regulador de acidez (E-331iii)
88662.description: Known as Trisodium citrate, E-331iii is a food additive used as an acidity regulator and emulsifier. It is generally recognized as safe by the FDA and commonly used in beverages and processed foods to control pH levels.
88662.benefits: Controls acidity, stabilizes food products, acts as an emulsifier, improves flavor

sources.label: Food Additives - Trisodium Citrate Safety Evaluation
PubChem - Sodium Citrate

89361.name: Salt
89361.description: Essential mineral (sodium chloride) used for seasoning and food preservation, crucial for maintaining fluid balance and nerve function.
89361.benefits: Essential electrolyte, supports nerve transmission, aids fluid balance
89361.risks: Hypertension and cardiovascular risk with excessive intake

sources.label: Hemmelgarn et al. 2014 - Sodium intake and cardiovascular disease

89380.name: Vegetable Fibers (Oligofructose)
89380.description: Oligofructose is a type of short-chain fructooligosaccharide derived from vegetable fibers, functioning primarily as a prebiotic dietary fiber to promote beneficial gut bacteria.
89380.benefits: Prebiotic fiber supporting gut microbiota, may improve digestive health, assists in mineral absorption
89380.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, such as bloating, gas, and diarrhea

89587.name: Ácido Ascórbico (Vitamin C)
89587.description: Vitamin C compound used as a flour treatment agent to strengthen dough and improve baking performance.
89587.benefits: Dough strengthening, antioxidant properties, essential nutrient for humans
89587.risks: Irritation at very high doses, potential for interaction with certain medications at pharmacological levels

89623.name: Bovine Collagen Peptides
89623.description: Hydrolyzed protein derived from bovine connective tissue, used to support protein content and skin/connective tissue structure.
89623.benefits: Supports protein intake, may support connective tissue structure
89623.risks: Allergic sensitization in some individuals, contamination risk if poorly sourced

89745.name: Zucchero di canna
89745.description: Brown sugar derived from sugarcane, consisting primarily of sucrose with minor molasses content.
89745.risks: Excessive intake associated with weight gain, dental caries, metabolic impacts
