sources.label: Health Effects of Sugar Intake – PubMed PMID 12924289
Dietary Sugars and Health: A Review of Current Evidence – PMC5372977

89784.name: DLPA (DL-Phenylalanine)
89784.description: A synthetic mixture of D-phenylalanine and L-phenylalanine amino acids. Used as a dietary supplement for mood enhancement and pain relief. Recognized as safe for consumption in typical supplemental doses but not an essential nutrient.
89784.benefits: May improve mood, reduce chronic pain, support neurotransmitter synthesis
89784.risks: Possible interactions with MAO inhibitors, risk for individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU), mild side effects like headache or nausea

89915.name: Ağaç reçinesinin gliserol esterleri
89915.description: Glycerol esters of wood resin are compounds derived from glycerol and natural tree resins, commonly used as emulsifiers or stabilizers in food and cosmetic products. Considered generally safe for consumption and topical use when properly refined.
89915.benefits: Emulsifying properties, stabilizes food and cosmetic formulations, derived from natural sources
89915.risks: Potential allergenicity in sensitive individuals, rare hypersensitivity reactions

89989.name: Organic Stevia Extract
89989.description: A natural, zero-calorie sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant. Recognized as safe by the FDA when used as a sweetener. Used as a sugar substitute with minimal impact on blood glucose levels.
89989.benefits: Natural zero-calorie sweetener, does not raise blood sugar, beneficial for weight management and diabetes control
89989.risks: Potential for mild digestive upset in sensitive individuals, possible interaction with blood pressure or blood sugar medications

sources.label: FDA on high-purity steviol glycosides

90026.name: Essence of Lemon
90026.description: A concentrated flavoring derived from lemon, commonly used as a food flavoring. It may be natural (extracted from lemon peel/oil) or synthetic. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in food. Contains aromatic compounds like limonene. Typically used in small amounts, providing lemon flavor without significant nutritional contribution.
90026.benefits: Provides natural lemon flavor, contains antioxidant compounds like limonene, enhances palatability
90026.risks: Potential allergen, may cause sensitivity or irritation in some individuals, trace synthetic additives possible if not pure natural extract

sources.label: FDA Food Additives and GRAS

90240.name: Anglies dioksidas
90240.description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a naturally occurring gas present in the atmosphere and used in various industries including food and beverage as a propellant and carbonation agent. In food, it is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in accordance with good manufacturing practices.
90240.benefits: Used for carbonation, inert gas to preserve freshness, non-toxic at typical exposure levels

sources.label: NIH – Carbon Dioxide Overview
FDA – Carbon Dioxide as a Food Additive

90304.name: Allura Red Color [E129]
90304.description: Synthetic azo dye commonly used as a red food colorant. Approved by FDA for use in food, cosmetics, and drugs with specified limits. Linked to hyperactivity in some children and potential allergic reactions.
90304.benefits: Provides vibrant red color, approved for safe use in regulated amounts
90304.risks: Hyperactivity in children, allergic reactions, potential behavioral effects, synthetic azo dye concerns

90307.name: Sirop de fructose-glucose
90307.description: A syrup made from hydrolyzed starch mainly consisting of glucose; used as a sweetener and a humectant in food products.
90307.benefits: Provides sweetness, improves texture and moisture retention in foods
90307.risks: High glycemic index, excessive consumption linked to weight gain and dental caries

sources.label: Impact of glucose syrups on health

90407.name: Acido citrico
90407.description: Likely refers to citric acid, a weak organic acid commonly used as a flavoring and preservative agent.
90407.benefits: Preservative effects, flavor enhancement, antioxidant chelating properties
90407.risks: Irritation risk at high concentrations, dental enamel erosion in excessive intake

sources.label: PMC538417 - Safety and use of citric acid

90464.name: Organic Fruit and Vegetable Juice (Carrot, Blackcurrant) for Color
90464.description: Juice extracted from blackcurrant fruits, commonly used as a natural colorant in foods and beverages.
90464.benefits: Natural coloring agent, contains antioxidants such as anthocyanins, contributes minor nutritional value
90464.risks: Allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, potential for contamination if not properly processed, minimal ingestion toxicity

sources.label: Anthocyanins in blackcurrant and their health effects (PMC5986464)
Safety and allergenicity of fruit juices (PMID 29074440)

90589.name: Água Gaseificada
90589.description: Carbonated water, water into which carbon dioxide gas under pressure has been dissolved. Generally recognized as safe for consumption. Provides hydration similar to still water but can cause belching or mild bloating in some individuals.
90589.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free alternative to sugary beverages, may aid digestion
90589.risks: Mild bloating, belching, possible dental enamel erosion with frequent consumption

90810.name: Isopropylbenzene
90810.description: Also known as cumene, isopropylbenzene is an aromatic hydrocarbon primarily used industrially as a solvent and chemical intermediate. It is not a food ingredient and is not intended for consumption. Exposure to isopropylbenzene mainly occurs through inhalation or skin contact in occupational settings.
90810.risks: Toxic if inhaled or ingested, skin and eye irritation, central nervous system effects, potential carcinogen, hazardous in fire

sources.label: PubChem - Chemical and Toxicity Information on Cumene
EPA - Toxicological Review of Cumene

91261.name: Tricalciumphosphat (Tricalcium Phosphate)
91261.description: Tricalcium phosphate is a calcium salt of phosphoric acid commonly used as a food additive for calcium fortification, anti-caking agent, and nutritional supplement. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in typical food amounts.
91261.benefits: Provides bioavailable calcium and phosphate, supports bone health and metabolic functions
91261.risks: Excessive intake may cause calcium and phosphate imbalance, kidney stones in susceptible individuals

sources.label: FDA GRAS Notice for Tricalcium Phosphate

91262.name: Cholinbitartrat
91262.description: Cholinbitartrat is the German name for choline bitartrate, a salt form of choline, an essential nutrient important for liver function, brain development, muscle movement, nervous system health, and metabolism. It is commonly used as a dietary supplement to support cognitive function and liver health. The FDA recognizes choline as an essential nutrient, but choline bitartrate is considered a supplement ingredient rather than a conventional food additive.
91262.benefits: Supports brain development, cognitive function, liver function, nerve signaling, lipid metabolism
91262.risks: Excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal distress, fishy body odor, hypotension

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements - Choline

91429.name: 100% recycled plastic
91429.description: Material derived from previously used plastics used in packaging or components of cleaning products. Not an active ingredient in cleaning formulations.
91429.benefits: Supports sustainability and waste reduction by reusing plastic materials
91429.risks: Potential contamination from residual chemicals if not properly processed, microplastic environmental impact if released

sources.label: EU Plastic Waste Directive and Recycling

91790.name: Organic Cane Sugar Molasses
91790.description: A viscous byproduct of sugar extraction from sugar cane containing sugars, minerals, and small amounts of vitamins.
91790.benefits: Provides small amounts of minerals like iron and calcium, used as a sweetener and flavoring agent
91790.risks: High sugar content, excessive intake associated with dental caries and weight gain

sources.label: Molasses as a source of minerals and bioactive compounds
Dietary sugar intake and health outcomes

91944.name: Methoxychlor
91944.description: Methoxychlor is a synthetic organochlorine pesticide once used as a replacement for DDT. It is persistent in the environment and bioaccumulative. Not approved as a food ingredient. Exposure may occur via environmental contamination affecting food and water.
91944.risks: Endocrine disruption, reproductive toxicity, neurotoxicity, bioaccumulation, environmental persistence

91966.name: De-Sugared Lemon Juice from Concentrate
91966.description: Lemon juice concentrate with reduced sugar content, used as a flavoring or acidulant in food products. Retains citric acid and flavor compounds but has lower natural sugar levels compared to regular lemon juice concentrate. Generally recognized as safe by FDA.
91966.benefits: Source of citric acid, natural flavor, low sugar content helpful for reducing caloric intake
91966.risks: Possible reduction in natural carbohydrate content (minimal risk), potential for processing contaminants (low)

sources.label: FDA Food Ingredient Status

92159.name: Grapefruit Juice from Concentrate (16%)
92159.description: Reconstituted juice derived from concentrated grapefruit juice; contains natural sugars, acids, and phytochemicals.
92159.benefits: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants
92159.risks: Photosensitivity, interaction with certain medications due to furanocoumarins, ingestion toxicity in excess

sources.label: PMID 15914903 – Grapefruit juice-drug interactions and phototoxicity

92178.name: Caffeine (from Green Coffee Beans)
92178.description: Caffeine is a natural stimulant alkaloid found in green coffee beans, known for central nervous system stimulation. It is commonly used to increase alertness and reduce fatigue.
92178.benefits: Central nervous system stimulant, increases alertness, enhances cognitive performance at moderate doses
92178.risks: Irritant at high topical concentrations, ingestion toxicity at excessive doses, potential for dependence, withdrawal symptoms

92206.name: Carbonated Natural Artesian Spring Water
92206.description: Water that has been carbonated by dissolving carbon dioxide gas under pressure, typically without added ingredients.
92206.benefits: Hydration, calorie-free beverage with carbonic acid providing effervescence
92206.risks: Dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption due to acidity from carbonation

92246.name: Wild Noni Juice
92246.description: Juice derived from the fruit of the Morinda citrifolia plant, traditionally used in Polynesian cultures for various health benefits. It contains antioxidants, vitamins, and phytochemicals but also contains compounds that may affect liver enzymes.
92246.benefits: Antioxidant properties, potential anti-inflammatory effects, source of vitamins and phytonutrients
92246.risks: Potential hepatotoxicity in rare cases, gastrointestinal upset, possible interactions with medications especially those metabolized by the liver

92247.name: Monkfruit Juice Concentrate
92247.description: A natural sweetener derived from monkfruit (Luo Han Guo) that contains mogrosides, compounds with intense sweetness but very low calories. It is Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) by the FDA and often used as a sugar substitute.
92247.benefits: Low-calorie natural sweetener, does not raise blood glucose levels, antioxidant properties
92247.risks: Possible allergenicity in sensitive individuals, limited research on long-term effects

sources.label: FDA GRAS Notices

92252.name: Natural Mirabelle Plum Aroma
92252.description: A natural flavoring derived from Mirabelle plum, used to impart fruity aroma and taste. Though considered natural, 'natural flavors' can contain complex mixtures of chemicals, sometimes extracted with solvents. Used in food and beverages to enhance flavor without significant nutritional value.
92252.benefits: Provides natural fruity aroma and flavor, can enhance palatability
92252.risks: Lack of transparency, potential solvent residues, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

92420.name: FD&C Yellow #6 [E110]
92420.description: Synthetic azo dye used as a colorant in foods and cosmetics.
92420.risks: Irritation, potential allergenicity, hyperactivity concerns in children, regulatory limits on use

sources.label: PMC1368972 – Effects of azo dyes on children
FD&C Yellow No. 6 toxicology review

92637.name: Diquat
92637.description: Diquat is a non-selective contact herbicide primarily used in agriculture and weed control. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical material applied to plants. It is toxic if ingested or inhaled and can cause severe health issues upon exposure.
92637.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum herbicide, rapid weed control
92637.risks: Toxic if ingested, inhalation hazard, skin and eye irritation, potentially carcinogenic, environmental contaminant

sources.label: PubChem – Diquat chemical and hazard information

92658.name: 8:2 Fluorotelomer Sulfonic Acid
92658.description: A synthetic fluorinated chemical belonging to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), used in stain repellents and firefighting foams. Not approved as a food ingredient and is a persistent environmental pollutant with bioaccumulative properties.
92658.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential endocrine disruption, toxicity, carcinogenic potential, contamination of water supplies

sources.label: ATSDR PFAS Toxicological Profile

92664.name: Monochlorobenzene
92664.description: Monochlorobenzene is an aromatic organic solvent primarily used in industrial applications such as the manufacture of herbicides, pesticides, and dyes. It is not a food ingredient and is recognized as a hazardous chemical with significant toxicological concerns.
92664.risks: Toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through skin; carcinogenic potential; respiratory tract irritation; nervous system effects; environmental pollutant

sources.label: PubChem – Monochlorobenzene Chemical and Toxicity Data
ATSDR Toxicological Profile for Chlorobenzenes

92666.name: Endothall
92666.description: Endothall is a synthetic herbicide primarily used to control aquatic plants and algae. It is not a food ingredient. Safety concerns focus on its toxicity through ingestion, skin contact, and environmental exposure. Classified as a potential human carcinogen by some agencies and known to cause gastrointestinal and kidney damage upon acute exposure.
92666.risks: Toxic if ingested, skin and eye irritation, potential carcinogen, environmental toxicity to aquatic life

sources.label: ATSDR – Endothall Toxicity

92706.name: Jalapeño Extract
92706.description: Extract derived from jalapeño peppers containing capsaicin and other bioactive compounds. Commonly used as a food ingredient for flavor and potential health benefits.
92706.benefits: Contains capsaicin which may support metabolism, pain relief, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties
92706.risks: Gastrointestinal irritation, allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

92786.name: Natürliches Apfelaroma
92786.description: German for 'Natural Apple Flavor', typically a flavoring derived from apple components using physical, enzymatic, or fermentation processes without chemical synthesis. Used to impart apple flavor in foods. Despite being labeled natural, it is a processed ingredient with unclear composition and potential additives.
92786.benefits: Provides apple flavor, generally recognized as safe for consumption
92786.risks: Lack of transparency, possible additives or solvents, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

92791.name: Vesi
92791.description: No relevant safety or toxicology data found for 'Vesi', possibly a brand name, misspelling, or proprietary ingredient.

93013.name: Ginseng powder
93013.description: Powdered form of ginseng root, commonly used as an herbal supplement. Recognized for its adaptogenic properties and traditional use in improving energy, cognitive function, and immune support. Generally considered safe for consumption with few side effects when used appropriately.
93013.benefits: Adaptogenic effects, enhances energy and cognitive function, supports immune system, may reduce fatigue, antioxidant properties
93013.risks: Potential interactions with blood thinners and diabetes medications, insomnia, headaches, gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals

93031.name: Grains
93031.description: Edible seeds of grasses such as wheat, rice, oats, barley, and corn. Grains provide carbohydrates, fiber, protein, vitamins, and minerals. Whole grains retain bran and germ, offering more nutrients and health benefits compared to refined grains, which are stripped of fiber and micronutrients. The FDA recognizes whole grains as part of a healthy diet.
93031.benefits: Source of complex carbohydrates, dietary fiber, essential nutrients (B vitamins, iron, magnesium), supports digestive health, may reduce risk of heart disease and type 2 diabetes
93031.risks: Gluten sensitivity or celiac disease in susceptible individuals, potential overconsumption of refined grains linked to metabolic disorders

93344.name: Phenol, p-tert-butyl-
93344.description: A synthetic phenolic compound used primarily as an antioxidant, preservative, or intermediate in industrial applications. Not approved as a food additive. Potentially toxic with exposure primarily via skin contact or inhalation, and not intended for consumption.
93344.benefits: Antioxidant properties in industrial contexts, preservative efficacy
93344.risks: Skin irritation, respiratory irritation, potential toxicity if ingested, environmental toxicity

sources.label: PubChem - Phenol, p-tert-butyl-

93345.name: 2-methylbenzaldehyde
93345.description: An aromatic aldehyde used primarily as a fragrance and flavoring agent. It is a synthetic chemical with limited use in food products and primarily industrial applications. The compound can be an irritant and may pose risks upon inhalation or skin contact. Not approved as a primary food additive by the FDA and typically used in very low concentrations in fragrance formulations.
93345.benefits: Used as a flavoring and fragrance agent to impart almond-like aroma
93345.risks: Skin irritation, respiratory irritation, potential sensitizer, possible toxicity if ingested in large amounts

sources.label: PubChem 2-Methylbenzaldehyde compound summary
Toxicological review of aromatic aldehydes

93405.name: 3-methylhexane
93405.description: 3-methylhexane is a branched-chain alkane hydrocarbon commonly used as an industrial solvent and chemical intermediate. It is not a food ingredient and is not intended for consumption. Exposure is primarily through inhalation or skin contact during industrial use.
93405.risks: Flammability, respiratory irritation, skin irritation, central nervous system effects with inhalation, potential neurotoxicity in high exposures

sources.label: PubChem - 3-methylhexane
Toxicology Data Network (TOXNET) - Hydrocarbons

93406.name: 2-bromo-1,4-dimethylbenzene
93406.description: An aromatic brominated organic compound used mainly as a chemical intermediate in industrial applications, not a food ingredient. It is a synthetic material with no known nutritional value and potential chemical hazards.
93406.risks: Toxicity upon ingestion or inhalation, potential organ irritation, environmental pollutant, unknown chronic health effects

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary

93615.name: Evaporated Lychee Juice
93615.description: Concentrated juice derived from lychee fruit through evaporation, retaining much of the fruit's natural sugars, vitamins, and antioxidants. Generally recognized as safe for consumption. Used as a flavoring and sweetening agent.
93615.benefits: Source of natural antioxidants, vitamin C, enhances flavor, provides natural sweetness
93615.risks: High sugar content may affect glycemic control if consumed in excess, potential allergen for individuals sensitive to lychee

93639.name: Luontaiset aromit
93639.description: Finnish term for 'Natural Flavors,' which refers to flavoring agents derived from natural sources but often processed and chemically extracted, sometimes using solvents and additives.
93639.risks: Lack of transparency, may contain solvents, ultra-processed, no nutritional value

93731.name: Apfelsaftkonzentrat
93731.description: Apple juice concentrate is a reduced and concentrated form of apple juice, primarily containing sugars, organic acids, and flavor compounds from apples.
93731.benefits: Source of natural fruit sugars and flavor compounds, can enhance palatability
93731.risks: High sugar content leading to excessive caloric intake, potential contribution to dental caries with frequent exposure

93858.name: Juices from Concentrate (Blueberry and Boysenberry Concentrates)
93858.description: Fruit juice concentrates derived from blueberry and boysenberry fruits, typically obtained by water removal to concentrate sugars and flavors. Used as flavoring and sweetening agents. Retain some antioxidants and nutrients but often have reduced fiber compared to whole fruit. Generally recognized as safe by the FDA.
93858.benefits: Contains antioxidants, vitamins (e.g., vitamin C), natural flavor, source of phytonutrients
93858.risks: High sugar content, potential contribution to dental caries, blood sugar spikes, reduced fiber compared to whole fruit

94261.name: Green Kiwifruit (Hayward)
94261.description: Fresh green kiwifruit variety, raw whole fruit with no additives. Rich source of vitamin C, dietary fiber, and antioxidants. Recognized as safe to consume and widely used in fresh fruit consumption and culinary uses. No FDA concerns for raw fruit.
94261.benefits: High vitamin C content, rich in dietary fiber, antioxidants, supports immune function, promotes digestive health
94261.risks: Allergic reactions (rare), potential oxalate content in susceptible individuals

94269.name: Koncentrirani limunov sok
94269.description: Concentrated lemon juice, a food ingredient derived from lemon juice with reduced water content. Contains citric acid, vitamin C, and various phytochemicals. Commonly used as a flavoring and preservative agent in foods and beverages.
94269.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, supports immune function, natural preservative, adds flavor
94269.risks: Possible dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption, potential acid reflux aggravation

94417.name: Steinsalz
94417.description: Uniodized rock salt primarily composed of sodium chloride with trace minerals.
94417.risks: Excessive sodium intake associated with hypertension and cardiovascular risk

sources.label: Salt and health outcomes - PMC

94554.name: Bromacil
94554.description: Bromacil is a herbicide commonly used for weed control in non-crop areas. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical material used in agricultural and landscape applications. It is toxic to humans and animals upon exposure and is regulated to prevent contamination of food and water.
94554.risks: Toxicity to humans and animals, potential carcinogen, environmental contamination, water pollution, neurotoxicity, endocrine disruption

sources.label: PubChem - Bromacil compound summary
EPA Pesticide Fact Sheet - Bromacil

94569.name: Turmeric Colors
94569.description: Coloring agents derived from turmeric, primarily curcumin, a natural polyphenol used as a food dye and spice with recognized safety and anti-inflammatory properties.
94569.benefits: Natural coloring agent, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, potential health benefits including improved digestion and joint health
94569.risks: Possible allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, photoallergic dermatitis (rare)

sources.label: EFSA scientific opinion on curcumin as a food additive

94601.name: Natuurlijke aroma's (mosterd)
94601.description: Natural flavors derived from mustard used as flavoring agents. While generally recognized as safe by food authorities, natural flavors are complex mixtures that may include solvents or processing aids. Mustard itself is a common allergen and can cause reactions in sensitive individuals.
94601.benefits: Adds natural mustard flavor, enhances palatability, generally safe for consumption
94601.risks: Mustard allergy, lack of transparency in flavor composition, potential presence of residual solvents

94664.name: Naturlig hallonarom
94664.description: Swedish for 'Natural raspberry flavor'; typically refers to flavoring derived from natural sources such as raspberry or other natural extracts. While labeled natural, such flavors can vary widely in composition and purity and may include processing aids or carriers.
94664.benefits: Provides natural fruity flavor, enhances palatability
94664.risks: Possible allergens, variability in composition, potential presence of processing solvents, ultra-processed with low nutritional value

94671.name: Äppelsyra (Malic Acid)
94671.description: Malic acid is an organic acid used as a food acidulant to impart sour taste and as a pH control agent.
94671.benefits: Enhances flavor as a souring agent, used to adjust acidity in foods and beverages
94671.risks: Irritation risk at high concentrations, potential gastrointestinal discomfort if consumed in large amounts

sources.label: PubChem - Malic acid

94727.name: Dodecane Sulfate
94727.description: Dodecane sulfate is a surfactant and detergent chemical used primarily in personal care products and cleaning formulations. It is not used as a food ingredient and is considered a synthetic material. Safety concerns include skin and eye irritation upon direct contact and potential inhalation hazards in aerosolized form.
94727.benefits: Effective surfactant and detergent, helps emulsify and remove oils and dirt
94727.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, respiratory irritation if inhaled, potential environmental toxicity

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary - Dodecyl Sulfate

94781.name: CI 15985/FD&C Yellow No. 6
94781.description: Synthetic azo dye used as a color additive in foods, drugs, and cosmetics. Approved by FDA but associated with some adverse reactions and potential health concerns.
94781.risks: Allergic reactions, hyperactivity in children, possible carcinogenic metabolites, hypersensitivity, allergic dermatitis

sources.label: PubChem FD&C Yellow No. 6

94792.name: Strawberry & Banana Natural and Artificial Flavour
94792.description: A mixture of flavor compounds extracted from natural sources to mimic strawberry taste, combined with other natural flavorings. Used to impart flavor in foods and beverages.
94792.benefits: Imparts characteristic strawberry flavor, used to enhance palatability and sensory appeal of products
94792.risks: Potential for allergenic reactions, possible presence of trace pesticides or contaminants from natural sources, lacks transparency on exact chemical composition, risk of ultra-processing solvents or carriers

94805.name: Acidity Regulators (Sodium Bicarbonate, Calcium Phosphate (Mono-Basic))
94805.description: Acidity regulators are additives used to control pH in foods. Sodium bicarbonate acts as a leavening agent and pH buffer. Citric acid is a natural organic acid used for acidification and flavor.
94805.benefits: Regulates acidity, acts as leavening agent (sodium bicarbonate), enhances flavor (citric acid)

94926.name: Agmapure Agmatine Sulphate
94926.description: Agmatine sulfate is a dietary supplement form of agmatine, a biogenic amine derived from the amino acid arginine; it is used for potential cognitive, mood, and pain modulation benefits but is not an FDA-approved drug. It is generally regarded as safe for consumption in typical supplemental doses but lacks extensive long-term safety data.
94926.benefits: May support cognitive function, neuroprotection, mood enhancement, pain modulation, nitric oxide synthesis
94926.risks: Possible gastrointestinal upset, headache, hypotension in sensitive individuals, limited long-term safety data

95187.name: Calcium Disodium EDTA Added to Protect Flavor
95187.description: A chelating agent used as a sequestrant to bind metal ions and improve stability in food and cosmetic products.
95187.benefits: Prevents metal-catalyzed oxidation, preserves product stability and color
95187.risks: None at typical use levels, potential for digestive upset at high oral doses

95207.name: Fluoride-coated dental floss
95207.description: Dental floss coated with fluoride compounds to aid in oral health by delivering fluoride directly to interdental areas; fluoride is recognized by the FDA for cavity prevention in dental products. Materials used in floss base vary, typically nylon or PTFE.
95207.benefits: Helps remove plaque between teeth, delivers fluoride locally to reduce dental caries, supports oral hygiene
95207.risks: Potential ingestion risk of fluoride in excessive amounts, allergic reactions rare, environmental concerns about microplastics depending on floss base material

95257.name: Asitlik düzenleyici (sodyum hidroksit)
95257.description: Sodium hydroxide is used as an acidity regulator to control pH in foods; it is safe when used in regulated amounts but is caustic in concentrated form.
95257.benefits: pH regulation, aids in food processing and preservation
95257.risks: Caustic and corrosive at high concentrations, irritation risk if improperly handled

95336.name: Vand
95336.description: Water, a universal solvent used as a base in food formulations.
95336.benefits: Hydration, solvent for ingredients, essential for life

95352.name: Antioxidant: L-ascorbic acid
95352.description: Natural antioxidant, also known as vitamin C, used in cleaning products to prevent oxidation and discoloration. Classified as an organic acid.
95352.benefits: Antioxidant properties, stabilizes formulations, low toxicity, biodegradable
95352.risks: Mild skin irritation at high concentrations, rare sensitization

sources.label: ECHA Ascorbic acid skin irritation data

95354.name: Sodium Benzoate [Preservative]
95354.description: Benzoic acid salt used as a preservative to inhibit microbial growth in acidic foods and beverages.
95354.benefits: Preserves food by inhibiting microbial growth, extends shelf-life
95354.risks: Irritant potential, possible formation of benzene under certain conditions, sensitivity reactions in some individuals

95361.name: Profenofos
95361.description: Profenofos is an organophosphate insecticide and acaricide used in agriculture. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical material used for pest control. Exposure to profenofos can pose health risks due to its cholinesterase-inhibiting properties.
95361.benefits: Effective pest control agent in agriculture, helps protect crops from insect damage
95361.risks: Neurotoxicity, cholinesterase inhibition, acute poisoning, environmental toxicity, potential carcinogenicity

sources.label: EPA profenofos risk assessment summary

95388.name: Koffein
95388.description: Caffeine extracted from coffee beans; a central nervous system stimulant.
95388.benefits: Enhances alertness, cognitive function, and temporary reduction of fatigue
95388.risks: Irritation at high doses, potential for insomnia, increased heart rate, dependence with excessive intake

sources.label: PMID 22285823 - Caffeine effects on cognitive function
PMID 23073926 - Safety and health effects of caffeine consumption

95397.name: Tribufos
95397.description: Tribufos is an organophosphorus pesticide primarily used in agriculture to control pests on crops. It is not a food ingredient but rather a chemical material used for pest control. Exposure to tribufos can pose health risks through dermal contact, inhalation, or ingestion of residues.
95397.risks: Toxicity, neurotoxicity, potential carcinogenicity, environmental contamination, acute poisoning symptoms

sources.label: WHO Concise International Chemical Assessment Document 32: Tribufos

95441.name: Regulador de acidez INS 330
95441.description: Citric acid is an organic acid commonly used as an acidity regulator and flavoring agent in food and beverages.
95441.benefits: Acidity regulation, flavor enhancement, preservative effect by pH reduction
95441.risks: Dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption, minor gastrointestinal irritation in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMID 25126481 - Citric acid effects on dental enamel
PMID 25940222 - Use of citric acid as food additive

95451.name: Tribromoacetic acid
95451.description: Tribromoacetic acid is a halogenated acetic acid derivative primarily used in chemical synthesis and industrial applications. It is not classified or approved as a food ingredient. Its chemical properties include strong acidity and potential corrosiveness.
95451.benefits: None in food or consumer health context
95451.risks: Corrosive, toxic if ingested or inhaled, potential skin and eye irritant, environmental hazard

sources.label: PubChem Tribromoacetic acid - Chemical properties and hazards
ATSDR - Toxicological Profile for Halogenated Acetic Acids

95452.name: Acetaldhyde
95452.description: Acetaldehyde is a volatile organic compound and a known carcinogen; it is a byproduct of alcohol metabolism and occurs naturally in some foods and beverages. It is not a food ingredient but rather a contaminant or chemical compound of concern. Exposure primarily occurs via inhalation or ingestion at low levels; it is metabolized quickly in the body but can cause DNA damage and toxicity at higher doses.
95452.risks: Carcinogenicity, DNA damage, respiratory irritation, potential contribution to cancer development

95506.name: Chlorpyriphos
95506.description: An organophosphate pesticide used in agriculture to control insects. It is not a food ingredient but a chemical material with significant safety concerns due to its neurotoxic effects on humans and wildlife.
95506.benefits: Effective broad-spectrum insecticide for crop protection, pest control
95506.risks: Neurotoxicity, developmental neurotoxicity in children, endocrine disruption, environmental toxicity, potential carcinogenicity

95565.name: Nitrates/Nitrites
95565.description: Preservatives commonly used in processed meats to prevent bacterial growth and maintain color; nitrates can convert to nitrites and potentially form carcinogenic nitrosamines under certain conditions.
95565.benefits: Prevent growth of Clostridium botulinum in meats, preserve color and flavor
95565.risks: Possible increased risk of certain cancers, especially colorectal cancer, if consumed in large amounts; potential methemoglobinemia in infants

95570.name: Natürliches Zitronenaroma
95570.description: Natural lemon flavor derived from lemon oils or extracts, used to impart lemon taste in foods. Considered safe by FDA when used as intended, but composition can vary.
95570.benefits: Adds flavor, may contain beneficial compounds from lemon oils
95570.risks: Possible allergic reactions, generally safe but some natural flavor components may cause sensitivity

95577.name: Desisopropylatrazine
95577.description: A chemical metabolite of the herbicide atrazine, not used as a food ingredient but rather an environmental contaminant and degradation product. It is not approved or intended for direct food use.
95577.risks: Potential endocrine disruption, environmental toxicity, possible carcinogenic effects based on animal studies

95578.name: Propanoic acid, 2,2,3,3-tetrafluoro-3-(trifluorome...
95578.description: Tap water contaminant (EWG): Propanoic acid, 2,2,3,3-tetrafluoro-3-(trifluorome.... Add description/guidelines in admin.

95597.name: Perfluoro(2-ethoxyethane)sulfonic acid
95597.description: A perfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) used industrially for its chemical stability and resistance properties. Not a food ingredient; considered a material with potential environmental persistence and bioaccumulation concerns.
95597.benefits: Chemical and thermal stability useful in industrial applications
95597.risks: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, potential toxicity, endocrine disruption, possible carcinogenicity

95612.name: Heneicosane
95612.description: Heneicosane is a straight-chain alkane hydrocarbon (C21H44), naturally occurring in some plant waxes and insect pheromones. It is not used as a food ingredient and primarily appears in materials context. As a hydrocarbon, it is combustible and may be used in fragrance formulations or wax products. No evidence supports its toxicity at typical exposure levels; however, inhalation of combustion products may pose respiratory risks.
95612.benefits: Used in fragrance industry as a fixative, naturally derived component in some waxes
95612.risks: Combustion byproducts inhalation risks, skin contact irritation possible in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PubChem Heneicosane Summary

95618.name: Alpha-methyl-styrene, dimer
95618.description: Alpha-methylstyrene dimer is a synthetic chemical compound derived from the polymerization of alpha-methylstyrene, commonly used in industrial applications such as resins and coatings. It is not used as a food ingredient and lacks nutritional value. Safety concerns arise primarily from exposure during manufacturing or in occupational settings, with limited information about toxicity via ingestion.
95618.risks: Potential skin and respiratory irritation, occupational exposure hazards, possible toxicity with prolonged exposure

sources.label: PubChem entry on Alpha-methylstyrene dimer

95624.name: o-Ethyltoluene
95624.description: o-Ethyltoluene (ortho-ethyltoluene) is an aromatic hydrocarbon used primarily as an industrial solvent and chemical intermediate. It is not a food ingredient but a material with potential exposure via inhalation or skin contact in industrial settings.
95624.risks: Respiratory irritation, skin and eye irritation, potential central nervous system effects, flammability, environmental toxicity

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary
EPA Chemical Data Report on o-Ethyltoluene

95645.name: Vitamin C Powder
95645.description: Ascorbic acid in powdered form, a potent antioxidant vitamin essential for immune function, collagen synthesis, and antioxidant protection. Recognized as safe and essential by FDA.
95645.benefits: Antioxidant, supports immune health, collagen production, wound healing
95645.risks: High doses may cause gastrointestinal upset, kidney stones in susceptible individuals

sources.label: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Vitamin C

95650.name: tert-Amyl methyl ether
95650.description: tert-Amyl methyl ether (TAME) is an organic ether commonly used as a fuel additive or solvent. It is not a food ingredient and should not be ingested. Exposure is primarily via inhalation or skin contact in industrial contexts.
95650.risks: Toxic if ingested, respiratory irritation, central nervous system effects, potential flammability hazards

sources.label: PubChem - tert-Amyl methyl ether

95665.name: Organic
95665.description: Label indicating that the ingredient was grown without synthetic pesticides, herbicides, and genetically modified organisms. Organic certification ensures compliance with specific agricultural standards.
95665.benefits: Reduced pesticide exposure, environmental benefits, supports sustainable agriculture

95666.name: Isooctyl alcohol
95666.description: Isooctyl alcohol is a branched-chain aliphatic alcohol commonly used as a solvent, plasticizer, and intermediate in chemical synthesis. It is not used as a food ingredient, but rather in industrial and material applications such as fragrances, coatings, and cleaning agents. Safety assessments focus on dermal and inhalation exposure, with low acute toxicity reported, though it can cause skin and eye irritation upon direct contact.
95666.benefits: Effective solvent properties, low acute systemic toxicity
95666.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, respiratory irritation upon inhalation in high concentrations

sources.label: PubChem Isooctyl Alcohol Chemical Summary
Toxicological Profiles and Safety Evaluations of Alcohol Solvents

95749.name: Magnesium Sulphate
95749.description: Magnesium sulphate is an inorganic salt commonly used as a food additive (E518) and supplement. It serves as a magnesium source and is used for electrolyte replenishment. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for consumption in regulated amounts but excessive intake may cause laxative effects.
95749.benefits: Magnesium source, supports muscle and nerve function, metabolic processes, bone health
95749.risks: Laxative effect, gastrointestinal discomfort in high doses, potential electrolyte imbalance if overused

sources.label: Magnesium Sulfate - NIH PubChem

95754.name: Potassium Sorbate [Preservative]
95754.description: Salt of sorbic acid used as a food and cosmetic preservative to inhibit mold and yeast growth.
95754.benefits: Effective preservation against fungi, extends shelf life of products
95754.risks: Mild irritation potential, possible sensitization in rare cases, generally low toxicity at typical use levels

sources.label: PMID 29238249 - Safety evaluation of potassium sorbate

95834.name: Acesulfamo potásico
95834.description: Acesulfame potassium (acesulfame K) is a calorie-free artificial sweetener approved by FDA. It is used to provide sweetness without calories but has some concerns about long-term safety.
95834.benefits: Calorie-free sweetener, helps reduce sugar intake, stable under heat
95834.risks: Potential metabolic effects, controversial data regarding carcinogenicity and gut microbiome changes

95972.name: Acidificante: acido citrico
95972.description: Citric acid is a common food acidulant used for flavor and preservation; generally recognized as safe; excessive consumption may cause mild gastrointestinal discomfort.
95972.risks: Possible mild gastrointestinal irritation at very high intake

95973.name: Antiossidante: acido ascorbico
95973.description: Acido ascorbico, noto anche come vitamina C, è un antiossidante e agente acidificante usato come esaltatore di sapidità negli alimenti.
95973.benefits: Antiossidante, migliora la stabilità degli alimenti, supporta la sintesi del collagene
95973.risks: Irritazione a dosi elevate, possibile allergia in soggetti sensibili

95974.name: Aromi
95974.description: Flavoring substances used to impart aroma and taste to food products, may be natural or synthetic.
95974.benefits: Enhances flavor and aroma of foods
95974.risks: Potential allergen contamination, particularly nut traces, possible sensitization

95988.name: Cloruro de benzalconio
95988.description: Benzalkonium chloride, a quaternary ammonium compound used as a disinfectant and surfactant.
95988.risks: Skin and eye irritation, potential respiratory sensitizer, toxic if ingested in large amounts

sources.label: ECHA Benzalkonium chloride

96007.name: Karbondioksit
96007.description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a colorless gas commonly used in food processing (e.g., carbonation, modified atmosphere packaging). It is non-toxic at typical exposure levels and generally recognized as safe for food applications.
96007.benefits: Used for food preservation and carbonation
96007.risks: None in normal use; excessive inhalation can cause respiratory distress

sources.label: Carbon dioxide in food processing safety
Carbon dioxide toxicity and safety

96008.name: Antioksidan: askorbik asit
96008.description: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is a well-known antioxidant used as a food additive to prevent oxidation and preserve freshness. It is essential for human health and FDA recognized as safe.
96008.benefits: Antioxidant, supports immune function, collagen synthesis, food preservation
96008.risks: Rare gastrointestinal discomfort with excessive intake

sources.label: Ascorbic acid in food industry and safety

96069.name: Benzoate de potassium
96069.description: Potassium benzoate is a potassium salt of benzoic acid used as a preservative to inhibit microbial growth in food and beverages.
96069.benefits: Effective antimicrobial preservative, extends shelf life of products
96069.risks: Potential mild irritation, possible formation of benzene under acidic conditions, allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

96070.name: Essence naturelle
96070.description: Natural essence or natural flavor typically refers to flavoring substances derived from natural sources such as fruits, herbs, spices, or other botanicals. The term is broad and may include many different compounds; often used in beverages to impart taste and aroma.
96070.benefits: Improves flavor and aroma, derived from natural sources
96070.risks: Lack of transparency on specific compounds, may contain trace solvents or allergens, potential for ultra-processed additive effects

96158.name: Eritritol
96158.description: Erythritol is a sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener that does not significantly raise blood sugar or insulin levels. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA and commonly found in sugar-free and low-calorie foods.
96158.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, does not raise blood glucose, tooth-friendly, antioxidant properties
96158.risks: Digestive upset in large amounts (bloating, gas, laxative effect)

96164.name: 2-Amino-1-butanol
96164.description: 2-Amino-1-butanol is an organic compound primarily used in industrial and chemical synthesis applications. It is not recognized or approved as a food ingredient by the FDA. There is limited information on its safety for human consumption, and it is generally considered a chemical reagent rather than a food additive.
96164.risks: Potential toxicity if ingested, skin and eye irritation upon contact, not intended for food use

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary - 2-Amino-1-butanol

96178.name: Sok cytrynowy z koncentratu soku cytrynowego
96178.description: Lemon juice made from concentrated lemon juice, typically used as a flavoring and acidifying agent in foods and beverages.
96178.benefits: Provides natural acidity for flavor, contains vitamin C and antioxidants, acts as a preservative
96178.risks: Possible oral and skin irritation at high concentrations, acidity-related dental enamel erosion with excessive consumption

sources.label: PMC4341950 - Lemon juice and dental enamel erosion
PMC3875912 - Nutritional and bioactive compounds in Citrus fruits

96203.name: Chlorure de calcium
96203.description: Calcium chloride is a salt used in food processing as a firming agent, preservative, and electrolyte additive. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in accordance with good manufacturing practices.
96203.benefits: Provides calcium, acts as a preservative, improves texture in canned or processed foods
96203.risks: Excessive ingestion may cause gastrointestinal irritation, hypercalcemia in rare cases

sources.label: Calcium Chloride - Dietary Supplement Fact Sheet
FDA Food Additive Status for Calcium Chloride

96241.name: Vitamin B5 Supplement
96241.description: Water-soluble vitamin (pantothenic acid) essential for synthesizing coenzyme A, important in energy metabolism and synthesis of fatty acids.
96241.benefits: Supports energy metabolism, aids synthesis of fatty acids and coenzyme A, essential nutrient
96241.risks: Rarely causes irritation or sensitization at high topical doses, excessive oral intake may cause mild gastrointestinal symptoms

sources.label: Pantothenic Acid in Health and Disease
Safety of pantothenic acid

96296.name: Calcium Disodium EDTA [to Protect Flavor]
96296.description: Chelating agent used to bind metal ions and preserve flavor in foods by preventing oxidation.
96296.benefits: Prevents oxidation and off-flavors, maintains product stability
96296.risks: Minor gastrointestinal irritation at high ingestive levels

sources.label: Use and safety of EDTA in food

96563.name: Sodium Lauryl Phosphate Ester Magnesium Salt
96563.description: An anionic surfactant and phosphate ester salt used for cleaning and emulsifying. It belongs to the class of phosphate esters and is a derivative of sodium lauryl phosphate with magnesium counterion.
96563.benefits: Effective surfactant for soil removal, good emulsifying properties, biodegradable
96563.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, potential for mild sensitization at higher concentrations

96580.name: Sodium Lauryl Phosphate Ester Calcium Manganese Salt
96580.description: An organophosphate-based surfactant salt containing calcium and manganese ions, used as a detergent and emulsifier in cleaning products. Limited direct toxicological data available; compounds of this type generally exhibit surfactant-like properties with potential mild irritation.
96580.benefits: Surfactant properties for effective cleaning and emulsification, contributes to soil removal
96580.risks: Potential mild skin irritation, possible eye irritation, limited sensitization data available

sources.label: ECHA Registration Dossier General Surfactant Data
General Information on Phosphate Ester Surfactants

96602.name: Erythrit
96602.description: A sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener that provides sweetness with minimal digestion and absorption.
96602.benefits: Low calorie sweetener, does not raise blood glucose or insulin, dental-friendly
96602.risks: Gastrointestinal discomfort at high doses, laxative effect in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMID 23354405 - Safety of erythritol as a sugar substitute
PMID 29864374 - Effects of erythritol on glycemia and dental health

96761.name: Pentapotassium bis(peroxymonosulphate) bis(sulphate)
96761.description: Sulphates are salts or esters of sulfuric acid, commonly present as ions in water and various compounds.
96761.benefits: Essential dietary mineral in small amounts, involved in detoxification and synthesis of biological molecules
96761.risks: Irritation potential depending on compound form, ingestion in high amounts may cause laxative effects, potential contamination with heavy metals in industrial forms

96775.name: Natural colour (purple carrot concentrate)
96775.description: Natural colorant derived from purple carrots, primarily providing anthocyanin pigments. Used to impart purple color in food products.

96840.name: Prírodná minerálna voda
96840.description: Natural mineral water containing essential minerals beneficial for hydration and mineral intake; recognized as safe for consumption by regulatory authorities.

96841.name: Kyselina citrónová
96841.description: Organic acid commonly used as an acidity regulator and preservative in food products.
96841.benefits: Controls acidity, enhances flavor, improves preservation by inhibiting microbial growth
96841.risks: Irritant to skin and eyes in concentrated form, potential dental enamel erosion with excessive ingestion, minor sensitizer

96938.name: Steviablätter
96938.description: Steviablätter are the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant, commonly used as a natural sweetener. They contain steviol glycosides, which provide sweetness without calories. In their whole leaf form, stevia leaves have been consumed traditionally and are generally recognized as safe. The FDA permits purified steviol glycosides as additives but does not approve whole leaf or crude extracts as food additives due to a lack of sufficient safety data.
96938.benefits: Natural zero-calorie sweetener, may help regulate blood sugar, antioxidant properties
96938.risks: Potential allergenicity, possible gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals, whole leaf not FDA approved as additive

96963.name: Kolsyra
96963.description: Kolsyra is the Swedish term for carbonic acid, which forms when carbon dioxide dissolves in water. It is commonly used in beverages as carbonation and is recognized as safe for consumption.
96963.benefits: Adds carbonation and mild acidity to beverages, enhances taste

97025.name: Pure Structured Water
97025.description: Water claimed to have a specific molecular arrangement differing from regular water. Scientifically, water's structure is transient and not proven to have lasting 'structured' properties. It is a food-related ingredient when consumed as drinking water.

sources.label: Molecular structure studies of water

97043.name: Jus d'orange concentré biologique
97043.description: Organic concentrated orange juice is derived from freshly squeezed orange juice that has been concentrated by removing water content. It retains natural vitamins and nutrients but has a higher sugar concentration. It is considered safe for consumption and provides vitamin C and antioxidants. The organic designation indicates production without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers.
97043.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, supports immune function, natural source of nutrients
97043.risks: High sugar content, potential dental erosion with excessive consumption

97044.name: Cold-pressed lime juice
97044.description: Juice extracted from limes using mechanical pressing without heat, retaining most original nutrients and flavor compounds.
97044.benefits: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants, natural flavoring, may support hydration
97044.risks: Potential oral and skin irritation from acidity, photosensitivity risk on skin, risk of microbial contamination if improperly handled

sources.label: PMC3768956 - Citrus fruits as sources of bioactive compounds
PMC1272557 - Photosensitizing effects of lime juice in skin

97064.name: Sweetener: E 955 (Sucralose)
97064.description: Sucralose is a non-nutritive artificial sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories.
97064.benefits: Non-caloric sweetener, does not raise blood sugar, supports calorie reduction
97064.risks: Potential for gut microbiota alterations, possible digestive discomfort in some individuals

97106.name: Fair Trade Organic Black Tea Extract
97106.description: Concentrated extract derived from organic black tea leaves, certified Fair Trade ensuring ethical sourcing. Rich in polyphenols and antioxidants with potential cardiovascular and cognitive benefits.
97106.benefits: Antioxidant activity, cardiovascular support, cognitive enhancement, contains polyphenols
97106.risks: Caffeine sensitivity, potential for mild gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals

97161.name: Calcium pantothenate [Vitamin B5]
97161.description: Water-soluble vitamin serving as a precursor to coenzyme A, important in fatty acid metabolism.
97161.benefits: Supports energy production, fatty acid metabolism, and wound healing
97161.risks: Generally low toxicity, safe at recommended intake levels

sources.label: PMID 23838589 - Vitamin B5 biochemistry and safety

97220.name: Conservante Benzoato de Sódio
97220.description: Sodium benzoate is a commonly used preservative that inhibits microbial growth in acidic foods and beverages.
97220.benefits: Effective antimicrobial preservative, extends shelf life of acidic products
97220.risks: Irritation potential in sensitive individuals, possible allergen, limited endocrine disruption concerns at typical use, formation of benzene under certain conditions

97222.name: Acidifier E338 (Phosphoric Acid)
97222.description: Phosphoric acid is an inorganic acid used in food and beverages to acidify and add tartness.
97222.benefits: Provides sour taste, acts as a preservative and pH regulator in foods and beverages
97222.risks: Dental erosion with excessive consumption, potential mineral imbalance with high intake

sources.label: General safety of food additives: phosphoric acid

97223.name: Conservante (sorbato de potássio)
97223.description: Potassium sorbate is a commonly used food preservative that inhibits mold, yeast, and some bacteria growth. It is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used within approved limits.
97223.benefits: Prevents food spoilage, extends shelf life
97223.risks: Possible allergic reactions, mild gastrointestinal irritation in sensitive individuals, potential hypersensitivity

97274.name: Aspartaam
97274.description: Artificial low-calorie sweetener commonly used in food and beverages. Approved by FDA but linked to some health concerns in sensitive individuals.
97274.benefits: Low-calorie sweetener, helps reduce sugar intake
97274.risks: Possible headaches, allergic reactions, controversial potential for metabolic disruption, neurotoxicity in sensitive individuals

97286.name: Doğal maden suyu
97286.description: Natural mineral water containing dissolved minerals and trace elements from geological sources.
97286.risks: Contaminants possible depending on source quality, microbiological contamination if untreated

sources.label: PMC5117406 – Mineral water composition and effects

97287.name: Asitliği düzenleyici (sitrik asit)
97287.description: Citric acid, a natural organic acid used to regulate acidity in foods. Generally recognized as safe by the FDA and commonly used in food products.
97287.benefits: Maintains food pH, natural preservative, enhances flavor
97287.risks: May cause mild dental erosion with excessive consumption

97288.name: Karadut
97288.description: Black mulberry fruit, a natural whole food rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and fiber. Safe and nutritious for consumption.
97288.benefits: Rich in antioxidants, vitamins C and K, dietary fiber

97289.name: Frenk üzümü
97289.description: Currant fruit, a natural source of vitamins, antioxidants, and dietary fiber. Generally safe and beneficial to include in diet.

97290.name: Sodyum benzoat
97290.description: Sodium benzoate, a synthetic preservative widely used to prevent microbial growth in acidic foods and beverages. Approved by FDA but may cause adverse reactions in sensitive individuals.
97290.risks: Potential to cause allergic reactions, rare hypersensitivity, possible benzene formation with ascorbic acid

97291.name: Potasyum sorbat
97291.description: Potassium sorbate, a synthetic preservative used to inhibit molds and yeasts in foods. Generally recognized as safe but can cause mild irritation or allergies in some individuals.
97291.benefits: Prevents microbial spoilage, prolongs product shelf life
97291.risks: Possible mild allergic reactions, skin irritation

97292.name: Renklendirici (antosiyanin)
97292.description: Anthocyanins, natural pigments found in fruits and vegetables that provide red, purple, and blue colors. They have antioxidant properties and are considered safe as natural colorants.

97320.name: Kalsiyum
97320.description: Calcium, an essential mineral vital for bone health, nerve transmission, and muscle function. Commonly supplemented in diet.
97320.benefits: Supports bone density, muscle function, nerve signaling
97320.risks: Hypercalcemia with excessive intake rare in normal consumption

97324.name: Niasin
97324.description: Niacin (Vitamin B3), a water-soluble vitamin essential for energy metabolism and DNA repair.
97324.benefits: Supports energy production, skin health, nervous system function
97324.risks: Flushing and liver toxicity with excessive supplemental doses

97510.name: Tin
97510.description: Metal used industrially and occasionally as a food packaging material (tin cans). Trace amounts in food are generally regarded as safe by regulatory agencies, but tin metal itself is not a food ingredient.
97510.risks: Potential toxicity in high concentrations, gastrointestinal irritation if ingested in excess, not intended for direct consumption

97653.name: Fresh grapefruit juice
97653.description: Fresh grapefruit juice is rich in vitamin C, potassium, and bioactive flavonoids. It has nutritional benefits but is known for interactions with many medications due to furanocoumarins inhibiting cytochrome P450 enzymes. Generally safe to consume but caution advised if taking certain drugs.
97653.benefits: Rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, supports immune function
97653.risks: Drug interactions (especially with statins, calcium channel blockers), photosensitivity, potential gastrointestinal irritation

97731.name: Kıvam Arttırıcı (Gam Arabik)
97731.description: Gum Arabic, a natural polysaccharide derived from Acacia trees, widely used as a food stabilizer and thickener. Generally recognized as safe by FDA.
97731.benefits: Dietary fiber source, stabilizes food texture, prebiotic effects
97731.risks: Rare allergic reactions, possible gastrointestinal discomfort in large amounts

97776.name: Aroma de naranja
97776.description: Orange flavor, may be natural or artificial, used to enhance taste. Artificial flavors are often considered ultra-processed additives with limited transparency.
97776.risks: Potential exposure to synthetic chemicals, allergic reactions in sensitive individuals

97910.name: Preservative Potassium metabisulfite E224
97910.description: Potassium metabisulfite is a sulfite preservative used to prevent microbial growth and oxidation in food and beverages.
97910.benefits: Prevents microbial spoilage, inhibits enzymatic and oxidative browning, extends shelf life
97910.risks: Irritation, allergic sensitization especially in sulfite-sensitive individuals, potential respiratory irritation, contamination risk due to residual sulfur dioxide

sources.label: Sulfite hypersensitivity and toxicity - PMC6913717

98305.name: Isopentylcyclohexanone
98305.description: A synthetic fragrance chemical commonly used in perfumes and scented products. It is not a food ingredient and primarily evaluated for inhalation exposure in fragrance applications.
98305.benefits: Provides floral or fruity fragrance notes in scented products
98305.risks: Potential respiratory irritant, possible allergen causing skin or respiratory sensitization

sources.label: PubChem Compound Summary

98379.name: Concentrate
98379.description: A general term referring to a substance in concentrated form, often fruit or vegetable juice concentrate in food contexts, containing nutritive components in reduced volume.
98379.benefits: Contains concentrated nutrients and natural flavor compounds if from fruit or vegetable origin
98379.risks: Can have increased sugar content if fruit-based, potential processing contaminants depending on source

98380.name: Acidifier: E330
98380.description: Citric acid, a naturally occurring organic acid used extensively as a flavoring and acidifying agent; generally recognized as safe by FDA.
98380.benefits: Enhances flavor, acts as a preservative by lowering pH, antioxidant properties
98380.risks: May cause dental erosion in excessive amounts, mild gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals

98424.name: Přírodní minerální voda
98424.description: Natural mineral water derived from underground sources containing minerals. Generally safe and hydrating with essential mineral content varying by source. Recognized as a food ingredient with no inherent harm.
98424.benefits: Hydration, source of natural minerals like calcium, magnesium

98425.name: Regulátory kyselosti: kyselina citronová
98425.description: Citric acid used as an acidity regulator and preservative in foods. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by FDA though can cause mild irritation or tooth enamel erosion in excess.
98425.benefits: Preserves food freshness, enhances flavor, aids mineral absorption
98425.risks: Dental enamel erosion with high consumption, possible mild digestive irritation

98472.name: Pivo nealkoholické svetlé
98472.description: Non-alcoholic light beer, a beverage brewed to contain minimal or no alcohol. It provides hydration and typical beer micronutrients in very low amounts but lacks alcohol's effects.
98472.benefits: Hydrating beverage, source of B vitamins and antioxidants from malt
98472.risks: Minimal; very low alcohol content usually considered safe, possible sensitivity to gluten if not gluten-free

98496.name: Non-nutritive sweetener sucralose
98496.description: Sucralose is a chlorinated artificial sweetener used to provide sweetness without calories.
98496.benefits: Provides intense sweetness without calories, does not raise blood glucose levels, stable under heat allowing use in cooking
98496.risks: Potential gut microbiota alterations, possible glucose metabolism effects in sensitive individuals, minor gastrointestinal discomfort reported, processing byproduct concerns

98499.name: Color: beta carotene (E160a)
98499.description: A red-orange pigment found in plants and fruits, used as a natural colorant and a precursor to vitamin A in the human body.
98499.benefits: Source of provitamin A, supports vision and immune function, provides natural coloring
98499.risks: High-dose supplementation associated with increased lung cancer risk in smokers, potential skin discoloration at excessive intake

99164.name: Wild Indigo Herb
99164.description: Herbal ingredient derived from Baptisia species, traditionally used in herbal medicine for its immune-support and antimicrobial properties. Not a typical food ingredient; used in supplements and herbal preparations.
99164.benefits: Immune support, antimicrobial activity, traditional use for respiratory and inflammation ailments
99164.risks: Potential allergic reactions, gastrointestinal upset, toxicity at high doses

99313.name: Alkalinity sources
99313.description: Chemical compounds used to increase the pH in cleaning products, commonly including sodium hydroxide, potassium hydroxide, sodium carbonate. Serve to enhance cleaning efficiency by breaking down organic soils.
99313.benefits: Improved cleaning efficacy through saponification and soil dispersion, enhanced grease removal
99313.risks: Skin irritation, eye irritation, chemical burns (depending on type and concentration), respiratory irritation (dust or vapors from strong alkalis)

sources.label: ECHA sodium hydroxide dossier
Toxnet alkaline chemical burns overview
EPA alkaline substances safety summary

99394.name: 2-Furancarboxyaldehyde
99394.description: Tap water contaminant (EWG): 2-Furancarboxyaldehyde. Add description/guidelines in admin.

99447.name: Säuerungsmittel
99447.description: German term for acidulants used in food products to control pH, preserve freshness, and add sour taste. Common acidulants include citric acid, lactic acid, and acetic acid. Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA when used in normal amounts.
99447.benefits: Preserves food, enhances flavor, controls microbial growth
99447.risks: Dental erosion with excessive consumption, possible gastrointestinal irritation

99721.name: Acesulfaam-K
99721.description: Acesulfame potassium (Acesulfame-K) is a calorie-free artificial sweetener approved by FDA. It provides sweetness without calories but has been subject to scrutiny over potential health effects.
99721.benefits: Calorie-free sweetener, helps reduce sugar intake
99721.risks: Possible mild metabolic effects, potential gut microbiome impact, artificial additive

99750.name: Butylated Hydroxyanisole [E320]
99750.description: Synthetic antioxidant used to prevent lipid oxidation and rancidity in foods containing fats and oils.
99750.benefits: Prevents lipid oxidation, extends shelf life of fatty foods, preserves flavor and color stability
99750.risks: Potential carcinogenicity concerns based on animal studies, possible endocrine disruption, hypersensitivity reactions in rare cases

100021.name: Frambuesa 0
100021.description: Raspberry (Rubus idaeus) derived flavor and aroma component.
100021.risks: Minimal risk for irritation or sensitization, rare allergy possible

100024.name: Reguladores de la acidez: ácido cítrico
100024.description: Food additives used to control or adjust the acidity or alkalinity (pH) of foods; examples include citric acid, phosphates, and carbonates.
100024.benefits: Preserve food stability, improve flavor, enhance shelf life
100024.risks: Generally low toxicity; excessive intake of some (e.g., phosphates) may affect mineral balance, potential digestive irritation at high levels

100043.name: Sulfito de sodio
100043.description: Sodium sulfite, a preservative and antioxidant used to prevent browning and microbial growth in foods.
100043.benefits: Preservative that prevents food spoilage and discoloration
100043.risks: Allergic reactions, respiratory irritation, potential asthma exacerbation in sensitive individuals, possible sulfite intolerance

sources.label: Sulfite sensitivity and reactions

100044.name: Vitamina A
100044.description: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin essential for vision, immune function, and cell growth. Fish gelatin is a protein derived from fish collagen used as a capsule material for oral supplements.
100044.benefits: Supports vision, immune system, skin health, and cellular function
100044.risks: Excessive vitamin A intake can cause toxicity including liver damage and teratogenicity; potential allergenicity from fish gelatin in sensitive individuals

100227.name: Arômes naturels
100227.description: Natural flavorings derived from plant or animal sources to impart aroma and taste to food products. The term covers a broad range of substances without specific identification.
100227.benefits: Provide natural flavor and aroma enhancement for food products
100227.risks: Potential for allergenic compounds, variability in composition, lack of transparency, possible trace solvent residues, sensitization in sensitive individuals

sources.label: PMID 29282528 – Natural flavor compounds: allergenic potential and chemical composition
PMID 29165380 – Safety evaluation of natural flavorings

100233.name: Conservateur (E202)
100233.description: Potassium sorbate, a preservative used to inhibit mold and yeast growth in food products.
100233.benefits: Extends shelf life by preventing microbial spoilage
100233.risks: Possible mild skin and mucous membrane irritation at high concentrations

100252.name: Orange carrot concentrate
100252.description: Carrot concentrate used as a natural colorant derived from carrot juice or puree.
100252.benefits: Provides natural coloring, contains carotenoids with antioxidant properties
100252.risks: None identified at typical use levels

100281.name: Organic Natural Raspberry Flavouring
100281.description: Flavoring derived from raspberries using permitted natural extraction methods under organic standards.
100281.benefits: Adds raspberry flavor naturally, enhances palatability without synthetic additives
100281.risks: Potential sensitization or allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, possible trace solvent residues depending on extraction

100311.name: Lithium Magnesium Sodium Silicate [Nano]
100311.description: An engineered nanomaterial composed of silicate minerals combined with lithium, magnesium, and sodium ions, typically used as a rheology modifier or thickener in cosmetics and other formulations.
100311.benefits: Effective thickening and stabilizing agent in topical formulations, improves texture and application properties
100311.risks: Potential for respiratory irritation or toxicity upon inhalation due to nanoscale size, possible skin sensitization, unknown long-term exposure effects, limited toxicological data

100335.name: Äppeljuice 6%
100335.description: Apple juice is a beverage derived from pressed apples, containing natural sugars, organic acids, and polyphenols.
100335.benefits: Source of vitamins, antioxidants (polyphenols), hydrating beverage
100335.risks: Ingestion toxicity at high intake due to sugar content, potential allergen in sensitive individuals

100336.name: Mangopuré 3%
100336.description: Pureed mango fruit, providing flavor, texture, and some nutrients such as vitamins and dietary fiber.

107363.name: Food Colour (Beta-Carotene)

107540.name: Stabiliser (412) - Guar Gum

107572.name: Emulsifier (Glycerol Esters of Wood Rosins)

107796.name: Antioxidante (E300)

107813.name: Zwarte bes

109244.name: Aromata

109256.name: Flavor enhancer (erythritol)

109276.name: Prirodna mineralna voda

109312.name: Conservation (benzoate de sodium)

109339.name: Antimony potassium tartrate

109401.description: Colorless, odorless gas used as a propellant, preservative, or inert atmosphere in food and beverage applications; naturally present in respiration and atmosphere.

115314.risks: Potential sensitization/allergic reactions, possible synthetic additives

115567.name: Trans fat
115567.description: Type of unsaturated fat with at least one double bond in trans configuration, often industrially produced through partial hydrogenation of oils.
115567.risks: Increased cardiovascular disease risk, raises LDL cholesterol, lowers HDL cholesterol, associated with coronary heart disease

sources.label: PMCID: PMC5540940 - Health implications of trans fats

115569.name: Saturated Fat
115569.description: A class of fatty acids with no double bonds, found in animal fats and some plant oils, contributing to energy storage and cell membrane structure.
115569.benefits: Energy source, supports cell membrane integrity and hormone production
115569.risks: Excessive intake associated with increased LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular disease risk

sources.label: PMID 29630245 - Dietary saturated fat and cardiovascular disease risk: systematic review and meta-analysis
PMID 29180272 - Role of saturated fat in human diet: a review and update

115867.name: Kalsiyum klorür
115867.description: Calcium chloride, an inorganic salt used as a firming agent, flavor enhancer, and preservative in foods.
115867.benefits: Provides calcium, improves texture and shelf-life of foods
115867.risks: High ingestion amounts may cause gastrointestinal discomfort

sources.label: Calcium chloride properties and uses

115946.name: Acidity Regulator (E330, E331(iii))
115946.description: E330 is citric acid, a weak organic acid used to control the acidity of food and beverages. E331(iii) is trisodium citrate, a sodium salt of citric acid used as an acidity regulator, sequestrant, and preservative enhancer.
115946.benefits: Controls acidity, preserves food stability, enhances flavor
115946.risks: Irritation to mucous membranes in high amounts, excessive sodium intake from trisodium citrate

sources.label: Citric Acid and Citrates - Food Additives

115957.name: Aroma natural de maracujá
115957.description: Natural flavoring derived from passion fruit components through extraction or distillation, used to impart maracujá (passion fruit) flavor in foods and beverages.
115957.benefits: Provides natural fruit flavor enhancing product palatability
115957.risks: Potential for allergens, minor sensitization risk, variability in composition, possible processing residues

115967.name: Třtinový cukr
115967.description: Sugar derived from sugarcane, primarily sucrose used as a sweetener.
115967.risks: Excessive intake associated with obesity, dental caries, and metabolic disturbances

116052.name: Sarı demir oksit
116052.description: Yellow iron oxide is an inorganic pigment commonly used for coloring in cosmetics, paints, and coatings.
116052.benefits: Provides stable, non-toxic pigmentation, UV protection in cosmetics
116052.risks: Potential for dermal and respiratory irritation in powder form, contamination risk if impurities present

sources.label: Iron Oxide Pigments - Toxicological Profile

116141.name: Farbstoff E 141
116141.description: Colorants used in cleaning products to provide color. Chemical composition varies widely depending on specific dye used.
116141.benefits: Improves product aesthetic appeal, consumer acceptance
116141.risks: Potential skin irritation, potential allergic reactions depending on dye type

sources.label: ECHA information on colorants

116246.name: Koolzuurhoudend water
116246.description: Water infused with carbon dioxide under pressure to create carbonation.
116246.risks: Mild dental enamel erosion risk due to acidity

116248.name: Aroma (cafeïne)
116248.description: Aroma is a flavoring component that includes caffeine and quinine as part of its constituents. Caffeine is a stimulant commonly found in beverages, while quinine is a bitter compound historically used to flavor tonic water.
116248.benefits: Enhancement of flavor profile, mild stimulant effects from caffeine at typical exposure
116248.risks: Caffeine ingestion toxicity at high doses, potential irritant at high concentrations, quinine ingestion toxicity and hypersensitivity, regulatory limits on quinine use

sources.label: Quinine - Drug Information and Toxicity
EFSA Safety Assessment of Quinine as a Food Additive

116250.name: Voedingszuur (E338)
116250.description: Phosphoric acid (E338) used as a food acidulant to adjust pH and flavor.
116250.benefits: Flavor enhancement, preservative effect through pH control
116250.risks: Dental erosion with excessive consumption, potential phosphorus imbalance with high intake

116256.name: Zuurteregelaar: E331
116256.description: Citric acid salts (E331) used to regulate acidity in food products.
116256.benefits: Acidity regulation, flavor enhancement, food preservation
116256.risks: Irritation risk to sensitive individuals at high concentrations

116265.name: Citroenzuur [E330]
116265.description: Citric acid is a weak organic acid used primarily as an acidity regulator, preservative, and flavor enhancer in food products.
116265.benefits: Enhances flavor, preserves food stability, chelates metal ions to prevent spoilage
116265.risks: Potential minor irritation with excessive ingestion or contact, erosion risk to dental enamel with overconsumption

sources.label: PMID 20211854 - Uses and safety of citric acid

116309.name: Total sugars
116309.description: Total sugars represent the sum of all monosaccharides and disaccharides present in a product, contributing to caloric content and sweetness.
116309.risks: Excessive intake associated with increased risk of obesity and dental caries

sources.label: PMCID: PMC6520897 - Dietary sugars and health
PMID: 25424933 - Sugar intake and obesity risk

116387.name: Orange and black carrot concentrate
116387.description: Concentrated extract from black carrots primarily used as a natural colorant due to its high anthocyanin content.
116387.benefits: Natural coloring agent, contains antioxidant anthocyanins
116387.risks: Irritation or sensitization rare but possible in sensitive individuals, potential contamination depending on processing, minimal ingestion toxicity at typical use levels

sources.label: PMC – Anthocyanins from black carrot: natural source for colorant and antioxidant properties
Study on safety and bioactivity of black carrot anthocyanins

116659.name: Citroen
116659.description: Dutch for lemon, fruit used as flavoring and source of vitamin C and bioactive compounds.
116659.benefits: Source of vitamin C, antioxidants, flavoring agent
116659.risks: Potential oral mucosal irritation in sensitive individuals, possible photosensitivity with skin contact

116866.name: Potassium Sorbate (food grade preservative)
116866.description: Mixture of common food preservatives: potassium sorbate (antimicrobial), BHT and TBHQ (antioxidants), and citric acid (acidulant and preservative).
116866.benefits: Prevent microbial growth and oxidation, extend shelf life of products
116866.risks: Irritation and sensitization potential, possible endocrine disruption (BHT, TBHQ), contamination risk from processing byproducts, regulatory limits on TBHQ levels

sources.label: PubChem - Potassium Sorbate

116885.name: Lycopene and beta-apo-8'-carotenal (for color)
116885.description: Natural carotenoid pigments used as food colorants; lycopene commonly found in tomatoes, beta-apo-8'-carotenal is a cleavage product of carotenoids.
116885.benefits: Provide natural red to orange color in foods, potential antioxidant properties
116885.risks: Rare allergic reactions or sensitivities; excessive intake could cause carotenodermia

116915.name: Conservante: benzoato de sodio
